blue-lattice-noise.look: Plain render at 8 cells: soft gray blobs about one cell across with no large light or dark areas. Wide view at 32 cells: an even, felt-like grain with no drift. Hillshade at 24 cells: uniform pebbly orange peel. Threshold 0.3: scattered specks that are fairly evenly spread, though some are elongated or fused, so not the near-uniform stipple the catalogue promised. Next to the Simplex panel on the existing sheet it reads as very similar at the same frequency. The literal quintic Laplacian (mode 0) is a pixelated square mosaic with obvious grid-aligned cells at both 8 and 24 cells, and 5 point versus 9 point stencils look nearly the same. Order 2 hat is the one distinct look: ringed dots with halos on a flat gray floor. Parity with warp is a warped plaid, regular and quilt-like. 3D iso 0 is a generic sponge with nothing special about it.
blue-lattice-noise.dims: 2D and 3D measured with check and vol. 4D not written (the harness has no 4D); the kernel moments for 4D are alpha = 3 by the same formula.
blue-lattice-noise.range: 2D default: [-0.913, 0.878] over 8 seeds and offsets, std 0.25, mean 0.000; 3D [-0.956, 0.906] on one 128 px slice, std 0.29; far coords fine, no NaN. Gains (0.6 in 2D, 0.85 in 3D) were set from these measurements and are not analytic bounds. mode=0 peaks at about +-1.0 with the measured constants.
blue-lattice-noise.artifacts: Mode 0 shows the grid strongly. Hat default still has a mild lattice imprint from the jittered grid: axis statistic 4.8 to 7.7 at window 32 across 4 seeds, isoCV about 0.3. Jitter 1 with R=1 lowers the grid feel but gives a sparser dots-on-gray field.
blue-lattice-noise.node_shape: If built at all, a BlueNoise generator: Order (1,2), Jitter, Radius (clamped to 1 + (1 - Jitter) / 2 so the 3^d window stays exact), Amplitude Min, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. Drop Laplacian and Parity.
blue-lattice-noise.port_notes: Hat kernel in s = r^2 / R^2 with no sqrt: 2D (1-s)^3 (1-5s), order 2 (1-s)^4 (1-14s+28s^2); 3D (1-s)^3 (1-11/3 s), order 2 (1-s)^4 (1-10s+17s^2); generally alpha = (d/2 + 4) / (d/2) for order 1. Each impulse has zero integral by construction, so low frequency suppression needs no neighbour stencil. Amplitude sign from one hash bit and magnitude from a bit field. Same window as CellularDistance.
blue-lattice-noise.params_text: plain render is mode=2,order=1,jitter=0.7,R=1.15,ampmin=0.6,gain=0.6 (the jittered zero-integral hat kernel, not the catalogue's Laplacian). Literal catalogue form: mode=0 (stencil=0 is the 5 point Laplacian, stencil=1 the 9 point), order=2 applies it twice, mode=1 is Parity, warp=0.8 adds the warp. Distinct alternate: mode=2,order=2 (ringed dots).

master.one_liner: Value-style lattice noise built on the discrete Laplacian of white lattice values (or on parity-alternated values), giving a coherent noise with zero DC and power ~k^4 at low frequency: fine, even, blob-free texture whose thresholds give evenly spread specks.
master.look: A uniform, grainy 'felt' or pebble-bed with no blobs, no drifts, no light or dark regions larger than a couple of cells; at any coverage the threshold set is small evenly spread specks of near-uniform size (stipple), and inverting the threshold gives evenly spread holes. Hillshade: fine even bumps like sandpaper or orange peel. Parity mode: a warped checkerboard with random contrast, quilt or cobble like. Clearly different from every red/pink noise on the sheet.
master.algorithm:
Lattice values v_c = rnd11(Hash(seed, c)).
Laplacian mode: L_c = 2d * v_c - sum_a (v_{c+e_a} + v_{c-e_a})   (integer-weight discrete Laplacian; Order 2 applies it twice over the 2-neighbourhood).
Field: f(x) = tensor-quintic interpolation of L over the 2^d corners of the cell containing x (exactly Value noise with L in place of v). Needed hashes: the corners' axis neighbours = the 4^d block minus its corner cubes (2D: 12, 3D: 32, 4D: ~80).
Normalise: var(L) = (4d^2 + 2d)/3 for uniform v, interpolation attenuates further; scale by a measured constant per dimension and order.
Parity mode: L_c = (-1)^(sum_a c_a) * (0.5 + 0.5 rnd01(h_c)); same interpolation (a jittered-amplitude checkerboard, power concentrated at the lattice Nyquist). Optional: run the result through a cheap DomainWarp inside the node to break the checker regularity.
Spectrum: the Laplacian transfer function is |sum_a (2 - 2cos k_a)| ~ |k|^2, so power ~ k^4 near k = 0; the quintic interpolation rolls off above Nyquist: a band-pass ring peaking around 0.3-0.5 cycles per cell with no low-frequency content.
master.why_new: Every existing coherent noise is low-frequency dominated (blobs, continents). A blue coherent noise is the missing detail layer: added to terrain it adds texture without moving coastlines (zero local mean), as a dither it breaks Terrace banding without clumps, and thresholded it is a scatter mask with even density. Not expressible: there is no blur/convolution node, Perlin's k^2 rolloff still looks blobby, and FBm with gain > 1 remains pink at the top octave.
master.simd_plan: Value.inl with a bigger hash block: 12 / 32 / ~80 hashes (int ops only) + 2^d-corner interpolation; ~1-1.5x Perlin in 2D, ~1.5x in 3D, ~2x in 4D. Order 2 roughly doubles the hash count. Dimension agnostic with GenT; tiles through 4D.
master.continuity: C2 (quintic interpolation of per-corner constants), same as Value noise.
master.params: Mode enum (Laplacian, Parity); Order (int 1..2); Feature Scale; Seed Offset; Output Min/Max.
master.risks: Still a grid lattice: the Laplacian stencil is axis aligned, so the FFT ring will show four lobes (axis statistic > 1); a simplex-lattice variant (Laplacian over the 6 hex neighbours in 2D) is more isotropic but a bigger port. Parity mode is regular unless warped. Low-frequency suppression means the field cannot be used alone for terrain, only as a detail/dither/scatter layer.
master.cost_note: Value.inl with a bigger hash block: 12 / 32 / ~80 hashes (int ops only) + 2^d-corner interpolation; ~1-1.5x Perlin in 2D, ~1.5x in 3D, ~2x in 4D.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: hat 2D about 4 ns (9 hashes and 9 kernel polynomials, CellularDistance class), 3D about 12 ns; Laplacian mode0 2D about 2 ns (12 hashes and bilinear quintic)

branchwork-caves.look: Vol cast (passages shown as solid): a real connected 3D tube network. Thin inlets merge into thicker trunks, stacked levels with vertical pits between them, and trunks on different levels running in different directions. Nothing like wormy thresholded noise. It does read a little like scaffolding, because the segments are straight and the three lattice directions are visible. Plan view: dark branching channels on a white rock plateau, twigs ending in small round pits at the shafts, trunks clearly thicker downstream, polyline zigzag. Threshold at P50 looks crowded because P50 is not the wall level. XZ slice: flattened ellipses on gently undulating bedding lines, with a few vertical shafts joining them.
branchwork-caves.dims: 2D (one bedding plane) and 3D (stacked planes with shafts) measured. 4D not written; the idea only proposes a crossfade and it would not tile.
branchwork-caves.range: -1 to 1 by clamp (rock plateau at 1), measured over 8 seeds, mean 0.43, 0 NaN. Iso 0 is the tube wall.
branchwork-caves.artifacts: Flow axis of one layer is very obvious in the wide plan view: parallel diagonal streams. Across layers the axis changes by 60 degree steps, which helps in 3D. Polyline straightness shows in the cast. c0ratio 1.57, max slope 83: small jumps remain from keeping only the top 4 edges by raw distance (slope 65 at top 3 with the wider cap, 10 at top 6; computing area for all edges would end them but cost more). A faint thin vertical line is visible in the XZ slice, cause not identified. Sinkhole mode is coded (surf param, flare), but the vol view placed the ground plane as a wall through the cube, so it told me nothing and I did not keep it; treat sinkholes as unverified.
branchwork-caves.node_shape: Members: Feature Scale, Layer Thickness, Upstream Rows K, Radius Base, Radius Exponent, Radius Offset, Max Radius, Flattening, Shaft Chance, Shaft Radius, Bedding Undulation, Warp Amplitude, Surface Source (optional hybrid), Output {Field, LogArea}, Seed Offset.
branchwork-caves.port_notes: Key trick that removes the shaft alignment risk in the idea: site positions are hashed without the layer and only the flow bits use the layer seed, so every site is a node on every layer and a shaft at a lower layer source always links two passages (by construction; not checked by a connectivity count). Per layer flow rotation uses true triangular lattice labels: a 60 degree step maps (e,r) to integer (E,R), so the jitter hash is still shared. Radius offset rb lets twigs fade out continuously, which gives sparse branchwork instead of a tube on every edge. Clamp at cap keeps the layer bracket switch invisible as long as (T - undulation) * k - rmax > cap; true at defaults (2.4 vs 0.22). Sorting the top 4 edges per lane needs masks; consider all edges with K=4 if the look survives. Bug worth keeping in mind: a smooth min with a 1e9 operand returns 0 through lerp rounding, so the no-shaft distance is a small constant.
branchwork-caves.params_text: K=12,top=4,cap=0.22,r0=0.07,rb=0.08,re=0.4,rmax=0.3,tz=2,k=1.8,shaft=0.3,rs=0.11,warp=0.9,wf=0.13,ub=0.5,uf=0.15,rot=1 (all code defaults) at --window 16; vol uses --set inv=1 --window 12 to show the passages as a solid cast.

master.one_liner: 3D SDF of karst conduits: directed river networks on bedding planes, tube radius from exact catchment area, vertical shafts at sources, sinkholes where shafts meet the surface. Builds on the CatchmentRivers lattice.
master.look: True branchwork caves: small inlets merging into a large trunk passage, stacked levels linked by pits, unlike the wormy blobs of thresholded noise. A 2D slice shows a plan map of passages.
master.algorithm: Layer n=floor(z/Tz). In each of the two nearest bedding layers, run the 2D CatchmentRivers lattice in plan, with flow along dip direction and layer-specific seed. Tube SDF: elliptical cross-section: d=sqrt(dist2D^2+(k*(z-z_n))^2)-rho(area), with rho~c*area^0.4 and k>1 for flattened phreatic tubes. Shafts: sites with area=1 and hash
master.why_new: Thresholded noise caves have no flow hierarchy, and passage size has no relation to connectivity. Here passages grow downstream by construction, using exact area.
master.simd_plan: 2 layers x CatchmentRivers lattice search + walkers at K=16, plus 3D shaft checks. Estimate 60-100 ns in 3D. 2D is one layer with z=0. 4D would be crossfaded time; no tiling.
master.continuity: C0 for the SDF given smooth-min, with area lerped along segments as in CatchmentRivers; layer seam hidden because tubes fade from z distance before layer switching if Tz exceeds the tube's vertical radius.
master.params: Layer Thickness, Lateral Scale, K (int), Radius Coefficient, Flattening k, Shaft Chance, Dip Angle (float), Surface Source (optional hybrid).
master.risks: Not tested. Depends on the CatchmentRivers look being solved. Shaft alignment with both layers is the fiddly part; missed alignment gives dangling passages. Fairly niche compared to its cost. In 3D the axis bias is less visible, an advantage.
master.cost_note: Estimate 60-100 ns in 3D.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D 60-100 ns, 3D 120-200 ns (2 layers x 20 edges x 3 hashes, 4 edges x 2 endpoints x 12 rows x 2 walkers x 2 layers = 384 walker hashes, shafts, 4 warp Perlins, 2 undulation Perlins). Above the catalogue's 60-100 ns guess. Scalar 2D measured 1013.4 ns, which benefits from a walker early out the port cannot use.

chaos-map-noise.look: Liquid chrome. Smooth white eye shaped islands with faint nested rings, separated by dark grainy veins and silky streaks that wrap around them. N=10-16 FTLE is the good output: streamers stay readable; N=32 turns them into fine white noise. Orbit mean alone is dull (large soft black eyes on flat gray with faint horizontal bands). Noise driven K gives a real order versus chaos gradient: K0=0.5 is mostly flat bands with some eyes, K0=1.6 is mostly black grain. Hillshade reads as metal pebbles lying in a banded sediment. Wide view: rows of blobs, stretched horizontally, not random looking. XZ slice of the 3D form: similar chrome but with an obvious grid of crossing seams at the lattice.
chaos-map-noise.dims: 2D and 3D measured (3D is the Froeschle map with I2 from noise, z-continuity mean 0.019 per dz=1e-3, max 0.80, no NaN). 4D not run; Orbit4 takes four coordinates so the code form exists, the harness has no 4D command.
chaos-map-noise.range: -1 to 1 by construction (clamped), measured -1.000 to 1.000 over 8 seeds, mean 0.61, 0 NaN. Histogram is skewed: most samples are in the upper half, with a spike at 1.
chaos-map-noise.artifacts: c0ratio 1.23, max slope 1327: the chaotic veins are effectively discontinuous and will alias and change with resolution, as the idea warned. 2 pi lattice is hidden by warp in the close view but visible as rows in the wide view and as a grid in the XZ slice. Horizontal bias from the KAM tori (axis ratio 17.5). Field is not centred, mean about 0.6, so a vol at iso 0 is a solid cube with cracks (rendered, looked at, not kept); a useful iso would be near 0.6.
chaos-map-noise.node_shape: Members: Period, K Base, K Noise (hybrid), Iterations, Coupling (3D/4D), Output {Lyapunov, OrbitMean, Mix}, Warp Amplitude, Warp Frequency, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
chaos-map-noise.port_notes: Used one tangent vector renormalised every 8 iterations instead of the 2x2 matrix from the idea: cheaper and the float does not overflow. All iterations branch free; one Sin + one Cos per iteration, one Floor for the wrap. Observable is 2 pi periodic in both inputs, so no seam at the frac. Fixed cadence renormalise needs a Sqrt and a Log every 8 iterations. Scalar ratio includes 12 std::map param reads per sample with an empty map (effect not measured separately).

master.one_liner: Iterate an area-preserving chaotic map (Chirikov standard map; Froeschle 4D map) from the sample's fractional position with its kick strength read from noise, outputting orbit stretch: KAM islands, island chains and chaotic seas.
master.look: The phase portrait of a Hamiltonian system: large smooth 'eyes' (islands) with nested resonance chains of smaller eyes along their rims, embedded in a grainy chaotic sea whose extent is controlled locally by the noise-driven K. Spatially it reads as whirlpools, nested cat's-eyes, chained beads: nothing remotely like it on the sheet. Use for ornamental/alien textures, fluid-like eyes, bead chains, as a mask for 'order vs chaos' regions.
master.algorithm:
theta = 2*pi*frac(x*Period), I = 2*pi*frac(y*Period); K = K0 + K1*n(p) (n smooth noise so chaoticity varies across space).
  (jt, ji) tangent vector = (1, 0) and (0, 1) tracked as 2x2 M = I
  for k in 0..N-1:                           // N = 16..40
      s = sin(theta), c = cos(theta)
      I = I + K*s ; theta = theta + I        // mod 2*pi via theta - 2*pi*Floor(theta/(2*pi)) on theta only
      M = [[1 + K*c, 1],[K*c, 1]] * M        // tangent map
      acc += cos(theta)                      // orbit average (optional output)
  FTLE = log(||M||_F / sqrt(2)) / N          // or sigma_max closed form
  Output enum: Lyapunov (FTLE remapped), OrbitMean (acc/N), Mix.
3D/4D: Froeschle map on (theta1, I1, theta2, I2) with coupling b, 4D node uses all four coordinates; 3D node sets I2 (or theta2) from noise(p). Smooth DomainWarp upstream breaks the visible 2*pi lattice.
master.why_new: A fixed iteration count of a symplectic map gives genuine Hamiltonian phase-space structure (KAM tori, resonances) with no counterpart in noise literature; letting noise drive the control parameter lets the ordered/chaotic character vary smoothly across space, so the pattern reads as a texture rather than a math plot.
master.simd_plan: One noise eval + N iterations each ~ Sin/Cos (shared polynomial), Floor, ~12 flops and a 2x2 (or 4x4) matrix product; N=32 ~ 600 flops: 2D ~15-20 ns (~15x Perlin), 3D/4D similar plus the 4x4 tangent product (~2x). Tiles on the 2*pi lattice by construction; GenTileable2D works via the noise term only. Everything branch-free.
master.continuity: Continuous inside regular (island) regions; effectively discontinuous in chaotic regions because of sensitive dependence (the grainy sea is the look). FTLE is bounded by log of the matrix norm so no NaNs; OrbitMean bounded in [-1,1].
master.params: Period float, K0 float, K1 hybrid (noise-driven kick), Iterations int, Coupling float (4D/3D), Output enum, Seeded (noise n), VariableRange.
master.risks: Visible 2*pi periodicity (needs upstream warp or K variation to hide); 'math plot' flavour; chaotic regions alias badly at any resolution; 3D story is weaker (noise-driven extra coordinate rather than a true 3D map).
master.cost_note: One noise eval + N iterations each ~ Sin/Cos (shared polynomial), Floor, ~12 flops and a 2x2 (or 4x4) matrix product; N=32 ~ 600 flops: 2D ~15-20 ns (~15x Perlin), 3D/4D similar plus the 4x4 tangent product (~2x).

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D about 10 ns at N=12 with 3 Perlin evals (warp x2, K) plus 12 sincos iterations. 3D about 20 ns. Scalar measured 515.7 ns.

escape-noise.look: Default (Julia, c = i): dark soft field threaded by thin bright veins that follow the noise contours, and every vein has short dendritic twigs and small loops growing off it. Reads as lightning, crackle glaze or glowing filaments. Hillshade shows a blue basin with fringed, branching ridges. XZ slice has the same character. Threshold at the median is only smooth blobs, because the fractal detail lives in the thin top end of the range. Other presets at N=32: Mandelbrot seahorse and elephant are mostly a white plateau with small dark fish-shaped holes (dull); preset 2 (-0.5,0.55 r=0.3) is plateau with crenellated shores; rabbit, San Marco and Siegel are hard edged blobs; preset 7 (Julia c=0.285,0.01) is contoured marbling; Trap output on the dendrite gives black blobs in a bright veined matte. First try with a wide c range was nearly all interior plateau.
escape-noise.dims: 2D and 3D measured (3D uses two perlin3 sources, same loop; z-continuity mean 0.0023 per dz=1e-3, max 0.40). 4D not run; the loop does not depend on dimension, only the two noise calls do.
escape-noise.range: Measured -0.483 to 1.000 over 8 seeds, mean -0.053, 0 NaN. Not centred: a port needs ScaleOutput on the measured range.
escape-noise.artifacts: c0ratio 1.45, max slope 641: gradient at the set boundary is unbounded, so the veins alias and thin out in the 4x wide view (speckled network). Terrain test failed as a plain height: relief of preset 2 is flat mesas with step cliffs and spiky fringes, no slope, not usable without softening. Vol at iso -0.25 was mostly solid with pockets (looked at, not kept); membranes are expected at higher iso, not rendered. Default look is close to a ridged perlin at large scale; the twigs are what is new. Continuity recheck: a very small real step remains, 0.003 at probe steps from 1e-3 to 1e-6 in a 0.6 unit window near the origin. The low c0ratio itself (plain 1.45, straddling 1.49) is mostly the steep set boundary.
escape-noise.node_shape: Members: Mode {Mandelbrot, Julia}, Centre X/Y, Radius (hybrid), JuliaC X/Y, Iterations, Escape Radius, Output {Count, Banded, Trap, Mix}, Shape, Trap X/Y, Noise Frequency, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. Presets matter: most c values are dull blobs.
escape-noise.port_notes: Written with freeze after escape, so it ports as mask + Select. Smooth count verified by reasoning continuous across escape bands; not-escaped lanes report N and the clamp joins them. One Log and one Log2 at the end, Pow only for the Shape curve (could be Sqrt). Scalar ratio includes about 15 std::map reads per sample on an empty map, not measured separately.
escape-noise.params_text: preset=3,out=0,N=24,fs=0.4,shape=0.6 (code defaults; preset 3 = Julia mode, c = i, z0 = 1.2*(n1, n2)) at --window 16. Terrain test: preset=2,shape=1,N=32 --hscale 60.

master.one_liner: Escape-time of z^2 + c where c (or z0) is read from two seeded noises: fractal coastlines and dendrites from a single octave at ~4x Perlin.
master.look: Mandelbrot mode: smooth noise-like low regions, plateaus where c(p) falls inside the set, and between them fractal coastlines with fjords and islands at every scale that follow the contours of the underlying noise: 'plateau islands with infinitely crenellated shores'. Julia mode with c near the set boundary (e.g. c = i): dendritic lightning/fern/river-delta structures threaded through the noise. Orbit traps give nested 'eye' and 'spiral' ornaments inside. Entirely absent from the sheet; terrain mesas with fractal shorelines, lightning masks, ornamental textures.
master.algorithm:
a = n_1(p), b = n_2(p) in [-1,1] (two seeded Simplex/Perlin, any dimension).
Mode Mandelbrot: c = Centre + Radius*(a, b), z = 0.   Mode Julia: c = JuliaC (param), z = Centre + Radius*(a, b).
  n = 0; (zx, zy) as float32v
  for k in 0..N-1:                                        // N = 16..48 fixed
      r2 = zx*zx + zy*zy
      inside = r2 <= R2                                   // mask, R = 2..4 (escape radius)
      nx = zx*zx - zy*zy + cx ; ny = 2*zx*zy + cy
      zx = Select(inside, nx, zx); zy = Select(inside, ny, zy)   // freeze after escape
      n  = n + Select(inside, 1, 0)
  nu = n + 1 - log2( log(sqrt(r2_final)) / log(R) )     // smooth iteration count, clamp to [0,N] (not-escaped lanes: nu = N)
  Output enum: Count = nu/N ; Banded = sin(nu*freq) ; Trap = min_k |z_k - T| accumulated in-loop (orbit trap, textures the interior) ; Mix = Count with Trap inside.
master.why_new: Pulls back a fractal boundary through a smooth map, so a constant tiny iteration count yields unbounded boundary detail without octaves. Cost is dominated by just two noise evaluations, so it is one of the cheapest 'look' nodes and works identically in 2D/3D/4D.
master.simd_plan: 2 noise evals + N iterations of ~8 flops + 2 Selects + 1 compare; N=32 is ~300 flops. 2D ~5 ns (~4-5x Perlin); 3D ~7 ns; 4D ~12 ns, i.e. almost dimension-independent extra cost. One Log and one Log2 at the end. Tiles in 4D trivially.
master.continuity: Continuous (smooth iteration count is continuous across escape bands; interior plateau is constant) but with unbounded gradient at the fractal set boundary; Trap output continuous.
master.params: Mode enum (Mandelbrot/Julia), Centre X/Y floats, Radius hybrid, JuliaC X/Y floats, Iterations int, EscapeRadius float, Output enum, Trap X/Y floats, Band Frequency float, Seeded, ScalableGenerator.
master.risks: Recognisably 'Mandelbrot-ish' if parameters are left at defaults; aliasing when rendered at low resolution; interior is flat unless Trap/Mix is used; R and the log smoothing need care at nu near N.
master.cost_note: 2D ~5 ns (~4-5x Perlin); 3D ~7 ns; 4D ~12 ns, i.e. almost dimension-independent extra cost.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D 5-8 ns, 3D 8-10 ns at N=24 (2 noise evals + 24 iterations of about 8 flops and 2 Selects). Scalar measured 282.3 ns.

exact-gaussian-noise.look: Plain Uniform render: high contrast soft blobs with a flat histogram, reading as an even-area black to white cloud with faint polygon hints. Gaussian mode: lower contrast soft blobs. FBm of it: cloud-like, with a convincing rough terrain hillshade. Coverage ramp at freq 3: black dominates on the left and white on the right, with holes and islands morphing through a labyrinth in between. It works as advertised, with a soft blob edge. Fractal coverage ramp: a fractal coast with exact land share. 3D at cov 0.10: separate blobs. 3D at cov 0.35: a connected sponge. The catalogue's grid and simplex lattices do not look like the promised smooth noise: quintic weights give a soft pixel mosaic and simplex (0.5-r^2)^4 weights give a soft hexagon mosaic, because one vertex dominates most of each cell.
exact-gaussian-noise.dims: 2D and 3D measured (check and vol; 3D continuity at dz=1e-3 is max 0.0087). 4D not written (no harness support), the construction is dimension independent.
exact-gaussian-noise.range: Mode 1 and 2: exactly [-1,1], measured [-1.000, 1.000] over 8 seeds; 3D [-0.998, 0.997]. Mode 0 is f/3, so it can pass 1: measured [-1.244, 1.348] over 8 seeds.
exact-gaussian-noise.artifacts: Exactness is per point, so one image still fluctuates: per image std 0.02 to 0.038 of coverage on a 16 x 16 cell view. Faint polygon creases where one kernel dominates; these grow when jitter rises with the radius bound (max slope in f at freq 1: J .7 R 1.15 4.4, J .5 R 1.25 2.9, J .3 R 1.35 2.1, J 0 R 1.5 1.4). The harness hash needed one extra remix before the Box-Muller bit split. Axis statistic 29 at window 8 is a small window effect and was not chased further.
exact-gaussian-noise.node_shape: ExactGaussian generator: Mode (Gaussian, Uniform, Coverage); Coverage (hybrid 0..1); Softness; Lattice (Jittered, Grid, Simplex or Hex); Jitter (clamps Radius to 1 + (1 - Jitter) / 2); Octaves and Gain (unit L2 amplitudes, independent seeds); Feature Scale; Seed Offset; Output Min/Max.
exact-gaussian-noise.port_notes: Weights may use any hash bits as long as the bits feeding the Gaussian stay independent: jitter from a second hash mix, Gaussian from the first. f = sum w g * InvSqrt( sum w^2 ). With J <= 1 and R >= the worst nearest point distance, sum w^2 never reaches 0. A plain FractalFBm on top loses exactness, because its normalisation is not L2, so octaves belong inside the node. erf is A&S 7.1.26. Lattice 1 is a cheap discovery of its own.
exact-gaussian-noise.params_text: plain render is mode=1 (Uniform),lattice=2,jitter=0.5,R=1.25,freq=1.5. Coverage: mode=2,cov=0.3,soft=0.02; coverage ramp images: mode=2,freq=3,covsrc=1,soft=0.02,jitter=0.7,R=1.15 and mode=2,freq=1.2,octaves=5,gain=0.55,covsrc=1,soft=0.02,jitter=0.7,R=1.15. Terrain style: mode=0,octaves=5,gain=0.55. Catalogue lattices: lattice=0 (grid), lattice=1 (simplex).

master.one_liner: Value-lattice noise whose marginal is exactly N(0,1) at every point (L2-normalised weights over Gaussian corner values), with an erf output mode that is exactly uniform and a hybrid Coverage mask whose area fraction is exactly what you asked for.
master.look: Like Value noise but without the lattice-period amplitude modulation (ordinary value noise has only half the std at 2D cell centres; the L2 normalisation removes that beat), so blobs look more even and the grid is less visible. Uniform mode is a flat-histogram field: equal area at every grey level. Coverage mode with a spatially varying hybrid gives leopard spots (c~0.2) morphing into zebra labyrinth (c~0.5) into holes (c~0.8) with constant feature size: animal coats, lichen, lakes-vs-land ratio maps. Good for terrain masks where sea level must mean an exact land fraction.
master.algorithm:
Lattice: integer grid, 2^d corners c_i of the cell containing x (same as Value noise).
Per corner: h = Hash(seed, c_i); u1 = ((h & 0xFFFF) + 0.5) / 65536; u2 = ((h >> 16) + 0.5) / 65536;
  g_i = sqrt(-2 ln u1) * cos(2*pi*u2)            // Box-Muller, exactly N(0,1); |g| <= 4.7 because u1 >= 2^-17
  (cheaper option: g_i = PhiInv(u) via odd polynomial on (2u-1) with clamped tails; loses exactness in the last 0.5% of mass)
Weights: t_a = quintic(frac(x_a)); w_i = prod_a (corner bit a ? t_a : 1 - t_a)   // standard tensor weights, sum = 1
f = sum_i w_i g_i / sqrt( sum_i w_i^2 )            // key step: for fixed x this is a unit-L2 combination of iid N(0,1) => exactly N(0,1)
   (sum w_i^2 >= 1/2^d > 0 always, so no 0/0; the 1/sqrt is a smooth positive factor)
Mode Gaussian: out = f * (1/3), VariableRange around +-1 (tails beyond 3 sigma clipped by Output Min/Max)
Mode Uniform:  u = 0.5 * (1 + erf(f / sqrt2))  with A&S 7.1.26 (t = 1/(1+0.3275911|z|), 5-term poly * exp(-z^2), restore sign); out = 2u - 1   // exactly uniform
Mode Coverage: c = Coverage(x) (hybrid); out = smoothstep((c - u) / Softness) mapped to [-1,1]  // fraction of plane with out>0 is exactly c, even when c varies in space
Optional Lattice enum: Grid (above) | Simplex (OpenSimplex-style kernels (0.5-r^2)^4 as the w_i, same L2 normalisation; max vertex distance 0.577 < 0.707 so the norm never vanishes).
master.why_new: No existing node has a known marginal. Thresholds on Perlin/Simplex/Value give coverage that drifts with octaves, gain and position in the lattice. Here coverage c is exact by construction, pointwise, with a hybrid: 'water covers 30 percent' is one parameter, not a trial-and-error threshold. Percolation becomes a knob: in 2D the c=0.5 set is critical (neither phase connects), c>0.5 makes that phase percolate; in 3D a Gaussian excursion set percolates above about 16 percent volume, so c in [0.16,0.84] gives a bi-continuous sponge, outside it isolated blobs. It is also the Gaussianiser stage that StatBlend and CdfRemap need to be exact.
master.simd_plan: Pure lattice code like Value.inl: 2^d hashes, 2^d x (Log, Sqrt, Cos) for Box-Muller, tensor weights, one Reciprocal-sqrt (InvSqrt) for the norm; erf = 1 Exp + poly. No window search, branch-free. 2D ~2-3x Perlin, 3D ~3x Perlin (8 corners), 4D 16 corners ~3-4x Perlin; GenT<P...> parameter-pack implementation works since it is dimension agnostic. Tiles correctly through the 4D torus.
master.continuity: C2 with quintic weights (sum w_i^2 is a smooth positive function, erf and smoothstep are smooth); Coverage mode is C1 where Coverage is C1.
master.params: Mode enum (Gaussian, Uniform, Coverage); Coverage (hybrid, 0..1); Softness (float, width of the mask edge in probability units); Lattice enum (Grid, Simplex); Feature Scale; Seed Offset; Output Min/Max.
master.risks: Box-Muller costs three transcendentals per corner; the polynomial PhiInv alternative is cheaper but clips tails. Grid lattice still shows some axis alignment (less than Value noise but more than Simplex). Exactness is per point; neighbouring points are strongly correlated, so coverage over a small window fluctuates like any noise. Gradient-noise version does not work (dividing by the Gaussian variance sqrt(sum w_i^2 |d_i|^2) is 0/0 at lattice points and the limit is direction dependent).
master.cost_note: 2D ~2-3x Perlin, 3D ~3x Perlin (8 corners), 4D 16 corners ~3-4x Perlin; GenT<P...> parameter-pack implementation works since it is dimension agnostic.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: lattice 2 2D about 7 ns (9 hashes, 9 Box-Muller with Log, Sqrt and Cos, 1 InvSqrt), 3D about 25 ns; erf adds about 0.5 ns. Grid lattice 2D about 3 ns but it looks like a mosaic. A polynomial inverse normal in place of Box-Muller would cut the cost, at the price of clipped tails.

isolated-extrema-noise.look: Plain: bright soft discs of varied size and height scattered on a black floor, like a starfield or bubbles, with no visible grid at jitter 0.7. Craters: round pits with raised rims on a flat plain; the relief reads convincingly as a pocked lunar surface. Base 0.5 relief: separate conical peaks standing on a low rolling fbm plain, like volcanic islands, none joined. 3D vol: separate balls of varied size floating in the cube, none touching. Warping makes bumps into stretched ellipses and adds nothing now that the grid is hidden. The catalogue's fixed radius form is worse: at jitter 0.5 the bumps are tiny dots, and at jitter 0.3 clear grid rows appear.
isolated-extrema-noise.dims: 2D and 3D measured (check, vol; 3D z-continuity max 0.0040 at dz=1e-3). 4D not written; the code is dimension agnostic.
isolated-extrema-noise.range: [0.000, 0.939] over 8 seeds, mean 0.028, std 0.094; far coords fine; 3D [0, 0.657] on one slice. Unipolar by default, and mostly the floor value 0 (area above 0.02 is 14.5 percent). Would need Output Min/Max remapping to sit in [-1,1].
isolated-extrema-noise.artifacts: The floor is flat by design, so the field alone is sparse. Bumps never cross a cell line, which leaves a statistical gap along the grid; it was not visible in the images at jitter 0.7, and rotation (rot) is available. Density at 0.5 with dsoft 0.08 gives 54.5 percent of cells with some signal at T=0.02, since the fade extends the active set by dsoft/2, so 'exact density' holds for the midpoint of the fade rather than for any signal. Height from radius (hr) makes small bumps low, which is what keeps tiny bumps near cell borders from reading as sharp pins.
isolated-extrema-noise.node_shape: IsolatedBumps generator: Jitter, Radius Fraction, Radius From Position (bool, default on), Height Min/Max, Height From Radius, Density (hybrid 0..1), Density Soft, Shape (Dome, Crater), Bipolar (bool), Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. Base can be left to Add in the graph. Overlap can be dropped: it loses the guarantee and looks like existing splats.
isolated-extrema-noise.port_notes: New over the catalogue: per point inscribed radius rc = 0.5 - max( |ox|, |oy| [, |oz|] ), R = rf * rc, A *= lerp( 1, 2 * rc, hr ). This fits a bigger and more varied bump at any jitter, needs no extra window and holds the guarantee at rf <= 1. Divide t^2 by R^2 with a guard for rc = 0 (jitter 1). Kernel (1-t^2)^3 with a Select at t^2 >= 1; Crater is k * ( 1 - 2.2 ( 1 - t^2 )^2 ) * 1.6.
isolated-extrema-noise.params_text: plain render is jitter=0.7,rf=1,radmode=1,hr=0.7,hmin=0.35,hmax=1,density=0.9,dsoft=0.08. Craters: shape=1,hmin=0.5 with relief --hscale 40. Hills on terrain: base=0.5 with relief --hscale 70. Catalogue fixed radius: radmode=0,jitter=0.5.

master.one_liner: Disjoint-support bump noise: one compact kernel per active jittered cell, radius constrained so bumps never overlap or cross cell borders, giving exactly one maximum per active cell, superlevel components that are always single convex discs, exact feature counts, and a hybrid density control, from a 1-cell window.
master.look: A field of separate domes (or craters when Bipolar) on a flat floor, each sitting in its own cell, sizes and heights random, never fused: like raindrops on glass, lunar craters that never cut each other, tree crowns in a plantation, pores in foam. Thresholded at any level: scattered discs with controlled count that never merge. With a Base noise: terrain with islands that never join, or guaranteed isolated hills.
master.algorithm:
Cell c = floor(x), h = Hash(seed, c). Point p_c = c + 0.5 + Jitter * rnd11(h) * 0.5 per axis (Jitter in [0,1]).
Radius r = RadiusFraction * 0.5 * (1 - Jitter) in cells (RadiusFraction <= 1 guarantees the bump stays inside its own cell: |p_c - cell centre| <= Jitter/2 and r <= (1 - Jitter)/2, so support never reaches the cell boundary and never overlaps a neighbour; the window is the single cell).
Active weight: a_c = smoothstep( (Density(x) - rnd01(h')) / DensitySoft ) with Density a hybrid in [0,1] (continuous fade-in instead of a hard gate, so spatially varying density stays continuous).
Amplitude A_c = lerp(Height Min, Height Max, rnd01(h'')) ; Bipolar flag flips the sign for half the cells (pits).
Kernel K(t) = (1 - t^2)^3 for t < 1 else 0 (C2 at the edge), t = |x - p_c| / r.
Out = Base(x) * BaseAmp + a_c * A_c * K(t)   (Base is a hybrid, default 0).
Guarantees (Base = 0): every active cell contributes exactly one strict local maximum at p_c; for any threshold t > 0 each connected component of {out > t} is one convex disc centred on p_c; the number of components above t in an area is Binomial(cells, P(A_c a_c > t)), i.e. exact expected density per cell. With a weak base (|grad Base| * BaseAmp small compared to A_min * 2.6 / r) the maxima shift slightly but remain one per bump.
Overlap flag: r up to 1 cell with a 3^d window, loses the guarantee, gives standard sparse-convolution 'pebbles'.
master.why_new: CellularDistance F1 discs merge whenever two points come close, and per-cell heights via CellularValue multiply are discontinuous at Voronoi borders. This node gives exact Morse control (one maximum per active cell, nothing else), topology control (all superlevel components are genus-0 discs), exact density via a hybrid, and it costs half a Perlin because the window is one cell. Good as a placement/feature field where every maximum should be an object.
master.simd_plan: One hash per lane (three bit fields), one kernel polynomial, one Sqrt-free t^2 compare (kernel in t^2: (1 - t^2)^3 needs no sqrt), Select for t^2 >= 1, plus the hybrid Density/Base evaluations. ~0.5x Perlin in all dimensions (dimension agnostic GenT). Overlap mode = 3^d window like Cellular.
master.continuity: C2 (kernel is C2 at its edge, zero before the cell boundary; the density fade is C1), so C1 overall when Density varies.
master.params: Jitter; Radius Fraction (0..1); Height Min / Height Max; Density (hybrid 0..1); Density Soft; Bipolar (bool); Base (hybrid), Base Amp; Overlap (bool, 3^d window); Feature Scale; Seed Offset.
master.risks: Looks sparse by nature: the flat floor dominates (that is the feature, but it is not a general-purpose noise). Jitter and radius trade off (jitter 0.5 gives radius <= 0.25 cell). The underlying grid is visible at low jitter; Overlap mode exists for a more organic look at the price of the guarantee.
master.cost_note: ~0.5x Perlin in all dimensions (dimension agnostic GenT).

measured.scalar_note: 1.78 is the harness speed command with default params, which includes the std::map param reads per sample (3.25 when a --set string makes the map larger). Kernel alone with params held in a struct: 7.5 ns against perlin2 50.3 ns, ratio 0.15. The scalar perlin2 pays for Cos and Sin in rndDir2, so 0.15 flatters it against the real Perlin node.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 2D about 0.6 ns, 3D about 0.7 ns, 4D about 0.8 ns (1 hash per lane, a few bit field extracts, one polynomial, no window)

knot-flow.look: Reads as sawn timber at once: long parallel grain lines of varying width that part and close around scattered oval knots, with concentric rings inside each knot and calm stretches between them. Threshold is a believable black and white plank. The 3D solid is a stack of thin sheets that dimple and bulge around knots, closer to strata around concretions than a branch; an XZ slice parallel to the layers shows soft blotches rather than lines. Wide view holds as a band of fine wavy lines with a horizontal FFT streak, by design.

dims.2D: works, measured c0ratio 7.81, max slope 129.4. Density 1 with large knots measured c0ratio 7.83.
dims.3D: works, measured z continuity max 0.0522 for dz=1e-3; The comparison shows layered sheets draped around spherical knots
dims.4D: Eval4 implemented with a 3^4 window and exponent 4; measured on an oblique plane (slice4=1): c0ratio 7.77, range -0.970..0.965, 16.13x perlin2 scalar (794.7 ns)

knot-flow.artifacts: Very strongly anisotropic by design, axis stat about 60. Max slope is high where rings=3 inside small knots. Overlapping knots at density 1 merge into odd double eyes, as, and flat cores at rings=0 look like blurry smears; no seams were visible. Lines cannot cross because they are level sets of one scalar; they can only pinch and close. The catalogue risk of crossing stripes did not appear. 3D knots are spheres, not branches, so a slice does not show a cone or a limb, and this is not a tree model; radial trunk curvature needs a separate source. Range stays near -0.97..0.97 with a slight negative mean of -0.028.
knot-flow.node_shape: KnotFlow: Frequency hybrid, Grain Direction float, Knot Density hybrid, Knot Radius Min/Max float, Ring Spacing float, Along Grain Stretch float, Warp hybrid, Profile enum (Sawtooth, Cosine), Skew float, Width Variation float, Grid Jitter float, Seed Offset, Feature Scale, Output Min/Max
knot-flow.port_notes: Fixed 3^D window in warped coordinates, cell index uses s = n + warp. Per feature: hash, one sqrt, integer power (R/r)^D, Select between outside and inside, smoothstep window. Density is a mask times weight. Influence ends at fade = 1.05, safe for jitter 0.8 because reach is 1 + (1 - J) / 2 = 1.1. Widths and tone are functions of psi only, using 1D noise, so a port can use a small 1D hash. Far coords (4e4) measured fine, std 0.449.
knot-flow.params_text: freq=3.5,dir=1.5707963,density=0.4,rmin=0.12,rmax=0.36,jitter=0.8,fade=1.05,rings=3,along=0.55,warp=0.35,wscale=0.7,wstretch=5,profile=0,skew=0.8,tone=0.25,widthvar=0.5 (the code defaults). Smooth stripes: profile=1. Few big knots: density=0.15.

master.one_liner: Layers that bend smoothly around scattered obstacles using windowed potential-flow doublets, for wood grain around knots, strata around concretions and wakes behind rocks.
master.look: Plank-like parallel lines that flow around round knots with rings inside, and streamlines closing behind them; it reads as sawn timber at once. Could also read as draped sediment around concretions, or raked gravel around stones.
master.algorithm: s=n.x+warp*source(x). For each feature in the 3^D window: dy=s-(n.p_i); r=|x-p_i| measured with the warped coordinate along n (x' = x with s replacing the n component); outside=(n.p_i)+dy*(1-(R/r)^D); inside=(n.p_i)+A*(R-r), giving concentric rings; target=Select(r>R,outside,inside); w=smoothstep(1,R,r); psi+=gate*w*(target-s). Output a stripe profile of psi*freq, such as an asymmetric sawtooth min(fr/0.8,(1-fr)/0.2) for early and late wood. On the circle r=R, psi is constant, so stripes hug the knot. The exponent D makes it dimension-agnostic: 2D is the cylinder stream function, while 3D and 4D use the analogous sheet deflection.
master.why_new: A domain warp cannot wrap stripes around a disc without pinching or crossing them; this formula keeps lines non-crossing because it is a stream function. The published wood work (Larsson et al.) merges a trunk and knot distance field with a smooth minimum, whereas this is a much cheaper stripe-only approach and needs no trunk model.
master.simd_plan: Per feature: hash, one sqrt, integer power of (R/r). Estimated 5.5 ns in 2D (5x Perlin, 1.4x CellularDistance), 16 ns in 3D, 50 ns in 4D. Try 2^D corners with jitter (not tested for this idea). Window fade guarantees no seams.
master.continuity: C0 outside core; at r=R both branches equal n.p_i, so psi is C0 with a slope change. Dense scanlines: 0 jumps. A sawtooth profile adds a creased peak by design, not a jump, as the prototype's form is triangular.
master.params: Frequency (hybrid), Direction, Knot Density (hybrid), Knot Radius Min/Max, Ring Spacing A, Profile Skew, Warp Source (hybrid).
master.risks: Overlapping knots add perturbations and can pinch lines or make stripes cross, since superposition is not exact with windowing. Only 2D was rendered; 3D sheet deflection is a formula-level claim. This is a look, not a tree model, so whole-trunk ring curvature needs a separate radial source.
master.cost_note: Estimated 5.5 ns in 2D (5x Perlin, 1.4x CellularDistance), 16 ns in 3D, 50 ns in 4D.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 238.4 ns against perlin2 52.8 at the defaults, including 3 perlin for warp, width and tone. The scalar loop skips empty cells, which a SIMD port cannot do. Params read once in the speed run.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: about 7 to 9 ns 2D, about 20 ns 3D, about 55 ns 4D (the catalogue gave 5.5, 16, 50 without the width and tone terms)

magic-noise.look: Glassy black and white rings: closed concentric contours like agate bands or oil film eyes, tight clusters of thin rings beside calm soft blobs where dmod lowers the distortion. Threshold shows rings inside rings, a topology no other noise here gives. Wide 4x view holds even filigree with a loose diagonal cell rhythm but no exact repeat that I could see. The 3D form slices into the same glass cells and the isosurface reads as thin curved shells with ring cut faces, slightly jagged at the raymarch step.

dims.3D: works, measured z continuity max 0.0344 for dz=1e-3; The comparison shows agate like shells
dims.4D: Eval4 implemented; measured on an oblique plane (slice4=1): c0ratio 7.89, range -1..1, 4.84x perlin2 scalar with a 3D perlin as its source

magic-noise.artifacts: Range saturates over 8 seeds (-1..1) at these defaults; at low d the range collapses and shifts (depth 2 d 0.7 read 0.64..1.00, depth 5 d 0.7 read -0.40..-0.32), so d is not safe to take low without a remap. Mean over 8 seeds measured -0.000 at the defaults but single windows at seeds 1 to 4 read -0.066, 0.032, 0.005, -0.090. Pure trig form measured a mean of 0.099. High distortion turns to chaos: depth 5 d 4 is white static, and depth 3 d 4 has static patches; dmod too high does the same in regions (dmod 0.8 at d 2.5). FFT has a diagonal cross, axis stat 14.2. Max slope is high, so a 1 px per feature view aliases. Seeds all share one family.
magic-noise.node_shape: MagicNoise: Depth int, Distortion hybrid, Spin bool or seed driven rotation, Phase Drift hybrid, Seed Offset, Feature Scale, Output Min/Max
magic-noise.port_notes: No lattice and no per point hash: 3 + 3*Depth FS::Sin/Cos, constant loop, seed gives 3 phases and a rotation. Distortion as a HybridSource is what produces the calm and intricate zones. Direction tables are hand picked per dimension; 2D from the catalogue scaled by sc, 3D and 4D picked for this prototype with no long range test beyond the check run. Far coords (4e4) measured fine, std 0.599. A Modulus by 2*pi on each dot would help precision further out; not tested.
magic-noise.params_text: depth=3,d=2.2,sc=1.2,spin=1,drift=1.5,dscale=0.21,dmod=0.35 (the code defaults). Pure trig with no source: drift=0,dmod=0. Agate bubbles: depth=5,d=1.5,dmod=0,drift=0. Blender's lattice form: blender=1.

master.one_liner: Blender's Magic trig-feedback made seedable and non-repeating with incommensurate plane waves, at a cost that does not grow with dimension.
master.look: Agate eyes, oil-film rings, glassy interference blobs, psychedelic contours. Depth 3: rings in soft cells. Depth 5: intricate filigree. Blender's lattice form: diagonal repeating tiles (visible in my test). Prototype: dcc_lens modes 4 (Blender) and 5 (quasi-periodic).
master.algorithm: Blender form: a,b,c are sin/cos of diagonal combinations, then depth steps a=Cos(a-b-c)*d, etc., periodic on a diagonal lattice. Proposed form: phases p1,p2,p3 from seed bits; three unit-ish direction vectors at incommensurate angles and frequencies per dimension, e.g. 2D (.809,.588), (-.393,1.210), (-1.570,-.392). a=Sin(dot(u1,x)+p1); b=Sin(dot(u2,x)+p2); c=Sin(dot(u3,x)+p3). for i in 0..Depth-1 (constant): na=Sin(D*(b-c)+p1+1.1*i); nb=Cos(D*(c+a)+p2); nc=Sin(D*(a-b)+p3-0.7*i); a,b,c=na,nb,nc. out=(a+b+c)/3*1.5.
master.why_new: No lattice, no hash per point, and a look absent from the sheet: closed concentric contours with no cell structure. Same cost in 4D as in 2D, so it is the only family here where 4D (and GenTileable) is cheap. Not a graph: no Sin of a value, and feedback needs per-iteration phases.
master.simd_plan: 3+Depth*3 Sin/Cos, no hashing, constant loop. Depth 3: 12 trig calls, est 6-10 ns in every dimension; about 7x Perlin in 2D, 2x in 4D and 0.2x CellularDistance 4D. Far coords: wrap each dot with Modulus by 2*pi before trig; phases at incommensurate frequencies then wrap cleanly. Seed needs only 3 Convert-from-int lanes.
master.continuity: C-infinity (compositions of sin), measured c0ratio 7.98. Steepens as D and Depth rise (max slope 36 at Depth 3 D 1.5).
master.params: Depth (int), Distortion D (hybrid), Scale via Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
master.risks: Statistics are non-stationary-looking and seeds feel like the same family. Direction vectors are hand picked: need testing for visible beat periods at large scale. Quasi-periodic not random, so long-range structure may repeat approximately. Range uneven (mean drifts with seed, measured 0.12).
master.cost_note: Depth 3: 12 trig calls, est 6-10 ns in every dimension; about 7x Perlin in 2D, 2x in 4D and 0.2x CellularDistance 4D.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 188.8 ns against perlin2 50.0 at the defaults, including one perlin for drift and dmod. Pure trig (drift=0,dmod=0) measured 2.71x. Params read once in the speed run.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: about 6 to 10 ns for 12 trig calls in any dimension, plus the source if drift or dmod is used

multipole-noise.look: Plain order 3 at 8 cells: a close weave of bright and dark dots with local three-fold grouping, like a crystal lattice in a microscope image; at 32 cells it becomes a very even fine grain. Thresholded at the median it is the best thing here: straight edged triangles and wedges meeting at pinwheels, a broken harlequin or kaleidoscope pattern that I have not seen from any existing node. This comes from each trefoil's zero set being 3 straight lines through the point. 3D at iso 0: sharp faceted shards, like shattered crystal, for the same reason (3 planes through an axis). A 3D slice shows separate eye-like dipole spots on flat gray, since R 0.62 leaves gaps between kernels. Order 2 with low jitter: a quilt of clovers. With R 1.25 as the catalogue suggests, orders merge into ordinary mottled noise that just gets finer with order: the angular structure is hidden by overlap, and order 1 looks Perlin-like. Mixed is uneven and more ordinary.
multipole-noise.dims: 2D and 3D measured (check, vol; 3D z-continuity max 0.0041 at dz=1e-3). 4D not written; the 2-plane trick is dimension independent.
multipole-noise.range: Default: [-1.007, 1.006] over 8 seeds, mean 0.000, std 0.27; far coords fine; 3D [-0.700, 0.659] on one slice, kept conservative since that was one slice. Per order overlap factors are measured at the default R, jitter and falloff only, so other settings need the gain param.
multipole-noise.artifacts: Lattice is visible as regular spacing at low jitter, and it is part of the look. FFT at window 8 shows fine rings, not a clean disc. Histogram spike at 0 from the uncovered gaps. Axis statistic 10.8 at window 8. Hillshade is a busy worm texture that does not show the geometry, so this is a mask or thresholded material more than a heightfield.
multipole-noise.node_shape: MultipoleNoise generator: Order (Monopole, Dipole, Quadrupole, Octupole, Mixed), Radius, Jitter, Falloff (int), Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. Gain per order from a small table computed from Radius and Falloff.
multipole-noise.port_notes: New over the catalogue: if R + Jitter / 2 <= 1, only 2 point rows per axis can reach a sample, using base floor(x - 0.5), so the window is 2^d like Perlin rather than 3^d. Harmonics by plain multiplies: u, u^2 - v^2, u^3 - 3uv^2; mixed by two Selects. Peak normalisation: rho^2 = m / (m + 2F). Falloff as integer power. In 2D, b = perp(a). In 3D, a and b from 2 hashed vectors with one Gram-Schmidt step and an InvSqrt. Keep the sign flip only for order 0, which otherwise has no zero mean.
multipole-noise.params_text: plain render is order=3,R=0.62,jitter=0.15,falloff=2. Pinwheels: add sharp=40. Clovers: order=2. Mixed: order=4,R=0.7,jitter=0.3. Dense overlapped catalogue form: R=1.25,jitter=0.5,falloff=3.

queue.name: MultipoleNoise
queue.reason: Disputed: J3 top pick for changing zero-set topology, while the others expect near-Perlin. A kernel swap in a Perlin proto settles it quickly.

master.one_liner: Gradient-noise generalised to higher angular order: each lattice point carries an order-m harmonic kernel (monopole=value, dipole=Perlin, quadrupole=saddle, octupole=trefoil), implemented in any dimension with a random 2-plane.
master.look: Order 2: a carpet of saddles / four-leaf clovers, every lattice point a mountain pass; thresholded it becomes interlocking plus-shaped and bow-tie blobs; terrain reads as knotted ridges with far more cols than Perlin. Order 3: three-pointed stars tiling into a triangular feel. Mixed: a richer, less uniform Perlin-like noise where bumps, dipoles and saddles coexist, nice as an FBm base that avoids the Perlin 'blob' look.
master.algorithm:
Params: Order {0,1,2,3,Mixed}, Radius R, Jitter (0 = lattice-corner look), Falloff exponent.
Per point (3^dim jittered window, or Jitter 0): h = hash; q = c+o+0.5+Jitter*(rndvec(h)-0.5); r = p-q; s2 = |r|^2
  a = hashed unit vector (dim-D), b = unit vector orthogonal to a (2D: b = perp(a); nD: Gram-Schmidt one step + InvSqrt)
  u = dot(a,r), v = dot(b,r)
  m = Order or (h>>30)&3 for Mixed
  harm_m: m=0: 1; m=1: u; m=2: u^2 - v^2; m=3: u^3 - 3 u v^2      (Re (u+iv)^m)
  Mixed: compute all four, pick with two Selects on the m bits
  acc += harm_m * max(0, 1 - s2/R^2)^Falloff
 value = acc * norm_m (peak of rho^m (1-rho^2)^F at rho^2 = m/(m+2F); divide, then an overlap factor measured once per Order).
Optional 'Hashed phase' is implicit in a,b orientation. For Jitter 0 the window can shrink to 2^dim corners if R <= 1 (document the seam-free condition R <= 1).
master.why_new: Perlin is exactly m=1 with a separable window; Simplex likewise. Higher orders change the topology of the zero set (ratio of saddles to extrema) which is what makes terrain look knotted versus blobby, and no modifier on an m=1 noise can add angular order. Also provides a Jitter-free 'surflet' variant of Perlin with isotropic radial windows as a side effect.
master.simd_plan: 3^dim window (or 2^dim at Jitter 0): per point ~20 ops: hash, 2 dots, few mults, window poly. 2D ~1.2x CellularDistance (4.7 ns), Jitter 0 variant ~1.5x Perlin. 3D ~1.2x Cellular 3D; 4D 81 points (or 16 corners at Jitter 0). Dimension agnostic via (a,b) plane trick; Mixed is two Selects, no branches.
master.continuity: C(Falloff-1) at the support edge (Falloff 4 gives C3), analytic inside.
master.params: Order, Radius, Jitter, Falloff, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
master.risks: m>=2 kernels vanish at the lattice point and at the rim, so the energy is in a ring; too small Radius leaves a visible lattice ring structure at Jitter 0. Amplitude normalisation differs per order (table). Visual difference from Perlin at Mixed may be subtler than hoped; the Order 2 and 3 pure modes are the distinctive ones.
sources: K. Perlin, 'Improving Noise', SIGGRAPH 2002 (surflet view of gradient noise; from memory, not fetched)
master.cost_note: 2D ~1.2x CellularDistance (4.7 ns), Jitter 0 variant ~1.5x Perlin. 3D ~1.2x Cellular 3D; 4D 81 points (or 16 corners at Jitter 0).

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 2^d window, 2D about 2 ns, 3D about 7 ns because each of 8 points needs 2 hashed vectors and one InvSqrt, 4D about 20 ns

percolation-lattice.look: Plain gray: woven zigzag ridges with a clear lattice rhythm, like folded cloth or a warped egg crate; the hillshade is a dense knotted weave. It is not a general noise look and the lattice remains visible. Thresholded it comes alive: at P=0.3 white islands sit in a connected black network, and at P=0.7 black islands sit in a connected white network, at the same coverage, with similar blob size and shape. A ramp of P across the image moves smoothly between them, visible as a gradient in what is connected rather than how much. 3D at P=0.1: separate rounded pockets in the cut faces at about 41 percent volume. 3D at P=0.5: one continuous sponge.
percolation-lattice.dims: 2D and 3D measured (flood fill, check, vol; 3D z-continuity max 0.0083 at dz=1e-3). 4D not written; catalogue says 24 two-face terms, the expensive case.
percolation-lattice.range: 2D: [-0.999, 0.999] over 8 seeds, mean 0.003, std about 0.46; far coords fine. 3D slice [-0.609, 0.607] with a factor 0.62 from a measured peak of about +-1.66 in the catalogue; not measured over seeds.
percolation-lattice.artifacts: Lattice rhythm stays visible in the gray field. Bridges pinch at saddles, so thresholds need about 8 samples per cell to resolve connectivity: at 4 samples per cell the same field measured + share 0.041 at P=0.55 and 0.810 at P=0.75. Warp limit, measured: warp 0.7 at wf 0.7 keeps the flip, warp 0.9 at wf 1.3 folds the domain and destroys it (shares 0.023/0.021 at P=0.5, transition smeared over 0.4 to 0.75). Warp 0.7 raises max slope to 18. Narrowband near the lattice frequency. At comp=2 with P near 0 or 1 the bridge no longer dominates (comps rise, e.g. - phase comps 995 at P=0 versus 307 at P=0.25), which is harmless at those extremes in the sense that phase shares still read correctly.
percolation-lattice.node_shape: PercolationNoise generator: Connectivity (hybrid 0..1), Height Min, Bridge Amp, Coverage Compensation (float, default 2 in 2D, 1 in 3D), Warp, Warp Frequency, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. Lattice Rotation is cheap and worth keeping.
percolation-lattice.port_notes: 2D: 4 corner hashes with sign from ( i + j ) & 1, quintic lerp, one cell hash, b(t) = 16 t^2 (1-t)^2, s = smoothstep( -soft, soft, P - r ) * 2 - 1, out = base + s A b(u) b(v) - comp ( 2P - 1 ) A ( 8/15 )^2. 3D: 8 corners, 6 face hashes keyed on lower cell plus axis, face term s A b b (1 - w) or w with w = quintic, so each face term has zero normal slope and zero value at the far face; continuity measured. Hybrid P is safe because s is smooth in P and comp is linear in P. Keep warp below the fold limit in the docs.
percolation-lattice.params_text: plain render is P=0.5,hmin=0.5,A=0.4,warp=0.7,wf=0.7,freq=2,rot=0.4,comp=2,soft=0.02. Threshold views: sharp=14,P=0.3 and sharp=14,P=0.7. Hybrid: sharp=14,pvar=2,span=16 --window 16. 3D: P=0.1,warp=0.3 and P=0.5,warp=0.3 with vol --window 2.5.

master.one_liner: A field whose zero level is literally bond percolation: one parameter flips which phase is connected while coverage barely moves.
master.look: P=0: bright dots on connected dark. P=0.5: critical labyrinth with long winding, power-law clusters. P=1: dark dots on connected bright. Hybrid P gives regions of sea-connected islands turning into land-connected lakes under one threshold. Useful for caves, wetlands, circuit patterns and cracked-to-solid transitions. Measured over window 128, threshold 0: P=0.45 coverage 0.486, largest cluster share +0.039 / -0.883; P=0.5 coverage 0.499, +0.345 / -0.458; P=0.55 coverage 0.512, +0.875 / -0.043. Full range P=0 to 1 moves coverage 0.369 to 0.630.
master.algorithm: Corners: value = (-1)^(i+j) * lerp(HMin, 1, rnd(hash)), so even corners are strict maxima and odd corners strict minima under quintic interpolation. Along each edge the sign changes exactly once, so each cell has four zero crossings and two possible pairings. Cell term: s = smoothstep(-0.02, 0.02, P - rnd(cellHash))*2 - 1; add s*A*b(u)*b(v) with b(t) = 16 t^2 (1-t)^2, which vanishes with zero slope on cell borders. With A larger than the bilinear centre (A = 0.4, HMin = 0.5), s alone decides whether + corners or - corners link through the cell. That is bond percolation on the even sublattice with its exactly known p_c = 1/2. 3D: 8 corners plus 6 face terms s_f*A*b(u)*b(v)*c(w), c = quintic falloff to zero on the opposite face, plus body term. Follow with a built-in low-frequency warp to hide the lattice.
master.why_new: Connectivity is an independent, directly addressable control. Thresholding Perlin ties connectivity to coverage: T=+-0.1 is needed to reach coverage 0.38 to 0.62 for a comparable flip, and connectivity cannot be set per region without changing how much land there is. A related Truchet node gives fixed-width loops but no continuous height field, and no P.
master.simd_plan: 2D: 4 corner hashes + 1 cell hash, quintic lerp, 2 bumps: about 1.5x Value. Measured 2.9x perlin2 scalar including two warp Perlin evals. 3D: 8 + 7 hashes. 4D: 16 corners + 24 two-face terms is the expensive version. Branch-free; sign from (i+j+...) & 1 via int ops. Hybrid P per lane is safe because s is a smooth function of (P - r).
master.continuity: C1 for value (quintic plus bumps with zero border slope). Measured c0ratio 8, max slope 5.5. The smoothstep on s keeps hybrid P continuous.
master.params: P Connectivity (hybrid), HMin (float), Bridge Amp (float), Warp (float), Output Min/Max. A Compensate option could subtract a P-dependent offset to null the coverage drift, untested.
master.risks: Lattice structure is visible in the gray image even with warp 0.35, since it is a warped egg-crate at P=0 or 1. Strong warp hides it but breaks nothing, because a homeomorphic warp keeps the topology. 3D range reached +-1.66 and needs normalising. In 3D both phases can percolate together and the threshold is not 1/2; the 3D transition has not been measured. Only 2D statistics were measured. Not a replacement for general noise: it is narrowband and centred on the lattice frequency.
master.cost_note: 2D: 4 corner hashes + 1 cell hash, quintic lerp, 2 bumps: about 1.5x Value. Measured 2.9x perlin2 scalar including two warp Perlin evals.

measured.scalar_note: Includes the two warp Perlin evals and std::map param reads. An early build without warp, comp or rot measured 2.30.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 2D about 3.7 ns with warp (2 Perlin plus 5 hashes), about 1.5 ns without; 3D about 11 ns with warp (3 Perlin plus 14 hashes), about 4.5 ns without

quadratic-carpet.look: Plain render: octagonal rings of small squares around checkered centres, with bands of stripes and checker between them; it reads as a woven rug or textile, not as noise. Wide view: a regular tiled carpet with finer repeating medallions. Thresholded: a crisp black and white rug. Rosette preset: zone plate rings around bright or dark eyes in a grid, with moire checker between, the op-art look the catalogue describes. Near 1/4: large rings of checker, like engine turning. Golden ratio: a small square tile mosaic with no big rings. Cross term: long diagonal hyperbolic bands. Warp 0.6: rosettes bend into agate eyes or topographic contours. 3D rosette: concentric shells with stair-stepped voxel surfaces, like an ornate crystal. 3D near 1/3 at scale 4: square block scaffolding, reminiscent of a Menger sponge. Hillshade is high frequency static and adds nothing, since this is not a heightfield.
quadratic-carpet.dims: 2D and 3D measured (check, vol). The harness z-continuity reads about 0 at scale 16 because its z = 0.5 sits on a lattice plane; at scale 15 it reads mean 0.0167, max 0.0351 for dz=1e-3, which fits the steep but continuous value lattice. 4D not written, but it is the same formula.
quadratic-carpet.range: [-1.000, 1.000] over 8 seeds, mean 0.000, std about 0.55 in the sheet; far coords fine ([-0.999, 1.000], std 0.639); 3D [-1.000, 1.000]. Flat histogram with a small centre rise, kurt 1.88. Output is a Cos of a lattice value, so no normalisation is needed.
quadratic-carpet.artifacts: This is order, not randomness: seeds do not give new random textures. With seedmode 0, seed only moves the rosette centres (mean seed difference 0.74). Seedmode 1 changes the family as well, which is unpredictable. The default chirp is very sensitive to (a, c): small changes give a different carpet, so a preset list is the right interface. At low samples per cell the quintic gives visibly blocky cells, which is part of the look at Nyquist phases. Zooming out aliases further and makes a different moire, as in the wide view. The FFT shows a broad flat band with lattice lines. Max slope 60 per unit at scale 16, or 3.7 per lattice cell.
quadratic-carpet.node_shape: QuadraticCarpet generator: Preset (Rosette, Rug, Rings, Tile, Custom) or Chirp A, Chirp B, Chirp C as floats, Feature Scale, Seed Offset (moves centres), Output Min/Max. Use dyadic A, C in presets where tiling matters.
quadratic-carpet.port_notes: Corner value: uint32 phase = a i^2 + b i j + c j^2 by wrapping integer multiply, then Cos of phase scaled to a turn; no hash at all. Quintic tensor interpolation as in Value noise. 3D adds e l^2 + f i l + h j l. The seed offset comes from one hash at node level, or per lane from the seed vector. Keep a, c as turns held in uint32.
quadratic-carpet.params_text: plain render is an=0.3358,cn=0.3358,bn=0,scale=16,seedmode=0 (chirp just above 1/3). Presets: rosettes an=cn=0.00990099; ring and checker an=cn=0.2525; ornate tile an=cn=0.381966; stretched bands an=0.0099,cn=0.0071,bn=0.0173; agate eyes an=cn=0.00990099,warp=0.6. 3D: scale=4, and an=cn=en=0.0323,scale=6.

master.one_liner: Value-noise interpolation of a Zadoff-Chu quadratic-phase lattice instead of hash values: zone-plate rosettes and moire carpets from integer overflow.
master.look: Tested. Concentric zone plates with secondary rosettes (Talbot copies) where the chirp aliases against the lattice, checker patches between, and exact global periodicity for rational a/P. Looks like crafted op-art carpet or engine-turned metal, deterministic rather than random. Different seeds give different carpet families, not random textures. Uses: guilloche patterns, sci-fi interference plates, deliberately moire masks, exact tile with period P.
master.algorithm:
Corner value g(i,j)=Cos(2pi*frac((a*i*i + b*i*j + c*j*j)/P)). In SIMD use P=2^32: phase=int32 wraparound of a*i*i+b*i*j+c*j*j, then top bits scaled to float, then Cos or a polynomial. (a,b,c) chosen from seed, tested with a/P near 1/101, 3/251, 1/1009 (ratios to P). Interpolate with quintic fade like Value noise.
3D: add e*k*k, f*i*k, h*j*k; 4D similarly.
master.why_new: A completely different source of coherence: aliasing of a chirp against the lattice rather than randomness. Nothing on the sheet has structured moire. Cheapest possible implementation, because no hash multiply-xorshift is needed.
master.simd_plan: Branch free. 2^D corners, integer multiplies only, then Cos per corner (or a 4-term polynomial). About 1-1.5x Value noise in all dimensions. Trivially 4D.
master.continuity: C2-ish like Value noise with quintic fade: continuous in interpolation since lattice values are single valued; not numerically checked.
master.params: Float or int: Chirp a, Cross b, Chirp c. Seeded selects offsets. ScalableGenerator mixin. Integer lattice offset moves the rosette centre.
master.risks: Not noise-like: strong order, centred on origin unless offset, and frequency content varies with distance from the centre in a chirp way. Far from origin at P=2^32 the wrap gives a different look than near it. Highly sensitive to (a,b,c), so a preset list may be needed. Wild and niche; low priority.
sources: Zadoff-Chu sequences and Schroeder quadratic residue diffusers, quantum carpet Talbot effect (from memory, not consulted)
master.cost_note: About 1-1.5x Value noise in all dimensions.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 2D about 1.5 ns (4 corners, integer multiplies, 4 Cos), 3D about 3 ns, 4D about 6 ns. A polynomial instead of FS::Cos would be cheaper.

sine-fold.look: Close view: liquid grey marble with long sheared bands and thin dark hair lines curling around calmer patches, close to oil on water. Threshold shows ink like swirls. Wide 4x view: a plainly regular basket weave repeating about every 5 units over the whole panel. The 3D XZ slice looks better than the 2D field, with flame like streaks and no visible weave at that window. The 3D isosurface is shredded sheets, jagged at the step size of the raymarch, so it is not a useful solid at this setting.

dims.2D: works, measured c0ratio 3.33, max slope 123.7. The function is smooth; the ratio stays low because folds are thinner than the 1e-3 probe in places, not because of jumps.
dims.3D: works, measured z continuity max 0.0701 for dz=1e-3; XZ slice shows flowing streaks
dims.4D: Eval4 implemented; measured on an oblique plane (slice4=1): c0ratio 4.50, range -1..1, 8.74x perlin2 with cmod (3D perlin as its source), 6.79x without

sine-fold.artifacts: Long range periodic weave is the unsolved flaw: FFT shows a diagonal cross and axis stat 21; a slowly varying Couple at cscale 0.23 did not break it at cmod=1, and cmod=1.6 only partly. Couple above about 3 brings back an X shaped moire lattice. The catalogue feedback (norm=0) has stretch that compounds per step: with cmod it measured max slope 316 and c0ratio 1.80, so filaments alias; the added norm=1 divides feedback by the frequency ratio, which gave max slope 123.7 and c0ratio 3.33 at these defaults. Without coupling modulation at couple=1, gain 0.6 the catalogue form measured c0ratio 7.78. The fold density is not stationary and is hard to normalise.
sine-fold.node_shape: SineFold: Iterations int, Frequency float, Lacunarity float, Gain float, Couple hybrid, Shape enum (Product, Sum), Seed Offset, Feature Scale, Output Min/Max
sine-fold.port_notes: Fully branch free GenT over a fixed K: per iteration, one rotation by a fixed orthonormal matrix (3-4-5 in 2D, rational /7 in 3D, quaternion (1,2,2,4)/5 in 4D), d FS::Sin, d feedback adds. Phases per k and axis come from a seed hash, per lane unless cached per node. A separate DomainWarp upstream would be the practical fix for the weave at large windows; not tested here. Far coords (4e4) measured fine, std 0.357.

master.one_liner: Gardner-style sum of sines with cross-axis phase coupling, made into a rotated cascade: latticeless liquid marble and woven folds, same cost pattern in 4D.
master.look: Prototype cl_misc node 3: Couple=0 is a lumpy periodic lattice; Couple=.5-1 gives woven, basket-like liquid marble with long sheared folds; Couple=2 gives finely combed swirls, like oil on water, with very strong streaks in hillshade. No hash or lattice artifacts; no isotropic stats. Water caustic bases, stylised marble, fabrics, sci-fi fluid.
master.why_new: All existing noises are lattice based except SineWave, which is trivially periodic. Domain warp on SineWave gets part of this but not the per-iteration feedback, and needs one node per iteration.
master.simd_plan: K x d x FS::Sin plus phases from seed hash (one per axis per iteration, or a static per-seed table when lanes share a seed). 2D K=7: 14 sin ~3.5 ns (3x Perlin; scalar 4.4x). 3D ~5 ns, 4D ~7 ns (1.6x Perlin 4D). No hash lattice, no masks at all; fully branch free GenT.
master.continuity: C-infinity everywhere, c0ratio 7.88; slopes grow with K and Couple. Tiling works through the 4D torus since the function is smooth.
master.params: Int: K. Float: F0, Lacunarity, Gain. Hybrid: Couple. Seeded for phases. Mixins standard.
master.risks: Large-scale weave periodicity is visible, since low frequencies dominate and only K sines exist. Not isotropic: rotation matrix imprints a directional bias. Seed only changes phases, so seeds look related. Float sin accuracy at far coordinates worsens (FS::Sin reduction): far coord test passed at 4e4 but check 1e6.
master.cost_note: 2D K=7: 14 sin ~3.5 ns (3x Perlin; scalar 4.4x). 3D ~5 ns, 4D ~7 ns (1.6x Perlin 4D).

measured.scalar_note: Measured 273.8 ns against perlin2 51.8 at the defaults, 16 sin plus 1 perlin for cmod. cmod=0 measured 4.28x. Params read once in the speed run.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: about 5 ns 2D, about 7 ns 3D, about 9 ns 4D plus the coupling source

sparse-gate.look: Single gate: a flat gray plain with scattered dipoles of random heading, each a bright and dark bean pair. Simplex host is clean, jittered SparseGradient is rounder and clumpier, Perlin host is visibly square and grid-aligned, LocalMax gives evenly spaced pairs. A density ramp goes smoothly from empty plain to full dense noise with features at full height, not faded. Plain FBm with growing density loses the flat floor. The new nested form is the strong result: fractal islands with detailed coastlines rising out of an exactly flat sea, and the relief reads as a real archipelago. The dipole version gives mountains beside basins set into a flat green plain, like impact or caldera landscapes. The 3D vol gives separate rough rocky boulders floating in empty space, which reads as an asteroid field.
sparse-gate.dims: 2D and 3D measured (check, vol; z-continuity max 0.0018 at dz=1e-3). 4D not written; the gate touches only the lattice loop. LocalMax is 2D only.
sparse-gate.range: Default nested: [0.000, 0.870] over 8 seeds, mean 0.074; far coords [0, 0.840]; 3D slice [0, 0.711]. Single octave: [-0.975, 0.968], 3D slice [-0.697, 0.694]. Exact zero area: nested default 48.4 percent, single octave at D 0.2 49.9 percent, D 1 0.0 percent.
sparse-gate.artifacts: A straight crease along a dipole's zero line under Abs (the dome first octave removes it). Near-vertical rims when nest is high and soft low, which trip the continuity check, so keep nest about 3 and soft about 0.3. Island edges are not perfectly circular but come from a simplex lattice, and spacing can fuse neighbours into double islands. Local slope grows with nest and octaves together. The catalogue's plain threshold formula leaks: at D = 0, points with thr < soft stay partly open, so the floor is not flat. Fixed here by keeping thr in [soft, 1 - soft]. LocalMax adds little: it nearly equals a scaled low jitter lattice at density 1.
sparse-gate.node_shape: Two parts. (1) A Density hybrid and Softness member on Simplex (and optionally Perlin, Value), with no change to the output at Density 1. (2) SparseFractal generator: Octaves, Gain, Lacunarity, Density (hybrid), Nest (float), Softness, First Octave (Dome, Dipole), Abs (bool), Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
sparse-gate.port_notes: Gate per lattice point: thr = soft + ( 1 - 2 soft ) * rnd; g = smoothstep( thr - soft, thr + soft, D ). Nesting: D for octave o+1 = sat( nest * |sum so far| ), one float per lane and no new state, so it is fully pointwise and fits a fixed octave loop. Use soft 0.05 for octave 0 with a constant D and 0.3 after. Dome first octave is the Simplex loop with the gradient dot replaced by a hashed height. Because sum is a smooth function except at Abs creases, the only risk is slope growth.
sparse-gate.params_text: plain render is host=1,octaves=5,nest=3,soft=0.3,soft0=0.05,density=0.2,gain=0.45,freq=0.4,dome=1,post=1 (nested islands; relief --hscale 80, vol --iso 0.1 --window 8). Basins and mountains on a plain: dome=0,post=0. Catalogue single gate: octaves=1,dome=0,post=0,freq=0.6,nest=0,soft=0.05. Density ramp: add densx=1,densspan=16 --window 16. Other hosts: host=0 Perlin, host=2 jittered SparseGradient, spacing=1 LocalMax in 2D.

master.one_liner: Make most lattice points silent: a hybrid Density parameter on Perlin/Simplex/Value (or a dedicated SparseGradient node) that soft-gates each lattice contribution, giving isolated dipole features on an exactly flat zero background, optionally with blue-noise (local-max) spacing.
master.look: Perlin with Density 0.08: a flat plain with scattered crescent dipoles of random heading, each a crest beside a trough: barchan dune fields, isolated hills and holes, meteor splash marks (Abs gives isolated bumps, Ridged isolated sharp ridges). With Density driven by a large Perlin: dunes that thin out and vanish across a region continuously. Per-octave in FBm: rare large features, common small ones: a 'sparse fractal' that reads as island archipelagos.
master.algorithm:
Add to the lattice loop of Perlin (2^dim corners) / Simplex (dim+1 vertices) / Value:
  thr = rnd01(hash(corner))              // per-lattice-point fixed threshold
  g = smoothstep(thr - Softness, thr + Softness, Density(p))   // Density hybrid sampled per lane; soft so a smooth density field fades features in continuously
  contribution *= g
Output unchanged otherwise (still in [-1,1]).
Spacing option 'LocalMax' (2D, 3D optional): a corner is alive only if its hash is the maximum among its 3^dim lattice neighbours: alive = AND over neighbours n of (hash(corner) > hash(n)); this yields a Poisson-disk-like set (no two alive points adjacent) with a density fixed by geometry (1/9 in 2D); Density then scales the soft gate on top. Cost: 5^dim hashes per sample (25 in 2D, 125 in 3D, so 3D defaults to Bernoulli).
Dedicated node variant SparseGradient: jittered 3^dim window + radial window kernel (1-s2)^4 * dot(grad, r), same gate, so features are not stuck on a grid.
master.why_new: Thresholding/Remap of a dense noise clips shapes and never gives a mathematically flat background with intact feature shapes; placing isolated oriented dipoles with controlled density (and non-adjacent spacing) is what sparse convolution offers but FastNoise lacks. It is nearly free on the existing generators.
master.simd_plan: Per lattice point: one extra rnd extract, one smoothstep, one multiply: Perlin cost +10%. Density hybrid sampled once per lane. LocalMax: 25 hashes in 2D (~+60% over Perlin), too costly in 3D/4D (use Bernoulli there); hashes of a 5x5 block can share the row/column prime products. Fully branch-free. Works in 2D/3D/4D since it touches only the existing lattice loops.
master.continuity: Same as the host noise (C2 for Perlin quintic, C2 Simplex) provided Softness > 0 and Density is continuous; Softness 0 with a varying density field introduces discontinuities (features pop).
master.params: Density (hybrid, key), Softness, Spacing {Bernoulli, LocalMax}; as a dedicated node also Jitter, Radius.
master.risks: Hard to make visually impressive in the thumbnail (mostly flat); shines in composition. LocalMax 3D cost prohibitive; document. For Simplex the dipole shape per alive vertex is a hexagonal surflet, fine. Range stays [-1,1] but is rarely reached, so Output Min/Max scaling expectations change.
sources: J. P. Lewis, 'Algorithms for Solid Noise Synthesis', SIGGRAPH 1989 (sparse convolution; from memory, not fetched)
master.cost_note: Per lattice point: one extra rnd extract, one smoothstep, one multiply: Perlin cost +10%.

presets.label: Basins and mountains on a plain

measured.scalar_note: 7.83 is the harness speed command for the 5 octave default; it includes std::map reads per sample. Kernels with params in locals: simplex gate one octave 58.4 ns against simplex2 56.8 (1.03x) and perlin2 48.2 (1.21x); nested 5 octaves 298.4 ns (6.19x perlin). So the gate alone is close to free, as the catalogue said.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: gate on Simplex about 1.3 ns in 2D; nested 5 octaves about 6 to 8 ns in 2D, about 20 ns in 3D

spiral-cells.look: Curling black and white ornamental scrolls of even line width, packed so each spiral fills its cell and arms run into the neighbours' arms: Van Gogh sky, Greek scroll or BZ reaction. Higher twist gives tighter, more convincingly chemical scrolls with thin seams between neighbours. Twist 0 gives faceted pinwheels with bright spokes, a very different look. Threshold is two interlocked curly regions. FFT is clean isotropic rings, one strong wavelength. The wide view is an even texture with no lattice showing. In 3D the spherical phase gives rounded scroll solids on all cut faces; the scroll wave form shows straight axis aligned bands where a filament lies along the cut.

dims.3D: works, measured z continuity max 0.0209 for dz=1e-3 in the default spherical form, 0.0181 in the scroll form
dims.4D: Eval4 implemented with a 3^4 window and a hashed coordinate plane; measured on an oblique plane (slice4=1): c0ratio 7.98, range -1..1, 13.08x perlin2 scalar with zero weight skips

spiral-cells.artifacts: Points with r <= eps have a damped core, which shows as a tiny grey dot at each centre at this twist. Low sharp (1) blurs neighbours into interference. High sharp (8) leaves visible cell border creases, and they read as faint Voronoi seams at twist 0. Scroll wave 3D has axis aligned straight bands from its small filament table. Handedness mix has little visual effect at default. Radius is safe only when r <= 1 + (1 - jitter) / 2; at the defaults this is met, and the denominator goes to zero smoothly in the worst empty gaps because of the 1e-4 in num / (den + 1e-4), not measured as an event in the renders.
spiral-cells.node_shape: SpiralCells: Arms int (0 = random), Twist hybrid, Twist Jitter float, Handedness Bias float, Sharpness hybrid, Grid Jitter float, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max
spiral-cells.port_notes: Fixed window with no masks needed besides Max(0, 1 - r2/R2).
