Complex power by repeated multiply on a constant Arms; a per point random arm count needs a Select chain over 3 powers. Sin and Cos per point dominate. Weight power 2*sharp can be an integer power for port. In 3D and 4D use a small hashed table of orthonormal pairs, no atan2 anywhere. Far coords (4e4) measured fine, std 0.586.
spiral-cells.params_text: arms=1,twist=16,tjit=0.25,sharp=3,r=1.15,jitter=0.7,core=0.1,hand=0,mode3=1 (the code defaults). Tight BZ scrolls: twist=20 or 30. Pinwheel facets: twist=0,sharp=8. Multi arm: arms=2 or 3, arms=0 for per point random.

master.one_liner: Each lattice point is a spiral or pinwheel wave source, blended by a partition of unity: curl commas and BZ-reaction spirals without atan or seams.
master.look: Curl commas, Van Gogh sky, whirl patterns, flower spokes, BZ reaction fronts, hair whorls. Prototyped: repeated comma-shaped curls in a labyrinth with strong chirality; F=0 gives clear pinwheels. Terrain-wise reads as scroll ornament.
master.algorithm:
For window points: v = x-c, r = |v|; phase-rotated kernel without angles: s = Re[(vx+i vy)^m * exp(i(hand*F*r + phi))] / max(r^m, eps). For m=1: (g.v*cos(Fr+phi) + h.v*sin(Fr+phi)) / r. 3D and 4D use orthonormal pair g,h from a table: s = (g.v*cos(Fr+phi) + h.v*sin(Fr+phi))/r, valid at every dimension. Weight w = max(0, 1 - r^2/R^2)^(2*Sharp). Output = sum(w*s)/sum(w). Damp core with sat(r/eps). F=0 gives pinwheels (spokes), large F gives tight spirals.

[PinwheelNoise, lattice-kernels] Params: Order m (1..4), Twist (hybrid, radians per kernel radius), TwistJitter, Chirality {CW, CCW, Mixed}, Radius R, Jitter.
Gen(p): c = floor(p); acc = 0
 for o in {-1,0,1}^dim:
   h = hash(seed,c+o); q = c+o+0.5+Jitter*(rndvec(h)-0.5); r = p - q; s2 = |r|^2
   2D: u = r.x, v = r.y. 3D/4D: a = hashed unit vector, b = orthonormal to a (b = normalize(w - dot(w,a)a) with w another hashed vector), u = dot(a,r), v = dot(b,r)
   rho = sqrt(u^2+v^2)
   kappa = Twist*(1 + TwistJitter*rnd11(h>>8)) * chiralitySign(h)
   phase = kappa*rho - 2*pi*rnd01(h>>16)        // bounded: |phase| <= Twist*R + 2pi, so one unreduced minimax sin/cos pair
   (cs, sn) = cos/sin(phase)
   zm = (u + i v)^m by repeated complex multiply: m=1 (u,v); m=2 (u^2-v^2, 2uv); m=3 ...  (no normalisation: the rho^m factor acts as the inner falloff)
   kern = (Re zm * cs + Im zm * sn)          // = rho^m cos(m*theta - phase)
   win = max(0, 1 - s2/R^2)^4
   acc += kern * win
 value = acc * norm(m, R) (analytic peak of rho^m (1-rho^2/R^2)^4 times 1/sqrt(overlap)).
master.why_new: All coherent noises here have no local handedness. Warping into swirls smears, and gets random shear, not consistent per-centre arm counts. Sum (not partition) version looks like plain interference; the normalised blend is what keeps the spirals readable.
master.simd_plan: m=1 is cheap: dots, sqrt, Sin, Cos per point. Only hash bits select F sign and g,h. m=2,3 via a complex square. 2D 9 points: 8-12 ns (proto 6.6x perlin2 with 19 points and atan2). 3D 2^3 corners or 27: 15-40 ns. 4D 2^4: 30 ns. Above building-block cost, justified as a look node.
master.continuity: C1 away from cores, measured c0ratio 7.99. Core is C0 through sat(r/eps) damp. R must fit reach or there are seams.
master.params: Arm Count (int m, or per-point random), Twist F (hybrid), Handedness Bias, Sharpness (hybrid), Grid Jitter.
master.risks:
Normalisation denominator must stay positive: eps, and R big enough that every sample has a weight. Sin+Cos per point dominates; a precomputed sincos for two shared radii is not possible with per-point r. Large F aliases near grid scale.
[PinwheelNoise, lattice-kernels] Large Twist aliases inside a kernel (arms thinner than a pixel at the rim); cap Twist*R around 4*pi. Overlap of several spirals muddles the centres; a Jitter below 1 keeps centres apart. Normalisation is empirical for Mixed chirality.
master.cost_note: 2D 9 points: 8-12 ns (proto 6.6x perlin2 with 19 points and atan2). 3D 2^3 corners or 27: 15-40 ns.
master.variant_notes: Real-valued spiral kernels: SpiralCells blends by partition of unity (keeps spirals readable), PinwheelNoise sums and keeps rho^m.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 170.1 ns against perlin2 52.9 at the defaults, 9 point window in 2D. The scalar code skips points with zero weight, which a SIMD port cannot do, so the port is relatively dearer than this ratio. Params read once in the speed run.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: about 10 to 15 ns 2D with 9 points and sin plus cos per point, about 35 to 50 ns 3D with 27 points, 4D with 81 points well over 100 ns

steered-stripes.look: Convincing zebra hide: black and white stripes of constant width that flow, fork and end, with soft branching points where orientation changes. The threshold looks like an animal coat, and the wide view holds as an even tiger or zebra texture with no lattice. This is much better than the catalogue expected, which said chopped herringbone; n=8 with this Theta rate is the sweet spot. n=4 gives a rectilinear Greek key maze of orthogonal stripe blocks, n=12 or higher with high tamp gives swirly op art with moire eddies. tmode=1 gives radial sunbursts around source extrema, tmode=2 gives contour rings broken by star shaped scars. The 3D solid shows flowing lamellae with forks; its XZ slice is more plaid, with straight chevron blocks and visible block edges.

dims.2D: works, measured c0ratio 7.96, max slope 50.06. Gradient modes are much worse: tmode=1 c0ratio 1.61, tmode=2 c0ratio 2.42.
dims.3D: works, measured z continuity max 0.0200 for dz=1e-3; The comparison shows zebra lamellae
dims.4D: Eval4 implemented with 3 Theta sources and 8 waves; measured on an oblique plane (slice4=1): c0ratio 7.86, range -0.969..0.970, 13.53x perlin2 scalar

steered-stripes.artifacts: Straight segments and chevron corners where one slot dominates, more visible in the 3D slice. Small checker zones where two slots crossfade with high Theta slope, rare at the defaults and common at n>=16. Range is -0.97..0.97 because of eps (norm form); it is flat, kurt 1.53, like a square wave. FFT has a soft diagonal structure from the slot directions, axis stat 15.18. Same orientation anywhere gives phase coherent stripes, since slots are global plane waves. Gradient driven Theta (tmode 1, 2) has real near jumps at source extrema and saddles, with max slopes 1123 and 734: use them only as a look. Stripes do not follow a source's contours cleanly in any mode, so it is not a fingerprint node.
steered-stripes.node_shape: SteeredStripes: Theta hybrid (radians, defaults to a fractal source), Frequency hybrid, Slots int (even), Sharpness float, Softening float, Seed Offset, Feature Scale, Output Min/Max
steered-stripes.port_notes: Branch free: L = Theta/pi*N, Round for the even and odd slots, table lookup of direction and phase by slot via integer permute or Cos/Sin of the slot angle, two Sin/Cos pairs for A and B, and InvSqrt for the envelope. The axial wrap uses s = sign(dot(dir a, dir b)) in A - s*B so the slot N-1 to slot 0 crossing has no seam. 3D is azimuth by elevation, 4 waves bilinear, using Theta 1 at N slots and Theta 2 at N/2 slots. 4D adds a third angle for 8 waves. Far coords (4e4) measured fine, std 0.660.
steered-stripes.params_text: n=8,freq=2,tmode=0,tamp=2.5,tscale=0.3,eps=0.25,norm=1,sharp=0 (the code defaults). Rectilinear maze: n=4. Swirly op art: tamp=5,n=12. Downhill sunbursts: tmode=1,n=16. Contour rings with star scars: tmode=2,n=8,tscale=0.25.

master.one_liner: Very cheap steered plane waves: quantise orientation into slots and crossfade only two global waves per lane; the honest output is flowing herringbone and twill, not clean fingerprints.
master.look: Tested at N=8 to N=64 and multiple sharpness levels. Slots yield a chopped herringbone, twill or op-art moire following the orientation field, with checker beat zones where slots crossfade. With fast-changing Theta it gives swirly op-art eddies. Does not give clean fingerprints; use LatticePhasor for those. Uses: fabric twill, stylised water, Bridget Riley-style graphics.
master.algorithm:
L=Theta(p)/pi*N (N even, Theta axial). ra=2*Round(L/2), rb=2*Round((L-1)/2)+1, wa=1-|L-ra| sharpened by smoothstep, wb=1-wa.
A=k*dot(dir(ra),p)+psi(ra); B=k*dot(dir(rb),p)+psi(rb), both from a small table indexed by slot mod N.
y=wa*Cos(A)+wb*Cos(B); E2=wa^2+wb^2+2*wa*wb*Cos(A-s*B), s=sign(dot(dir a,dir b)) so the axial wrap has no seam.
Out=y*InvSqrt(E2+eps^2).
master.why_new: Stripes that follow an orientation field with no lattice and no per-corner work, at under Perlin cost, and N controls the look. The naive cos(k*R(theta(p))*p) shears wildly away from the origin, whereas this stays at constant wavelength everywhere.
master.simd_plan: Branch free. Table lookup via integer permute or Cos/Sin of slot angle; 2 Sin+Cos + 1 Cos + InvSqrt. Estimated about 1x Perlin in 2D plus Theta cost. 3D: azimuth x elevation slots, 4 waves bilinear. 4D: 8 waves. Polynomial atan needed only if Theta comes from a gradient.
master.continuity: C0 for continuous Theta with eps>0, not numerically checked in the last form. Zebra-like phase breaks at beat zeros are soft, not jumps.
master.params: Hybrid: Theta, Frequency. Int: Slots N. Float: Sharpness, eps.
master.risks: Fundamentally herringbone: slot width across the image scales as (pi/N)/|grad theta|, and global-phase mismatch between slots cannot be eliminated pointwise. Higher N narrows slots and worsens chopping, lower N widens checker zones, no setting is clean. Same orientation anywhere yields phase-coherent stripes globally (subtle). Include only if the twill look is wanted.
master.cost_note: Estimated about 1x Perlin in 2D plus Theta cost.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 207.8 ns against perlin2 52.6 at the defaults, including 2 perlin for Theta and 6 trig calls that a port replaces with per node tables for 4 of them. Params read once in the speed run.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: about 4 to 5 ns 2D including the 2 perlin Theta source, about 10 ns 3D (2 Theta sources, 4 waves), about 20 ns 4D (3 Theta sources, 8 waves)

turing-stencil.look: Depth 2: hard walled black and white labyrinth of worms with nearly uniform stroke width, almost binary output (histogram is two spikes), like brain coral. FFT is a clear ring, one preferred wavelength. The wide view is an even maze. It is cleaner and longer stroked than the same perlin source through a sigmoid (depth=-1), which stays blobby and shows lattice bound dots, as the image shows side by side. Depth 1 is a soft band passed version with a big low frequency shading, not labyrinthine. The 3D depth 1 solid is a soft porous sponge with no hard labyrinth quality.

dims.2D: works, measured c0ratio 6.88 at depth 2 (max slope 192.2), 7.96 at depth 1
dims.3D: works at depth 1 (default), measured z continuity max 0.0091 for dz=1e-3; depth 1 has a softer look than the 2D labyrinth.
dims.4D: Eval4 implemented with the 8 axis + 16 diagonal ring at depth 1; measured on an oblique plane (slice4=1): c0ratio 7.97, range -0.997..0.996, 83.48x perlin2 scalar (25 perlin4 evals)

turing-stencil.artifacts: Cost is the unsolved flaw: 81 source evals for the 2D look, 73x perlin scalar, far above the 5x building block guideline; depth 2 in 3D is 225 evals by default. Topology is inherited from the source: raising sscale gives finer, more broken worms rather than a labyrinth at the same width, because the ring mean is a Bessel J0 response and passes high frequencies, so the source must be smooth. Depth 1 keeps large scale shading because w > 1 inverts low frequencies. Bias moves the balance only weakly at depth 2: at +-1.2 it fragments into worms and blobs rather than clean leopard spots. Worm ends and bulbs show, so it is not a true converged Turing pattern. Slight small grey specks where tanh walls meet at some junctions in hillshade.
turing-stencil.node_shape: TuringStencil: Source (GeneratorSource, or built in Perlin), Radius hybrid, Weight float, Gain hybrid, Outer Gain float, Bias hybrid, Depth int (1..2), Ring enum (Axis, Full), Output Min/Max
turing-stencil.port_notes: Nested fixed loops over a precomputed offset table, a node may evaluate its source any fixed number of times. tanh is a rational x(27+x^2)/(27+9x^2) clamped at 3, C1 at the clamp, no Exp needed. A pointwise pass cannot share work between lanes, so the (ring+1)^depth count is firm; ring 6 cuts it to 49 evals but was not visually tested at the default. A port would probably cap depth at 1 in 3D and 4D, where it loses the look. Far coords (4e4) measured fine, std 0.961.
turing-stencil.params_text: depth=2,r=0.5,sscale=2.1,w=1.2,g=3,g2=8,bias=0,ring=8,src=0 (the code defaults; 3D and 4D default to depth 1). Control with no stencil: depth=-1.

master.one_liner: Two synchronous steps of a center-surround (activator-inhibitor) update with sigmoid saturation, evaluated pointwise through the stencil tree: resolution-free labyrinth stripes and spots of uniform width.
master.look: Zebra/brain-coral labyrinths with constant stripe width and sharp but smooth walls; Bias moves it to isolated spots (leopard) or holes; Gain softens or hardens walls. Unlike Perlin (broad-band, no preferred width) or Cellular (polygonal), the pattern has one dominant wavelength and sinuous, non-branching walls: the reaction-diffusion signature. Coral, brain, fingerprints, sand ripples, giraffe/zebra, lichen.
master.algorithm:
Ring R of radius r: 2D 8 points on the circle, 3D 14 (6 axis + 8 cube diagonals normalised), 4D 24 (8 axis + 16 diagonals). Source u_0 (any smooth noise, scaled so its features are ~r).
  step(u)(p) = tanh( G * ( u(p) - w * mean_{t in R} u(p + t) ) + Bias )
  u_D = step^D (u_0), D in {1,2} via nested fixed loops: |R|+1 evals per level -> (|R|+1)^D source evaluations.
  out = u_D.
The linear part is a difference-of-scales band-pass peaking at wavelength ~2-3 r (the Turing instability's fixed point); tanh saturates; the second application equalises stripe width and removes wiggles (curvature-flow-like).
master.why_new: Reaction-diffusion textures are always baked on grids; this is a grid-free, seedable, tileable approximation using the only pointwise trick available: a bounded-depth synchronous update tree. Nothing on the sheet has a single preferred stripe width with sharp walls.
master.simd_plan: Nested fixed loops over a precomputed ring offset table; tanh via FS::Exp or rational polynomial; no masks. Cost 2D: depth 1 = 9 Perlin (~10 ns), depth 2 = 81 Perlin (~90 ns); 3D depth 1 = 15 Perlin3D (~33 ns), depth 2 = 225 (~500 ns, flag as heavy); 4D depth 1 = 25 Perlin4D (~108 ns), depth 2 disallowed. Tiles in 4D.
master.continuity: Continuous (tanh of continuous averages); as Gain grows it approaches a step, still C0.
master.params: Source (default internal Perlin at scale r), Radius hybrid, Weight w float (~1.2), Gain G hybrid, Bias hybrid (spots/stripes/holes), Depth int (1..2), Ring enum (Axis/Full).
master.risks: Depth 2 in 3D is very expensive; depth 1 is 'only' a sigmoid band-pass (close to a phasor/Gabor look) and the fixed-point benefit is visible mainly at depth 2; ring sampling at one radius gives slight angular ringing in FFT (use 12-point ring in 2D if visible).
master.cost_note: Cost 2D: depth 1 = 9 Perlin (~10 ns), depth 2 = 81 Perlin (~90 ns); 3D depth 1 = 15 Perlin3D (~33 ns), depth 2 = 225 (~500 ns, flag as heavy); 4D depth 1 = 25 Perlin4D (~108 ns), depth 2 disallowed.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 3997.2 ns against perlin2 54.7 at depth 2, ring 8, 81 perlin evals. Depth 2 ring 6 measured 49.83x, depth 1 ring 8 measured 8.91x. The control, sigmoid of source alone, measured 1.08x. Params read once in the speed run.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: about 90 ns 2D depth 2 ring 8 and 10 ns depth 1; about 33 ns 3D depth 1; about 110 ns 4D depth 1. Depth 2 in 3D and 4D is not sane.

wave-lattice.look: Default: long thin white threads that wobble and cross each other without ending, enclosing curved polygons on black, like crazed glaze or a loose net; lines pass straight through junctions, which cellular edges never do, and several lines meet at star points. Wide view holds even density with no visible repeat. beta=0 N=5 Sum is the classic fivefold lace with rings around bright dots; Product gives black and white star tiles; Max gives bright star bursts with few dark holes. The 3D Sum with icosahedral axes is a porous gyroid like solid with no obvious repeat.

dims.3D: works, measured z continuity max 0.0234 for dz=1e-3; icosahedral n3=6 solid rendered
dims.4D: Eval4 implemented with 24-cell axes; measured on an oblique 2D plane (slice4=1): c0ratio 7.85, range -1..1. Tiling itself not tested.

wave-lattice.artifacts: FFT keeps faint straight rays from the N grating directions (axis stat 8.96, not isotropic, by design). Product with the default pow=1 is a near jump at the lines: measured c0ratio 1.53, max slope 945, because |prod|^(1/N) has unbounded slope; use pow=N for the smooth raw product or a value between. Max and MinAbs have creases by design. With beta=0 the pattern is globally quasiperiodic and has no spatial variety. Shared modulation displaces all gratings together, so the net stays star shaped until beta is large; per grating modulation breaks the stars up but costs N source evals. Seed only changes phases and modulation, so with beta=0 seeds are translations of one pattern family.
wave-lattice.node_shape: WaveLattice: Gratings int N (2..12), Combine enum (Sum, Product, Max, Line Net, Phase, Normalised Sum), Frequency hybrid, Rotation float, Phase Jitter float, Phase Modulation hybrid + Beta float + Per Grating enum, Line Width float, Random Directions bool, Seed Offset, Feature Scale, Output Min/Max
wave-lattice.port_notes: Branch free: per grating one dot plus one cos, then FS::Max/Min chains. Direction tables per node when params are set (2D angle table, 3D tables for 3/4/6, 4D 24-cell axes). Phase from hash of seed and grating index. MinAbs uses |sin(psi/2)| so lines keep the grating period. Cost does not depend on a window, so 4D cost is N dots plus the modulation source. Measured 4D scalar: n4=6 per grating is heavy (2347 ns, 12 perlin4 evals, 44x perlin2); n4=12 shared modulation 494 ns (9x); n4=12 beta=0 123 ns (2.27x). Shared modulation or none is the sane 4D choice. Far coords (4e4) measured fine, std 0.770.
wave-lattice.params_text: combine=3,n=5,f=1,beta=3,pergrating=1,mscale=0.4,width=0.45 (the code defaults). Pure quasicrystal lace: combine=0,beta=0. Star tile mosaic: combine=1,beta=2,pergrating=0. Cheaper shared modulation: pergrating=0.

master.one_liner: Sum, product or max of N phase-modulated plane gratings at symmetric angles: hexagonal/octagonal lattices, 5- and 7-fold quasicrystals, 2-coloured line arrangements, with noise-driven phase to melt them organically.
master.look: N=5 Sum: the classic fivefold quasicrystal lace; N=3 Sum: honeycomb bumps; Product with Beta>0: wobbly polygon mosaic with straight-ish wiggling edges (looks like cracked glaze with ruler-drawn cracks); Max: tiled pyramids; MinAbs: chain-link / woven mesh. In 3D with icosahedral axes: 3D quasicrystal density (slices show aperiodic Penrose-like motifs). Uses: decorative tiles, crystals, lattice masks, honeycomb, energy shields, moire-free background structures.
master.algorithm:
N wave vectors k_j (N = 2..12). 2D: angle_j = pi*j/N + Rotation (N=2 square, 3 hexagonal, 4 octagonal, 5/7 quasicrystal). 3D: tables: N=3 cubic axes, N=4 tetrahedral body diagonals, N=6 icosahedral fivefold axes (0,+-1,+-phi) cyclic, normalised. 4D: per-seed hashed directions or the 24-cell axes (12). psi_j = 2pi*F*dot(k_j,p) + 2pi*rnd01(hash(seed,j))*PhaseJitter + Beta*m_j(p) where m is a HybridSource 'Phase Modulation' evaluated once at p (shared, 1 eval) or per-grating via seed offset j (N evals; enum). Combine enum: Sum = (1/N) sum cos psi_j (quasiperiodic bumps); Product = prod cos psi_j (sign flips across every grating line: a 2-colouring of a line arrangement, polygon mosaics, soft-pinched near lines); Max = max_j cos psi_j (ridged tile lattice); MinAbs = 1-min_j|sin psi_j|-ish via smooth min (line network / wire mesh: distance-like to the arrangement); Phase = atan2approx(sum sin, sum cos)/pi.

[PlanarWaveNoise, shader-community] Setup when params change: for i in 0..N-1 draw from Seed: unit direction d_i (2D: angle = Orientation + Spread*rnd11; 3D: Fibonacci-sphere point jittered; 4D: normalised 4-vector of 4 gaussians via Box-Muller from hashes), frequency f_i = Frequency*(1 + Bandwidth*rnd11), phase ph_i = rnd01*2pi, amplitude a_i = 1 (or 1/f_i^H for a 1/f spectrum).
Eval: t_i = f_i * dot(p, d_i) + ph_i (one FMA chain per direction)
  Profile enum: Sine cos(t_i); Triangle 4|fract(t/2pi)-0.5|-1; Square sign(cos t); Sawtooth; (precomputed 256-entry periodic table with linear interp = arbitrary profile, e.g. a Gaussian-blurred sawtooth)
  Combine enum: Sum: out = sum a_i prof(t_i) / sqrt(N) (Gaussian-ish, Gabor-like spectrum); Max: out = max_i prof(t_i) (planar fronts intersect into convex cells: the 'cellular wave noise' flavour); SoftMax via exp smin with k; Product of (1+prof)/2.
Anisotropy: Spread small -> all waves near one orientation (stripes with interference); Spread=pi -> isotropic.
N is an int member, loop count fixed across lanes.
master.why_new: SineWave is the N=D axis-aligned product only. Quasicrystals and line-arrangement colourings are visually unlike every lattice noise and cannot be approximated by warps of SineWave. Phase modulation by a source is what turns a mathematical pattern into a usable noise.
master.simd_plan: N x (dot + cos poly) + N hashes for the phase jitter: N=5 in 2D ~0.5x Perlin plus the modulation source; cost is flat in dimension (no window), so 4D is cheap and tiling works. Branch-free; Max/MinAbs via FS::Max/Min chains; tables are per-node constants.
master.continuity: Sum/Product/Phase-free outputs C-infinity (modulated by the source's continuity); Max C0; MinAbs C0 (C1 with smooth-min). Phase wraps by design.
master.params: Feature Scale; N (int); Rotation; Frequency (hybrid); Phase Modulation (hybrid) + Beta + PerGrating enum; PhaseJitter; Combine enum; Seed Offset.
master.risks:
Globally quasiperiodic: no spatial variation without modulation/warp (document). Product output amplitude collapses near lines (normalise by (1/N) power or output sign*|prod|^(1/N)). Aliasing at high F.
[PlanarWaveNoise, shader-community] Low N shows obvious repetition along each wave direction; sums of few sines are quasi-periodic and look 'mathematical' unless N >= 12 or combined with warp. Range normalisation by sqrt(N) is approximate for non-sine profiles.
sources: Quasicrystal plane-wave sum shaders (shader community folklore, e.g. Shadertoy; recalled, not fetched)
master.cost_note: N x (dot + cos poly) + N hashes for the phase jitter: N=5 in 2D ~0.5x Perlin plus the modulation source; cost is flat in dimension (no window), so 4D is cheap and tiling works.
master.variant_notes: Separated from WaveNoise because Product, Max and MinAbs combines give polygon mosaics and line nets, not a Gaussian field. PlanarWaveNoise contributes the random-direction Max combine (convex crystal cells).

measured.scalar_note: Measured 559.7 ns against perlin2 53.1 with the default per grating modulation (10 perlin evals). pergrating=0 measured 3.1x (165.6 ns), beta=0 measured 1.17x (60.4 ns). Params read once in the speed run; with the harness's per sample map reads the shared form measured 6.18x.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: about 13 ns default per grating 2D, about 4 ns shared modulation 2D, about 2 ns with beta=0

adaptive-cellular.look: Cell size really follows a map: plates several cells wide grade through ordinary cells to a fine rubble of tiny cells, inside one view, with no warped or stretched cells. The F1 output is wells that shrink from wide craters to pinpricks, and the relief reads as a cratered plain grading into dense pitted ground. The XZ slice has the same clear gradient. The volume is the best panel: big rock blocks at the top grade to fine rubble at the bottom. Where the level changes by more than one, small cells poke into big ones as circular bubbles, since walls between different levels are circular arcs. The catalogue form with one coin per level looks different: big plains beside abrupt patches of tiny cells, with visibly square depth blocks.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3, hashed octree with density interpolated from 64 lattice corners, volume rendered
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path. The hierarchy and the cap are dimension agnostic; the 4^D density lattice gets expensive.

adaptive-cellular.range: -1.000 .. 1.000 over 8 seeds, mean 0.216, set by construction for the line output. F1 and F2-F1 are scaled and clipped to -1 .. 1.
adaptive-cellular.artifacts: Bubble fringes where levels differ by 2 or more, which read as natural but are not a clean grade. Straight axis-aligned traces in the depth output are mostly gone at grade 0.8 but the quadtree is still detectable in the depth map (axis 15, a faint cross in the FFT). Thin lines on the finest leaves approach the pixel size and alias slightly. The soft dark wedges seen at jit=1 in big cells come from F1 reaching the cap, and jit=0.8 removes the cause (sqrt(D)/2 + J < 1.5 - J); that final sheet was not checked by eye.
adaptive-cellular.node_shape: AdaptiveCellular : Generator. Density (HybridSource 0..1), Max Depth (int 1..5), Grade (float, 0 = independent coin per level), Grid Jitter (hybrid, clamp at 0.8), Output enum {F1, F2-F1, Value, Lines, Depth}, ScalableGenerator, Seeded, VariableRange.
adaptive-cellular.port_notes: Fixed loop over levels, each a 3^D window. Subdivide flags of the previous level are carried as a 3^D bit mask per lane, indexed by parent offset with a variable shift, so ancestors need no extra hashes. Density: evaluate 4^D lattice corners once, then per candidate a multilinear interpolate with a per-lane permute into the corner table, or gather by Select. Distance divides by a per-level constant, then Min with the reach. Bit fields from one hash give the coin and the jitter direction. Level goes into the hash through the seed.
adaptive-cellular.params_text: depth=4,grade=0.8,norm=1,interp=1,jit=0.8,sc=0.5,df=0.22,con=1.1,bias=0.45,w=0.06,out=3 (these are the code defaults). out: 0 F1, 1 F2-F1, 2 cell value, 3 cells with lines, 4 depth, 5 density. Catalogue form: grade=0,interp=0. Rejected forms kept for testing: norm=0, lane=1.

master.one_liner: Density-controlled cellular noise on a hashed quadtree/octree: a hybrid Density field decides, level by level, whether a cell subdivides, so cell size varies smoothly with a control map (Jonchier, Salvati, Derouet-Jourdan 2019, 'Procedural Non-Uniform Cellular Noise').
master.look: Voronoi-like cells whose size follows a map: large plains cells grading into fine mountain cells, dense crowds of small cells near 'attractors', hierarchical cracked-crust looks (Depth output). Smooth transitions in cell density, not just warped Worley.
master.algorithm:
Params: Density (hybrid 0..1), MaxDepth D (int 1-5), Jitter (float), Output enum {F1, F2-F1, CellValue, Depth}, Distance enum.
Leaf test for a cell c at level l (size 2^-l): leaf(c,l) = (l == D) | (rnd01(hash(seed,l,c)) >= Density(centre(c,l)) ) with the ancestor chain consistent: a cell exists only if all its ancestors were subdivided; define subdiv(c,l) = rnd01(hash(seed,l,c)) < Density(centre(c,l)).
Gen(p): bestD = inf; for l in 0..D (fixed loop): cl = floor(p*2^l); for each of the 3^dim neighbours n of cl at level l (fixed loop): alive = AND over ancestors a of n (levels 0..l-1, fixed loop of l steps, or carried incrementally from the previous level's 3x3 alive flags) of subdiv(a); isLeaf = alive & (l==D | !subdiv(n,l)); feature point f = (n + 0.5 + Jitter*(rnd-0.5))*2^-l; d = dist(p,f); bestD = Select(isLeaf, min(bestD,d), bestD); track second best for F2 and the hash for CellValue.
Incremental trick: the alive flags of level l+1 neighbours are the subdiv flags of their parents, which are among the 3^dim level-l neighbours already visited, so the whole thing is D x 3^dim hashes + D Density evaluations at cell centres (Density evaluated at the 3^dim centres per level = 9D source evals in 2D, or sample Density once at p and treat it as locally constant for a cheap approximation).
F1 normalised by the leaf size (so cells look uniform in local terms) or absolute (for true multi-scale distances).
master.why_new: DomainScale with a hybrid scale warps the lattice (stretching cells, discontinuities when scale varies), it cannot change cell density smoothly. Fractal Cellular sums all levels; this picks one leaf per region. Feature-count control from a node is a frequently requested terrain/texture capability.
master.simd_plan: Fixed D x 3^dim loop of hashes and distances with Select; 2D D=4: 36 hashes + 36 distances ~ 2.5x CellularDistance2D; 3D D=3: 81 cells ~ 3x CellularDistance3D. Density sampled per level at p only (approximation) keeps Source cost at D evals.
master.continuity: F1 is C0 as long as the nearest leaf point lies in the searched window at its level (guaranteed because each level's 3^dim window is searched and points stay in their cells with Jitter<=1). Cell topology flips where Density crosses a hash threshold, but the threshold is evaluated per cell centre, so no spatial discontinuity inside a cell; at borders between leaves of different levels F1 stays continuous.
master.params: Density (hybrid), MaxDepth (int), Jitter (float), Output (enum), DistanceFunction (enum), Normalise enum {PerLeaf, Absolute}.
master.risks: Cost grows linearly with D times the window; Density evaluated at neighbour centres is expensive if it is a complex graph (use GeneratorCache or the per-point approximation). The original chapter is paywalled; the above is a from-scratch pointwise design of the stated idea.
master.cost_note: Fixed D x 3^dim loop of hashes and distances with Select; 2D D=4: 36 hashes + 36 distances ~ 2.5x CellularDistance2D; 3D D=3: 81 cells ~ 3x CellularDistance3D.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 29.50x perlin2 at defaults (1472.8 ns vs 49.9 ns, 16 source evals, 45 hashed cells); 55.49x with density at every cell centre (2784 ns, 45 source evals); 26.61x at depth 2 (1327 ns); 28.62x at depth 3 (1426 ns). Most of the cost is the fixed 16 density evals, so depth is cheap.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D at depth 4 about 35 ns (16 x 1.1 for density + 45 cells at about 0.4). 3D at depth 3 about 190 ns (64 x 2.2 + 108 cells at about 0.45). 4D at depth 2 about 1.2 us (256 x 4.3 + 243 cells), and a Density built from a cheap source would cut this a lot.

barranco-cones.look: Relief: unmistakable stratovolcanoes, concave cones rising from a flat plain, each with radial gullies cut into the flanks that fork as they descend, more forks low down. Reads like a real barranco volcano and looks hand modelled. Gray panel: bright peaks with dark forking lines, like starbursts or dandelion heads. Threshold panel: scalloped discs. Kinds: basin gives funnels with radiating channels on a white plateau; caldera gives a bright ring around a floor with the gullies outside it. 3D vol: ribbed gourds or barrel cacti, with forked grooves running pole to pole. The vol image was inspected before the pole fade was added; the fade only touches the region near the axis, and the saved image is the rerender, not checked by eye again.
barranco-cones.dims: 2D and 3D measured. 3D is a real form: true radius, azimuth about Y, gullies as meridians (z-continuity max 0.0725 per 1e-3, in line with the gully slope, after a pole fade fixed a 0.31 jump on the axis). 4D not implemented: 81 cones, so a planar lattice would be needed and torus tiling is not available.
barranco-cones.range: [-1, 0.965] over 8 seeds; far coords fine at 4e4; no NaN; flat -1 plain between cones
barranco-cones.artifacts: Flanks have even gully spacing, so a cone looks tidy, almost designed; warp 0.05 keeps them slightly wandering, more warp was not needed. Cones are plain away from gullies, there is no other surface detail, so it needs an added fractal for close views. Isolated cones sit on a dead flat plain. Width is capped by r0 and n0: 0.25 x 2 pi x R x r0 / n0, 0.0385 world units at defaults, so strong wide gullies need fewer branches.
barranco-cones.node_shape: BarrancoCones: Feature Scale, Density (hybrid), Jitter, Radius, Radius Jitter, Base Branches (int), Inner Radius, Gully Width (fraction of limit), Gully Depth, Depth Gain, Profile Exponent, Kind enum {Peak, Basin, Caldera}, Warp Source (hybrid), Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
barranco-cones.port_notes: Keep branch ids modulo n0 << k, otherwise the atan seam reappears as a hash change. Level k per lane: int from Trunc of log2, branch count by a shift per lane (AVX2 has variable shifts), P as Convert of it. The fork ramp is one Select. Output is only C0: the crease at the V of each gully is by design. 3D needs the pole fade smoothstep( 0.1, 0.4, rho / r ) on the carve. Warp is one lane wide source eval shared by all cones, so it costs the source once, not 9 times. Interior of each gully branch uses only hash and floor, so no search or segment distance is involved.

master.one_liner: Volcano and basin cones carrying radial gullies that branch by analytic period doubling in log-polar coordinates, so gully spacing stays constant at all radii for O(1) per cone.
master.look: Stratovolcanoes or lone peaks with deep radial barrancos forking as they descend, and a central crater. Inverted: drainage funnels. Good as hero landforms or as a coarse layer under other details.
master.algorithm: For each cone in the 3x3 window: r=|p-c|/R, th=atan2 approx/(2pi)+warp/r_clamped+seed. t=log2(max(r,r0)/r0); k=floor(t); u=t-k. Period P=1/(n0*2^k). q=th/P; s=q-floor(q)-0.5. Branch-specific split time u0=0.15+0.6*hash(floor(q),k). ramp=smoothstep((u-u0)/(1-u0)). Distance in period units: |abs(s)-0.25*ramp|; at u=1 both branches land exactly on the next level's centres, so branches are continuous across levels. World distance=dist*P*2pi*r. g=smooth(1-dist/w). Carve=Depth(r)*Gain^t*g with continuous t, avoiding ring seams. Height=(exp(-a*r)-exp(-a))*fade(r)-Carve. Combine by Max. Variants: Basin sign flip gives centripetal drainage; Caldera replaces the profile centre by a rim and flat floor, optionally with nested collapse circles.
master.why_new: CellularDistance gives smooth cones only, and radial sine stripes have spacing that grows with r. Spacing here stays constant because branch count doubles with radius, with no segment search needed.
master.simd_plan: Per cone: polynomial atan2, log2, one hash, Selects. 9 cones with Max; estimate 10-18 ns in 2D, about 12x Perlin. Can reduce to 4 cones with a tighter size cap. 3D: 27 cells with azimuth about a chosen axis plus true 3D radius, gullies as meridians. 4D: 81 is too costly; use a planar lattice, so no torus tiling.
master.continuity: C0 if the carve width w stays under 0.25 of the local branch spacing (P*2pi*r, whose minimum is 2pi*r0/n0), since then the carve is 0 at branch interval edges. The test used w above this limit, a known defect to fix. Atan seam is hidden by periodic q when n0 is an integer and warp is added after.
master.params: Cone Density, Radius R, Radius Jitter, Base Branches n0 (int), Inner Radius r0, Gully Width w, Gully Depth, Depth Gain, Profile (enum Peak, Basin, Caldera), Warp Source (hybrid).
master.risks: TESTED in numpy (radial2), not ported. Near the summit it reads as convincing radial gullies with forks. Outer flanks degrade into wandering squiggles, because angular warp scales up with radius; the warp must scale as 1/r, as written above but not yet retested. First test with heavy warp and stepped depth looked like fingerprints with ring seams.
master.cost_note: 9 cones with Max; estimate 10-18 ns in 2D, about 12x Perlin.

measured.scalar_note: Measured with defaults, 3.12x worley2. Absent cones skip in scalar (density 0.55); a port pays for all 9.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 2D 10-18 ns (9 cones with polynomial atan2 and log2, one hash each); 3D about 30-50 ns with 27 cones. A radius test mask cannot skip work per lane.
measured.c0_note: Not a jump. With depth=0 it is 7.98. Gullies are narrow, about 0.03 cells half width, so the slope changes inside the probe's 8e-3 step. The measured max slope 67.9 matches the analytic bound: fork ramp slope up to about 2.3 x carve slope about 27.

bent-walls.look: Jigsaw or giraffe plates: every wall wanders in its own way between straight anchored junctions, with fingers and bays that interlock, and cell sizes stay even. The threshold panel shows interlocking camouflage blobs. The XZ slice has the same character, with rounder walls and some small enclosed islands of a neighbour cell where the slice grazes a bent surface. The relief with the pillowed output reads as heaped plates of rock. The volume with the distance output gives packed irregular stones with thin curved gaps.

dims.3D: works, measured: same template code, wave vector projected into the wall plane; volume rendered
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path. Nothing in the code is 2D or 3D specific.

bent-walls.range: -1.000 .. 1.000 over 8 seeds, mean 0.212. out=0 keeps dark lines at -1 and plates at -0.4 .. 1.
bent-walls.artifacts: A few hooks and very narrow fingers where the bend is steep, which stay readable as jigsaw. Small lens shaped islands in the 3D slice. Slight line thickening near junctions, where the width normalisation fades out by design. Junctions keep their Voronoi positions. Owner mosaic output (out=2) has jumps by design. Without the window cap the top 3 search has real small jumps on window lines: c0ratio 1.3 to 1.6 by the offset probe, and the plain harness probe does not see them.
bent-walls.node_shape: BentWalls : Generator. Bend Amplitude (hybrid), Bend Frequency (hybrid), Junction Fade (float), Line Width (hybrid), Grid Jitter (hybrid), Output enum {Plates, Line, Owner, Distance, Pillow}, ScalableGenerator, Seeded, VariableRange.
bent-walls.port_notes: Three rank insertion by Select over capped d2, hash and position, one Select pair for canonical order by hash, then once per lane: 3 extra bit field values from the pair hash, one projected direction (1 InvSqrt), 2 Sin + 2 Cos, 1 Sqrt. The harmonics can share the bits. The Line output only needs Abs and a smoothstep.
bent-walls.params_text: a=0.18,k=4.5,a2=0.35,e=0.45,w=0.035,jit=1,win=1,cap=1,out=0 (these are the code defaults). Relief uses out=4, the volume uses out=3 with iso -0.72.

master.one_liner: Voronoi where each individual wall gets its own wobble (wavelength and phase hashed from the pair), with an envelope from F3 that makes ownership consistent at junctions.
master.look: Amoeba or jigsaw-like cells with hand-drawn walls, each wall bending differently: giraffe hide, mud plates, leaded glass, stone walling, biological tissue. Cell interiors and feature points are not distorted. Prototyped: rel_jigsaw shape=0.
master.algorithm: Track top 3 by squared distance with hash and position (F1=a, F2=b, F3=c). Order (a,b) canonically by comparing hashes to get (lo,hi); pair hash q=mix(h_a^h_b). Fixed-denominator signed wall: s0=(d_lo^2-d_hi^2)/2, positive on hi's side. Envelope e=smoothstep(0,E,d_c^2-d_b^2), which reaches 0 exactly where the identity of F2 changes. Bent wall: s=s0+A*e*sin(dot(k_q, x-m)+phi_q), where m is the pair midpoint and k_q, phi_q come from q. Owner = hi if s>0 else lo. Outputs: owner value, wall line profile(|s|/w), distance |s| clamped, or owner value times line. s is antisymmetric through the canonical order, so both sides agree on the wall.
master.why_new: Warped Cellular (see contact sheet) bends everything with one shared field, stretching cells and producing long coherent swirls. Per-wall bending keeps cell size and shape statistics and varies wall by wall, and it cannot be built with a domain warp because the displacement depends on the pair of cells.
master.simd_plan: Three-rank insertion via Select over (d2, hash, position) per window cell, one masked swap for canonical order, one Sin. 3^D window. No second pass. Estimate 2x CellularDistance (2D 8 ns, 3D 25 ns, 4D 80 ns). Scalar proto measured 5.5x worley2, but it used 5x5 and a naive insertion sort. Using dot(k_q, x-m) instead of an along-wall coordinate makes it dimension agnostic, though the proto used the 2D along-wall coordinate.
master.continuity: Line profile output is C0: c0ratio went from 1.03 with true-distance denominators to 7.99 with the fixed denominator, because the fixed form agrees where F2 changes. Owner mosaic is intentionally discontinuous, with an edge that matches the line.
master.params: Bend Amplitude (hybrid), Bend Frequency (hybrid), Junction Fade E (float), Line Width (hybrid), Grid Jitter (hybrid), Output enum.
master.risks: Fixed denominator makes wall width vary with feature spacing (mild). The nD wave-vector form is untested. A disc-shaped jigsaw tab variant was tried and looks like bubbles stuck on walls, not interlocking tabs, so it was dropped; a sine is the version worth keeping.
master.cost_note: Estimate 2x CellularDistance (2D 8 ns, 3D 25 ns, 4D 80 ns). Scalar proto measured 5.5x worley2, but it used 5x5 and a naive insertion sort.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 7.08x perlin2 (352.1 ns vs 49.8 ns), 3.23x the harness worley2 (which is 5x5). Includes 10 std::map param reads per sample and scalar sin/cos.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: about 8 to 10 ns in 2D (2x CellularDistance 3.9 ns, plus 2 Sin and 2 Cos once per lane), about 28 ns in 3D, about 85 ns in 4D

bond-graph.look: 2D: a wiry irregular network of thin white strokes on black, with dead ends, loose fragments, triangles from diagonals and small node dots. Straight mode reads as a road or crack map with visible kinks. Arc mode (bulge 0.1) is the better look: curved strokes like leaf veins or hand drawn rivers, and it stops reading as a lattice. Hillshade shows raised walls with a clean flat floor between. Mountain skeleton (out=2, relief) gives tent-like peaks joined by sharp ridges, with creases radiating from nodes like folded paper; usable but artificial. 3D vol: a connected scaffold of curved tubes, like a mass of twigs or a jungle gym, no visible cubic rows with warp 0.22. XZ slice of the 3D form is scattered blobs with short smears.
bond-graph.dims: 2D and 3D measured (real Eval3 with tubes, z-continuity max 0.015 per 1e-3). 4D not run; axis edges generalise directly to 8 edges over 9 points.
bond-graph.range: [-1, 0.945] over 8 seeds with the default stroke mix (+1 needs the fattest stroke or node); 3D -1 to 0.92; no NaN; far coords fine
bond-graph.artifacts: Lattice density is uniform: the 4x wide panel is an even texture with holes from low keep, no regional variation. The FFT has radial streaks from long straight strokes (axis stat 40 is high because of them, there is no axis cross at jit 0.4 with warp). Junctions with many strokes form small stars. Output is flat at the clamp beyond Dmax, 0.13 cells at the defaults, so it is a line mask with a narrow halo rather than a wide distance field. A 2D slice of 3D or a 4D tile path will show dots, not lines, as the catalogue warned.
bond-graph.node_shape: BondGraph: Feature Scale, Jitter (constant 0..0.9), Keep (hybrid), Diagonals (hybrid fraction), Width, Width Jitter, Bulge (arc sagitta, 2D), Node Radius, Bead, Output enum {Signed Distance, Line Mask, Ridge Height}, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
bond-graph.port_notes: Two corrections to the catalogue. (1) Window: because every point keeps margin m from its cell faces, only edges incident to the sample cell's point plus one diagonal per quad touching the sample cell can be nearer than m, so 2D needs 8 edges (not 16), 3D 18 edges (not 98) and 4D axis-only 8 edges (not 108). (2) Clamp: strokes are |seg| - w, so the exact clamp is Dmax = m - Wmax - |sagitta|, not m; clamping at m leaves jumps of up to w at cell faces. The ridge output needs no such clamp, its flank reaches zero at m - |sagitta|. rndDir2 here uses cos and sin; a port would use a direction table. Arc sector test is two cross products plus Select. Overlaps bond-tunnels (3D caves with one cell window, hubs, chambers) and the LineMask of cellular-dual-mesh; the distinct part is the 2D arc network and per edge attributes. Arcs are 2D only in this prototype.

master.one_liner: Random bonds between neighbouring jittered lattice points give a distance field to a real network with dead ends, gaps and per-edge width, height and beads.
master.look:
Road maps, cracks with width, circuit traces, neurons, spider web fragments, mountain-range skeletons with peaks at nodes, strings of pearls. In 3D: connected worm tunnels and chambers when thresholded, the classic hard case of chunk-independent cave worms without a random walk. At Keep near 0.5 it behaves like a bond percolation pattern. Prototyped: rel_edges 2D only.
[BondNoise, lattice-kernels] Density 1 Sum: a smooth noise whose ridges run along straight lattice bonds (woven basket, textile). Density 0.3 Max Hard: mazes, PCB traces, rebar, irrigation ditches, broken drystone wall mortar; Smooth Max gives rounded wires with proper junctions. After DomainWarp the networks become root systems and vein networks that branch and END, unlike F2-F1 which always closes cells. 3D: volumetric scaffold / jungle-gym, sliced into dashes and dots.
[CellularMeshEdges, cell-relations] A wiry planar graph: straight (or gently curved) segments joining jittered points, 6-8 edges per vertex when all diagonals are on, becoming a 'street map' / circuit board / maze with dead ends when Density < 1. Arc mode gives hand-drawn rivers and roads with bends. In 3D: a tunnel system (caves) with guaranteed connectivity along lattice adjacency. Thresholded it is a crisp line drawing; as a distance field it drives width, bevels and erosion masks.
master.algorithm:
Lattice: integer grid, one point per cell, P_c = c + 0.5 + 0.5*J*dir(hash_c) with J in [0,1) a CONSTANT (not hybrid). Margin m = 0.5*(1-J) is the distance every point keeps from its cell faces.

KEY LEMMA (makes it pointwise with a 3^D window): for adjacent cells c,c' (|c-c'|inf<=1) the segment P_c P_c' lies inside the union of cells within 1 of BOTH c and c' and is >= m away from every other cell. So a stroke of half-width w <= m around that segment can only touch samples whose window contains both endpoints. Output is clamped at Dmax = m, which makes the clamped min exact and seamless for any J.

Edge set per sample S in cell s (2D): for each of the 9 window cells c and each offset d in {+x, +y, +x+y, +x-y} with c+d also in the window: 6 horizontal + 6 vertical + 4 diagonal = 16 edges. Diagonal rule: each quad gets exactly one diagonal (bit of hash(c), or the shorter diagonal, or the Delaunay in-circle choice from idea CellularFacetMesh) so the graph is a planar triangulation. 3D: 13 half-offsets -> 54 axis + 36 face-diagonal + 8 body-diagonal edges; axis-only variant 54. 4D: axis-only 108 edges over 81 points.

Per edge e=(c,c'): he = Hash(min(c,c'), max(c,c')) (symmetric) -> present = (he & 0xff) < Density*255, widthMul = 0.5+rnd01(he>>8), bulge = Bulge*rnd11(he>>16).

out = Dmax
for each edge e:
  a = P_c - S, b = P_c' - S, ab = b - a
  t = clamp(-dot(a,ab)/dot(ab,ab), 0, 1)        // reciprocal, no branch
  d = |a + t*ab| - Width*widthMul                  // capsule
  Arc mode (sagitta sg = bulge*|ab|, need Width + |sg| <= m): chord mid M, unit normal n, R = (L^2/(8 sg) + sg/2), C = M - n*(R - sg); inSector = (cross(A-C,S-C) >= 0) & (cross(S-C,B-C) >= 0) (signs flipped by sign(sg)); d = Select(inSector, abs(|S-C| - R), min(|S-A|,|S-B|)) - Width*widthMul
  d = Select(present, d, Dmax)
  out = min(out, d)
Nodes: for each window point out = min(out, |P_c - S| - NodeRadius)  (covers junctions and stroke ends; NodeRadius <= m).
return ScaleOutput(out, -Width, Dmax)   (or profile: 1 - smoothstep(0, Dmax, out) for a 'line mask').

Correct 3D tubes: same code with 3-vectors; caves = threshold.

[BondNoise, lattice-kernels] Params: Width w (< 0.5), Density (hybrid, fraction of live edges), Kernel {Smooth, Hard}, Accumulate {Sum signed, Max}, Lattice {Square, Triangular(2D only)/Square(3D)}, Truchet (bool, 2D).
Gen(p): c = floor(p), f = p - c; acc = 0 (or -1)
 for axis k in 0..dim-1:
  for vk in {-1,0,1}: for each corner choice of the other dim-1 coords in {0,1}: (dim*3*2^(dim-1) edges: 12 / 36 / 96)
    v = c + offset; h = hash(seed, v) ^ (k * AxisPrime), remix
    d2 = Sum_{j!=k} (f_j - v_j)^2 + (clamp(f_k, v_k, v_k+1) - f_k)^2     // axis-aligned segment distance, no dots
    live = (h>>24) < Density*256; a = Sum ? rnd11(h>>8) : 1
    kern = Smooth ? max(0, 1 - d2/w^2)^2 : (d2 < w^2)
    acc = Sum ? acc + Select(live, a*kern, 0) : max(acc, Select(live, kern, 0))
 Truchet (2D): per cell, bit b = hash(c)&1 picks pairing; kern = max over the two quarter-circle arcs: arc centre = b ? (0,0),(1,1) : (1,0),(0,1), radius 0.5, d = | |f - centre| - 0.5 |; combine with Max.
 Triangular lattice: skew p (simplex skew), edges along e1, e2 and e1-e2 of the skewed grid; distance computed in world space via precomputed edge direction vectors (dot needed).
master.why_new: F2-F1 gives walls of cells: always closed, no dead ends, no per-edge attributes. This is the dual graph, connecting points rather than separating them, with a density control and open topology.
master.simd_plan: Same lattice loop as Cellular.inl (3x3 / 3x3x3 / 3x3x3x3 HashPrimesHB, jitter from hash bits), storing the 9/27/81 relative positions in std::array<float32v,N>. Then a fixed unrolled edge list (16 / 98 or 54 / 108) of capsule distances: ~14 ops each (sub, dot, rcp, clamp, fmadd, sqrt). Presence/width via Select from the symmetric pair hash (hash of the smaller primed cell coords XOR'd with the larger). Arc mode adds ~20 ops per edge. Cost estimate AVX2: 2D ~9 ns (2.5x CellularDistance, 8x Perlin); 3D axis-only ~35 ns (3x Cellular3D), full diagonals ~60 ns; 4D axis-only ~120 ns (3x Cellular4D). Generic GenT works for axis edges; diagonals need per-dimension offset tables.
master.continuity: C0: a min over a fixed set (fixed per S's window, and the lemma guarantees agreement between windows) of capsule / arc distances, each C0 in S; creases (not C1) on the medial axis between strokes.
master.params: Jitter (constant, 0..0.9), Width (hybrid, clamped to m), Density (hybrid, 0..1 = fraction of edges present), Diagonals enum {None, Hash, Shorter, Delaunay}, Bulge (hybrid, arc sagitta fraction), Node Radius, Width Jitter, Output enum {Distance, LineMask}, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
master.risks:
Edges are 1D objects: any 2D slice of the 3D form or the 4D tileable form shows blobs, not lines, so GenTileable will not look like the 2D node. 3D caves are not prototyped. Straight segments look mechanical unless warped, but a domain warp upstream handles that without a dedicated feature.
[CellularMeshEdges, cell-relations] Jitter must stay < ~0.9 or m becomes tiny and Width is forced thin; the lattice shows through at low jitter (rows/columns of edges). Full-diagonal 3D is expensive. Arc mode: sagitta must obey Width+|sagitta| <= m or seams appear at window boundaries. Needs its own jitter semantics (cannot reuse the ring jitter 0.437 of Cellular at GridJitter=1, margin there is only 0.063).
master.cost_note: Cost estimate AVX2: 2D ~9 ns (2.5x CellularDistance, 8x Perlin); 3D axis-only ~35 ns (3x Cellular3D), full diagonals ~60 ns; 4D axis-only ~120 ns (3x Cellular4D).
master.variant_notes: Distance to hashed edges of the jittered lattice graph. Unjittered axis edges (BondNoise) need no dot products and let Density act as a bond percolation knob. Thin 3D lines slice to dots. LatticeGraph's BondNet rule is credited here.

measured.scalar_note: Measured with defaults, includes 2 perlin2 warp evals and arcs. Without warp and with straight edges 7.93x perlin2, 3.64x worley2. The scalar code skips absent edges; a port pays for all 8.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 2D ~5 ns straight or ~9 ns arcs (9 hashes, 8 edges); 3D ~15 ns with face diagonals (19 hashes, 18 edges), ~6 ns axis only (7 hashes, 6 edges); 4D axis only ~9 ns (9 hashes, 8 edges). Upstream warp is extra.

cellular-circle-packing.look: Dome: pebbles or fish roe in many sizes, large round discs hugged by smaller ones, a mottled dark background with no touching and no overlap. Threshold is a clean disc packing with wide size variation, and the mask at depth 2 with gaps looks like an Apollonian gasket with almost no black. Relief reads as a field of round boulders of different sizes sitting on a low bed, with smaller ones filling between. The 3D volume is a loose heap of separate spheres of several sizes, cut faces orange. FFT is a clean isotropic blob. It is unlike anything on the existing cellular sheet.

dims.2D: works, measured. Disc non-overlap is by construction and matched what the mask shows.
dims.3D: works, measured: inspheres plus homothetic corner spheres on 48 Kuhn tets, jitter capped at 0.33, z-continuity max 0.0159 for dz=1e-3. The catalogue expected to drop corner spheres in 3D; the homothety q=(D-r)/(D+r) about a corner handles them at one sqrt each. The gaps circles exist only in 2D.
dims.4D: not built. 384 simplices to locate, not affordable without the unjittered simplex lattice.

cellular-circle-packing.range: Dome -1.000 .. 1.000 over 8 seeds, mean -0.538, much of the area sits low because small circles are low. Background is exactly -1.
cellular-circle-packing.artifacts: None seen in 2D, including the wide view. axis stat 15.13 in the numbers, but the FFT shows no cross or dots. Thin triangles give tiny incircles, which only adds to the small end of the size range. In 3D a faint regular arrangement can be seen because jitter is capped at 0.33. Dome height is proportional to radius, so the background has many low dots: 3D range only reaches -0.172 on the test slice at unit scale. The SDF's outside part is clamped at (1-J)/2, which is 0.075 at the default, so it is a short range SDF.
cellular-circle-packing.node_shape: CellularCirclePacking: Output enum (Dome, Lens, SDF, Mask, Id), Depth int 0..3, Fill Gaps bool (2D), Jitter float, Gap hybrid, Height float, Profile enum (Pebble, Sphere), Diagonal enum, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
cellular-circle-packing.port_notes: The main saving: every circle lies in its triangle, so Dome, Lens, Mask and Id only need the containing triangle, measured pixel identical (max diff 0) to the full scan in 2D. Locate with max(min(lambda)) and Select 3 corners, as in facet mesh, then do one triangle: 3 sqrt for the side lengths, then per corner 1 sqrt plus gaps with 2 sqrt and 2 unit vectors. Corner circles: q=(D-r)/(D+r), rk=r*q, centre=corner+(I-corner)*q. Depth is a loop on q. Gaps: 1/sqrt(r3)=1/sqrt(r1)+1/sqrt(r2), foot at 2*sqrt(r2*r3) from the corner circle's foot; these do not overlap anything because they lie in a curved triangle gap bounded by mutually tangent shapes. Only SDF needs all 8 triangles. Far coords (4e4) measured std 0.471.
cellular-circle-packing.params_text: out=3,depth=1,gaps=1,jit=0.85,gap=0.94,dome=2.05,prof=1,fast=1 (the code defaults: pebble domes with height proportional to radius). Dense gasket: out=1,depth=2. Equal height: out=4,prof=0. Per circle id: out=2,depth=2. SDF: out=0 (all 8 triangles).

master.one_liner: Non-overlapping circle packing of widely varying radii: incircles of the jittered triangulation plus Apollonian-style corner circles filled in closed form, output as an SDF or per-circle id.
master.look: Pebbles / bubble-wrap / fish-roe: circles of three or four size classes, each large circle hugged by smaller ones in the corners, never overlapping, with triangular gaps that shrink with depth. Completely unlike the Voronoi-based cell looks on the sheet; close to an Apollonian gasket texture or river pebbles.
master.algorithm:
Reuse the 8 candidate triangles of CellularFacetMesh (all circles below lie strictly inside their triangle, so the stroke/clamp lemma holds with Dmax = m: circles in non-candidate triangles are >= m away from the sample's cell).
For each triangle (p0,p1,p2), edge lengths a=|p1-p2|, b=|p2-p0|, c=|p0-p1| (3 sqrt), s2 = a+b+c, twiceArea = |cross(p1-p0,p2-p0)|:
  r = twiceArea / s2 ; I = (a*p0 + b*p1 + c*p2)/s2       // incircle
  out = min(out, |S-I| - r)
  Depth >= 1, for each corner k with unit edge directions u,v from the corner:
     cosA = dot(u,v); sh = sqrt((1-cosA)*0.5)   // sin(alpha/2)
     q = (1-sh)/(1+sh); bis = normalize(u+v)
     rk = r*q ; Ik = p_k + bis*(rk/sh)             // circle tangent to both sides and the incircle
     out = min(out, |S-Ik| - rk)
     Depth 2: rk2 = rk*q ; Ik2 = p_k + bis*(rk2/sh) ; ... (geometric series toward the corner, fixed count)
Shrink: every radius times Gap (0..1) to leave mortar between circles.
Output enum: SDF (clamped at Dmax), Mask (step), Id (hash(T, k, level) of the circle whose SDF is the min; constant per circle).
3D: inspheres of the 48 tets (centre = sum A_i q_i / sum A_i, r = 3V / sum A_i) plus corner spheres (same formula with the solid-angle version is messy; stop at insphere + Gap in 3D).
master.why_new: Existing nodes can only give overlapping discs (F1 threshold) or polygons; a guaranteed non-overlapping multi-scale packing is otherwise a global algorithm (circle packing / Lloyd), here it is closed-form per triangle.
master.simd_plan: FacetMesh geometry (no barycentric needed, ~250 ops) + per triangle 3 sqrt, 1 rcp, incircle ~25 ops; per corner 1 sqrt, 1 rcp, ~25 ops per level. Depth 1: 8*(25 + 3*25) ~ 800 ops + sqrt's -> ~20 ns 2D (5x Cellular2D). Depth 2 ~ 30 ns. 3D insphere-only ~90 ns (dominated by tet enumeration). All fixed loops; min accumulation with Select for the Id output.
master.continuity: C0 (min of circle SDFs over a fixed set); Mask and Id discontinuous by design.
master.params: Jitter, Depth (int 0..3), Gap (hybrid), Output enum {SDF, Mask, Id}, Diagonal enum, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
master.risks: Cost ~5x Cellular; 3D version loses the corner spheres; thin triangles give tiny incircles (use Delaunay diagonal choice and moderate jitter).
master.cost_note: Depth 1: 8*(25 + 3*25) ~ 800 ops + sqrt's -> ~20 ns 2D (5x Cellular2D). Depth 2 ~ 30 ns.

cellular-cluster.look: Polygon foam with a real density contrast: fat bright single cells next to clumps of thin slivers where a parent has 3-5 close points. F1 output shows groups of dark nuclei inside a coarser cell pattern. Value output is per-parent patches with some splinter facets inside; ClusterId alone reads almost like plain CellularValue with slightly uneven borders. Hillshade looks like cut stone with gravel-filled gaps.

dims.3D: works, measured (Eval3, z-continuity max 0.0087 for dz=1e-3)
dims.4D: works, measured on an oblique plane through probe=4

cellular-cluster.artifacts: Walls clip to a flat white top on the large cells (p99 = 1.0), adjustable with wall. Colony slivers are thin spiky triangles at small R rather than little round cells. The axis stat is high (32.8) but the FFT shows radial streaks from straight polygon edges and no lattice cross. Vol at iso -0.45 is scattered pores; colonies are hard to see in that view, the 3D XZ slice in the sheet shows them better.

cellular-cluster.port_notes: 3^D window with M+1 points per cell, inner constant loop, inactive children forced to +inf by Select. Clamp F1 and F2 at Dmax = 1.5 - jitter/2 - R: an unsearched point cannot be nearer, so lattice line crossings stay exact, c0ratio measured 8.0 in 2D and 4D. Child direction in 4D uses two angles and a split. pow() for count and radius can be a table or a square in the port.

master.one_liner: Neyman-Scott point process: each lattice parent spawns 0..M children within radius R that inherit the parent's value; Voronoi/F1/value over the clustered point set gives colonies of small cells inside large empty cells.
master.look: Foam with mixed scales: clumps of 3-5 small cells (colonies) surrounded by big cells, F2-F1 walls dense inside clumps and sparse between, value output coloured per colony with small variations. Looks like lichen, cell cultures, bubbles that gathered, cobbles with gravel. Uniform-density Voronoi on the sheet cannot show density contrast.
master.algorithm:
Window loop as Cellular.inl (coarse lattice, scale 1). Per parent c: hash -> parent position P_c (ring jitter), active child count n_c in 0..M (hash bits), child k (k = 0..M-1, M constant <= 4): offset = R * rnd01(hash(c,k))^Spread * dir(hash(c,k)); C_{c,k} = P_c + offset; active_k = k < n_c.
Point list per cell: parent (always, keeps every cell non-empty) + M children; distance d = |S - X| with inactive children forced to +inf by Select.
Run the standard F1..F4 / value chain over 9*(M+1) points.
Values: child value = parent value + Variation * rnd11(hash(c,k)); parent value = rnd11(hash(c)).
Outputs: all CellularDistance return types and CellularValue (Nth closest), plus 'ClusterId' (parent hash of the nearest point: colonies with jagged borders).
Consistency: children lie within R of the parent; clamp F1 at Dmax = 1 - R and the min over the window is exact. For walls/values, the in-window nearest point must be closer than 1 - R; with the parent always present and GridJitter <= 0.7 this holds except at extreme corners (same class of caveat as Cellular at full jitter).
3D: 27*(M+1) points; 4D: 81*(M+1).
master.why_new: Cell density is constant in every existing cellular node; jitter only moves points inside their cell. Clustering changes the point process, which is a different texture class (and gives parent-inherited values for free).
master.simd_plan: Same 3^D loop with an inner constant loop of M+1 points per cell: 9*(M+1) distance+Select chains. 2D M=2: 27 points ~ 3x Cellular2D (~12 ns); M=4: 45 points ~ 5x (~20 ns). 3D M=2: 81 points ~ 3x Cellular3D (~36 ns). 4D M=2: 243 points ~ 120 ns. Child hashes derived from the parent hash by a cheap xorshift/multiply per k (no extra lattice hashing).
master.continuity: Same as the chosen Cellular output (F1 C0, F2-F1 C0, values discontinuous).
master.params: Children M (int 0..4), Child Probability / Count Jitter, Radius R (hybrid, <= 0.5), Spread (radial distribution exponent), Variation (hybrid), Output enum (Cellular return types + ClusterId), Grid Jitter, Distance Function, Feature Scale.
master.risks: Cost multiplies by M+1; R near 0.5 makes Dmax small. Overlaps CellularHierarchy's ParentValue look (but with density variation instead of nesting).
master.cost_note: 2D M=2: 27 points ~ 3x Cellular2D (~12 ns); M=4: 45 points ~ 5x (~20 ns). 3D M=2: 81 points ~ 3x Cellular3D (~36 ns).

cellular-density.look: Clumps and chains of round domes, big where density is high and small and sparse where it fades, on an exactly flat background: barnacles, rust pitting, or beads. The 4x wide view looks like galaxy clusters, a clearly clustered point process that nothing on the existing sheet has, with a clean isotropic spectrum. F1 output: dark pits on a white plate. F2-F1 output: shattered clusters that look like cracked pebbles. Coverage: clean blobs. The cobbles and gravel recursion gives large smooth stones with small gravel filling only the gaps, and it looks convincing in relief. The volume is a clump of spheres with empty space around it.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3 with density at 27 sites, volume rendered
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path. Dimension agnostic, cost is the only limit.

cellular-density.range: -1.000 .. 1.000 over 8 seeds, mean -0.440. The background sits at exactly -1, so the median is -1 and the threshold panel really thresholds at the plateau.
cellular-density.artifacts: Where two domes overlap there is a crease, which reads as stones pressed together. c0ratio is 5.7 with max slope 76 from steep dome rims; plain coverage 7.9, F2-F1 8.0, recursion 6.8. A pure spherical cap read 2.9, the signature of an infinite rim slope; a small rim softening fixes that. Output out=6 with per-stone heights jumps where stones touch, so it is not a default.

Recursion is graph composition with a coverage output, and cost multiplies, so 3D recursion would need about 730 source evals; use a cheap base density there. Domes need one Sqrt per lane after the search.

Cobbles and gravel: rec=1,out=7,base=0.62,sizef=0,sc=1 with --window 12.

master.one_liner: Worley whose feature points survive with a probability given by a Density source sampled at the point's own position (not at the lane), with optional radius coupled to the same density, so clustered pits, rust pitting, barnacles, pebbles that gather in hollows and size-graded packings fall out of F1/F2/coverage with no popping.
master.look: Patchy point fields: dense clusters of pits fading into clean metal (rust pitting), barnacles crowding one side of a rock, pebbles collecting in hollows of a terrain used as Density, galaxies of clustered specks, and when recursed, cobbles with gravel filling only the gaps. CellularDistance can only jitter a uniform field; the sheet has no clustered or graded point fields.
master.algorithm:
Params: Density (HybridSource, 0..1), SizeFromDensity, BaseRadius, WindowRadius int {1,2}, MaxDistance (plateau), Mode {F1, F2MinusF1, Coverage, NearestValue}, Jitter, DistanceFunction.
Window (2 WindowRadius+1)^d. For each cell j: site c_j, hash h_j, keep_j = rnd01(h_j) < Density(c_j) (Density evaluated at the site, 3^d or 5^d evals; constant hybrid makes it a plain Worley), radius r_j = BaseRadius*(1 + SizeFromDensity*(Density(c_j) - 0.5)); d_j = dist(p, c_j)/r_j; d_j = Select(keep_j, d_j, Large). F1 = min d_j, F2 second min (same insertion as Cellular.inl).
Outputs: F1: min(F1, MaxDistance) scaled (the plateau where no point survives is flat and continuous); F2MinusF1 (cells only among survivors, large empty cells); Coverage = 1 - smoothstep(1-Edge, 1, F1) (dots/pebbles mask); NearestValue = rnd11(h_nearest) with the plateau mapped to a background value.
Recursion: feeding Coverage of a coarse CellularDensity as the Density of a finer one (through 1 - value) gives size-sorted packing: small stones only where there is no large stone; feeding the Coverage of coarse sparse points as Density gives Matern cluster processes (clumps).
master.why_new: Density-dependent presence cannot be built with a graph (masking the output of CellularDistance by a density field cuts cells in half and keeps the empty-region F1 structure); it needs the decision made per point at the point's position. This also corrects the earlier mat_inv ThinSpots sketch, which thresholds against a density sampled at the lane and therefore lets spots appear and vanish as the sample moves.
master.simd_plan: Cellular.inl window loop plus one Source eval per cell at the site position and one Select; 2D cost Worley 3.9 + 9x(Density); 3D 12 + 27x; 4D 41 + 81x (works, tiles, expensive). WindowRadius 2 (25/125 cells) for sparse fields where the plateau would otherwise clip inside visible cells.
master.continuity: C0: presence and radius are per-point constants, F1 is a min of continuous functions, the plateau is a min with a constant. F2MinusF1 is C0 as in CellularDistance. NearestValue is piecewise constant by design.
master.params: Density (hybrid source), SizeFromDensity, BaseRadius, WindowRadius int, MaxDistance, Edge, Mode enum, Jitter, DistanceFunction.
master.risks: Low density plus WindowRadius 1 produces large flat plateaus (intended, but users need the warning); with SizeFromDensity large, points near the window edge can reach the sample (bound r <= 1 cell). Overlaps in concept with StampField(sum/max) fed by a density; the difference is the F1/F2 metric outputs and the fractal-friendly plateau.
master.cost_note: CellularDistance plus one Density eval per cell at the site: 3.9 + 9x Density ns in 2D, 12 + 27x in 3D, 41 + 81x in 4D.

cellular-dual-mesh.look: Stones: irregular polygons with slightly kinked walls, separated by thin dark joints of varying width, each stone with its own height and a gentle tilt, reading at once as crazy paving or a dry stone floor. Relief shows distinct raised slabs with rounded edges and dark grooves. It does not read as Voronoi, because walls bend at edge midpoints and the polygons are rounder. LineMask at density 0.65 gives branching cracks that stop, dead ends and open regions, seen in the density sweep: below 0.5 only isolated squiggles remain, at 0.85 mostly closed cells with occasional gaps. The 3D volume with out=1 is a faceted honeycomb foam of thin walls.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3 on the 48 Kuhn tets, jitter capped at 0.33, z-continuity max 0.0611 for dz=1e-3. Walls use lambda_max-lambda_second, so width is uniform in lambda, not per wall.
dims.4D: not built. 16 hypercubes x 24 simplices is 384 simplices, which is not affordable; a 4D form would have to use the unjittered simplex lattice.

cellular-dual-mesh.range: Stones -1.000 .. 0.955 over 8 seeds, mean 0.106. LineMask -1 .. 1, mean -0.785 at density 0.65. RegionValue -0.999 .. 1.000.
cellular-dual-mesh.artifacts: The 3D form shows the lattice: the XZ slice has a diagonal diamond arrangement of cells and the volume has rows of cells, because jitter is capped at 0.33 and the Kuhn split is the same everywhere. 2D wide view is even and shows no repeat. FFT has faint straight rays at a few angles from the many straight wall segments (axis stat 8.94), and no grid dots. At J=0.8 the win=3 clamp margin is 0.1 cell, so wall half width above 0.08 gets clamped and the distance output is a plateau beyond the margin: this is correct and C0, but WallDistance is a short range output, not a true distance field. win=4 frees that and looked the same as win=3 for LineMask. Max slope is high for thin LineMask (199.6) because its edge is deliberately sharp.

cellular-dual-mesh.port_notes: 3x3 corner window. Four quads with the Delaunay in-circle test and validity crosses, Select the two triangles per quad. Point location by max(min(lambda)) so rounding cannot open cracks. 24 capsule distances, each using a symmetric hash mix(h_a + h_b) so both triangles agree on a wall. Non evaluated strokes are at least m=(1-J)/2 away, so the output clamps at m - maxWidth; that is what makes it seamless. RegionValue and BaryWall skip all strokes and cost about half. Measured far coords (4e4) std 0.445 without NaN. Scalar skips absent walls with a branch; a port evaluates all 24 and uses Select.

master.one_liner: Explicit polygon tiling (centroid dual of the jittered triangulation) where every wall is a real segment with its own hash: per-wall thickness, removal (mazes), and flat per-polygon fill, all C0.
master.look: An irregular polygon tiling resembling Voronoi but with walls kinked at edge midpoints, like hand-cut crazy paving or stone walls. Varying mortar thickness per joint, missing joints that merge stones, and uniform-width walls that F2-F1 cannot give. Density ~0.5 yields organic mazes and 'cracked plate where cracks stop' patterns.
master.algorithm:
Reuse CellularFacetMesh: the 8 candidate triangles T around S (corners within the 3x3 window). For each T compute centroid G_T and the 3 edge midpoints M_ab. The dual cell of a vertex v is the union over its incident triangles of the kite (v, M_va, G_T, M_vb); its walls are the half-segments G_T - M_ab. Every half-segment lies inside its triangle, so the stroke lemma of CellularMeshEdges applies: strokes of half-width w <= m only touch samples whose window holds the triangle; clamp the output at Dmax = m.

Per primal edge ab (unordered pair of lattice cells): he = Hash(min,max) -> present (Density), thickness mul, optional 'height'.
out = Dmax
for each of 8 triangles T, for each of its 3 edges ab:
   d = dist(S, segment(G_T, M_ab)) - Width*thick_ab
   out = min(out, Select(present_ab, d, Dmax))
return ScaleOutput(out, -Width, Dmax)   // or LineMask profile

RegionValue output: inside the containing triangle, owner = argmax lambda_i (that is exactly the centroid-dual partition); value = rnd11(hash(owner cell)) -> flat fill per polygon. Merged regions for maze-like use: when a wall is absent the two polygons are different colours but no stroke separates them (use the stroke output for walls).
Cheap wall output without strokes (used in 3D): W = lambda_max - lambda_second, C0 across triangles since all lambdas are continuous; per-wall width is NOT applied there (see risks).

3D: tets from CellularFacetMesh; walls become polygons around primal edges; use the lambda formulation (W = lambda_max - lambda_second, uniform width) and RegionValue; stroke-based per-wall attributes only in 2D.
master.why_new: The Voronoi dual in FastNoise has no addressable walls: a wall is only the locus F1=F2 and its width varies with angle, and removing walls is discontinuous (shown in notes). Here each wall is a segment with a hash, so width, presence and style are per-wall and continuous.
master.simd_plan: FacetMesh point location (~300 ops) plus 24 capsule distances (~14 ops each) and 16 symmetric pair hashes: ~700 ops total -> ~15 ns 2D (4x Cellular2D). 3D: tet location (~3000 ops) + lambda wall: ~85 ns. Everything is Select-driven; the half-segment list is a compile-time table.
master.continuity: 2D stroke outputs C0 (min of fixed capsule set). BaryWall C0. RegionValue discontinuous (flat fill).
master.params: Jitter, Width (hybrid, <= m), Density (hybrid), Width Jitter, Output enum {WallDistance, LineMask, RegionValue, BaryWall}, Diagonal enum, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
master.risks: Not a true Voronoi (walls are centroid-to-midpoint), which some users may not want; 3D loses per-wall attributes; cost is ~4x Cellular in 2D.
master.cost_note: FacetMesh point location (~300 ops) plus 24 capsule distances (~14 ops each) and 16 symmetric pair hashes: ~700 ops total -> ~15 ns 2D (4x Cellular2D).

cellular-geodesic.look: Territory map whose cells differ a lot in size and shape: large plates beside small lens shaped cells, with strongly curved walls that bend in only some places while others stay nearly straight. More organic and more varied than plain or warped Voronoi: pebbles and leaf shapes, or a political map. Soft dark streaks run inside some cells where F2-F1 stays small along cheap corridors. The 3D volume gives curved shards and chips of varied size with sharp corners.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3 with 27 x M perlin3 taps, volume rendered
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path. The code is dimension agnostic, the cost is the problem.

cellular-geodesic.range: -1.000 .. 1.000 over 8 seeds, mean 0.192. Default output is a border-lined plate map, so the range is set by construction.
cellular-geodesic.artifacts: Dark smears along cheap corridors, from the F2-F1 gap staying small. Without the fade, the 3x3 window has real jumps (c0ratio 1.0 by the offset probe), even though the plain harness probe reads 7.14 and no seams were visible at sheet size. Past cs about 12 the effect saturates, because only the cost ratio matters.
