cellular-geodesic.port_notes: Window loop as Cellular.inl, with M source evals per candidate at fixed fractions of the segment, then one Sqrt and masked min. All candidates pay the full cost, since early out per lane is impossible. Only a cheap source is practical in 3D. A cheaper form that samples cost once per candidate at the midpoint would be worth trying, since M=2 measured 25x and held c0ratio at 7.2, but its look was not viewed. Window fade: one hermite on |v|^2 and one lerp per candidate.
cellular-geodesic.params_text: cs=14,cf=0.6,m=4,src=2,w=0.035,win=1,fade=1,capw=0.35,r0=0.75,out=0 (these are the code defaults). src: 0 perlin, 1 ridged (thin expensive lines), 2 rivers (thin cheap lines), 3 two octaves. out: 0 territories with borders, 1 F1, 2 F2-F1, 3 owner, 4 cost, 5 borders over cost.

master.one_liner: Cellular distance where each candidate's distance is its straight-line length weighted by a cost source integrated along the segment: territories whose borders bend around mountains.
master.look: Voronoi cells that shrink in high-cost regions and swell in low-cost ones; borders are curved, asymmetric and bow away from ridges, so a CellValue map reads as political/biome territories that respect the terrain or follow rivers (cost = ridged noise). F2-F1 cracks become denser in costly regions. Distinct from warped cellular, which bends but never redistributes territory.
master.algorithm:
Same 3^d window, jittered feature points q_j and hash as CellularDistance. Cost C(x) = 1 + CostScale*max(0, S(x)) (or 1 + CostScale*(S+1)/2), S a GeneratorSource.
  for each candidate j (fixed 3^d loop):
      v = q_j - p ; L = |v|
      c = 0 ; for m in 1..M: c += C(p + ((m-0.5)/M)*v)     // M = 2..4 midpoints, fixed
      D_j = L * c / M
      maintain F1, F2 and the winning cell's hash via masked min (as Cellular.inl does)
  Output enum: F1, F2, F2-F1, CellValue (hash of winner), CellIndex, Ratio.
master.why_new: Anisotropic/weighted metrics are impossible by warping (a warp cannot make one cell take land on the far side of a ridge). The midpoint cost integral is the pointwise trick that approximates geodesic distance with a fixed number of source evaluations; gives a 'borders that mean something' map that is otherwise a global shortest-path computation.
master.simd_plan: Reuse Cellular.inl window loop; inner fixed M loop adds M source evals per candidate; everything masked-min. Cost ~ 3^d x M x S + cellular: 2D M=3 Perlin cost: 27 Perlin = ~33 ns (~8x CellularDistance 2D); 3D 81 Perlin3D = ~190 ns; 4D 243 Perlin4D ~ 1 us (4D only with a Value-noise cost or M=1). Window correctness same class as existing jitter caveats; keep CostScale <= ~1 to limit out-of-window winners.
master.continuity: C0 like Worley (min of continuous functions); CellValue piecewise constant by design.
master.params: Cost Source (GeneratorSource), Cost Scale hybrid, Samples M int, Jitter hybrid, Distance Function enum, Return Type enum (F1/F2/F2-F1/Value/Index), Seeded, ScalableGenerator.
master.risks: Expensive in 3D/4D; large CostScale lets far points win and the 3^d window then seams; straight-line integral is only an approximation of geodesic distance (fine for smooth cost at cell scale).
master.cost_note: Cost ~ 3^d x M x S + cellular: 2D M=3 Perlin cost: 27 Perlin = ~33 ns (~8x CellularDistance 2D); 3D 81 Perlin3D = ~190 ns; 4D 243 Perlin4D ~ 1 us (4D only with a Value-noise cost or M=1).

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 38.58x perlin2 at M=4 (1898 ns vs 49.2 ns, 36 source evals); 25.19x at M=2 (1256 ns, measured before the fade); 29.74x at M=3 with plain perlin cost (1506 ns, before the fade)
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D about 45 ns at M=4 on a Perlin cost (36 x 1.1 + cellular 3.9); 3D about 245 ns (108 x 2.2 + 12) at M=4; 4D is about 1.4 us at M=4 or 350 ns at M=1, which needs a cheaper cost

cellular-hex-lattice.look: At jitter 0, a perfect honeycomb. At 0.12 slightly irregular hexes, like basalt column tops. At 0.25, the default, organic polygons of very even size with no rows and no small cells; hillshade reads as cobbled paving or a basalt pavement with raised rounded slabs, and threshold shows a stone path layout. The wide view is an even mottling with no visible repeat or row. 3D Kelvin foam at jitter 0 is exactly the classic honeycomb of hexagon and square faces, and at 0.2 it becomes a believable irregular foam with thin flat walls. The XZ slice shows rounded polygon cells mixed with small squares from the BCC square faces.

dims.2D: works, measured: hexagonal, 7 candidates, cube round
dims.3D: works, measured: BCC, two sublattices, 16 candidates, z-continuity max 0.0136 for dz=1e-3. vol_kelvin shows real truncated octahedra.
dims.4D: works, measured on an oblique plane (slice4=1): D4, two sublattices, 32 candidates, c0ratio 7.89, range -1 .. 0.999. I used D4 rather than the catalogue's A4*: it needs no sort and packs better, and the code is the same GenT as 3D. Tiling itself not tested.

cellular-hex-lattice.range: Pillows -1.000 .. 1.000 over 8 seeds, mean 0.021. F1 is normalised by the spacing, 3D range -0.984 .. 0.566.
cellular-hex-lattice.artifacts: At low jitter the lattice is the look, on purpose. FFT has strong straight rays and a six fold star (axis 23.30). A slice through BCC at jit=0.2 still has a recognisable pattern of big and small cells. Brute force bound check against a wide search: 2D with 7 candidates: F1 no error up to jit 0.35, 0.0075% wrong at 0.45 (worst 0.108); F2-F1 no error up to 0.35, 0.0273% at 0.40; edge no error up to 0.29, which matches the catalogue's 0.289, 0.0020% at 0.35. shell=2 with 13 candidates: F1 no error even at 0.45. 3D with 16 candidates: F1 no error up to 0.40; F2-F1 no error up to 0.25; edge no error up to 0.20, 0.0033% at 0.25, 0.0567% at 0.40. 4D with 32 candidates: F1 no error up to 0.40. Sample counts: 200000 and 150000 in 2D, 30000 to 100000 in 3D, 12000 to 15000 in 4D, so rare errors could still exist at these limits. Non Euclidean metrics are not tested.
cellular-hex-lattice.node_shape: A Lattice enum (Square, Hex/BCC/D4) on the existing Cellular nodes rather than a new node, with Grid Jitter documented as a fraction of spacing and clamped at 0.29 in 2D and 0.2 in 3D and 4D for exact edge outputs, or 0.35-0.4 for F1. It needs the edge distance output to show its best look; that output is cellular-edge-distance. Return Types as CellularDistance, Euclidean only.
cellular-hex-lattice.port_notes: 2D: axial coords, cube round branch free via Select on the largest rounding error, constant table of 6 offsets. 3D and 4D: for sublattice s in {0,1}: floor(p/a - s/2), corners by bit test; the second sublattice hashes with a different seed. a = 2^(1/3) and 2^(1/4) for unit density. The same code handles both dims, so a generic pack works. Candidates are stored for the edge pass. FastNoise's shell jitter (jmode=1) avoids the pow; its look at the same radius was not viewed. Far coords (4e4) std 0.536.
cellular-hex-lattice.params_text: out=4,jit=0.25,jit3=0.2,shell=1,jmode=0,base=0.45 (the code defaults: Pillows, jitter as a fraction of the nearest neighbour spacing; 3D and 4D capped at jit3). Perfect honeycomb: jit=0. Kelvin foam: out=5,wall=0.04,jit=0. Irregular foam: out=5,wall=0.05. Edge: out=3,jit=0.15. Cracks: out=1,jit=0.29. Square lattice reference: cube=1.

queue.name: CellularHexLattice
queue.reason: Honeycomb, BCC and A4* candidate tables save up to 2.5x in 4D at low jitter (J4 top pick). Hex 2D alone justifies a Lattice enum.

master.one_liner: Cellular on A_d* lattices (hex, BCC, A4*): honeycomb, basalt columns and Kelvin foam at low jitter, with fewer candidates than the cubic window in 3D and 4D.
master.look: Prototype cl_cell modes 7, 8. j=0: perfect honeycomb and hex tile; j=.15: basalt column tops, irregular hex; j=.29: organic polygons but much more even in size than the jittered square grid. Hillshade with exact edge distance gives crystal-pyramid hexes. BCC slices would show Kelvin-cell (truncated octahedron) foam.
master.algorithm:
2D: axial coords q=x-y/sqrt3, r=2y/sqrt3; cube-round to nearest lattice point (branch free via Select on largest rounding error); candidates = self + 6 neighbours (Voronoi-relevant vectors). Site = lattice point + jitter in a disc of radius j. Worst-case bound j<=(|2nd shell|-2Rc)/2 = .289 at spacing 1.
3D BCC: two offset cubic lattices; pick nearer of Round(x) and Round(x-.5)+.5; candidates = self + 8 at (+-.5,+-.5,+-.5) + 6 axis = 15; j<=.148 at cube size 1 (~.186 at unit density).
4D A4*: nearest point by the Conway-Sloane rank method, a sorting network in masks; 30 relevant vectors plus self = 31 (permutohedron has 2^(d+1)-2 facets).
Then usual F1 and value logic. Edge distance works with the same candidates.

[CentredLattice (BCC/D4 cellular and kernel windows), lattice-kernels] Lattice = union of Z^dim and Z^dim + (1/2,...,1/2) (scaled so nearest-neighbour distance is 1: in 3D this is BCC, in 4D D4* (a lattice whose Voronoi cell is the 24-cell), in 2D the centred square, which is just a rotated square, so 2D uses offset rows instead: point (i,j) at (i + 0.5*(j&1), j*sqrt(3)/2), window i-1..i+1, j-1..j+1 = 9 points but hexagonal cells).
3D/4D Gen(p): for sublattice s in {0,1}: ps = p - 0.5*s; c = floor(ps); for each of the 2^dim corners o: q = c + o + 0.5*s + Jitter*(rndvec(hash(seed, c+o, s))-0.5)*JitterScale; evaluate the candidate (distance for cellular, kernel for StrokeNoise/Multipole/Pebble...).
Jitter bound: with Jitter <= 0.5 (in sublattice cell units) every point whose unjittered Voronoi cell could contain p is one of the 2^dim corners of its sublattice cube, so F1 is exact; above that the same rare-seam tolerance as today's jitter 1 applies.
Hash includes the sublattice bit (seed ^ s*PrimeW or an extra prime) so the two sublattices are independent.
master.why_new: Low jitter square-lattice Cellular exposes a square grid, so the regular-but-organic foam look is unavailable. A domain shear in a graph distorts the distance metric. The survey cites more densely packed lattices (Wyvill & Novins) as reducing directional artifacts. Worley explicitly warned that jittered lattices leave odd patterns.
master.simd_plan:
2D: 7 cells + cube round ~3.5 ns vs 3.9. 3D: 15 cells ~7 ns vs 12. 4D: 31 cells + sort ~16 ns vs 41, a 2.5x saving and the best way to cheap tiling cells. Candidates are a fixed constant table of offsets, so loop count is constant.
[CentredLattice (BCC/D4 cellular and kernel windows), lattice-kernels] Two sublattice passes of 2^dim corners: the existing per-candidate code is reused; window loops change from 3^dim to 2 x 2^dim. 2D offset-row form needs (j&1) parity via an integer AND and a per-row x shift. Branch-free. Cost 2D ~same as today (9 candidates), 3D ~0.6x, 4D ~0.4x of current Cellular.
master.continuity: F1 C0 (c0ratio 8.00), edge distance C0 (8.00). Jitter is bounded for correctness; the 2D prototype used a box of +-.289 (corner radius .41 exceeds the disc bound), with no visible seams, but a disc or box of +-.2 is the safe spec.
master.params: Hybrid: Grid Jitter (clamped to the bound). Enum: same return types and distance functions as CellularDistance. Could be a Lattice enum on Cellular<>.
master.risks:
Cost saving exists only at low jitter; matching full-random look needs the second shell (13 in 2D, 27 in 3D), no gain. The bound looks unintuitive to users (scaled 0-1 jitter hides that). Only the 2D form was prototyped, and the 3D, 4D bounds are hand derivations. Non-Euclid metrics break the shell argument. F2 needs more shells.
[CentredLattice (BCC/D4 cellular and kernel windows), lattice-kernels] Jitter above 0.5 reintroduces seams more readily than the 3^dim square window; the lab must brute-force-check F1 exactness vs jitter. 2D offset-row hex has a different jitter geometry from 3D BCC (two code paths). Many users will see 'hex worley' as known; the value is speed in 3D/4D plus foam shapes.
merged_from: #163 CentredLattice (BCC/D4 cellular and kernel windows) (lattice-kernels, fable)
master.cost_note: 2D: 7 cells + cube round ~3.5 ns vs 3.9. 4D: 31 cells + sort ~16 ns vs 41, a 2.5x saving and the best way to cheap tiling cells.
master.variant_notes: Could be a Lattice enum on existing Cellular nodes. Candidates: 7/15/31 at low jitter via Voronoi-relevant vectors, or the two-sublattice 8/16/32 form. Hand-derived jitter bounds need a brute-force check.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 96.2 ns vs perlin2 51.4 (Pillows with edge pass). F1 alone 82.7 ns, 1.62x. With shell jitter on both, F1 measured 81.7 ns against 80.8 ns for the square 3x3 reference, so 2D saves nothing, as the cube round costs what the 2 fewer candidates save. 3D F1 with shell jitter 211.5 ns vs square 238.2 ns, 0.89x. 4D F1 with shell jitter 363.0 ns vs square 3^4 587.9 ns, 0.62x. Pillows 3D 367.7 ns, 7.05x, and 4D 707.4 ns, 14.13x, both with the uniform ball jitter, which uses a pow per site.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured on SIMD: about 4 ns 2D, about 8-11 ns 3D, about 20-25 ns 4D for F1, against the handbook's Cellular 3.9 / 12 / 41. Scalar saving was smaller than the candidate ratio (16/27 = 0.59, 32/81 = 0.40) because hashing and two floor passes do not scale down.
measured.c0_note: Pillows 7.90, F1 8.00, 3D oblique plane 7.81, 4D oblique plane 7.89. CellValue 1.00 by design.

cellular-metric-field.look: Ellipse with F2-F1: plump elongated pebbles and leaf shapes with curved walls, each pointing its own way, with a bright streak inside each cell along its long axis. Viewed at asp 1.8 in a grid panel and at asp 2 on a full sheet; the sheet at the final 1.8 was not checked by eye. Ellipse F1: streaky stars. Owner plates: rounded curved stones. Polygon F1: star faceted pyramids, low-poly pits with sharp creases in hillshade and relief, unlike anything on the existing sheet. Polygon plates: angular walls with kinks. The volume at asp 1.8: chunky flattened rock fragments with curved faces. Field alignment at asp 2.6 is only moderate: cells lean together locally but do not form flow bundles, and it shows hard window corners there.

dims.3D: works, measured: ellipse as d^2 = |v|^2 + B (v.n)^2 with no frame needed, volume rendered. Polygon with tetra, cube and octa normals runs and passes check (z-continuity max 0.0024), but only its 2D image was viewed.
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path. The ellipse form is dimension agnostic.

cellular-metric-field.range: -1.000 .. 1.000 over 8 seeds with out=1, mean -0.152, clipped by construction. Polygon F1 with out=0 was -0.998 .. 0.957 before the fade.
cellular-metric-field.artifacts: Without the fade, the 3x3 window has real jumps at every aspect tried from 1.2 up (c0ratio 1.0 by the offset probe), and at asp 2 the sheet shows a few short straight notches in F2-F1 and an axis cross in the FFT, while the plain harness probe still reads 8.0. F2 mismatch against 5x5 without the fade: asp 1.8 1.1%, asp 2 2.0%, asp 3 7.2%, F1 mismatch 0.8% to 1.6% at asp 3. Plain Cellular at aspect 1 reads 8.0, so the jumps come from the metric. The fade removes the jumps at any aspect by the probe, but the look of the faded version at high aspect was not viewed.
cellular-metric-field.node_shape: Members on Cellular, or CellularMetricField : Generator. Metric enum {Ellipse, Polygon}, Anisotropy (hybrid, document limit 1.8 at full jitter), Rotation Spread (0 aligned, 1 random), Angle (hybrid, optional), Size Jitter, Grid Jitter (hybrid), Return Type enum.
cellular-metric-field.port_notes: Ellipse: one extra hashed direction, one dot and one FMA per candidate, reusable from the jitter direction bits. Polygon: per-site N by hash bits needs a max over the largest N with masks, or a 16 entry direction table; 3D needs a rotation table. Field aligned costs one source eval per candidate, so keep it an option. Window fade: one hermite on |v|^2 and one lerp per candidate, or a plain Min where the metric equals Euclid.
cellular-metric-field.params_text: metric=0,asp=1.8,out=1,field=0,jit=1,win=1,fade=1,capw=0.25,r0=0.85 (these are the code defaults, F2-F1 pebbles). Polygon crystal look: metric=1,out=0. Field aligned: field=1,ff=0.15,asp=2.6.

master.one_liner: Each site carries its own elliptical metric, so bisectors become curved conics and cells become leaves, flames and pebbles, optionally all aligned to a hybrid angle.
master.look:
Ellipse: leaf, feather, pebble, stretched grain with curved cell boundaries. Polygon: star-faceted crystal pyramids; hillshade looks like low-poly crystal. Prototyped both: visibly different from isotropic and global-metric Cellular variants on the sheet.
[CellularMetricField, lit-classic] Prototype cl_cell modes 5, 6. Asp 1.6: curved, plump pebble cells with bowed walls, like river stones or dried clay. Asp 3-4 (5x5): lens or blade cells, overlapping like bark or feathers. Aligned Angle field: elongated cells following a flow, like wood cross grain, muscle, or stretched bark.
[CellularMetricJitter, cell-relations] Cellular Manhattan on the sheet is rigidly axis-aligned; rotating each cell's metric turns it into a shattered mosaic of rotated squares/diamonds overlapping like crystals grown with independent orientation (F1 shows rotated pyramids, F2-F1 shows angular zigzag walls). Aspect gives elongated ellipse-ish cells whose walls are conic arcs (curved), aligned by a source field: fish scales following a flow, tension cracks. Twist makes pinwheel cells whose iso-lines are squares rotating with radius.
master.algorithm:
For window points: u = R(h)*v (per-point rotation from a table). Metric Ellipse: d = sqrt(u.x^2 + (A*u.y)^2 [+...]), A>=1 so d>=|v|. Metric Polygon: d = K_N * max_k dot(u, n_k), per-point N=3,4,5,6 chosen by masks (3D: tetra, cube, octa normals). Multiply by per-point size. F1 (optional F2, index value). Output F1, value of winner, or F2-F1. Polygon metric gives a piecewise linear heightfield.

[CellularMetricJitter, cell-relations] Window loop as Cellular.inl. Per window point c: v = S - P_c.
  theta_c = Rotation*rnd01(hash bits)*2pi, or theta from Angle hybrid sampled at P_c (coherent orientation field); (cos,sin) from the 256-entry table (or reuse the jitter direction vector as the rotation frame: free).
  Twist: theta += Twist * |v|   (needs FS::Sin/Cos per point; only matters for non-Euclid or stretched metrics)
  v' = R(theta) v ; v'' = (v'.x / a_c, v'.y * a_c) with a_c = Aspect*(1 + AspectJitter*rnd11)
  d_c = DistanceFunction(v'')   (reuse CalcDistance: Euclid, Manhattan, MaxAxis/Chebyshev, Minkowski)
then the usual F1..F4 / value selection, ReturnType, etc. (this is a drop-in extension of the Cellular base: 'Metric Rotation Jitter', 'Aspect', 'Twist').
3D: rotation from a 256-entry random rotation matrix table (9 fmadd per point), aspect along the rotated x axis; twist about the rotated z axis.
Consistency: metric ratio rho = max stretch (sqrt(2) for Chebyshev vs Euclid, a^2 for aspect a). The in-window minimum is guaranteed only when rho * (nearest in-window Euclid distance) < 1 + margin; practically seamless for Aspect <= 1.5 with GridJitter <= 0.7; a Wide Window option (5x5, 2D only) removes the limit at 2.8x cost.
master.why_new: DomainAxisScale applies one stretch to all cells and keeps boundaries straight. Size Jitter gives circular weights. Per-site anisotropy gives curved walls and coherent elongation following a field, which no graph can produce because metric selection happens inside the search.
master.simd_plan: +1 dot, +2 FMA, +1 hashed direction per candidate inside the existing 3^dim loop: ~1.15x CellularDistance in all dimensions, same window. 2D direction via sin/cos poly of a bounded angle or via a 16-entry direction table indexed by hash bits (permute on AVX2). Branch-free.
master.continuity: F1 C0 at Asp 1.6 (c0ratio 8.00, no visible seams). At Asp 3 in a 3x3 window, rectangular seams are clearly visible; they disappear at 5x5.
master.params: Metric enum, Anisotropy (hybrid), Rotation Spread (0 aligned, 1 random, or from a hybrid angle), Size Jitter, Grid Jitter, return type enum.
master.risks:
Aspect limit is tight with 3^d; users will push past it. F2 suffers before F1. Output range shifts with Asp. Bisectors are not exact when Asp differs between sites, but that is the look. 3D not prototyped.
[CellularMetricJitter, cell-relations] Window inconsistency at high anisotropy (needs the 5x5 option or a clamp); per-cell rotation of a Euclid metric without aspect/twist is a no-op (document). Rotated Chebyshev F2-F1 walls are polylines, not smooth.
[ShapedCellular, stamp-scatter] The Jitter clamp reduces randomness at high anisotropy; document. Polygon metric with per-cell rotation needs the direction table rotated per cell (n rotations per cell). Superellipse Pow cost in 3D/4D.
master.cost_note: +1 dot, +2 FMA, +1 hashed direction per candidate inside the existing 3^dim loop: ~1.15x CellularDistance in all dimensions, same window.
master.variant_notes: Per-site rotated, stretched or polygonal metric. Window limit found by test: aspect about 1.8 fits 3x3, aspect 3 shows clear seams until 5x5. A hybrid Angle gives field-aligned cells; Twist needs Sin/Cos per candidate. Could become members on Cellular.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 8.85x perlin2 (444.9 ns vs 50.3 ns) for random per-site ellipse; 23.56x with field=1 (one perlin per candidate, 1175 ns); 18.31x polygon metric (911.7 ns, scalar loops of sin and cos that a table would replace)
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: ellipse 2D about 4.5 ns, 3D about 14 ns, 4D about 47 ns (1.15x CellularDistance). Field aligned adds 9, 27 or 81 source evals. Polygon about 8 ns in 2D with a normal table.

cellular-relaxed.look: Even polygon cells with no tiny slivers and no visible rows; threshold looks like dried mud or giraffe skin with walls of nearly equal width, and hillshade shows even roof shaped cells. The wide view is a uniform weave. In a side by side at window 12, plain J1 has obvious tiny cells beside big ones, plain J.7 is more even but its rows show, and relaxed J1 keeps the irregular layout while removing the small cells. That is a real gain but moderate, you have to compare to see it. The 3D volume at iso -0.65 is a tight pack of irregular polyhedral blocks with thin gaps and no visible lattice.

dims.3D: works, measured: 125 hash block, nb3=6 used for the volume, z-continuity max 0.0032 for dz=1e-3. Cost is the flaw.
dims.4D: not built. 625 hashes and 81 x 8 or more terms is far over the budget, the catalogue's 300 ns guess is optimistic against 3D's measured cost.

cellular-relaxed.range: Edge distance output -1.000 .. 1.000, mean -0.464 over 8 seeds; far coords max 0.788. The scale constant is a chosen 3.2, so typical maximum is below 1.
cellular-relaxed.artifacts: Measured in 2D at J1, with sites computed in a large block: plain NN p05 0.275, NN cv 0.336, cell area cv 0.243, smallest cell 0.146 of the mean. Relaxed NN p05 0.638, cv 0.135, area cv 0.154, smallest 0.576. Plain J.7 for reference: p05 0.463, cv 0.219, area cv 0.173, smallest 0.472. So one relaxed step beats lowering jitter to 0.7 on every number. Relax strength matters: relax 0.6 at R 1.05 overshoots and collapses pairs (NN min 0.016) and looks no better; the catalogue's inverse distance kernel peaks at NN p05 0.523, area cv 0.192. A second frozen iteration with relax 0.2 gave area cv 0.146, no clear gain. Window exactness is unchanged: against an 81 site reference, F1 wrong at 0.0003% of samples (worst 0.012), F2 0.0100% (worst 0.218), edge 0.0223% (worst 0.126); plain J1 is 0.0003%, 0.0143%, 0.0353%. Prune window exactness was not measured, and with 0.36 sites per cell at R=1 the 3x3 window is thin, so jumps are possible there. Not a real blue noise spectrum: the FFT has straight rays from the polygon walls and no clean ring.
cellular-relaxed.node_shape: CellularRelaxed: as CellularDistance plus Relax hybrid (0..0.4 useful), Relax Radius float, Max Displacement float, Grid Jitter hybrid; Return Type includes Edge Distance. Better shipped as a Relax param on the existing Cellular nodes than as a separate node, with a Neighbours enum for 3D.
cellular-relaxed.port_notes: Hash a 5^D block, 25 in 2D. For each of the 3^D candidates, a fixed loop over its neighbours with a compact kernel t*t/|r|, t=max(0,1-r2/R2), then clamp the displacement. All inputs to a candidate's displacement are its own neighbours, so every sample agrees. Avoid the sqrt with an approximate InvSqrt. The kernel is zero beyond R, but a SIMD port pays for every term anyway. 3D nb3=6 needs only 27 + 54 hashes. Far coords (4e4) std 0.373.
cellular-relaxed.params_text: kind=0,relax=0.3,radius=1.3,maxdisp=0.45,jit=1,out=3,iters=1 (the code defaults: compact repulsion, edge distance output). Cracks: out=1. Prune: kind=2,radius=1. Catalogue's inverse distance kernel: kind=1,relax=0.1. Cheaper 3D: nb3=6.

master.one_liner: One pointwise repulsion/Lloyd-style relaxation step on the jittered feature points before the distance test, giving blue-noise cells of uniform size without grid alignment.
master.look:
Repel: even skin or honeycomb-like cells with few tiny slivers and no grid. Prune: larger, airier cells, usable as guaranteed non-overlapping stamps, for tree or boulder placement. Prototyped: rel_relax, mode=0,1,2. The difference from plain jitter is real but subtle in repel mode and stronger in prune mode.
[CellularRelaxed, dynamics-iteration] Evenly sized, evenly spaced cells: foam, basalt columns, reptile scales, honeycomb-like but still irregular; F2-F1 cracks of uniform width and spacing, F1 bubbles of equal size. Existing CellularDistance at low jitter regularises but shows the grid; at jitter 1 it clumps. This is the 'centroidal Voronoi' look in one node.
master.algorithm:
Hash window 5^d (2-ring) of feature points q (jitter as usual), candidates = inner 3^d.
  for each candidate c (fixed loop):
      disp = 0
      for each n in c's own 3^d neighbourhood, n != c (fixed loop, all inside the 5^d window):
          r = q_c - q_n ; disp += r / (dot(r,r) + eps)     // inverse-distance repulsion
      disp *= Relax ; disp *= min(1, MaxDisp / (|disp| + 1e-9))  // clamp so points stay inside their cell
      q_c' = q_c + disp
  Then the usual F1/F2/CellValue/Index over q_c'.
Optional Iterations 2 with frozen neighbours (Jacobi approximation, no bigger window).

[ShyPoints, cell-relations] Raw point q_c from hash. Repel: p_c=q_c+sum over 8 (or 6 in 3D) neighbours n of K*max(0,R^2-|q_c-q_n|^2)^2*unit(q_c-q_n). Prune: c is dead if any neighbour n has |q_c-q_n|<r and h_n>h_c (a local rule, so independent of evaluation order; survivors are guaranteed at least r apart). Then normal F1/F2/value over relaxed or surviving points with dead cells' distance forced large.
master.why_new: Point-set relaxation is normally a global iterative process; computing each candidate's one relaxation step from its own neighbourhood (available via the 2-ring hash window) makes it stateless. Makes a hard thing (uniform cells) a parameter.
master.simd_plan: Hashes only for the 2-ring (cheap), then 3^d x (3^d - 1) repulsion terms, each a sub, dot, Reciprocal and FMA; then the standard distance pass. Cost 2D: 25 hashes + 72 terms + 9 dists = ~4x CellularDistance 2D (~15 ns). 3D: 125 hashes + 702 terms = ~10x (~120 ns). 4D: 81x80 terms is too much; use only the 2d axis neighbours in 4D (81x8 = 648 terms, ~300 ns) and say so. Consistency across samples holds because each candidate's displacement depends only on its own 1-ring.
master.continuity: C0 for F1/F2 (positions are smooth functions of hashes and the min is continuous); CellValue piecewise constant.
master.params: Relax hybrid, MaxDisp float, Jitter hybrid, Iterations int (1..2), Distance Function enum, Return Type enum, plus Cellular's existing params.
master.risks:
3D/4D cost; clamping is needed to keep the 3^d candidate window correct (MaxDisp <= (1 - Jitter)/2 cell), so strong relaxation needs lower jitter; one step is only an approximation of CVT (good enough visually).
[ShyPoints, cell-relations] Visual gain over jitter is modest in Repel mode. Prune needs a wider F1 window, and 3D gets very expensive. A single step does not produce a real blue-noise spectrum (not measured).
master.cost_note: Cost 2D: 25 hashes + 72 terms + 9 dists = ~4x CellularDistance 2D (~15 ns). 3D: 125 hashes + 702 terms = ~10x (~120 ns).
master.variant_notes: ShyPoints reports the visual gain over jitter is modest in Repel mode and stronger in Prune mode.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 313.9 ns vs perlin2 49.5 (2.77x the 5x5 worley2). inverse kernel 148.0 ns, 2.99x, cheaper only because the scalar compact kernel has a sqrt. Prune 277.6 ns, 5.52x. 3D with 26 neighbours 3705.7 ns, 74.04x; 3D with 6 axis neighbours 1475.2 ns, 28.13x. These are not reduced by relax=0, since the loop still runs.

cluster-cellular.look: Black ground with small round spots forming readable macro shapes: dotted rings, open arcs, short straight trails and tight clumps, plus a thin scatter of lone spots. Reads as fairy rings, constellations, debris rings. The 3D XZ slice shows clumps and partial rings. levels=2 at the two settings tried was only faint specks with no readable second-level clustering, so that part of the idea is not shown to work.

dims.3D: works, measured (shells and balls of spots; a slice shows only partial rings)
dims.4D: runs and is continuous on an oblique plane through probe=4, spots are rare in the slice, mean -0.993

cluster-cellular.artifacts: Parents sit on rows: in the main view and the 4x view the clusters line up along the coarse lattice, because the parent jitter must stay small for rings to fit inside a parent cell (pjit=0.18 of the cell). Mean -0.95, most of the field is flat floor, so it is a mask or a stamp layer more than a noise. Max slope 62 per unit because the spots are small in the default framing. out=2 F1 measured c0ratio 8.00 after fixing a first version that jumped at spot rims. Scalar speed mode=1 3.02x, levels=2 2.71x perlin; levels=2 is cheaper because most parents die before the shape code.

cluster-cellular.port_notes: 3^D child candidates, each one child hash plus one parent hash from an integer floor division by Ratio. The window function (1-t^2)^2 replaces exp, so no Exp op is needed. Alive is a pure function of the child point, so C0 held at 7.9 in every dimension. Reach limit: spot radius below 1.5 - jitter/2 child cells. Parent regularity needs a real fix before a port: options are a smaller Spread with larger parent jitter, or a shifted second parent lattice.
cluster-cellular.params_text: ratio=14,fine=10,mode=4,rad=0.8,rjit=0.4,jit=0.9,spread=0.27,sjit=0.3,width=0.045,pjit=0.18,pdens=0.72,bg=0.025 (these are the defaults; mode=1 only rings, mode=0 blobs, mode=2 arcs, mode=3 trails)

master.one_liner: Spots arranged by macro shape (clumps, fairy rings, arcs, trails) with a single parent-cell lookup per child, so 2x hash cost whatever the number of children.
master.look:
Prototype at ratio 10 in a 28-unit window: clear rings of small spots (fairy rings, atolls, meteor debris rings); at blob mode, tight clumps with large empty spaces, i.e. star clusters, mushrooms, pox, rock outcrops. Prototype with too small a ratio was merely sparse, so the shape requires ratio >= 8.
[ClusterCellular, hierarchy-multiscale] Voronoi cells of 2-3 discrete size classes where the small cells appear only in clusters around a parent, and clusters themselves cluster: archipelagos with islets around main islands, settlements with hamlets around towns, galaxy groups, lichen/mould colonies, foam with daughter bubbles. Kernel mode gives dotted clumps at nested scales. Distinct from CellularDistance (uniform size) and from a density-controlled Voronoi (smoothly varying size): sizes are quantised and spatially clustered.
master.algorithm:
Fine lattice for children, coarse parent lattice with integer Ratio. For each of the 3^dim child candidates: parent cell P = floor(childCell/Ratio) with exactly one parent hash (not a window of parents). Parent centre Cp = (P+0.5)*Ratio + small jitter (<20%), spread S = Spread*rnd(parent). Survival probability from child feature position c: d = |c-Cp|. Blob: exp(-d^2/S^2). Ring: exp(-(d-S)^2/Width^2). Arc: ring times angular window from dot(unit(c-Cp),dir). Trail: distance to a parent-hash segment. Decision: alive = rnd(child) < prob(d). Requires S + 2*Width < Ratio/2 - jitter so clusters cannot cross parent bounds, otherwise clipped. Alive is a pure function of the feature, so no sample-dependent pops. Value = max or sum of alive bump(|p-c|/r). Generalises: any analytic parent shape can drive child placement.

[ClusterCellular, hierarchy-multiscale] Levels K (default 3), spacing s_k = s_0 / Lacunarity^k. Point of level k in cell c: pos = (c + 0.5 + jitter(h)*Jitter) * s_k, h = HashPrimes(k, c). Activity:
  active_0 = true (top level always on -> bounded search)
  active_k(pos) = (rnd01(h) < Fill_k) & (|pos - parentPos| < Radius * s_{k-1}) & active_{k-1}(parentPos)
  where parentPos is the level-(k-1) point of the cell floor(pos / s_{k-1}); the chain is unrolled k times (k hashes).
  Per-cell count variant: each cell holds up to 4 candidate points, candidate j active iff j < count(h) with count geometric (P(count>=j)=CountKeep^j); inactive candidates get distance +inf via Select.
  Search: for each level k, 3^D window around floor(p/s_k): for each cell, for each candidate: d = |pos - p| / (s_k * SizeWeight^k) if active else +inf; keep F1 (and F2, nearest hash) across all levels.
Outputs: Distance (F1, normalised by level spacing so clusters of small cells read as small cells), Value (rnd11 of nearest hash), Level (k of nearest, as discrete value), Kernel = sum over active points of (1 - d)^2 clamped (soft blobs, galaxies), F2-F1 (cell walls).
master.why_new: Jittered grids give even coverage, and a Density source would need one eval per child and cannot draw thin rings cheaply. Point patterns with heavy clumping (a Neyman-Scott process) have no node at present, and a spatial arrangement at two scales cannot be made from a graph because alive is a per-feature property.
master.simd_plan: Per candidate: child hash + parent hash (integer floor division by Ratio, or float floor) + exp or polynomial approx of prob. 2D ~2x CellularDistance = 8 ns. 3D ~25 ns. 4D ~85 ns. Replace exp with a rational window to lower cost.
master.continuity: C0 for mask reaching zero inside the 3-cell reach. Per-feature decisions cannot create sample-space jumps; only hard clipping at parent boundaries is possible, avoided by the S bound.
master.params: Ratio (int), Mode enum (Blob/Ring/Arc/Trail), Spread, Spread Jitter, Ring Width, Child Radius, Parent Density, Child Density, Background
master.risks:
Parent lattice can show periodic arrangement at Ratio spacing because parents sit near cell centres with limited jitter. Large empty regions affect normalisation and mean. Constraint between Spread and Ratio is awkward for artists; expose Spread as a fraction of Ratio.
[ClusterCellular, hierarchy-multiscale] Cost grows with Levels; keep K<=3. Parent lookup uses the parent cell containing the child, so children near a parent-cell edge whose parent point sits across the edge are missed (slight anisotropy, invisible in practice).
master.cost_note: 2D ~2x CellularDistance = 8 ns. 3D ~25 ns.
master.variant_notes: Child survival decided per feature from a parent lattice. ClusterScatter draws macro shapes (rings, arcs, trails); ClusterCellular nests levels.

conic-cells.look: Overlapping feathers or fish scales: each cell is a long scale with a pit at its root, a smooth back and a crisp lip where the next scale overlaps. With the hybrid wind the scales turn across the field and the 4x wide view looks like a school of fish or a feather pattern swirling around, which is the most striking panel. In hillshade the default terrain colouring makes it look like peacock eyes. Rings give ringed eggs. The relief reads as a scaled surface. The 3D slice shows rounder cells because the XZ slice is mostly across the wind. The volume is packed eggs pointing one way.

dims.3D: works, measured: unit wind with wz=0.3, volume rendered as egg shaped solids all pointing one way
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path. The metric is dimension agnostic. Tiling needs a 4D wind vector.

conic-cells.range: -0.965 .. 0.999 over 8 seeds, mean -0.144, at the default out=5 with the analytic norm.
conic-cells.artifacts: A few thin bright creases near lips where the wind turns fast. The spectrum is deliberately anisotropic (axis 21.6). With flow=0 the output at e=0.65 and catalogue shift 0.6 showed c0ratio 36, a seam signature with max T error 0.046: the catalogue's claim of a perfect match at shift 0.6 did not hold over a wider view.

conic-cells.port_notes: Only the distance changes: Sqrt(|v|^2) minus e times dot(v, w), plus a per-lane window offset by Round(p - 1.2 e w). Wind angle needs Sin and Cos once per lane, or a vector source. No extra source evals besides the wind. Window offset rounding per lane is free in the existing loop since it only changes the integer base. Window fade with a hybrid wind: one hermite and one lerp per candidate, on the distance to the shifted window centre. A constant wind does not need it: it read 8.0 without the fade.

master.one_liner: Voronoi with a wind-biased eccentric cone metric: cells become overlapping scallops and rings become nested arcs pointing downwind, for scales, ropy lava and scalloped ice.
master.look: Hillshade shows overlapping fish-scale or roof-tile plates all pointing downwind, with a smooth back and a sharp lip. Rings give eccentric targets and arcs resembling ropy pahoehoe lava or scalloped cave walls.
master.algorithm: T(x)=min over the window of (|v|-e*(v.w)), with v=x-p_i, unit wind w, and eccentricity e in [0,1). Level sets are conics with a focus at the seed, and boundaries are hyperbolae. Window: seeds that matter lie upwind, so centre the 3^D window at floor(x-shift*w) with shift about 0.6. Output T, or cos(2*pi*f*T) for nested arcs.
master.why_new: No existing metric is directional: Manhattan, MaxAxis and Minkowski are all symmetric, and domain scale only stretches cells without making an asymmetric scallop. Sits close to CellularDistance in cost for a very different output.
master.simd_plan: Replaces the distance calculation only, so it could be a DistanceFunction option. Same window count: about 4.5 ns in 2D (1.1x CellularDistance), 14 ns in 3D, 45 ns in 4D. Rounded shift per lane is fine for a constant wind.
master.continuity: C0: min of continuous functions, with a cusp at each seed. At e=0.65 the shifted 3x3 window matched a 7x7 reference exactly over 360x360 samples (0 mismatches), while unshifted 3x3 mismatched 1.3% with max error 0.29.
master.params: Eccentricity (hybrid, keep at or below about 0.8), Wind Direction (hybrid), Grid Jitter (hybrid), Output {Distance, Rings}, Ring Frequency.
master.risks: Window match was tested only at one e, seed and region; higher e needs a larger shift or window. A hybrid wind changes the window shift across space and can cause small seams. Output range grows as about (1+e) and depends on window.
master.cost_note: Same window count: about 4.5 ns in 2D (1.1x CellularDistance), 14 ns in 3D, 45 ns in 4D.

dome-heap.look: A heap of rounded balls: big smooth domes on top with smaller ones visible only in the gaps, and smaller again at the bottom of those gaps. The relief view reads at once as boulders with cobbles and gravel between them, with true occlusion. The gray view looks like cumulus tops seen from above. Hillshade shows crisp dome outlines. Sizes span about a decade. No lattice in the 4x view.

dims.3D: works, measured, the XZ slice looks like the 2D field
dims.4D: works, measured on an oblique plane through probe=4

dome-heap.artifacts: Small domes never sit on big ones, they only fill gaps, because height follows radius. FFT has a few faint radial streaks but no axis cross; the axis stat is high (37.95) and isoCV 1.08 because a few large discs dominate one small panel. Near the window edge the relief cuts through domes, which is just the crop. SDF mode (sdf=1): the first try at fine=0.9, levels=3, keep=0.85 was nearly solid in vol (mean 0.5, min -0.045), so I deleted that image. A sparser setting was not looked at, so the 3D conglomerate use is not shown. sphere profile c0ratio 4.2 is vertical rims, not jumps, and it looks about the same as the lens.

dome-heap.port_notes: Levels x 3^D candidates, Max only, no id tracking. Lens and parabola need no sqrt. Radius limit: r <= 1.5 - jitter/2, so full jitter allows r up to 1 and size jitter stays seamless. Height multiplies the profile; an added pedestal would jump at the rim. Each level uses seed + L*prime and a 45 degree rotation in xy so lattices do not line up. Consider this over SplatKernel's single level Dome when you want the size range. Levels=2 costs half.

master.one_liner: Z-buffered piles of domes across several lattice levels, whose size jitter can be as extreme as you like and stay seamless, because each level's domes fit its own window.
master.look:
Boulder fields, pebble beaches, bubbles, caviar, cell clusters, with large rounded forms partly burying smaller ones. In 3D the union of balls can be thresholded for rocky volumes.
[PebbleNoise, lattice-kernels] Heightfield of packed stones: each feature is a true hemisphere/ellipsoid with a vertical tangent at its rim, big ones half-burying small ones, sizes spread over a decade. Jitter 0 + equal radii = cobblestones; small radii + K=3 = gravel; Flatten 0.3 = river stones; SmoothMax = pebbles under a sand drape; SignedDistance in 3D sliced = conglomerate/breccia rock with circular clasts of mixed size; also bubble wrap, frog spawn, foam.
master.algorithm:
best=0. For L=0..Levels-1: fr=Lac^L; for each lattice point in the 3^D window around p*fr: h=hash(seed+L*prime, cell). keep=rnd(h>>a)<Keep. s=seed position (full 0..1 jitter in the cell). r=Radius*(1-SizeJitter*rnd(h>>b)), required r<=1 so a dome cannot leave the window (a seed two cells away is at least 1 lattice unit from the sample). q=r*r-|p*fr-s|^2. z=Profile(q)*(1+HeightJitter*rnd(h>>c))/fr, where Profile is sqrt(q) for sphere, or q/r for a parabola with no sqrt. best=max(best, Select(keep and q>0, z, 0)). Output best normalised by (Radius*(1+HeightJitter)). This is a pointwise cousin of the dead leaves model, with height ordering instead of random layer order.

[PebbleNoise, lattice-kernels] Params: RadiusMin, RadiusMax (cells, <= 1 - Jitter/2), PointsPerCell K (1..3), Flatten (0..1), HeightJitter, Blend {Max, SmoothMax(k), SignedDistance}, Density (hybrid), Jitter.
Gen(p): c = floor(p); best = Floor (e.g. -1 or 0)
 for o in {-1,0,1}^dim, for j in 0..K-1 (fixed):
   h = hash(seed, c+o) * (j==0 ? 1 : OddConst_j) then remix
   q = c+o + 0.5 + Jitter*(rndvec(h)-0.5); r = p - q
   u = rnd01(h>>12); rho = RadiusMax * exp(-u * ln(RadiusMax/RadiusMin))   // log-uniform; Exp available; or rho = lerp(Min,Max,u^2)
   z = HeightJitter * rnd11(h>>20)
   cap = z + Flatten * sqrt(max(0, rho^2 - |r|^2))        // exact sphere profile, 0 outside
   alive = (h>>24) < Density*256
   Max:      best = max(best, Select(alive, cap, Floor))
   SmoothMax: best = best + log1p-free softmax: use MaxSmooth formula from Blends with smoothness k
   SignedDistance (3D volumes): best = min(best, |r| - rho) (union-of-balls SDF)
 value = ScaleOutput(best, Floor, RadiusMax + HeightJitter).
master.why_new: Per-cell radius in CellularDistance is limited to about one cell size and yields one scale. Stacking levels gets a real power-law size distribution with occlusion, unlike additive octaves, where small things sit on big ones and never get buried. Graph versions with MaxSmooth need one Cellular per level and cannot do per-dome radius or height.
master.simd_plan: Levels x 3^D distance evaluations, with Max only and no id tracking. Using the parabola profile saves one sqrt per candidate. About 3.5 ns per level in 2D, 11 in 3D, 38 in 4D; 4 levels is 14 / 44 / 150 ns. In 4D recommend at most 3 levels.
master.continuity: C0. Each dome reaches 0 at its rim, so max is continuous. Sphere profile has vertical tangents at the rim (c0ratio 3.31, high slope); parabola has finite slope. An early version with a height pedestal jumped, so height must multiply the profile, never be added to it.
master.params: Levels (int), Lacunarity, Radius, Size Jitter, Height Jitter, Keep (hash probability), Profile enum, plus Size Slope mapping L to Keep so artists set the pebble-to-boulder ratio.
master.risks:
The 4D cost is heavy. The background reads flat where Keep is small. Hybrid radius at the pixel would be continuous but stops being a fixed sphere; radius should stay per seed.
[PebbleNoise, lattice-kernels] Log-uniform radii + small RadiusMin leaves bare floor between stones unless K>=2; coverage must be tuned. Max-union is not physically stacked (small stones can poke through big ones when z jitter is large). Vertical rims produce aliasing in hillshade at low Feature Scale.
master.cost_note: About 3.5 ns per level in 2D, 11 in 3D, 38 in 4D; 4 levels is 14 / 44 / 150 ns.
master.variant_notes: Max of domes. Levels=1 with log-uniform radii is PebbleNoise, which adds an SDF output for 3D conglomerate.
