fan-field.look: Mountain massifs with a smooth apron around their foot and faint radial marks spreading across the dark plain, with small pinched star marks where fans start. Individual fans are hard to read: no clear scalloped lobes in the gray or relief view. A plain blurred mask would give nearly the same apron. Four iterations: first too faint and far from the front; taller fans gave blocky tongues with cliff sides; toe creases gave streaks and notches at the apex; a distance gate made apexes continuous along the front but even softer. Tongue kind is the most visible: tent shapes on the plain. Cirque kind is nearly invisible. 3D vol: smooth blobby surfaces with tiny pimples, dull.
fan-field.dims: 2D and 3D measured. 3D is real (27 cells, stamps grow out of an iso surface along its gradient). 4D not run, 81 x 5 mask evals is not sensible.
fan-field.range: [-1, 0.952] over 8 seeds; far coords fine; no NaN; 3D z-continuity max 0.0041 per 1e-3
fan-field.artifacts: Pinched star marks at apexes where several sector edges converge. With taller fans the sector side forms a cliff. Small mask islands get fans in all directions. c0ratio 7.7 with no sign of jumps.
fan-field.node_shape: FanField: Mask Source, Level, Front Distance, Length, Height, Half Angle, Lobes, Kind enum {Fan, Cirque, Tongue}, Jitter, Include Mask (bool), Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. Not recommended on this evidence.
fan-field.port_notes: Reach bound: L * 1.25 <= 2.5 - j cells for the 5 x 5 window, 1.5 - j in 3D. Combining stamps by 1 - prod( 1 - f ) is zero neutral and order independent, so it adds no seams, unlike a polynomial smooth max. It is a clean general trick. The unique ability is real: sampling a mask and its gradient at the feature point lets a stamp know where it is and which way is downhill, and hybrids cannot do that. Forward difference gate on estimated distance needs the gradient for every cell. If this comes back, it should be as a generic oriented stamp node with far stronger stamps, not as fans.
fan-field.params_text: defaults: kind=0,ms=0.17,oct=2,level=0,bd=0.55,length=1.6,height=0.4,halfangle=0.95,lobes=0.3,k=7,rough=0.45,jit=0.45 ; fans only: out=1 ; tongues: kind=2 ; cirques: kind=1

master.one_liner: Front-anchored oriented stamps: features are kept only where a mask source crosses a level at the feature point and are oriented along the mask's downhill gradient there, producing alluvial fans and bajadas along mountain fronts (or cirques, deltas and landslide tongues with other profiles).
master.look: Scalloped aprons of coalescing cones spreading from the mountain front onto the plain, concave-up, with faint distributary ridges; apexes only where the front is. Prototyped: fans (c0 7.8 after feathering). The look is still subtle at the prototype's density (many small fans); fewer, longer fans with a sharper mountain front read better.
master.algorithm: Mask source M (e.g. the continent/mountain noise), Level c, Band b. Jittered lattice, (2R+1)^2 window with R=2 (fan length up to 2 cells). Per cell point q: m0 = M(q), gate g = 1 - smoothstep(0, b, |m0 - c|) (apex lies on the front); if g>0 (mask arithmetic, no branch): gradient at q by forward differences (dim extra M evals), axis u = -grad/|grad| (downhill of the mask). d = p - q, r = |d|, cosang = dot(d,u)/r. sector = smoothstep(cosw-0.25, cosw+0.25, cosang) blended to 1 near the apex (sat(r/0.08)) so the apex is isotropic. Length L = Length*(0.6+0.8*rnd); profile = exp(-2 r/L) * (1 - smoothstep(0.6L, L, r)) * (1 - 0.5*sat(1 - r/(0.25L))) (concave-up, rounded apex, toe fades); lobes = 1 + 0.15*ringnoise(angle, 10, h)*sat(r/0.3L) (distributary channels, see PolarCells). fan = max over cells of g*Height*sector*profile*lobes. Output max(mountain, fan + plain) where mountain = max(0, M)*scale, or output the fan field alone for Add in a graph. Kinds: Fan (sector 50-70 degrees), Cirque (uphill half-bowl: u = +grad, bowl profile), Delta (fan with Level = sea level), Tongue (narrow sector, flat top).
master.why_new: Stamps exist in sibling lenses and hybrids let a mask scale a stamp, but hybrids are sampled at the current position, not at the feature point, so a graph cannot say 'place this feature only on the contour and point it downhill'. Sampling the mask (and its gradient) at the feature point is the trick that makes placement and orientation coherent per feature.
master.simd_plan: 25 cells x (1 + dim) mask evaluations in 2D (75 Perlin ~85 ns) plus per-cell Sqrt, Exp, a polynomial atan2 for lobes (optional). Cost cut: evaluate the gate first for all 25 cells (25 evals) and only compute gradients for cells where any lane is gated (masked, still constant loop). 3D: 125 cells x 4 evals, too heavy except with R=1 (27 x 4 = 108). 4D: not planned. Realistic tier: 2D terrain node, 20-90x Perlin depending on mask source.
master.continuity: C0: gate, sector, profile and lobes are all smooth in p; max over a fixed window. Measured 7.79. Seams if Length > R cells.
master.params: Mask Source, Level, Band, Length, Height, Half Angle, Kind enum, Lobes, Jitter, Include Mask bool (output composite or fan field only).
master.risks: Medium confidence on the look: needs tuning of density vs. front scale, and fans should merge smoothly (smooth max). Mask gradient at the apex can point along the front when the front is wiggly, orienting a fan sideways. Expensive with multi-octave masks; recommend a GeneratorCache'd low-octave mask.
master.cost_note: 25 cells x (1 + dim) mask evaluations in 2D (75 Perlin ~85 ns) plus per-cell Sqrt, Exp, a polynomial atan2 for lobes (optional).

measured.scalar_note: Measured with defaults, 6999 ns per sample scalar, 57.86x worley2: 25 cells x 3 mask evals x 2 octaves, plus sample side mask and detail. Before the distance gate, the mask unit gate measured 88.55x, because ungated cells skipped the gradient.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 2D 100-180 ns with a 2 octave Perlin mask (150 Perlin evals); 3D 27 x 4 evals, 150+ ns. Scales with the mask cost, far outside the target unless the mask is cached.

gradient-metric-cellular.look: Contour aligned at k 5 with 5x5: long fibrous cells in bundles that follow the guide's contours and close into concentric loops around its extrema, like bark, muscle or wood around a knot. Slope aligned (align=1): long cells radiating from extrema in star bursts, like palm fronds or leaf venation, very striking. The relief of F1 is swirling folded ridges, like wind carved rock. The 27 cell volume gives flattened curved shards. The 125 cell volume gives thin folded sheets, like shale or lamellae.

dims.2D: works, measured, at 5x5 for the full look and 3x3 for a softer one
dims.3D: works, measured, 27 and 125 cell volumes both rendered. Cells flatten along the guide's level sets.
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path. The formula is dimension agnostic, and only needs 5 taps.

gradient-metric-cellular.range: -1.000 .. 1.000 over 8 seeds with out=1, clipped by construction with the k scaled gap, mean -0.367
gradient-metric-cellular.artifacts: Star shaped needle clusters at the guide's flat points, softened by eps but still there. Owner output (out=2) is 1.0 by design, and the plates output measures c0ratio 1.3 to 1.8 at k 3 to 8, because its lines are very thin; no jump was seen and F2-F1 measures 7.8 to 8. With win=1 the fibres are lost: cells stay as soft blocks with some contour alignment, and k above 5 changes little.
gradient-metric-cellular.node_shape: GradientMetricCellular : Generator. Guide (GeneratorSource), Stretch k (hybrid, >= 1), Alignment enum {Contour, Slope}, Sample Distance, Wide Window (bool: 5^D), Grid Jitter (hybrid), Return Type enum, ScalableGenerator, Seeded, VariableRange.
gradient-metric-cellular.port_notes: Guide taps once per lane (D+1), then per candidate one dot, one FMA and the fade (Min, Max, hermite on |v|^2), all branch free. Inverse of gl + eps is one Reciprocal per lane. The 5x5 window in 2D is a larger constant loop; offer it as an option, with the 3^D window as the cheap default in 3D and 4D.
gradient-metric-cellular.params_text: k=5,gf=0.22,eps=0.05,h=0.08,out=1,align=0,fade=1,r0=0.6,win=2 in 2D and win=1 in 3D (these are the code defaults). Radial sprays: align=1. Terrain: out=0. Volume: out=1 with iso -0.45.

master.one_liner: Cellular distance using a per-lane metric stretched by a sampled gradient, so cells flow along any field's contours with no displacement.
master.look: F2-F1 gives long fibrous cells bundled along the guide's contours, closing in loops around its extrema: bark, muscle, stretched scales, drawn-out mud cracks. F1 gives flowing wood-like streaks. Contrast with Warped Cellular on the contact sheet: cells there are bent but keep rounded proportions, while these are consistently elongated in a controlled direction.
master.algorithm: g from guide stencil at p. Standard CellularDistance window search, with distance d^2 = |dp|^2 + B (dp.g)^2/(|g|^2+e), where dp = site - p, B = k-1 >= 0. No frame needed in any dimension. Use F1, F2-F1, etc. as usual. e fades the anisotropy where the guide is flat, which removes the direction singularity. Enum for the slope-aligned version: |dp|^2 + B(|dp|^2 - (dp.g)^2/(|g|^2+e)).
master.why_new: Directional stretch whose amount and direction you can dial and paint, independent of position, with sites unmoved. Lets cell patterns align to terrain contours. A warp cannot produce a controlled uniform aspect ratio. Because the metric is evaluated at the sample and dp is bounded by the window, there is no far-origin shear.
master.simd_plan: Same window as CellularDistance plus (D+1) taps once per lane, one extra dot and mul per candidate. 2D 3.3+3.9 = about 7 ns, 3D 8.8+12 = about 21 ns, 4D 21.5+41 = about 62 ns on a Perlin guide. Metric computed once before the window loop.
master.continuity: Same class as CellularDistance. Measured c0ratio 6.73 at k=5 with a 3x3 window, and the 5x5 window gave the same mean and ratio, so window truncation was not visible at that k. Discontinuity would appear at extreme k, where a far site should beat every window site.
master.params: Stretch k (hybrid, >=1; shrink is disallowed since it would need a larger window), Alignment enum, Guide source, Sample Distance h, usual Cellular members.
master.risks: Seams at k well above about 8 from window truncation, needing a clamp or documented limit. This is not a true anisotropic Voronoi with a metric at the site, so cell shapes vary slightly with the sample point, but this was not noticeable.
master.cost_note: 2D 3.3+3.9 = about 7 ns, 3D 8.8+12 = about 21 ns, 4D 21.5+41 = about 62 ns on a Perlin guide.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 15.28x perlin2 at defaults, 5x5 window (750.6 ns vs 49.1 ns); 9.61x with the 3x3 window (479.4 ns vs 49.9 ns). The guide is one perlin with 3 taps in both.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D about 15 ns with 5x5 (3.3 guide + 11 window) or 8 ns with 3x3. 3D about 22 ns with 27 cells, about 70 ns with 125 cells. 4D about 65 ns with 81 cells.

hard-core-cellular.look: Discs: separate round dots of a few sizes, spread very evenly, none touching, with no clumps and no empty holes; the wide view is an even scatter with no visible lattice. FFT is concentric rings from the disc shape with no cross or grid dots. Relief with Stamp is an evenly spaced field of sea stacks or standing stones in a flat sea. The 3D volume is an even cloud of separate spheres of similar size. Reads as rivets, lichen dots, tree crowns or bubbles. It is plain by design and sparse: coverage at the guaranteed radius is about 9 percent (calculated from the radius, not measured). Rank mode is a blocky square checker mosaic and Smooth is a value noise like field with clear horizontal and vertical lattice lines. Neither is attractive; both show the grid. The value is in the point set, not in those two outputs.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3, z-continuity max 0.0512 for dz=1e-3
dims.4D: works on an oblique plane through the same template (slice4=1), range -1 .. 0.961. Too expensive to be a good tiling path as it stands. Tiling itself not tested.

hard-core-cellular.range: Discs -1.000 .. 0.999 over 8 seeds, mean -0.902, most of the area is background at -1. Smooth -1 .. 1, mean -0.001. Rank -1 .. 1, mean 0.000.
hard-core-cellular.artifacts: Census of the claims. Rank histogram over 360000 cells in 2D and 1728000 in 3D: flat within 1%, chi2 fine for both hash forms (raw hash 2.2 and 4.8 on 8 dof, 20.6 on 26 dof), so the FastNoise hash has no neighbour correlation that hurts this. Top rank fraction 0.11126 against exact 0.11111. Adjacent top rank pairs: 0. Spacing of top rank sites at J .8: NN min 1.236 (guarantee 2-J=1.2), p05 1.544, mean 2.147, cv 0.198; a random 1/9 thinning of the same sites: NN min 0.228, p05 0.651, mean 1.598, cv 0.442. At J1: min 1.046 against 0.062. Density is fixed at 1/9 in 2D and 1/27 in 3D unless below>0, which drops the guarantee. Smooth peak claims were not measured. Max slope 57.8 with the 1-t^4 rim on small discs.
hard-core-cellular.node_shape: HardCoreScatter (name proposal): Output enum (Discs, Distance, Stamp, Rank, Smooth), Rank Below int (0 = top rank only, hard core guarantee), Radius hybrid, Radius Variation float, Height Variation float, Jitter float, Source (optional, stamped once), Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. Rank and Smooth could be dropped.
hard-core-cellular.port_notes: 5^D hash block, then 3^D candidates each with 3^D-1 integer compares; with below=0 the rank is just an AND of masks, so no count is needed. Then a masked distance for each candidate. Clamp F1 at 1+(1-J)/2, the nearest a site outside the window can be. Radius at most (2-J)/2 keeps discs apart, so one Source eval suffices for Stamp. Use max of domes rather than nearest site, so that a user radius above the guarantee stays C0. In 3D, rank compares on face neighbours only would save most of the compares but weaken the guarantee; not measured. Far coords (4e4) std 0.363.
hard-core-cellular.params_text: mode=3,below=0,jit=0.8,scale=3,radius=0.6,rvar=0.35,hvar=0.3,hmix=1 (the code defaults: Discs). Stamped: mode=4. F1 distance: mode=2. Rank: mode=0. Smooth: mode=1. Denser, no guarantee: below=1 or more. Merged domes: radius=1.

master.one_liner: Rank each cell's hash among its 3^d neighbours: exactly uniform per-cell ranks, and the top-rank cells form a hard-core (Matern-like) point set with guaranteed minimum spacing, giving spots that never touch at exact density and a blue-noise scatter with a hard guarantee.
master.look: Rank mode: a cellular mosaic where bright cells are always surrounded by darker ones (a checker-like, 'dappled' anti-clustered mosaic unlike CellularValue's random clumps). Smooth: an even, bumpy field whose peaks are spaced >= 2 cells apart, with no large bright or dark regions. HardCoreDistance thresholded: evenly spread, non-touching discs (lichen patches, craters that do not overlap, tree crowns, bubbles, rivets); hillshade: a bed of separate domes at even spacing. Versus CellularDistance F1 the discs never merge and the count per area is exact.
master.algorithm:
h_c = Hash(seed, c) for integer cells.
rank_c = sum over the 3^d - 1 neighbours n of c of [h_n < h_c]  in {0 .. 3^d - 1};  u_c = rank_c / (3^d - 1).
Facts: P(rank_c = r) = 1/3^d exactly for every r (ties negligible with 32-bit hashes); two cells with rank = 3^d - 1 (local maxima of the hash) can never be adjacent (each would have to beat the other), so top cells have Chebyshev spacing >= 2 and density exactly 1/3^d per cell; more generally no 3^d block holds more than (3^d - R) cells of rank >= R.
Modes:
  Rank: out = 2 u_{floor(x)} - 1 (cellular steps, like CellularValue but with anti-correlated neighbours).
  Smooth: quintic tensor interpolation of u over the 2^d cell centres around x (needs a 4^d block of hashes).
  HardCoreDistance: feature point p_c = c + 0.5 + Jitter*rnd11*0.5 for cells with rank_c >= RankMin (others masked to +inf); out = F1 distance to the nearest selected point over the 3^d window (ranks of those cells need the 5^d hash block). With RankMin = 3^d - 1 and Jitter j the selected points are at least 2 - j cells apart, so thresholding F1 at radius r < 1 - j/2 gives discs that never overlap, at exactly 1/3^d points per cell.
master.why_new: CellularDistance/CellularValue points are Poisson-like per cell: discs merge, densities fluctuate, and thinning them (CellularValue < p) breaks the spacing. Blue-noise point sets with a minimum distance are exactly what scattering needs, and FastNoise cannot produce one; this does it from hashes alone, pointwise, with a provable spacing and exact density, and the Smooth mode is a coherent noise whose maxima are guaranteed separated (one extremum per 3^d block at most).
master.simd_plan: Hash-only inner loops: Rank 2D = 9 hashes, Smooth 2D = 4x4 block = 16 hashes with the 9 compares per centre done on the block (3D 64, 4D 256 hashes); HardCoreDistance = 5^d hashes (25 / 125 / 625) + 3^d distance tests. Each hash ~6 int ops, so 2D Smooth ~1x Perlin, 3D Smooth ~1.5x Perlin 3D, 2D Distance ~1.3x CellularDistance, 3D ~1.6x, 4D ~2x (heavy, like all 4D cellular). Compares are int masks summed with Masked adds; all branch-free.
master.continuity: Rank: discontinuous (cell steps, by design); Smooth: C2; HardCoreDistance: C0 (F1-type kinks), continuous across cells because masked points simply drop out of the min.
master.params: Mode enum (Rank, Smooth, HardCoreDistance); Rank Min (int 0..3^d-1, controls density: top rank = 1/3^d); Jitter; Feature Scale; Seed Offset; Output Min/Max.
master.risks: Hash-count explosion in 4D distance mode. Spacing guarantee is in cells, so with Jitter near 1 the Euclidean guarantee weakens (2 - j). Top-rank density 1/9 (2D) is fixed; lower RankMin trades density for a weaker clustering bound. The 'uniform rank' property holds per cell, not for the Smooth field.
master.cost_note: Each hash ~6 int ops, so 2D Smooth ~1x Perlin, 3D Smooth ~1.5x Perlin 3D, 2D Distance ~1.3x CellularDistance, 3D ~1.6x, 4D ~2x (heavy, like all 4D cellular).

measured.scalar_note: Measured 39.7 ns vs perlin2 51.8. Caution: the scalar code skips the distance for unselected cells with a branch, 8 of 9, and the compiler unrolls the fixed 2D loops. A SIMD port pays for all 9. Smooth 22.5 ns, 0.44x. F1 distance 39.7 ns, 0.78x. Stamp 52.3 ns, 1.05x before rvar. 3D Discs 326.9 ns, 6.40x. 3D Smooth 143.1 ns, 2.81x. 4D Discs on an oblique plane 2026.0 ns, 39.76x.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured on SIMD: about 5-6 ns 2D, about 25-35 ns 3D, about 200 ns 4D; 2D and 3D from the catalogue's op count against CellularDistance, 4D by scaling scalar at 10:1. 4D has 625 hashes and 6480 compares.
measured.c0_note: Discs 7.42, Stamp 7.54, Smooth 8.00, F1 distance 8.00, 3D oblique plane 7.47, 4D oblique plane 7.47. Rank is flat per cell, so the probe's number is meaningless there and it is discontinuous by design. Picking the nearest site's height made an early version jump (1.46) when discs overlapped; max of domes fixed that at any radius.

lava-columns.look: A clean field of soft discs in many sizes, fused here and there into dumbbells and blobs with real necks, on a black background. Reads as oil droplets or lava lamp blobs; no column pattern visible in a still, FFT is a clean ring. Vol: separated smooth spheres with a few short necks. Frames at t=0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75: the blob layout changes substantially from frame to frame. At these spacings individual blobs can't be followed by eye, so the merge and split behaviour is what the algorithm gives, not something I watched.
lava-columns.dims: 2D measured (3 columns, x is across). 3D measured (9 columns, z-continuity max 0.0127 per 1e-3). 4D is the 3D code with t = w; I tested t as a param over frames and with test=1 and test=2, not through a separate 4-argument Eval.
lava-columns.range: [-1, 0.995] over 8 seeds with the 1 - exp( -S * g ) map; far coords fine; no NaN
lava-columns.artifacts: None seen in a still. Discs are flat topped after the exp map when blobs overlap. Speeds are large at t in radians: a smaller P or a Speed param would help animation control. A vertical axis is privileged by design. GenTileable's w path would not mean time.
lava-columns.node_shape: Mode of orbit-blobs: Motion enum {Orbit, Columns}, Radius, Radius Jitter, Sway, Period (power of two), Time (hybrid or w), Axis enum, Output Gain, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
lava-columns.port_notes: Radius limit is 1 - sway per column. r = r0 * ( 0.5 + rnd ), so r0 <= ( 1 - sway ) / 1.5, clamped in the prototype. Per column: speed from hash bits by table, one Floor of ys, 3 sites each with its own hash of ( column, iy mod P ). Mod P by AND. Sin and Cos of time are one pair per lane; per site sway rotates them with a table. No sqrt.
lava-columns.params_text: defaults: t=0.9,r0=0.5,g=2.2,sway=0.2,jx=1,jy=1,logP=4,out=0 ; volume: out=1 (raw field minus 0.5) with --iso 0
lava-columns.merged_into: orbit-blobs, as a Motion mode (Orbit, Scrolling Columns). Same kernel, same window size, same static look. Only the site positions differ. In animation this mode is the better lava lamp, because blobs really travel past each other.

master.one_liner: Metaballs that actually move: columns scroll at different integer speeds so blobs rise, pass, merge and split, with exact time loop at 3D cost.
master.look: Not prototyped. Expected in 3D iso: smooth round blobs with soft necks that stretch and pinch while rising. 2D (x,y) slice: oil-droplet discs and bridges with teardrops in motion. Static frame looks like metaballs, animation is the point: real topology change caused by motion rather than 4D boiling. For lava lamps, magma, oil, cell motion, slime.
master.algorithm: Vertical axis y, Time = w in 4D or hybrid Time param in 3D. For each column in 3x3 (x,z): hc = hash(col); v = table {+1,+2,+3,-1}[hc bits]; ys = y - v*Time*P/(2*pi); iy = floor(ys). For dy in {-1,0,1}: h = hash(col, (iy+dy) mod P); site s = (col_x + jx, iy+dy + jy, col_z + jz) + Sway*(sin(Time+ph), 0, cos(Time+ph)) with sway sine pre-computed once per lane and rotated by table ph; r = r0*(0.5+rnd01); d2 relative to (x, ys, z); k = max(1 - d2/(r*r), 0); S += k^3. Output 1-exp(-S*g) or S/(S+1), scaled. Because hash uses iy mod P and v is an integer, Time=2 pi shifts each column by exact multiple of P, so loop is exact. Mixed-sign v gives rising and sinking blobs. Keep r <= 1.0 plus sway so kernels fit the 3x3 columns.
master.why_new: Moving w through 4D Cellular or Simplex makes features fade in place, not travel. Translating the whole domain moves everything rigidly. Independent column speeds give relative motion, which is what makes blobs merge and split, at 3D window cost instead of a 4D window, and a built-in exact loop. Can't be done in a graph since per-column offsets occur inside the window.
master.simd_plan: Loop 9 columns x 3 y cells = 27 kernels in 3D, no sqrt: estimate 7 to 10 ns; can trim to 2 y cells by half-offset to reach 18 kernels. 4D same cost as 3D (vs 41 ns for 4D CellularDistance). 2D: 3 columns x 3 = 9 kernels, under 3 ns with Time. Mod P via AND with power-of-two P. Single sin and cos per lane, phase offsets from a small table.
master.continuity: C2 from compact (1-d2/r2)^3 kernel with the window containing all contributions; output map smooth. Continuous in time as well.
master.params: Time (hybrid, or w), Radius (hybrid), Density gain, Sway, Period P (int, power of two), Axis enum (optional).
master.risks: Untested. Vertical period P cells is visible if small, so P>=8. Vertical axis is privileged: columns may read as streams if speeds are too uniform. GenTileable: 4D mapping is continuous, but w on the torus does not mean time. Hybrid Radius varying per lane breaks kernel fit if above limit, so clamp.
master.cost_note: Loop 9 columns x 3 y cells = 27 kernels in 3D, no sqrt: estimate 7 to 10 ns; can trim to 2 y cells by half-offset to reach 18 kernels.

measured.scalar_note: Measured with defaults, 2.71x worley2.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 2D under 3 ns (9 kernels), 3D 7-10 ns (27 kernels, per column floor and speed select), 4D same as 3D.

level-dendrite.look: Terrain output is the good one: on the relief it reads as a mountain massif cut by steep sided valleys that join into trunks, with sharp dendritic spurs and flat blue bottoms where the deepest band is clamped. On the gray panel the valleys branch properly and curve in, with no star hubs at the big trunks. Network output is less good: curved thick trunks plus many thin straight twigs that cross each other, closer to a pile of sticks or cracked glass than to a river map. 3D vol: a thick lattice of tubes meeting at star hubs like jacks, clearly cubic, not tree like.
level-dendrite.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured with the R=1 hop=0 form (27 cells per level, z-continuity max 0.004 per 1e-3) and it works but shows the lattice. 4D not run and not sensible: 81 cells per level, no tiling path.
level-dendrite.range: [-1, 1] over 8 seeds with clamping at both ends; far coords fine; slope 4.6 per unit in terrain mode, 63 in network mode
level-dendrite.artifacts: Twigs cross in network mode, because long hops ignore neighbours. Valley walls have sharp folds at the elbow of the two segment curve. Clamped flat bottoms at -1 where the lowest band runs out; a port should give more headroom or smooth it. Hop 0 has grid corridors. Attach mode 1 (outlet on the parent's segment, from my own trial) floats: the parent's drawn segment does not follow the ghost it was projected onto, so tributaries end in empty space. I dropped it.
level-dendrite.node_shape: LevelDendrite: Levels (int), Long Hop Chance, Jitter (limit 1 - 3j - bend > stroke reach), Bend, Arrival Curve, Width, Width Growth, Slope, Output enum {Terrain, Network}, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. Upstream warp recommended, included in the prototype as warp.
level-dendrite.port_notes: Corrections to the catalogue and to rel_dendrite: hop 1 with jitter 0.4 and R 2 misses segments, its clearance 1 - 3j is negative. The bound used here is reach = 1 - 3j - bend cells, and strokes and terrain flanks both end at it. hop 0 can use R 1 (9 cells per level). Curved arrival: a child's segment becomes a 2 segment polyline through a mid point derived from the grandparent's direction, so tributaries arrive nearly tangent to the outflow, which removes star hubs without any search. It costs one extra hash per child and one extra segment distance. Evaluate each segment's profile and height separately and combine with Max and Min; choosing by nearest segment makes t jump across the elbow's medial axis, which gave c0ratio 3.6 until fixed. Hop is a per axis Select from hash bits towards the nearer neighbouring parent cell.
level-dendrite.params_text: defaults (terrain): mode=1,levels=4,hop=1,hopP=0.33,attach=2,jit=0.14,bend=0.25,kappa=0.7,fine=0.4,w=0.07,wgrow=1.5,slope=1,warp=0.2,wf=0.5 ; network: mode=0 ; 3D vol: mode=0,w=0.22,wgrow=1.2,fine=0.5,levels=3 with --iso -0.7

master.one_liner: A multi-level parent tree computed in O(1) per lattice cell gives connected branching networks and a monotone downhill valley terrain with no search.
master.look: Lightning, roots, cracks with hierarchy; terrain has V valleys that join downstream and drop monotonically. Prototyped: rel_dendrite, hop=1 for the non-grid form. Star-shaped convergence at parents is visible and more spidery than a real river.
master.algorithm: Level l has cell size s=fine*2^l and a jittered node per cell. Parent of cell c at level l: node at level l+1 in cell floor((c+hop)/2) with hop in {-1,0,1} from hash. Since the parent is itself a level l+1 child, all segments connect into trees. For each level, window +-2 cells: segment child->parent, width growing along t. Network output: max over levels of profile(d/w_l)*weight_l. Terrain output: node heights in strictly falling per-level bands; h_seg(t)+k_l*d with k_l chosen so distance reaches the cap of +1 by reach s_l; take the min over all segments and levels. The cap makes out-of-window segments irrelevant, so no seams.
master.why_new: Real hierarchical dendritic structure and monotone drainage, which are normally simulation results, with no pass over a grid. Ridged noise makes ridges with no tree topology.
master.simd_plan: Level loop is constant. Per level 25 cells in 2D with 2 hashes each and a segment distance. Scalar measured 12x worley2 with 4 levels. Estimate SIMD 2D 50-80 ns, well outside the 5x Perlin target, so justify it as a hero node. 3D with 125 cells per level is impractical without R=1 and small widths. 4D not practical, so tiling would need a dedicated fallback.
master.continuity: C0: network c0ratio 7.81, terrain c0ratio 8.00 with max slope 2.3. Terrain range measured -1 to about 0.67.
master.params: Levels (int), Hop (int enum), Width, Width Growth, Slope (float), Jitter, Output enum.
master.risks: Pure quadtree parents without hop guarantee no crossings but leave clear empty corridors along the top grid; hop fixes that and allows crossings. Nearest-of-4-parents would be better but it is essentially the published Dendry approach (Gaillard 2019, from memory, not checked) and costs 4x more. Poor 3D/4D story is a serious issue with the handbook's dimension rule.
master.cost_note: Estimate SIMD 2D 50-80 ns, well outside the 5x Perlin target, so justify it as a hero node.

measured.scalar_note: Defaults measured 4196 ns per sample scalar (37x worley2). Plain quadtree form hop=0,attach=0 measured 14.3x perlin2 but it has grid corridors.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: defaults 100-150 ns in 2D (4 levels x 25 cells x 3 hashes and 2 segments); hop=0 attach=0 15-25 ns (4 levels x 9 cells). Far outside the 5x Perlin target, hero node only.

local-frame-drainage.look: Height output: bright divides with black trunk valleys and side valleys that branch at acute angles pointing downstream, close to an erosion render on the gray and hillshade panels. Relief: a massif of smooth ridges with broad valleys and soft gullies on the flanks; convincing at this scale though the fine gullies are shallow. River mask (from the sweep at earlier parameters): long white trunks with shorter feather tributaries joining at acute angles, a clear hierarchy, rather than disconnected asterisks once the junction threshold was cut. The 4x wide panel is striking and also the main flaw: rosette shaped basins of similar size, each a dendritic star with white divides, like a field of snowflakes or leaf rosettes.
local-frame-drainage.dims: 2D measured. Eval3 is only the catalogue's fallback: two 2D evaluations cross faded along z (z-continuity max 0.0006 per 1e-3); the XZ slice shows vertical smears, so there is no real 3D network. 4D not implemented, no tiling. Reason: 216 heights and 26 neighbour compares per candidate per level in 3D.
local-frame-drainage.range: [-1, 1] over 8 seeds with clamps; mean about -0.1; far coords fine; no NaN
local-frame-drainage.artifacts: Star hubs at level 0 sinks, where all surrounding trunks converge; basin sizes are uniform, so at wide scale the rosettes repeat evenly. Trunks are straight between nodes without warp. Tributaries vanish on the bisector at trunk junctions, because the frame switches there and the fade hides it; it reads as a bare wedge, not a seam. River elevations are not monotonic, the profile just carves.
local-frame-drainage.node_shape: LocalFrameDrainage: Levels (int), Subdivision, Cell Scale, Jitter, Tilt, Height Jitter, Junction Radius, Junction Slide, Depth Gain, Width Gain, Valley Width, Line Width, Height Source (optional, node, level 0 only), Output enum {Height, River Mask}, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
local-frame-drainage.port_notes: The catalogue's window (3 x 3 candidates with 25 heights) has a clearance of only 0.5 - j cells, so tributaries could not get room or the frame would switch at cell borders. Used instead: 4 x 4 candidates centred on the nearest lattice corner with 6 x 6 heights, clearance 1 - j. d1 and d2 are clamped to the clearance and the frame fades out before it, which makes the output independent of everything outside the window. Lanes need per lane frames, stored as 6 float32v. Junction: a node within thrJ cells of the parent projects on it, plus a downstream slide of tiltJ x distance; the slide is what turned the combs into feathers. Junction radius of 0.8 gave perpendicular combs. Level 0 height source costs 36 evals. Lower bf should lengthen rivers and reduce rosettes, not tested in images.

master.one_liner: Isotropic hierarchical river tree at cost linear in levels: each finer level drains toward only the single nearest coarser segment, treated as a local frame. Dendry (Gaillard et al., from memory) is the known hierarchical relative, but it evaluates and caches parent structure.
master.look: Rivers and tributaries with a dendritic hierarchy in all directions, no global flow axis, and divides between them. Ridges appear as the medial axis of the parent network. Good for continental river masks and carved valleys.
master.algorithm:
Level 0: jittered points on a coarse lattice, hash heights, each flows to its lowest of 8 neighbours (steepest descent, acyclic because heights are strictly ordered). Use a 5x5 lattice to resolve outlets for the 3x3 candidates. Keep nearest segment S0, distance d0, second-nearest d0b.
Level k+1, cell size / 2 or 3: for each of the 25 points q, define height H(q)=dist(q,S_k)-alpha*dot(q-A,dir(S_k))+jitter*hash(q), an analytic function needing only the one parent segment, not a recursive evaluation. Steepest descent over 8 neighbours. If a point's H is below a threshold, its outlet is its projection on S_k, making a Y-junction.
The tilt alpha makes tributaries join at acute angles pointing downstream.
Fade f_k=smoothstep(0,w,d_kb-d_k) goes to zero at the medial axis of level k, where the parent frame switches. That is exactly a drainage divide, so finer rivers vanish there and the switch is invisible.
Height: h=sum_k Depth_k*profile(d_(k+1)/W_k)*f_k, plus a base of d0-based hillslope.
master.why_new: The naive approach is exponential because each child needs the parent field at every child point. Fixing a local frame per sample removes the recursion, using the fact that parent influence only changes at divides, which is where the fade hides it. CatchmentRivers offers exact area but has an axis; this has no axis but width by level only.
master.simd_plan: Per level: 25 hashes and heights, 9x8 neighbour comparisons by Select, 9 segment distances. Estimate 20-25 ns per level, 3 levels about 70 ns, about 60x Perlin and 18x CellularDistance. Cheaper variant: 4-way outlet. 3D: 125 points and 27x26 comparisons per level are too much; use 2D plane with z crossfade, or a 7-point 3D stencil, for root-like filaments. 4D no; no tiling.
master.continuity: C0 through f_k fade provided the window holds all segments that can be nearest and the top-2 distance tracking is correct. Outlet search can flip with parent choice only inside the faded zone.
master.params: Levels (int), Subdivision (2 or 3), Depth Gain, Width Gain, Tilt alpha, Jitter, Height Source for level 0 (optional; 25 evals).
master.risks: Not tested. Sinks exist at local minima of level 0 unless a tilt or height source is supplied, producing disconnected basins. Child streams can run parallel to the parent if alpha is too high. Stream elevations are not guaranteed monotonic. Y-junctions at a parent's endpoint need clamped projection. Highest implementation risk here apart from caves.
master.cost_note: Estimate 20-25 ns per level, 3 levels about 70 ns, about 60x Perlin and 18x CellularDistance.

measured.scalar_note: Defaults measured 4784 ns per sample scalar (42.75x worley2), 4 levels, level 0 heights from 36 perlin2 evals, 2 warp evals. Without height source at 3 levels the first run measured 29.57x perlin2.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 30-40 ns per level (36 hashes and frame distances, 16 x 8 height compares, 16 segment distances, top two), so about 150-200 ns for 4 levels with a level 0 source. Hero terrain node only.

modal-cells.look: Nodal lines default: a grid of square tiles, each holding a different clean line figure: diagonals, crossed diagonals, rounded quatrefoils, ovals, dot grids, wavy parallel bands. Reads as art deco tiling or an engraved plate, unlike anything on the existing sheet. Field output is a patchwork of checks, dots, stripes and soft lobes meeting on gray grid lines. The XZ slice of the 3D form has wobblier closed curves in each square. The volume at iso 0.08 is lumpy rounded chambers sliced by flat planes on the lattice. mvar=1.6 gives regions of big simple cells next to regions of fine busy ones. modes=2 looks muddier and I would not use it.

dims.3D: works, measured, Eval3 real, three term cyclic product
dims.4D: works, measured on an oblique plane through probe=4, four term cyclic product

modal-cells.artifacts: The grid is always there by design, the FFT has a strong cross and diagonals, so it is a pattern node, not a general noise. Many tiles repeat the same figure because few distinct low mode pairs exist at mmax=6; the mirror pairs and the same n,m recur, visible in the 4x view. Field needs gain and clamp because contrast varies by mode. NodalLines c0ratio 5.54 is thin lines (max slope 170 per unit), not jumps; lines stay crisp. High mmax aliases when a cell is small on screen.
modal-cells.node_shape: ModalCells : Min Mode, Max Mode (hybrid, read at the cell centre), Modes (int), Output enum (Field, NodalLines), Line Width (hybrid), Bubble (bool), Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max
modal-cells.port_notes: No window at all. 1 hash, integer mod for two bit fields, Select for n != m, 4 Sin in 2D. NodalLines needs Cos too, by computing sin and cos of the same angle. Do not read a hybrid Max Mode at the sample: that changes the mode set inside a cell and breaks the C0 guarantee, so read it at the cell centre with one extra eval. A hash-chosen sign keeps symmetric and antisymmetric figures. Sin of large k*pi*u is fine because u is local to the cell, so far coords measured the same (range -1 to 1, std 0.665 at 4e4).
modal-cells.params_text: out=1,mmin=1,mmax=6,modes=1,fine=0.75,width=0.04 (these are the defaults, nodal lines). out=0,gain=1.6 is the scalar Field; mvar=1.6,mvarf=0.2 lets a low frequency perlin pick each cell's mode ceiling; bubble=1 gives zero slope at seams. Vol: out=0,fine=1,mmax=4 at iso 0.08

master.one_liner: Each lattice cell vibrates as a Chladni drumhead with hash-chosen mode numbers, and C0 across cells is automatic because all modes vanish on cell edges, so no neighbours are needed.
master.look:
Tested. A mosaic of ornamental tiles: dots, checks, rosettes, each cell a different mode, all with exact nodal grid lines. Warped, it reads as bubbled ornamental glass or sci-fi panels. Very distinct from the sheet. Uses: panel greebles, tiles, decorative masks, and zero crossings exactly on a known lattice (useful for connected paths and grids).
[ChladniCell, math-physics] A grid of ornamental tiles, each with its own symmetric curvilinear nodal pattern (cymatics sand figures, Islamic/Art-Deco tiles, engraved plates); NodalLines mode gives crisp uniform lines; 3D: nodal surfaces in cubes giving chambered mineral/ bismuth-like structures in slices. Low modes: soft lobed bumps; high modes: fine woven lattices.
master.algorithm:
Cell i=Floor(p), u=p-i. h=hash(i); n=1+(h&255)%M; m=1+((h>>8)&255)%M; if m==n set m=1+m%M (Select; the degenerate case with minus sign is otherwise identically zero); sg=+-1 from bit 16.
Out=0.5*(Sin(n*pi*u)*Sin(m*pi*v)+sg*Sin(m*pi*u)*Sin(n*pi*v)).
3D: cyclic sum of three products, 4D: four. Optional bubble multiply by Sin(pi*u)*Sin(pi*v) for zero-slope seams (C1 at cost of a dark grid). Hybrid M lets a source select local complexity.

[ChladniCell, math-physics] Cells of side 1 (Feature Scale). No neighbour window: because sin(n pi u) is 0 at u=0 and u=1, each cell is independent and the field is C0 across edges.
Gen(seed, x):
  c = Floor(x); u = x - c (in [0,1)^d); h = hash(seed, c)
  f = 0
  for m in 0..Modes-1 (fixed):
    hm = rehash(h,m)
    n = MinMode + (hm bits) % (MaxMode-MinMode+1); k = same from other bits; if n==k: k = k+1 (Select)
    sigma = +-1 from a bit; amp = 1/(m+1) or rnd
    2D:  f += amp * ( Sin(n pi u) Sin(k pi v) + sigma * Sin(k pi u) Sin(n pi v) )
    3D:  cyclic antisymmetrised cube modes: f += amp*( S(n,u)S(k,v)S(l,w) + sigma*S(k,u)S(l,v)S(n,w) + sigma2*S(l,u)S(n,v)S(k,w) )
    4D:  same with 4 indices, 2 permutations
  Output Field:        v = f * normConst
  Output NodalLines:   grad f analytic (Cos terms, computed in the same loop) ; dist = |f| * InvSqrt(|grad f|^2 + eps) ; v = 1 - 2*Min(1, dist/LineWidth)   // constant-width Chladni sand lines
  Output EdgeFade (optional): multiply f by (4u(1-u))^q... to hide the plate border lines if undesired.
master.why_new: The only coherent cell node that needs no window at all (cheaper than Perlin in hash count), with an exact guarantee on where zeros lie: the zero set always contains the lattice, and internal crossing count is (n-1)(m-1)-like and hash-controlled. Fits the zero-crossing control brief directly.
master.simd_plan: Branch free. 1 hash, 4 Sin in 2D (6 and 8 in 3D and 4D by reuse), integer mod, Select. Window 1^D. Estimated about 1-1.5x Perlin in 2D and below Perlin in 3D and 4D.
master.continuity: C0 (verified numerically, ratio 8.0), kinks across cell edges due to different slopes. C1 with the bubble option.
master.params: Hybrid: Max Mode M. Enum: Bubble on/off. Seeded, ScalableGenerator.
master.risks:
The grid is always visible by design, and offset-lattice sums blur the identity (tested, it looked muddy). It is a pattern node, not a general purpose noise. Output contrast varies by mode. High M in a small cell aliases at small feature scales.
[ChladniCell, math-physics] The cell grid is visible in the zero set (plate edges) which is a style, not a bug, but limits use as terrain; sign and normalisation constants need measuring; high modes alias at low sampling.
master.cost_note: Estimated about 1-1.5x Perlin in 2D and below Perlin in 3D and 4D.
master.variant_notes: Chladni modes per cell, needing no window. ChladniCell contributes the NodalLines output with constant line width by analytic gradient.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 2D_lines: 1.14; 2D_field: 1.15; 3D_field_on_oblique_plane: 2.64; 4D_field_on_oblique_plane: 3.82
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: True; 2D: 1.5; 3D: 3.5; 4D: 7; basis: 1 hash and 4, 6, 8 Sin against Perlin's 4, 8, 16 hashes, catalogue says 1 to 1.5x Perlin in 2D; FS::Sin is not free, so the 3D and 4D numbers are rough

orbit-blobs.look: Soft blobs with real necks: dumbbells, L shapes and short chains on black, with brighter spots where kernels overlap. The threshold panel shows fused rounded islands with smooth concave necks, unlike the creased union of CellularDistance. Threshold sweep runs from fused blobs (0.12) to separate pearls (0.7). Vol default: a clump of rounded lumps fused in places. Vol foam: a rounded sponge with big smooth cavities. Frames across w: layouts shift, with blobs joining and parting between frames; each stays on its orbit by construction. FFT is clean with no lattice dots.
orbit-blobs.dims: 2D and 3D measured (3D z-continuity max 0.0093 per 1e-3). 4D is the 3D lattice with w as a phase; I tested w through a param (frames, test=1, test=2), not a 4-argument Eval, and tiling through it should hold because it is continuous in w.
orbit-blobs.range: [-1, 0.966] over 8 seeds. Raw field peak measured at 2.45 for ppc=1, 3.5 for ppc=2, so the node compresses above the threshold with 1 - exp; value 0 is the threshold surface. Far coords fine, no NaN.
orbit-blobs.artifacts: One point per cell shows a slightly even spacing at the wide view at jit 0.35, not bad enough to read as a grid. Bright overlap peaks are rare, which is why the output is compressed above threshold. Kink in slope at the threshold surface from the piecewise map, not visible.
orbit-blobs.node_shape: MetaBlobs (OrbitBlobs): Feature Scale, Radius (hybrid, clamped), Radius Jitter, Jitter, Points Per Cell (1-2), Motion enum {Orbit, Columns}, Orbit Amp X/Y/Z, Omega, Phase (hybrid), Threshold, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. lava-columns is merged here as the Columns motion.
orbit-blobs.port_notes: Clearance 1.5 - J - amp cells, so Radius * ( 1 + Radius Jitter ) <= 1.5 - J - amp; the prototype clamps. Kernel max( 1 - d2 / R2, 0 )^3 has no sqrt and is C2. No sorting, only a sum, so one Sin and Cos pair per lane plus about 20 ops per point. Rotating the lane's sin and cos by a per point phase from a table avoids per point trig. Orbit frame: table of orthonormal pairs by hash bits. Graph can't express this: no existing node sums overlapping kernels with a position per feature.

master.one_liner: Sum of compact Wyvill kernels on jittered lattice points that travel closed Lissajous orbits parameterised by w: metaball necks, lava-lamp rise-and-sink, exact-period looping at 3D cost.
master.look: 3D iso-surface: smooth merging droplets with proper necks (metaballs); low threshold gives a fused foam/sponge of rounded cavities, high threshold separate pearls. Animated in w: blobs rise, sink, pass each other, merge and split, exactly the lava lamp, looping with period 2pi/Omega. 2D slice: soft discs that fuse like mercury; animated: drifting, merging ink drops.
master.algorithm:
Window 3x3x3 (3x3 in 2D). Per cell k, for j in 0..PointsPerCell-1 (fixed int):
  h = Hash(k, j); c = k + 0.5 + Jitter*rnd3(h)
  per-point phase phi (table by bits), orbit frame u,v (table of random orthonormal pairs by bits)
  S,Cw = Sin/Cos(Omega*(w + Phase(p))) once per lane; s = S*cphi + Cw*sphi, cc = Cw*cphi - S*sphi
  c(w) = c + OrbitAmp * (u*cc + v*s)          // per-axis amplitude vector OrbitAmp, default (0.1, 0.4, 0.1) = lava lamp
  R = Radius * (1 + RadiusJitter*rnd11(h>>16))
  r2 = |p - c(w)|^2 / R^2; k = Max(1 - r2, 0); field += k*k*k    // Wyvill, C2, compact
out = field - Threshold, ScaleOutput over [-Threshold, Kmax - Threshold] (Kmax measured constant per PointsPerCell). Window validity: Radius <= 1.5 - Jitter - |OrbitAmp|max, so blobs may be larger than cells and overlap. 4D = 3D lattice + w phase (so tiling via GenTileable2D still holds).
master.why_new: CellularDistance F1 gives a union of hard spheres with creases where they meet and cannot add overlapping influences; CellularLookup cannot either. This gives smooth union/necks, per-blob size, and an exact animation loop without a 4D lattice (41 ns Cellular 4D avoided).
master.simd_plan: Cellular.inl window loop, no sorting; per point ~20 ops (orbit 6 FMA, distance 8, kernel 5). 3D with 1 point/cell: ~27 points ~ 1x CellularDistance 3D (12 ns); 2D ~4 ns; 4D same as 3D plus one Sin/Cos per lane.
master.continuity: C2 in space and C-infinity in w (Wyvill kernel is C2 at its support edge); gradient bounded by PointsPerCell*27*max kernel slope/Radius.
master.params: Radius (hybrid), RadiusJitter, Jitter, PointsPerCell (int 1-2), OrbitAmp X/Y/Z, Omega, Phase (hybrid), Threshold, Feature Scale, Seed.
master.risks: Lattice-regular density (one point per cell) shows as even spacing at low Jitter; large OrbitAmp forces a small Radius to keep the window valid. Kmax normalisation is a measured constant.
sources: from memory, not consulted: Lewis 1989 sparse convolution noise; Wyvill soft objects
master.cost_note: 3D with 1 point/cell: ~27 points ~ 1x CellularDistance 3D (12 ns); 2D ~4 ns; 4D same as 3D plus one Sin/Cos per lane.

measured.scalar_note: Measured with defaults, 3.22x worley2. ppc=2 measured 639 ns against 350 ns for ppc=1. rnd and table lookups are real cos and sin calls in the scalar code, a port has them in tables.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 2D ~4 ns (9 points), 3D ~12 ns (27 points), 4D same plus one Sin and Cos per lane.

pebble-pack.look: Sparse round domes of several sizes on a flat black ground, like polka dots or scattered mounds, never touching. With Stamp the relief is the best view: an archipelago of separate rocky islands in a flat sea, each with its own Perlin texture and no overlap, which is a genuinely pleasant look. The 3D volume is a loose cloud of separate true spheres. It reads as sparse, not as a pebble floor. The small discs at high pow almost vanish.

dims.3D: works, measured with 125 hashes and 702 distances; z-continuity max 0.0134 for dz=1e-3. nb3=6 is cheaper, but pairs at (1,1,0) offsets are then outside the neighbour set, so disjointness is not guaranteed; not measured.
dims.4D: fixed radius only, measured on an oblique plane. In that mode it is a thresholded F1 of low jitter, which a graph can already do. The full form needs 625 hashes, not built.

pebble-pack.range: Dome -1.000 .. 1.000 over 8 seeds, mean -0.667. Background is exactly -1. Stamp -1.000 .. 1.000 after a clamp; unclamped it reached 1.567.
pebble-pack.artifacts: Coverage is low by construction: 0.37 at the defaults, 0.34 at J .9 pow .6, 0.42 at J .7 pow .3, up to 0.51 at J .5 with no weights, where the grid starts to show. Second pass inflation would need a 7^D window. The catalogue's proof is incomplete: it only covers pairs in the neighbour set. Census over 39204 discs: neighbour pairs never overlapped, but pairs two cells apart overlapped 13 times at J1 pow 1.5 clamp 1 (worst 0.285) and 23 at pow 3. A clamp of 1 - J/2 is required, which is the default here: at J .9 clamp .55 and J .8 clamp .6 the census shows 0 overlaps; J1 clamp .55 still shows 1-2 (clamp is above 1 - J/2 = .5).
pebble-pack.node_shape: Not proposed as its own node. As a Stamp output on CellularCirclePacking: Source (stamped once), Stamp Scale, Per Disc Seed. If kept standalone: Jitter, Pow, Fill, Value Mode (Dome, Lens, Id, Size, Stamp), Source.
pebble-pack.port_notes: 5^D hashes, 3^D candidates each with 3^D-1 distances: 72 sqrt and divides in 2D, 702 in 3D, which is the cost problem; comparing squares and taking one sqrt at the end would remove most of the sqrts. Pick the disc with smallest t=d^2/r^2. The rim profile 1-t^4 has bounded slope and no sqrt. Far coords (4e4) std 0.535.
pebble-pack.params_text: val=0,jit=0.8,pow=0.6,rclamp=0.6,hmul=1.7,prof=1 (the code defaults: Dome). Stamped islands: val=4 (stampf=5,stampa=0.25). Per disc id: val=2. Fixed radius: fixedr=1. Big contrast: pow=3.

master.one_liner: Non-overlapping discs with pairwise weighted radii, provably disjoint, so any-node stamps need just one Source eval, in any dimension.
master.look: Prototype: separated domes of many sizes with no touching, or Perlin-textured discs. Reads as pebbles, bubbles, bacteria, polka-dot skin; used as a mask gives exactly non-colliding spot placement. Coverage is lower than expected at about 25-35%, so it looks like sparse pebbles rather than a full cobble floor unless layered.
master.algorithm: Per feature i: weight w_i (hash)^Pow. Radius r_i = min over neighbour cells j of d_ij * w_i/(w_i+w_j), clamped to 1. Pairwise proof: for any pair r_i <= d_ij*w_i/(w_i+w_j) and r_j <= d_ij*w_j/(w_i+w_j), so r_i + r_j <= d_ij, hence disjoint. The neighbour set must be symmetric. Radius is a pure function of lattice coordinates, not of the sample. Implementation: hash and store features for the 5^2 block; for each of 9 candidates compare with its 8 neighbours (72 distances) or 4 edge neighbours + 4 corners subset that is symmetric. At most one disc contains p, so select it with Select: dome height, or local coordinates (p-c)/r plus seed h for exactly 1 Source.Gen. Optional Survivor mode (Matern II): feature dies if a higher-priority neighbour is within Exclusion radius, also a pure function, giving a blue-noise spot set.
master.why_new: Size Jitter in CellularDistance produces weighted cells, not disjoint round objects with gaps. Circles cut by Max of cellular get flat clipped boundaries. The disjointness guarantee turns any-node stamping into a K=1 problem with no fade and no overlap ordering, which is what makes 3D and 4D affordable.
master.simd_plan: 2D: 25 hashes + 72 distances (store in arrays of float32v on stack, allowed as small tables) ~20-30 ns + 1 Source. 3D: 125 hashes and 27x6 face neighbours, ~80-100 ns + 1 Source. 4D: 625 hashes is too much; use 4D with 8 axial neighbours and 81 candidates, stored hash count 3^4 + 8 faces... expensive, about 300 ns; justify only for tiling or fall back to fixed radii from a fixed jitter bound (r=(1-Jitter)/2) which is free. Fixed-radius mode is a cheap 3x3 scan, which is the recommended cost-saving mode for 3D and 4D.
master.continuity: C0 with profile (1-t^2)^0.75 or lower power: c0ratio 4.67 at jit 0.5 (steep domes near the edge; sqrt profile has infinite slope at edge). Any profile reaching 0 at t=1 is seamless because radii are global.
master.params: Jitter, Pow (size contrast), Fill (<=1), Profile enum, Source (optional stamp), Exclusion Radius, Value Mode (dome, id, size)
master.risks: Only moderate coverage; a second-pass inflation would need a 7^dim window. Reduced jitter reintroduces a visible grid. Cost is quite high for what is a sparse pattern; the K=1 Source advantage is the justification. Two layers via Max would lose disjointness, though only at the combine level.
master.cost_note: 2D: 25 hashes + 72 distances (store in arrays of float32v on stack, allowed as small tables) ~20-30 ns + 1 Source.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 273.0 ns vs perlin2 49.8. Stamp 320.0 ns, 6.26x, including one perlin3 in the local frame. Fixed radius 93.4 ns, 1.83x. 3D 26 neighbours 2431.0 ns, 48.44x; 3D 6 neighbours 1612.0 ns, 32.42x. 4D fixed radius on an oblique plane 314.9 ns, 6.14x.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured on SIMD: about 25 ns 2D plus source, about 160-240 ns 3D, by scaling scalar at 10:1. The catalogue's 3D guess was 80-100 ns.
measured.c0_note: Dome 7.85, Stamp 7.76, 3D oblique plane 7.82, fixed radius 4D oblique plane 6.48.

polar-cells.look: Volcano default: a field of separate steep cones on a flat floor, each with a small summit pit and flank ribs that run down to a scalloped star shaped foot. The relief view reads at once as a volcanic archipelago with gullies. Other kinds in the sweep: star shaped sinkholes in a white plain, thin ribbed peaks, craters with irregular raised rims that overlap (Stack), and pie wedge fans. 3D XZ slice is star bursts. The 3D volume is lumpy rock clumps with a craggy surface, like asteroids.

dims.3D: works, measured, angular noise is value noise of the unit direction (no atan), vol is real
dims.4D: works, measured on an oblique plane through probe=4

polar-cells.artifacts: Mean -0.59, most of the area is floor at this density. Fans look the least natural, hard edged wedges with a hidden apex. The Fan apex first jumped (c0ratio 1.27, direction singular there), fixed by opening the sector to full near the apex, now 7.04. Tower 7.0 and Volcano 7.44 are sharp apex and rib slopes, max slope 18 per unit. The axis stat is high (53) but the FFT shows radial texture and no lattice cross, and the 4x view shows no lattice.
polar-cells.node_shape: PolarCells : Kind enum (Volcano, Bowl, Tower, Crater, Fan), Combine enum (Max, Min, Sum, Stack), Spokes (int), Gully, Harmonic, Radius, Radius Jitter, Amp From Size, Caldera, Rim Height, Rays, Density, Feather, Sector, Grid Jitter, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max
polar-cells.port_notes: 3^D window. R is clamped to (1.5 - jitter/2) / (1 + Gully*(1+Harmonic)), so a star tip cannot leave the window. Stack uses the same cell mod 3 fold order as SplatKernel rather than an age sort. 2D: fastAtan2 plus ring noise with integer index wrap; power of two Spokes would make the wrap an AND. Value noise of the unit direction scaled by Spokes works in 3D and 4D and needs no atan, and it would also work in 2D if the exact spoke count does not matter. Per lane Spokes would mean a Select, so keep it constant. Prototype's early mask skips the angular noise outside the outer radius; a port pays it for every candidate. Cost is dominated by 2 ring lookups with 4 hashes per candidate.
polar-cells.params_text: kind=0,comb=-1,spokes=12,fine=0.75,jit=0.9,rad=0.72,rjit=0.45,gully=0.32,harm=0.35,cald=0.14,dens=0.9,ampexp=0.7 (these are the defaults, volcano field). kind=1 star sinkholes, kind=2 ribbed towers, kind=3 stacked rayed craters, kind=4 fans. Vol: kind=2,comb=1,fine=0.7,dens=0.8,rad=0.8,gully=0.45,spokes=6 at iso -0.75

master.one_liner: Cellular feature field where each feature has its own polar frame and a periodic angular noise, so radially structured landforms (volcanoes with flank gullies and calderas, star-rimmed sinkholes, ribbed karst towers, star dunes, rayed craters) emerge from a single node.
master.look: Clusters of volcanic cones with radial spurs and gullies and a summit pit; fields of star-shaped sinkholes separated by sharp residual hills (cockpit karst); conical ribbed towers; with Youngest combine, overlapping craters where new ones cut old rims. Prototyped: Volcano / Cockpit / TowerKarst / YoungestWins (the last one is discontinuous as implemented, by design of the hard overwrite; a feather fixes it). Scalar cost 7.3x Perlin.
master.algorithm: Jittered lattice, 3x3 window (3x3x3 in 3D). Per cell: point c, radius R = Radius*(1 - RJit*rnd), hash h. dx,dy = p - c, r = |d|, angle in turns a = atan2(dy,dx)/(2*pi) (polynomial). Periodic angular noise: ringnoise(a, n, h) = quintic-lerp of rnd11(mix(h, k mod n)) over n lattice points on the circle (periodic by index wrap), plus a 3n harmonic at 0.25 amplitude. Star radius: R_eff = R*(1 + Gully*ang); rr = r/R_eff. Profiles (enum Kind): Volcano: cone = smoothstep(1-rr) minus 0.6*sat(1 - r/(Caldera*R))^2; Bowl (doline/cockpit): -(1-t^2)^2 with t = sat(rr); Tower: (1-t)^2; Fan: profile only inside a sector (see FanField); Crater: bowl + raised rim exp(-(rr-1)^2/s) + rays via a second angular noise with amplitude growing with r. Combine (enum): Max (hills), Min (depressions), Sum, Youngest (per-feature age hash, the newest covering feature overwrites: needs an edge feather of width Feather to stay C0). In 3D the angular noise lives on a sphere: use the two angles (atan2(dy,dx), asin(dz/r)) on a lat-long lattice, or cheaper, use 3D value noise of the unit direction scaled by n.
master.why_new: CellularDistance has no notion of 'around the feature point': every radial variation an artist wants (gullies down a cone, rays from a crater, distributaries on a fan) is impossible because the only per-cell quantities are distance and one value. Adding a per-feature periodic angular noise, with amplitude that vanishes at the apex, is the small primitive that unlocks all of these.
master.simd_plan: 9 cells x (1 Sqrt, 1 polynomial atan2, 2 periodic lerps with 4 hashes, profile ~10 ops, Select by Kind resolved at compile/dispatch time or by masks): ~5-7x Perlin in 2D; 27 cells in 3D ~20x Perlin; 4D 81 cells ~60x, feasible. Angular noise lattice index via Convert of a*n and masked wrap (n power of two preferred: wrap is an AND).
master.continuity: C0 for Max/Min/Sum (measured 7.6-7.7): the angular term is multiplied by r implicitly through rr, so the apex singularity is harmless. Youngest combine is C0 only with Feather > 0 (smoothstep between the overwriting feature's edge and its interior).
master.params: Feature Scale, Jitter, Radius, Radius Jitter, Kind enum, Combine enum, Spokes (int n), Gully (angular amplitude), Harmonic, Caldera Fraction, Rim Height (crater), Ray Length, Feather (Youngest), Density (hybrid: feature is skipped when rnd > density, so a mask thins volcanoes regionally).
master.risks: Features larger than one cell leak out of the 3x3 window (seams): clamp Radius*(1+Gully) to 1 cell. Polynomial atan2 accuracy near the +-x axis must be C0 across the branch cut (handle with the standard octant-folding form). Density thinning changes which cells participate, fine for Max/Min, slightly jumpy for Sum (feather the density too).
master.cost_note: 9 cells x (1 Sqrt, 1 polynomial atan2, 2 periodic lerps with 4 hashes, profile ~10 ops, Select by Kind resolved at compile/dispatch time or by masks): ~5-7x Perlin in 2D; 27 cells in 3D ~20x Perlin; 4D 81 cells ~60x, feasible.

poly-gauge.look: Facets: Voronoi cells become cut gems, each a pyramid with its apex at the site and straight creases running to the cell corners; hillshade shows sharp planar facets, a clearly different structure from the round cones of F1 and the roof lines of edge distance. Threshold is a set of polygons that are exact shrunken copies of the cells. The 3D volume at iso 0.05 is a heap of separate faceted rocks, each with flat faces, very convincing as rubble. Rings seen in a sweep: op art nested polygons that meet at walls. Kite mosaic: shattered tile of kites and darts, where each Delaunay edge owns one kite, that looks unlike any Voronoi mosaic.

dims.3D: works, measured: same template, z-continuity max 0.0078 for dz=1e-3
dims.4D: works, measured on an oblique plane through the same template (slice4=1): c0ratio 8.00, range -1 .. 0.911. Tiling itself not tested.

poly-gauge.range: Facets -1.000 .. 0.996, mean -0.333 over 8 seeds. Uniform -1.000 .. 1.000, mean -0.001, which confirms uniformity. Rings -1 .. 1, mean 0.000.
poly-gauge.artifacts: Two very close sites make dark needle slashes across a cell, visible in the gray image at J=0.9. FFT has strong straight rays from the planar facets, by design (axis 16.22). Measured seams against a 5x5 brute force reference: at J=1, 0.185% of 2D samples differ, worst 0.162; at J=0.9, 0.063%, worst 0.106; at J=0.8, 0.0093%, worst 0.057. 3D at J=1 0.026%, worst 0.079; at J=0.9 0.0072%, worst 0.052; at J=0.8 no samples above 1e-3 of 250000. These are small rare steps that the 7x7 continuity probe did not catch. Two catalogue claims failed when measured: (1) a pass 2 window centred on the winner seams far more, not less: at J=1 2.46% of samples differ, worst 0.79, c0ratio 1.15, because it misses neighbours two cells from the winner, while the sample window holds both sides of any wall the sample is near; (2) the dmin floor is not C0: dmin=0.25 gives c0ratio 1.10, because once the floored term is below 1 another neighbour's term can win differently on the two sides of a wall. FastNoise style jitter of 0.437 cell already bounds the closest pair at 0.126 and max slope near 30, so use jitter instead of a floor. Mode 6, a per kite apex height, jumps along the creases and is not a usable output. Continuity recheck: the probe with its samples straddling the lattice lines reads c0ratio_straddle 1.83 where the plain probe reads 8.00, and the step stays 0.077 as the probe step shrinks from 1e-4 to 1e-5, so this is a real jump on lines the plain probe never crosses, not a steep slope. So the 8.00 above does not show this default is C0.

master.one_liner: Voronoi cells turned into exact flat-faceted pyramids: 0 at the feature point, 1 on every wall, using the bisector with each neighbour.
master.look:
Cut-gem or low-poly rock cells with straight creases from the feature point to each Voronoi vertex. Rings are nested polygons rather than F1 circles. The kite mosaic looks like shattered tile and is not a Voronoi mosaic. Good for crystal ground, cobbles, stylised rock, armour plates, normal-map masks. Prototyped: rel_gauge, grid mode=0,1,2,3.
[CellCoverage, distribution-topology] Faceted pyramids with polygon contours. Halftone: stipple of shrinking and growing polygons with even blue-ish spacing whose local mean reproduces the source gray level. Good for cracked tiles, mosaics, stippled masks, exact scatter density and rubble. Measured per-cell coverage at a level targeting 30 percent over 441 cells: U mean 0.3000 std 0.0016 (pixel quantisation scale); (F1/F2)^2 std 0.039; F1^2 std 0.063.
master.algorithm:
Pass 1: normal F1 over the 3^D window, storing all p_j and keeping p_i of the winner with Select. Pass 2: g = max over j != i of 2*dot(x-p_i, p_j-p_i) / max(|p_j-p_i|^2, dmin^2). g is the polygon's gauge (Minkowski) function: g=0 at p_i, g=1 exactly on the wall with j, and linear along any ray from p_i. Outputs: (a) 1-2g, pyramid with planar facets; (b) (1-g)*v_i, per-cell apex height with walls still at a shared base; (c) tri(g*k), rings that are perfectly scaled copies of the cell polygon; (d) facet id: hash(h_i ^ h_j) of the winning j, which gives a kite mosaic where each Delaunay edge owns one kite (symmetric, so both halves match).

[CellCoverage, distribution-topology] Pass 1: find nearest site s1 and its lattice cell c1, as CellularDistance does. Pass 2: over neighbours j of c1 (window centred on c1 per lane, not on the sample, so the facet set is a pure function of the cell and cannot seam): rho = max_j 2*dot(p - s1, s_j - s1) / |s_j - s1|^2. Then rho = 0 at the site and 1 on every wall, and level sets {rho < c} are exact homothetic copies of the cell, covering exactly c^D of it. U = rho^D is exactly uniform per cell. Outputs: Uniform = 2U - 1. Halftone = smoothstep(-w, w, Level - U) with Level from a hybrid sampled at s1 (extra source eval, as CellularLookup does), so each polygon's inked area fraction equals the source value at its site.
master.why_new:
F1 gives round cones and F2-F1 gives uneven ridge height and width; neither has planar facets or a constant wall value. It needs the F1 point's relation to every neighbour, so no graph of existing nodes can produce it. The per-wall kite mosaic has no equivalent at all.
[CellCoverage, distribution-topology] F1 and F1/F2 level sets cover a different fraction per cell, so large cells fill differently from small ones. Here thresholding has an exact area meaning cell by cell, and Halftone preserves local mean without any neighbour pass. Another lab lens prototyped this gauge (rel_gauge) for its facets; the additions here are the rho^D exact-uniform output, the coverage guarantee, and area-exact halftoning.
master.simd_plan: Fixed-size stack arrays for the window points. Pass 2 uses a masked reciprocal (den floor handles j==i by giving a value below 1 once masked out). No branches. 3^D window, the same hashes as CellularDistance plus one dot and one reciprocal per cell. Estimate: about 1.4x CellularDistance (2D 5-6 ns, 3D 17 ns, 4D 60 ns). Measured scalar with 3x3: 0.8x worley2. Generic GenT works since nothing is dimension-specific. 3D prototyped through the same template.
master.continuity: C0: every wall has g=1 from both sides. check gives c0ratio 8.00 in 2D with win=1 and win=2, and z-continuity is fine in 3D. Facet-id mode is intentionally discontinuous.
master.params: Grid Jitter (hybrid), Min Spacing dmin (float), Output enum (Facets, ApexHeight, Rings, FacetId), Ring Count (hybrid), VariableRange.
master.risks:
Two very close feature points make steep needle creases (max slope about 30 without dmin). The dmin floor stays C0 because both sides of a wall use the same den. A 3x3 pass 2 can miss a neighbour outside the window at high jitter, though check showed no jumps at the FastNoise jitter radius of 0.437.
[CellCoverage, distribution-topology] Exact homothety needs Euclidean bisectors, so other distance functions do not apply. 4D is expensive. Reduced 3^D windows need the jitter limit or facets will be missed and contours bend. Halftone Level sampled at the site makes spot size stepwise per cell, which is correct but visible at low density.
master.cost_note: Estimate: about 1.4x CellularDistance (2D 5-6 ns, 3D 17 ns, 4D 60 ns). Measured scalar with 3x3: 0.8x worley2.
master.variant_notes: The polygonal gauge, with rho^D making output exactly uniform per cell (CellCoverage), so a threshold covers exactly X percent of every cell (measured std 0.0016 vs 0.063 for F1^2). Halftone and kite-facet outputs included.

rosette-cells.look: A coat of separate marks: each is a mid gray rounded plate with three to six bright dashes around it, sometimes with a centre dot. It is clearly a rosette arrangement and much closer to leopard or jaguar than a thresholded F1 ring, but stylised: at smaller rings it reads as sprockets or paw prints. Warp 0.12 only slightly softens it. In 3D the volume is a cloud of balls cut into stripes and patches, like sliced fruit, and the XZ slice shows striped discs, not rosettes.

dims.3D: works, measured, broken spherical shells from a cos product
dims.4D: runs on an oblique plane through probe=4, same shell form

rosette-cells.artifacts: Rosettes that crowd a neighbour are cut by a straight line, the Voronoi edge through the F2-F1 fade, which looks mechanical. Lowering jitter to 0.6 removed some of that but then lattice rows showed in the 4x view, so jitter stays at 0.75. c0ratio 4.35 is steepness, not jumps: it rises to 7.72 at fine=0.25 as the same shapes get bigger; max slope 407 per unit comes from lobes changing fast near the apex. 3D lobes read as stripes because they are a product of two cosines.
rosette-cells.node_shape: RosetteCells : Ring Radius, Radius Jitter, Ring Width (hybrid), Lobes Min, Lobes Max, Lobe Bias, Wobble, Inner Tone, Dot Probability, Dot Radius, Edge Fade, Grid Jitter (hybrid), Feature Scale, Seed Offset
rosette-cells.port_notes: Same cellular pass as CellularDistance, keeping F1, F2, nearest vector and hash. No atan: cos(n theta + phi) comes from powers of (dx + i dy), written as fixed terms up to T6 with Select by per-lane n. Prototype uses an actual loop for n but the same maths. Keep the ring off the apex with a fade on F1. Unsolved: cell-edge clipping and the stylised shape; a real coat needs a DomainWarp in front and softer dashes.

master.one_liner: Leopard and jaguar coats: each cell holds a broken wobbly ring, a darker interior and sometimes a centre dot, shaped by one polar evaluation at the nearest seed.
master.look: Clusters of 3-6 dark blobs around a slightly darker centre: recognisable as leopard rosettes. Lobe count, ring radius and dot probability span spots to rosettes to jaguar. Also applicable to lichen or coral polyps with altered profiles.
master.algorithm: Find F1, F2, nearest vector v and hash in the 3^D window. dir=v/|v|. n=3+floor(4*r3); wobble=1+0.18*cos2(dir,phi)+0.1*cos3(dir,phi), using Chebyshev forms; rr=R*(0.75+0.5*r5). ring=smoothstep(w,0.5w,|F1-rr*wobble|); lobes=smoothstep(-0.25,0.15,cosn(dir,phi)); inner=smoothstep(rr,0.7rr,F1)*0.35; dot=(r6<0.3)*smoothstep(0.07,0.04,F1); edge=smoothstep(0,0.12,F2-F1); out=max(ring*lobes,inner,dot)*edge. cos(n*theta+phi) comes from rotating dir by phi with a table or by recurrence, so atan is not needed. In 3D: shell(F1) with lobes from a product of cos along hash axes.
master.why_new: Reaction-diffusion gets rosettes by simulation, with tissue growth, which is not pointwise. Graphs can threshold F1 into rings but cannot break each ring with its own angular lobes.
master.simd_plan: Cellular pass plus one polar evaluation: about 5.5 ns in 2D (1.4x CellularDistance), 14 ns in 3D, 43 ns in 4D. n varies per lane, so use a Select between precomputed recurrence terms up to T6, or fix n per node for lower cost.
master.continuity: C0: a seam at the F1 switch is removed by edge (F2-F1), which zeroes the field at the cell boundary. Dense scanlines: 0 jumps. Random-pair ratio 9.9.
master.params: Ring Radius, Ring Width (hybrid), Lobes Min/Max, Lobe Sharpness, Inner Tone, Dot Probability, Wobble, Grid Jitter (hybrid).
master.risks: Stylised and specialised, so less of a general building block. The prototype used atan2; the Chebyshev port is untested but mathematically equal. Cell-confined rings are clipped by edge when the seed is close to a neighbour. The Malheiros preprint PDF was unreadable through the fetch tool, so biological staging is not drawn from it.
master.cost_note: Cellular pass plus one polar evaluation: about 5.5 ns in 2D (1.4x CellularDistance), 14 ns in 3D, 43 ns in 4D. n varies per lane, so use a Select between precomputed recurrence terms up to T6, or fix n per node for lower cost.

sign-code-regions.look: ID mode: a curved camouflage mosaic. Rounded regions of many sizes in flat tones, overlapping like layered tissue paper, curves running straight through each other in X crossings. Regions are non-convex and vary a lot in size. It does not read as Voronoi at all. Lac above 1.5 goes noisy, near 1 it is cleanest. Parity: a black and white woodcut of interlocking curved shapes, very graphic, the crossings show plainly. Soft parity at lac 1: smooth undulating surface with pits and creases, a bit like hammered metal; at lac 1.6 it is grainy with flat gray. Weighted: soft terraced clouds, close to plain fbm, the dullest mode. 3D parity vol: interlocked sheets with hard edges, cut faces with sliver patterns. Hillshade of ID shows thin dark and light borders, as expected for jumps.
sign-code-regions.dims: 2D and 3D measured (real Eval3 with perlin3). The 3D z-continuity max of 1.92 per 1e-3 is the region jumps, as in 2D. 4D uses the same loop with a 4D source and needs no window; not run here.
sign-code-regions.range: [-0.997, 0.991] over 8 seeds in ID mode; values come from the hash of the code. Far coords fine, no NaN. Only 2^Bits distinct values per seed; the histogram panel shows discrete bars.
sign-code-regions.artifacts: Thin slivers where two curves run nearly together, visible in parity and vol, sometimes with stair stepped edges at pixel scale because of jumps. Same code value recurs across the map, so distant regions share a tone; fine for biomes, not for unique IDs. No antialiasing at borders in ID mode. Curves come from a low octave source, so at wide view the mosaic is an even texture without large scale variation.
sign-code-regions.node_shape: SignCodeRegions: Source (GeneratorSource), Bits (int), Lacunarity, Threshold (hybrid), Threshold Jitter, Softness (beta), Mode enum {ID, Parity, Soft Parity, Weighted}, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
sign-code-regions.port_notes: No window and no search. Integer code in lanes: code = code * 2 - mask (a true mask is -1). Parity needs popcount, or running xor of the bits, which is simpler in lanes. Finish with the standard hash. Source is called at seed + i and position * f, one call per bit, so cost is Bits x source. The prototype's Threshold Jitter draws a per bit offset from a hash of the seed and bit index, which varies the area each bit covers. A graph cannot do this, since no sign and integer hash node exists; only Weighted can be approximated by Terrace plus Add.

master.one_liner: Regions keyed by the sign bits of several noises, hashed to a value: curved mosaics with X-junctions instead of Voronoi Y-junctions.
master.look: Tested. Same-frequency bits look like overlapping translucent curved shapes, as in layered tissue-paper collage. Lacunarity 1.4 gives multi-scale curved camouflage. Curves cross straight through each other. Uses: biome and territory IDs with curved borders, geological cross-cutting veins, camouflage, stained glass that is not Voronoi.
master.algorithm:
code=0; f=1. For i in 0..Bits-1: code=code*2 + (S(seed+i, p*f) > Threshold); f*=Lacunarity.
Out=rndNeg1To1(hash(code, seed)).
Optional modes: Parity (xor of all bits, two-colour map with soft variant product of Clamp(beta*n_i)); Weighted (sum 2^-i * sign, ordered plateaus, soft variant with Clamp(beta*n)).
master.why_new: Every region node on the sheet is Voronoi, with convex-ish cells, Y-junctions and uniform size. This yields non-convex regions of wildly varied size with X-junctions, and a stable per-region value, with no window at all. It cannot be expressed in the graph, since there is no sign or hash-of-int node.
master.simd_plan: Branch free. Bits constant loop: Bits x source (Bits=5, Perlin: about 5.5 / 11 / 21 ns for 2D / 3D / 4D). Integer code in lanes, standard hash finish. Identical code for all dimensions. No window.
master.continuity: Discontinuous by design at region borders (ID mode). The soft Parity and Weighted modes are C0.
master.params: Int: Bits. Float: Lacunarity. Hybrid: Threshold (per bit via offset), Softness. Source required.
master.risks: Many tiny slivers occur when curves nearly coincide or lacunarity is high. With few bits the 2^Bits values collide and repeat across the map by construction, so non-adjacent regions with the same code share a value; that is a feature for biomes but not for unique IDs. A soft ParityFractal mode looked noisy in the prototype, so keep it optional.
master.cost_note: Bits constant loop: Bits x source (Bits=5, Perlin: about 5.5 / 11 / 21 ns for 2D / 3D / 4D).

measured.scalar_note: Measured with defaults: 5 bits with a built-in 2 octave source, so 10 perlin2 evals. With oct=1 (5 evals) 361.8 ns against perlin2 50.7 ns, about 7.1x. In a real node the source is a generic input.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 5 bits of Perlin 5.5 / 11 / 21 ns in 2D / 3D / 4D plus a hash finish, as the catalogue says; double with a 2 octave source.
measured.c0_note: 1.0 is by design in ID and Parity modes, region borders are jumps. Soft Parity and Weighted are C0 through the clamp.

splat-kernel.look: Crater default: flat plain with round pits of many sizes, raised rims, later craters cutting earlier rims. The relief view reads straight away as a cratered moon surface. Sweep of the other kernels: Cone gives soft peaks, Wyvill merges into metaball slugs, Ring gives overlapping ring stains, GaborScratch gives thin straight hairlines at random angles on flat gray, Dome+Max gives a heap of overlapping balls. In 3D the Ring kernel makes intersecting hollow shells like cut foam.

dims.3D: works, measured, Eval3 real: Ring gives hollow spherical shells in vol
dims.4D: works, measured on an oblique plane through probe=4

splat-kernel.artifacts: Sum kernels spend most of their area on the floor (mean about -0.8). Dome has c0ratio 2.86 from its vertical rim tangent, by design. GaborScratch 6.71 because the lines are very thin; its carrier is barely visible at aspect 8, it reads as a line and not a wave packet. Sum gains are measured constants for default params, so they need recomputing from radius and density in a port. FFT shows concentric rings from the disc shape, no lattice cross. No lattice visible in the 4x view.

splat-kernel.port_notes: 3^D window. Stack is not a sort: candidates are folded in an order fixed by (cell mod 3) per axis, the window holds exactly one cell per colour, so every sample agrees on the order and lerp(h, k, cover) is C0 (measured 7.99). Overlap order is then lattice colour order, which I could not see as a pattern in the sheet. Kernel and Combine resolved outside the loop. Sqrt per candidate can be skipped for Wyvill. Reach limit rad <= 1.5 - jitter/2. Overlaps dome-heap at Dome+Max and the judged crater-field node, which has size levels and ejecta that this one does not.
