queue.name: SplatKernel
queue.reason: Lewis sparse convolution with a kernel enum in the Cellular loop. thin-spots and isolated-extrema-noise are modes. Check the density-dependent normaliser.

master.one_liner: Sparse-convolution noise with a shaped per-feature kernel (crater, bump, cone, ring, Gabor scratch, Wyvill blob) and per-point size/amplitude/orientation jitter, combined by Sum / Max / Nearest-on-top: craters, boulders, metaballs, scratches, spots (Lewis 1989 sparse convolution; PPTBF windowed-Gabor kernels, Guehl 2020).
master.look: Lunar/planetary crater fields with raised rims and overlap ordering, boulder/cobble fields (Dome+Max), metaball slime (Wyvill+Sum), scratches and brushed hairline marks (GaborScratch), polka/spot stains, pebble beaches. Shape-driven features rather than distance fields, visibly different from CellularDistance's smooth bowls.
master.algorithm:
Params: Kernel enum {Cone, Gaussian, Wyvill, Crater, Ring, GaborScratch, Dome}, Combine enum {Sum, Max, Min, NearestOnTop}, Radius (hybrid, <=0.5 cell for a 3x3 window... use 3^dim window with Radius<=1.0 cell), RadiusJitter, AmpJitter (float), Density (hybrid 0..1: probability a cell has a feature), Profile params (CraterDepth, RimWidth, ScratchFreq, ScratchLength).
Gen(p): ic = floor(p), fp = p - ic; acc = identity for Combine; for each offset o in [-1..1]^dim (fixed): c = ic+o; h = hash(seed,c); present = rnd01(h) < Density; centre = o + rnd(h) (jitter in [0,1)^dim); R = Radius * (1 + RadiusJitter*(rnd-0.5)); A = 1 + AmpJitter*(rnd-0.5); d = |fp - centre| / R (0 at centre, 1 at rim); k = kernel(d, dirs from h): Cone: 1-d; Gaussian: exp(-4d^2); Wyvill: (1-d^2)^3; Dome: sqrt(max(0,1-d^2)); Crater: -CraterDepth*(1-d^2)^2 + rimHeight*exp(-((d-1)/RimWidth)^2) (bowl plus raised rim, then clamp to d<1+2RimWidth); Ring: exp(-((d-0.7)/0.1)^2); GaborScratch: exp(-4 d^2 * aspect) * cos(2pi ScratchFreq * dot(fp-centre, dir_h)) with an elongated Gaussian along dir_h (PPTBF-style window x Gabor). All masked to 0 where d>=1 (or 1+rim) and where !present.
Combine: Sum: acc += A*k; Max: acc = max(acc, A*k); NearestOnTop: keep the k of the cell whose rnd 'height' is largest among overlapping kernels (Select by a per-cell priority) -> crater overlap order like real impact sequences. Normalise: Sum by sqrt(expected count) (measured constant), others already in [-1,1].
3D: 27-cell window, spherical kernels (craters in 3D = cavities in a density field); 4D: 81 cells (justified only for tiling).

[SparseImpulse (Craters, Boulders), lattice-kernels] For window points: gate = smoothstep(0, Softness, Density(x) - rnd01(h)). Density is sampled at the sample position, so features fade in and out rather than pop, keeping C0 with a per-lane hybrid. Radius R = lerp(Rmin, Rmax, rnd^k), heavy tailed. t = |v|/R. Profile enum: Crater = (t<1 ? t^2-1 : 0) + RimH*exp(-(t-1)^2*RimS) with outer fade; Bump = (1-t^2)^3; Ring = bump((t-1)/w); Dipole = (g.v/R)*(1-t^2)^3. Sum = sum(gate * R^AmpExp * profile(t)). Clamp or normalise by a measured constant.
master.why_new: CellularDistance only gives distances; shaping it with Remap/Terrace cannot produce overlapping summed features, raised rims, elongated scratches, or density thinning. This is the general sparse-convolution node FastNoise lacks (and the PPTBF paper shows a windowed Gabor kernel covers cells/cracks/grains/scratches/spots/stains/waves).
master.simd_plan: Same lattice window and loop structure as CellularDistance (3^dim fixed loop), per cell one hash + kernel (<= 1 Exp + 1 Cos). 2D ~ CellularDistance2D x 1.3; 3D ~ 27 kernels ~ 1.5x CellularDistance3D. Kernel/Combine enums resolved outside the loop (template or per-node switch), branch-free inside.
master.continuity: C1 for Bump and Crater (t^2 factor at the boundary), C0 for Cone, discontinuous for Disc. Max combine is C0. Measured c0ratio 8.0 for Crater.
master.params: Kernel (enum), Combine (enum), Radius (hybrid), RadiusJitter, AmpJitter, Density (hybrid), CraterDepth, RimWidth, ScratchFreq, ScratchAspect, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
master.risks:
Radius must stay within the window (clamp to 1 cell, else seams). Sum normalisation depends on Density/Radius (compute expected variance analytically from the kernel or scale at param-set time). GaborScratch at high frequency aliases like any oscillatory kernel.
[Splatter, terrain-tools-engines] Extent <= 1 cell bounds the largest shape to about half the point spacing (use fractal octaves or a coarser cell with K>1 for big+small mixes); Source kernel cost; variance normalisation in Sum mode depends on Density and SizeBias (measure).
master.cost_note: 2D ~ CellularDistance2D x 1.3; 3D ~ 27 kernels ~ 1.5x CellularDistance3D.
master.variant_notes: Sparse convolution with analytic kernels. SparseImpulse contributes the smooth density gate that keeps a hybrid Density continuous; Splatter adds K>1 kernels per cell and a Source kernel mode that overlaps StampScatter.

thin-spots.look: Patches of round whole spots of mixed sizes on a flat floor, thinning to fewer and smaller spots toward the patch edge, never cut by the mask. Threshold view shows dotted patch borders. With prof=2 it is black pits on white like rust pitting or leather pores, prof=3 rings like bubbles. In 3D the volume is a cloud of separate balls that gets sparser and smaller away from the dense core.

dims.3D: works, measured, Eval3 real (vol shows balls)
dims.4D: works on an oblique plane through probe=4, coverage built from two perlin3 because the harness has no perlin4

thin-spots.artifacts: Spots stay at one per cell, so dense regions saturate at a fixed packing, not a solid mass. Flat floor makes the mean strongly negative. c0ratio 5.26 for the lens profile is steep small rims (max slope 127 per unit at fine=3), not jumps; the cone profile measures 7.93. A relief view of pits at hscale 90 gave deep shafts, it is not a terrain and I deleted that image.
thin-spots.node_shape: ThinSpots : Coverage (hybrid), Radius (hybrid), Softness, Size Jitter, Grid Jitter, Profile enum (Lens, Dome, Pit, Ring, Cone), Output enum (Height, SpotValue), Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max
thin-spots.port_notes: 3^D candidates, one hash per candidate plus mixed bit fields, coverage read once per lane before the loop. No sqrt needed for Lens or Pit because the profile uses d2 only. Height multiplied by on so a spot reaches 0 before its radius does, keeping C0. Reach limit: rad below 1.5 - jitter/2.
thin-spots.params_text: fine=3,rad=0.55,sjit=0.5,jit=0.85,soft=0.35,covf=0.11,cgain=2.2,cbias=0.55,covo=3,prof=0 (these are the defaults; prof=2 pits, prof=3 rings, prof=4 cone; cov=1,cval=x constant coverage)

master.one_liner: Per-spot thresholding against a coverage hybrid read once at the sample, so whole spots shrink away individually instead of being cut by a mask: pits, freckles, rust pores, lichen, stipple.
master.look: Look-tested (m=1). Clusters of full round spots fade to a dithered edge of ever smaller spots following the low-frequency field, unlike Multiply where spots are sliced. Reads as rust pitting edge, leopard fade, gravel patches, pores on leather. Coverage can be a StrataBands output for ring-porous wood pores.
master.algorithm: C=Coverage(p), one hybrid eval per lane. For each cell in 3x3: centre c(h), threshold t=rnd(h), size s=R*(.5+.5*rnd). on=smoothstep(t,t+Soft,C*(1+Soft)). r=s*on. d2=|p-c|^2/(r^2+eps). Spot profile Dome (sqrt(1-d2)), Pit (negative), Ring (rim) or Cone, masked when d2<1. Output Max (or Min for pits). Since C is read at the lane, a spot's radius near its threshold varies gently over its own disc. Reach fits window if R<=1-jit/2.
master.why_new: CellularDistance cannot change density across space, and Multiply or Remap with a mask truncates features. The hard thing it makes easy is spatially varying feature density with intact features, for just one coverage eval, where CellularLookup style sampling would need 9.
master.simd_plan: 9 candidates, 1 hash plus mix bit fields, 1 optional sqrt deferred until the max (track max of 1-d2): about CellularDistance 2D cost, 3.5x Perlin. Coverage is 1 eval. Scalar proto 6x Perlin with a 3-octave fbm coverage. 3D 27 candidates, about CellularDistance 3D. 4D 81, about CellularDistance 4D, so real tiling works.
master.continuity: C0 everywhere with Coverage continuous, since r goes to 0 smoothly and profile is 0 at the rim. Measured c0ratio 3.3 because Dome has a vertical tangent at the rim; Cone or a (1-d2)^2 profile gives C1 and measured smoothness.
master.params: Coverage (hybrid), Radius (hybrid), Softness, Size Jitter, Grid Jitter, Profile enum, Combine enum (Max, Min), plus Value mode to output a per-spot value.
master.risks: Fast-varying Coverage distorts spot shape (they become egg-shaped), which is usually fine. High coverage saturates at a fixed density, so a second layer is needed for dense packing. R above window budget produces seams, so clamp it.
master.cost_note: 9 candidates, 1 hash plus mix bit fields, 1 optional sqrt deferred until the max (track max of 1-d2): about CellularDistance 2D cost, 3.5x Perlin.

wandering-columns.look: 3D is the real result. Columns view: a bundle of round columns that lean, wave and squeeze past each other, like kelp or bent organ pipes, with cut faces showing them narrowing and swelling. Walls view (F2 - F1): a honeycomb of thin walls that twists along the axis, cells opening and closing as columns pass each other, top face a clean Voronoi, sides with curved sheet walls; looks like coral or a stretched sponge. Beaded view: swelling and pinching tongues, more chaotic, like flames. 2D default: bright strands waving along y and crossing in X shapes, like braided hair or a curtain. XZ slice is a standard Voronoi, as expected.
wandering-columns.dims: 2D and 3D measured. 4D is the 3D window with w added to the phase: I tested w as a param (check at w=1.57, c0ratio 8.0, frames). Loop is exact in form because the harmonics use phase and 2 x phase; not numerically tested as it was for the blob nodes.
wandering-columns.range: [-1, 1] over 8 seeds, clamped; far coords fine; no NaN; 3D z-continuity max 0.0022 per 1e-3
wandering-columns.artifacts: The 2D form's F2 - F1 has horizontal bars where two strands cross, because 1D F2 - F1 is constant outside a close pair; that is why 2D defaults to F1. Slice 1 reduces the bars but costs 9 cells. Bending is visibly wavy at this kappa, though the second harmonic hides the sine shape. Strong axis in the 2D FFT and in any vertical slice, by design. Columns never branch. Beaded F2 - F1 is only approximate, since the taper is not a metric.
wandering-columns.node_shape: WanderingColumns: Axis enum, Wander Amp, Bend Frequency, Second Harmonic (amp and ratio), Jitter, Taper, Phase (w rate), Distance enum, Output enum {F1, F2 - F1, Value}, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
wandering-columns.port_notes: Cellular.inl 2D window with an offset per cell. Sin and Cos of the path are lane wide, computed once, and each column rotates them with a table, so cost is 2-4 FMA per cell. Keep J + amp <= 1 (Cellular's jitter bound); defaults J 0.5 with half-range offset and amp 0.42 fit it. Harmonic 2's w rate must be an integer multiple for a closed loop; my first code used 1.3 and I changed it to 2. Unlike a warp of Cellular 2D, adjacency between cells changes along the axis, which the walls view shows.
wandering-columns.params_text: defaults: out=0,slice=0,jit=0.5,amp=0.42,kappa=1.1,k2=1.73,a2=0.45,phase=1,w=0 ; 3D columns: out=0 with --iso 0.2 ; twisting walls: out=1 with --iso 0.35 ; beaded: out=0,taper=0.45,kappa=2 with --iso 0.25 ; 2D as a vertical slice of 3D: slice=1,sz=0.5

master.one_liner: A 2D cellular field whose feature points wander independently along the third axis on closed sinusoidal paths: bundles of bending columns and twisting honeycomb cracks at Cellular-2D cost in 3D, phase-animated by w.
master.look: 3D: a forest of vertical columns that lean, bend and squeeze past each other (basalt columns with curvature, organ pipes, kelp, cable bundles, vertical cave shafts); F2-F1 iso-surface: a honeycomb of crack walls that twist with height; Taper makes beaded or budding columns. Horizontal 2D slice: an ordinary Voronoi that morphs as you move up (cells change neighbours); vertical slice: wavy curtains / wood-grain bands.
master.algorithm:
Axis = Y (enum). Window 3x3 in (x,z). Per cell k: h = Hash(k); base c = k + 0.5 + Jitter*rnd2(h); phases phi1, phi2 from bits (table); S,C = Sin/Cos(Kappa*y + Phase*w) once per lane;
 c(y) = c + WanderAmp * (S*cphi1 + C*sphi1, S*cphi2 + C*sphi2)   // each column follows its own ellipse as y changes
 optional second harmonic from more bits for less regular paths; optional per-column radius modulation rho(y) = 1 + Taper*(S*cphi3 + C*sphi3) applied as d / rho (columns swell and pinch)
 d = |(x,z) - c(y)| (Euclid; or the Cellular distance enum)
 keep F1, F2, winner hash. Outputs: F1, F2-F1 (cracks between columns), Value (column id), F1 with SizeJitter.
Validity: Jitter + WanderAmp <= 1 (same bound class as Cellular jitter). 2D Gen: a 1D window of 3 cells in x with centres wandering along y: wavy vertical bands. 4D: w adds phase (loops with period 2pi/Phase), tiles via GenTileable2D because continuous in all four coords.
master.why_new: AddDimension(Cellular 2D) gives straight prisms; DomainWarp bends all columns coherently with the same field, never past each other and never changing cell adjacency. Independent per-column motion changes the topology and costs ~1/3 of Cellular 3D.
master.simd_plan: Cellular.inl 2D window loop plus one Sin/Cos per lane and 2-4 FMAs per cell for the phase-table recombination. 3D ~1.3x CellularDistance 2D (~5 ns), 2D ~2 ns (3-cell window), 4D same as 3D.
master.continuity: F1/F2-F1: C0 like Cellular; the column paths are C-infinity in y and w.
master.params: Axis enum, WanderAmp, Kappa (bend frequency along the axis), Jitter, Taper, Phase (w rate), Distance enum, Output enum (F1 / F2-F1 / Value), Feature Scale, Seed.
master.risks: With one harmonic the bending is visibly sinusoidal; add a second harmonic or a hybrid WanderAmp. Columns are strictly non-branching (that is also the feature).
master.cost_note: 3D ~1.3x CellularDistance 2D (~5 ns), 2D ~2 ns (3-cell window), 4D same as 3D.

measured.scalar_note: Measured with defaults (3 cell 2D form), 1.62x worley2. The 9 cell form that 3D uses measured 595 ns through slice=1, against perlin2 50.7 ns, about 11.7x. Each column's phases use real cos and sin in the scalar code; a port has them in a table.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 3D about 5-7 ns (9 cells plus 2 Sin and Cos pairs per lane), 2D about 2-3 ns, 4D same as 3D.

fractal-spectrum.look: Center hybrid: blobs change size continuously across the image at unchanged contrast, big soft forms in one corner running into near pixel grit in another. The threshold panel shows the blob size gradient plainly, and the histogram stays Gaussian. Detail mode (shape=1): reads like FBm hills, but some flanks are glass smooth and others rough, with no contrast change, and the relief view looks like a believable landscape with rough patches. Two bands: large soft hills covered in fine sand with nothing between, clearly different from plain FBm in the hillshade. Narrow width without a hybrid gives a band pass labyrinth that looks like one Perlin octave. Volume: pore size runs from large caverns to fine sponge across one cube.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3 with a fixed rotation per octave, z-continuity max 0.0065 for dz=1e-3, vol rendered
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D path; the algorithm only needs source calls and one 4D rotation constant

fractal-spectrum.range: default -0.828 .. 0.866 over 8 seeds, mean 0.000 (K=0.72 measured scale). 3D is lower: -0.638 .. 0.570 on one slice, std 0.166 vs 0.213 in 2D, so 3D wants its own constant.
fractal-spectrum.artifacts: No seams, FFT is radially symmetric. Pattern Odd looks the same as All in gray at flat tilt, and Cantor is only mildly different, so these two enums are not worth having; All and Two Bands are enough. Two bands alone is reachable with Add of two FBm, so the unique part is the hybrid Center, Width or Detail with variance normalisation. All octaves are paid for even where their weight is near zero.
fractal-spectrum.node_shape: FractalSpectrum : Generator. Source, Octaves (int), Lacunarity, Center (hybrid), Width (hybrid), Tilt (hybrid), Detail (hybrid, alternative weight shape: Gain^i * sat(Detail - i)), Shape enum (Bell, Detail), Pattern enum (All, Two Bands), Octave Rotation (bool), VariableRange.
fractal-spectrum.port_notes: Fractal.inl octave loop with per octave weight computed from hybrids sampled once, sum and n2 accumulated, then sum * InvSqrt(n2 + eps) * K. Use the compact bell (1 - u^2/9)^3 clamped if Exp shows in a profile (compact=1 is implemented). Rotation is a per octave constant, composed in the loop: golden angle in 2D, a fixed Rodrigues matrix in 3D. A 4D rotation still has to be chosen. Measured range stays inside +/-1 in 2D with K=0.72 for all three modes tested. Hybrid cost is one source sample per hybrid.
fractal-spectrum.params_text: plain render is oct=6,f0=0.5,center=2.2,cvar=3,width=1,hf=0.22 (Center hybrid). Rough terrain mode: shape=1,detail=3.5,cvar=4,gain=0.5. Two bands: pat=3,tilt=1,width=50,cvar=0,oct=7. Vol image: cvar=2.5,center=2,f0=1,oct=5

queue.name: FractalSpectrum
queue.reason: Hybrid per-octave weights at constant variance: a strong graph control that is still FBm visually. Only normalisation needs testing.

master.one_liner: Fractal driven like an equaliser: hybrid Center, Width and Tilt in octave units, at constant variance everywhere, with optional Cantor or two-band spectra.
master.look:
Smooth patches running into gritty ones with no change in contrast. Sweeping Center is a zoom through scale without changing the pattern's seeds. Narrow Width gives clean band-pass labyrinth patterns. Two-band spectra give large soft forms with fine grit and nothing in between, which FBm can never do.
[FractalSpectrum, hierarchy-multiscale] Same family as FBm but (a) detail amount varies across space without any seam or popping (LOD by camera distance, roughness maps, 'fine detail only in valleys'), (b) spectra that are not power laws: peaked mid-band (sand ripples over smooth dunes), hollowed mid-band (big shapes + grain only), rising-to-fine (blue-ish grain), and (c) no octave lattice alignment (RotationStep ~ golden angle) so the sheet's faint grid-like crossings in multi-octave Perlin/Value disappear.
master.algorithm:
For i in 0..Octaves-1: x=(i-Center(p))/Width(p). w_i=Bell(x)*2^(-Tilt(p)*i)*Pattern[i]. Bell is exp(-x^2/2) or the cheaper compact (1-x^2/9)^3 clamped. Pattern is a constant table from an enum: All, Odd only, Cantor (digits 0,2 in base 3), or Two Bands. sum+=w_i*Source(seed+i, R^i*p*Lac^i), with R a fixed golden-angle rotation (2D) or fixed rotation matrix per octave. Output=sum/sqrt(sum w_i^2+eps), so local variance is constant regardless of how many bands are active.

[FractalSpectrum, hierarchy-multiscale] Precompute when params change (small tables, MaxOctaves <= 16): for octave i: a_i from log-linear interpolation of (Coarse, Mid, Fine) at i = 0, N/2, N multiplied by Gain^i; freq_i = prod_{j<i} Lacunarity * 2^(rnd11(seed,j)*LacJitter); R_i = rotation by i*RotationStep (2D angle; 3D: rotation about a hashed axis per octave; 4D: two plane rotations) composed, stored as matrices.
  Gen: det = Detail(p) (hybrid, 0..MaxOctaves); F=0; n2=0
  for i in 0..MaxOctaves-1 (uniform):
     w_i = a_i * Min(Max(det - i, 0), 1)      // last partial octave fades in linearly (or smoothstep)
     F += w_i * noise(R_i * p * freq_i, seed+i)
     n2 += w_i * w_i
  out = F * InvSqrt(n2 + eps) * NormGain       // variance-preserving: amplitude independent of how many octaves are on
Optional: Weighted Strength and Ridged variants reuse the same weights.
master.why_new: Hybrid Gain on FBm can only tilt from the top scale and changes contrast. Width and Center are the parameters artists actually think about (feature size and how many sizes), and bimodal or gapped spectra are not reachable by any Gain or Lacunarity setting. Per-lane normalisation is impossible in a graph without many extra nodes.
master.simd_plan: Same as FBm: Octaves evals of the source regardless of weight (no skip possible), plus about 8 ops per octave for weight. Golden-angle rotation is a per-octave constant. Cost: octaves x source + 3 hybrid evals. Exp can be replaced with the polynomial.
master.continuity: C1 if source and hybrids are C1. Measured c0ratio 5.05 only because high octaves are steep; no jumps seen.
master.params: Source, Octaves (int), Lacunarity, Center (hybrid), Width (hybrid), Tilt (hybrid), Pattern enum, Octave Rotation.
master.risks:
Output is not bounded by construction: measured about +/-1.46. Needs measured scaling or soft clamp. All octaves cost even when weighted zero. Cantor and Odd patterns may look only subtly different from FBm; only Bell with varying Center and Width was prototyped.
[FractalSpectral, signal-phase] Weight renormalisation per lane changes the variance where few octaves are active (RMS mode fixes). All octaves are always paid for even where the band excludes them (inherent to data-parallel). Name clash risk with 'band-pass' expectations: it is a band in octave index, not a spatial filter.
[FractalSpectrum, hierarchy-multiscale] Low novelty by design; its value is usability. Variance normalisation changes the look relative to FBm when Detail is low (single octave at full amplitude).
master.cost_note: Cost: octaves x source + 3 hybrid evals.
master.variant_notes: Per-lane octave weights with variance normalisation. Includes hybrid band Center/Width/Tilt, gapped spectra (Cantor, two-band), a fractional Detail cut-off, and per-octave rotation and lacunarity jitter.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 9.53x perlin2 (480.6 ns vs 50.4 ns), 6 octaves plus 1 hybrid perlin. Plain 6 octave FBm through the same harness code measured 524.0 ns in the same run, so the spectrum weights are not measurable above timing noise. Both numbers include about 18 std::map param lookups per sample, which a port does not pay.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D about 8 ns, 3D about 16 ns, 4D about 30 ns at 6 octaves of Perlin (handbook octave costs plus one hybrid source and about 8 ops per octave).

iso-focus-fractal.look: Smooth bald domes and smooth basins joined by a crinkled green band exactly at the level. The threshold panel shows a real fractal coast with inlets and small islands, while the gray field is calm away from it. The histogram is bimodal with a dip at the level. Relief: rounded hills with rough skirts at the waterline; striking, a bit stylised for terrain. Volume: at iso 0 a fully rugged rock surface, at iso 0.55 the same field gives smooth pebbles, which shows the idea working in 3D. Moving the level with a hybrid moves the crinkled band to other heights.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3, z-continuity max 0.0155 for dz=1e-3, vol rendered at two iso values
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D path; the algorithm only needs source calls

iso-focus-fractal.range: -0.973 .. 0.955 over 8 seeds, mean 0.001, with K=0.36 (measured). 3D slice -0.609 .. 0.470, std 0.255 vs 0.370 in 2D.
iso-focus-fractal.artifacts: At focus 0.25 and gain 0.5 a ribbed contour shows along the shore, a visible step where the gate shuts. Default settings keep that small but a thin shelf around the coast is still readable in the hillshade. Level values far from the source range get no detail, as expected. Did not measure coastline equality against FBm of the same seed; the coast differs in detail from plain FBm because gated octaves are smaller on the way there.
iso-focus-fractal.node_shape: IsoFocusFractal : Generator. Source, Octaves (int), Gain (hybrid), Lacunarity, Level (hybrid), Focus (hybrid), Octave Rotation (bool), VariableRange.
iso-focus-fractal.port_notes: Fractal.inl octave loop with rem tracked as a per octave constant table, plus Abs, one smoothstep and FMulAdd per octave. Range constant measured at gain 0.65; it depends on gain, so a port needs a small fit or a table. Gate radius is relative to rem, which also makes the node stable against Octaves changes. 4D needs nothing extra.
iso-focus-fractal.params_text: plain render is oct=7,gain=0.65,focus=0.55,lac=2,f0=0.5,level=0 with golden angle octave rotation. Level hybrid: lvar=0.6,lf=0.3. Vol images: f0=1 with --iso 0 and --iso 0.55. Reference FBm: plain=1

master.one_liner: Octaves that exist only near a chosen level set: fractal coastlines and surfaces with smooth interiors, at FBm cost.
master.look: Soft hills and basins with an intricately crinkled shore. In 3D, smooth cave-field interiors with a detailed surface, closer to a distance field. A threshold looks like FBm but the height field does not.
master.algorithm: rem=sum of amplitudes. h=a0*Source0. For i=1..Octaves-1: rem-=a_(i-1); gate=1-smoothstep(0, Focus*0.7*rem, |h-Level(p)|); h+=a_i*Source_i(p)*gate. The gate radius tracks how much the remaining octaves could still move the value, so with Focus>=1 almost any point able to change sides of the level still gets all its detail. Points that could never reach the level stay smooth.
master.why_new: Weighted Strength and hetero-terrain tie detail to high or low values, not to a specific level, and detail shows everywhere else. This aims detail exactly at the set you threshold, which keeps the look of FBm's coastline but a calm heightfield for shading, slopes and gradient-based uses. A graph would need a Fade plus Remap per octave.
master.simd_plan: Same as FBm plus about 6 ops per octave. Fixed loop on Octaves. No early out; gated octaves are still evaluated. Cost about 1.05 x FBm.
master.continuity: C1 if source is C1: smoothstep of |d| has zero slope at d=0, so the abs kink vanishes. Measured c0ratio 3.58, driven by steep high octaves, no jumps seen.
master.params: Source, Octaves, Gain (should be hybrid), Lacunarity, Level (hybrid), Focus Width.
master.risks: Visual change is subtle at low Gain; it needs Gain above 0.5 to show. Periodic-level variant (many contours) looked close to plain FBm and was dropped. Claimed coastline equivalence with FBm at Focus>=1 is reasoned, not tested. Output range is not exactly FBm's; measured +/-0.76 with proto scaling.
master.cost_note: Cost about 1.05 x FBm.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 8.87x perlin2 (447.2 ns vs 50.4 ns) for 7 octaves. Plain FBm of the same 7 octaves in this prototype (plain=1) measured 476.1 ns in the same run, so the gate does not exceed timing noise. Numbers include about 10 std::map param lookups per sample.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D about 8.5 ns, 3D about 16.5 ns, 4D about 32 ns (7 octaves of Perlin at handbook costs, about 1.05x FBm).
measured.c0_note: 3.48 at default scale comes from steep high octaves at the harness step. With f0=0.05 (same field, features 10x larger than the step) it measures 7.48, so no jumps.

kifs-fractal.look: Default: multi scale soap foam. Big smooth bright bubbles with a pale gradient, surrounded by necklaces of smaller and smaller bubbles with dark lace rims, down to the pixel. Threshold at P50 is a striking cheese or sponge network with a very wide range of hole sizes. Hillshade: pale flat domes in dark green lace. Wide view: dense foam at all scales, no visible grid. XZ slice: same foam, with a faint mirror symmetry showing in the big blobs. Vol: a cluster of rounded pebbles and rubble with bubble shaped cut faces. Kali constant matters a lot: cx 0.4 cy 0.3 gives a thin black fractal coast on white with glow dots, cx 0.6 cy 0.5 mixes the two. Mandelbox at N=4: rows of dash shaped plates in a loose flow, at N=7 pixel noise. Menger: warped window panes in panes on a white ground, DE adds soft glow. Sierpinski: arrow shaped dark flakes branching on white. Quilt: square tiles of different kaleidoscopic medallions, very ornamental, with hard seams.
kifs-fractal.dims: 2D and 3D measured, all four folds written for both, with 3D rendered only for Kali (XZ slice and vol). 3D z-continuity mean 0.0070 per dz=1e-3, max 0.29. 4D not run; Kali and the tri fold are dimension agnostic.
kifs-fractal.range: Clamped to -1..1. Measured over 8 seeds: Kali foam -1.000 to 1.000 mean 0.129; Mandelbox DE -0.700 to 0.627; Menger -1.000 to 1.000 mean 0.442; Sierpinski -0.999 to 1.000 mean 0.304. Per preset constants needed in a port. 0 NaN.
kifs-fractal.artifacts: c0ratio 1.50, max slope 1335 for the default: continuous folds, but gradient density is fractal, and the finest rims alias into dots. Not stationary without the mirror tile: tile=0 measured mean 0.935, and far coords std 0.127, mostly flat white as predicted (|p| large leads to the fixed point -C), so the mirror tile is required. Mirror tile symmetry shows slightly in the XZ slice. Most constants are dull, presets are required, as the idea warned. Quilt has seams by design. Mandelbox and Sierpinski presets look less finished than Kali.
kifs-fractal.node_shape: Members: Fold {Kali, Mandelbox, Menger, Sierpinski}, Iterations, Scale S, Fold Constant X/Y/Z/W (hybrid), Constant Noise Amp + Frequency, Warp Amp + Frequency, Min Radius, Fixed Radius, Tile {None, Mirror, Quilt}, Tile Period, Output {OrbitTrapMin, OrbitTrapAvg, DistanceEstimate, LastLength, Lace}, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. Ship with presets.
kifs-fractal.port_notes: Fixed loop, all branch free as Abs, Min/Max swaps, Select and Reciprocal. Kali needs Max(r2, 1e-3). Only one output is needed per node, so the trap Exp and running Sqrt can be compiled out by output. The mirror tile uses a rotation by a fixed angle first to hide the axis alignment of the tile. The per=2 tile suits Menger, Sierpinski and Mandelbox (attractor in [-1,1]); with per=3 they were mostly empty. Related to domain-kifs, which folds the domain of a source; here the orbit itself is the output and the look is far stronger.
kifs-fractal.params_text: fold=0,out=4,tile=1,N=8,cx=0.8,cy=0.7,cz=0.55,ca=0.12,cf=0.3,w=0.35,wf=0.4,per=3,scale=0.5,rot=0.3 (all code defaults: Kali foam) at --window 8. Other presets: cx=0.4,cy=0.3 coast; fold=1,out=2 Mandelbox; fold=2,out=4 Menger; fold=3,out=3 Sierpinski; tile=2,w=0,ca=0,out=3 quilt at --window 12.

master.one_liner: Kaleidoscopic IFS / escape fold fractals as a texture: Kali inversion, Mandelbox box+sphere fold, Menger and Sierpinski folds iterated a fixed count with orbit-trap, distance-estimate and smooth-escape outputs; hybrid fold constant for spatially varying Julia sets.
master.look:
Self-similar structure at every scale from only ~8-12 iterations: Kali gives electric filaments, organic cathedral veins and exponential peaks/holes when used as displacement; Mandelbox orbit traps give crystalline boxes-in-boxes circuitry; Menger gives sponge slices; Sierpinski gives gasket lattices. In Tiled mode: a quilt of distinct fractal medallions.
[InversionLace, dynamics-iteration] Verified in prototype. With warp: bubble clusters, soap foam and lace rims with fine detail of varying scale, small dark cracks between; without warp a clear periodic ornament grid. Good for alien organic detail, cellular foam, tooled metal or ornament, procedural filigree.
master.algorithm:
p = x*Scale (optionally Tiled: p = frac(x)-0.5 with the fold constant C hashed per cell, giving a quilt of different fractal tiles). dr = 1; trapMin = inf; trapAvg = 0
for it in 0..Iterations-1 (fixed):
  Kali:       r2 = dot(p,p)+eps ; dr *= 1/r2 ; p = Abs(p)/r2 - C
  Mandelbox:  p = Clamp(p,-1,1)*2 - p                                       // box fold
              r2 = dot(p,p); m2 = MinRadius^2; f2 = FixedRadius^2
              k = Select(r2<m2, f2/m2, Select(r2<f2, f2/r2, 1))             // sphere fold
              p *= k; dr *= k; p = S*p + C; dr = dr*|S| + 1
  Menger:     p = Abs(p); sort components descending (2-3 compare/Select swaps); p = S*p - C*(S-1); dr *= S
  Sierpinski: fold across the 3 planes x+y, x+z, y+z (p.xy = (p.x+p.y<0)? -p.yx : p.xy etc. via Select); p = S*p - C*(S-1); dr *= S
  trapMin = Min(trapMin, dot(p,p)); trapAvg += Exp(-TrapScale*dot(p,p))
Outputs: OrbitTrapMin = 1 - 2*Sqrt(trapMin)/range ; OrbitTrapAvg = trapAvg/Iterations*2-1 ; DistanceEstimate = Sqrt(dot(p,p))/dr (Mandelbox: 0.5*log(r)*r/dr) clamped and remapped ; LastLength = tanh(|p|).
Seed: perturbs C by Seed*0.001 and picks a per-iteration rotation angle from a hash (optional 'Twist' param, 1 sincos per iteration).

[InversionLace, dynamics-iteration] Warp: q=p+W*(n1(p*0.5), n2(p*0.5)). Fold: rotate by a small fixed angle, then a=tri(q,period). c=c0+Ca*(n3(p*0.35), n4(p*0.35)). Repeat N (8..12): a=|a|/Max(a.a,1e-3)-c; L=|a|; acc+=|L-last|; last=L. Output 0.7*log(acc/N+0.01). Direct folding works in any dimension. Prototype: dyn_lens mode=39,N=8 and without warp mode=14,N=10 for comparison.
master.why_new: FBm is only statistically self-similar; these are geometrically self-similar with sharp hierarchical detail (sci-fi hull plating, circuitry, mineral veins, alien ornament) and are cheap. Hybrid C lets a slow noise morph the fractal across space, which is unique to a node implementation.
master.simd_plan: Fixed Iterations loop; per iteration Abs/Clamp/Min/Select and one Reciprocal; no lattice. Est. AVX2 10 iterations: ~2-4x Perlin in 2D, dimension agnostic (GenT; Sierpinski/Menger folds generalise to d planes). 4D works (Kali is any-dimensional). Guard dot(p,p) with eps, clamp DE.
master.continuity: Fold maps (Abs, Clamp, sphere inversion, plane folds) are continuous, so OrbitTrapMin/Avg and LastLength are C0 with fractal-dense gradient creases; DistanceEstimate is continuous outside the set and ill-defined inside (clamped); none are differentiable in a useful sense.
master.params: Fold enum {Kali, Mandelbox, Menger, Sierpinski}, Iterations (int 2-20), Scale S (hybrid), Fold Constant C X/Y/Z/W (hybrid per axis), Min Radius, Fixed Radius, Trap Scale, Output enum {OrbitTrapMin, OrbitTrapAvg, DistanceEstimate, LastLength}, Tiled (bool), Seed.
master.risks:
Not stationary: the pattern is anchored at the origin and changes with distance from it; untiled mode cannot tile and breaks the 'same look everywhere' expectation (document as texture, not noise). Tiled mode has hard cell seams. Output ranges must be measured per fold.
[InversionLace, dynamics-iteration] Parameter space is touchy: most c values are dull and only some give lace, so presets are needed. Faint periodicity remains without enough warp. Aliasing at N>10. Range needs a measured constant.
[KaliFoldFractal, shader-community] Not stationary: the pattern's character drifts with distance from the fold axes; large coordinates converge quickly to boring regions (|p| large -> |p|/|p|^2 -> 0 -> -c fixed point). Output range is parameter-dependent; needs VariableRange. Aliasing: infinite detail means it must be used at modest Iterations or with mip-aware scales.
master.cost_note: About 2-4x Perlin in 2D at 10 iterations, and dimension agnostic.
master.variant_notes: Generator form with orbit traps. InversionLace shows a noise warp plus noise-driven constant turns the periodic ornament into foam and lace; good c values are rare, so presets are needed.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D about 7 ns (4 Perlins for warp and constant, 8 iterations at about 10 ops + 1 Reciprocal + 1 Sqrt). 3D about 14 ns. 2-3 ns without warp and noise driven constant. Scalar measured 373.6 ns, which also computes an Exp per iteration for an unused output.

morse-lock-fbm.look: Terrain with calm plains, smooth rounded summits and smooth lake floors, with hard rough relief on the slopes between them. The relief beside classic FBm reads as far more natural: classic is uniformly crumpled, this has terrain types. The threshold has a few clean wiggly coasts and no dust. Lock=1 is nearly the base octave with fine wrinkles on flanks. Volume: smooth wall bands with rough patches, and much less floating dust than classic on the same seed. The hard knee (added here, q^2 / (q^2 + (1-q)^2)) keeps stronger detail on slopes and brings extrema close to base at lock=1.

dims.3D: works, measured continuity (z max 0.0020 for dz=1e-3), vol rendered and viewed; topology not counted in 3D, and MaxSlope 2.2 was not tuned separately for 3D Perlin
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D path; needs a 4D Perlin gradient or 5 source evals per octave

morse-lock-fbm.range: -0.851 .. 0.845 over 8 seeds, mean 0.001, normalised by sqrt(sum a^2) with no other constant. 3D slice -0.512 .. 0.344, std 0.190.
morse-lock-fbm.artifacts: The gate has no knowledge of the amplitude's own gradient, so a few extra extrema remain (20-25 vs 17-23 at lock=1, hard knee, one extra lake on seed 2024). Below lock 0.5 topology gains are small. Plains are slightly blank at lock 0.7 and above. Max Slope is a per source constant; it was only used for Perlin here.
morse-lock-fbm.node_shape: MorseLockFBm : Generator. Source, Octaves (int), Gain, Lacunarity, Lock (hybrid; 0 = classic FBm), Knee enum (Soft, Hard), Max Slope (float, per source), Gradient enum (Analytic Perlin, Forward Differences), VariableRange.
morse-lock-fbm.port_notes: Fixed octave loop, branch free. q = g2 * Reciprocal(g2 + l2 + eps); the hard knee adds 4 ops and one divide. A generic Source needs forward differences: (1 + D) evals per octave at step about 0.02 / f. A Perlin only path can carry gradient in the kernel, which is the affordable form, but FastNoise has no gradient output on Generator, so the port has to choose between FD on any source, or a node hard coded to Perlin or Simplex internally. Gradient accumulation in world space: if a port uses octave rotation it must rotate the octave gradient back, the prototype has no rotation and uses lac=2.03 to avoid lattice coincidence.
morse-lock-fbm.params_text: plain render is oct=6,gain=0.5,lac=2.03,f0=0.5,lock=0.6,hard=1,slope=2.2. Topology clean mode: lock=1,hard=1. Classic FBm: lock=0,hard=0. Vol: f0=1

master.one_liner: fBm whose octaves cannot create new extrema or islands: coastlines get fractal detail but keep the topology of the base octave.
master.look: Hillshade has smooth lake floors and rounded summits with wrinkled flanks. Thresholded, it gives one clean wiggly coast with no dust islands or pinholes. Useful for terrain, continents, coastlines and masks that must stay clean at every threshold. Measured at 6 octaves, window 8, threshold at median: classic fBm 96 islands / 97 lakes / 12573 extrema; Lock=1 gives 10 / 9 / 186; the base Perlin octave alone gives 10 / 9 / 75, so the island and lake counts match the base exactly on that seed. A second seed gave 88 / 90 / 12242 classic and 6 / 10 / 203 locked. Lock=0.5 gives 22 / 21 / 3907.
master.algorithm: F = S0(p), g = grad S0(p). For octave k = 1..N-1: f = lac^k, a = gain^k, evaluate n = Sk(p*f) and its gradient gn (forward differences, step ~0.02/f). glen = |g|. Limit lim = glen / (MaxSlope*f), where MaxSlope is the source's max gradient per unit frequency (2.2 for unit Perlin). k_ = lim / (a*Lock). amp = a * k_^2 / (1 + k_^2). F += amp*n; g += amp*f*gn. Rationale: if the amplitude of octave k keeps its slope below |g|, the sum's gradient cannot vanish there, so no new critical point can appear. Detail fades at hilltops, valley floors and saddles, and is full strength on flanks. Normalise by sqrt(sum a^2).
master.why_new: FBm and Weighted Strength gate on value, so neither removes dust. Domain-specific remedies need a global pass; this one is pointwise. It is the inverse of derivative-damped fBm, which suppresses detail on slopes. Here detail lives on slopes and dies at critical points, with a stated topological reason. The graph cannot do it because amplitude depends on the accumulated gradient of earlier octaves.
master.simd_plan: Fixed octave loop, branch-free. Each octave costs (1+D) source evals with forward differences: 2D 3, 3D 4, 4D 5, so 6 octaves of Perlin is about 18 / 24 / 30 Perlin evals. A dedicated analytic-gradient Perlin path measured 8x perlin2 scalar for 6 octaves, against 6x for plain fBm. The gate is one Sqrt-free ratio using g2 directly: k^2 = g2 / (MaxSlope*f*a*Lock)^2. All dimensions and tiling come through the source.
master.continuity: C1 when the source is C1. amp is a smooth rational function of g2 and is 0 where g = 0, so it does not introduce a crease. Measured c0ratio 7.8.
master.params: Lock (hybrid, 0 = classic fBm, 1 = full lock), Gain, Lacunarity, Octaves, Max Slope (float, per source type), Source.
master.risks: The gate ignores the gradient of amp itself, so extrema drop about 60x but do not reach the base count (186 vs 75). Lock=1 removes a lot of roughness (std 0.288 vs 0.313 and a less craggy look), so 0.5 may be the practical default. Max Slope must suit the source, and FD cost is high for expensive sources. Tested only in 2D.
master.cost_note: A dedicated analytic-gradient Perlin path measured 8x perlin2 scalar for 6 octaves, against 6x for plain fBm.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 7.87x perlin2 (400.0 ns vs 50.8 ns) for 6 octaves on the analytic gradient Perlin path. Classic with the same code path (lock=0,hard=0) measured 445.0 ns in the same run, so the gate is below timing noise. Numbers include about 10 std::map param lookups per sample.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D about 9 ns, 3D about 18 ns on a dedicated analytic Perlin path; forward differences on a generic source about 20 ns in 2D and 50 ns in 3D (3 and 4 source evals per octave).

multiplicative-cascade.look: Density: hard black voids of many sizes cut into soft cloudy clumps, with smaller voids nested in the clumps; reads as rain radar, gas clouds or lichen, and looks like nothing in the existing set. Without per level decay of Intermittency it is nearly binary with pepper holes at the finest level, which looks worse; the decay (my addition) fixes that. Multifractal relief: smooth rolling plains with clusters of jagged needles, roughness truly patchy and inherited, striking but spiky, less usable as terrain than morse-lock. Volume at iso -0.6: mostly solid with ragged rugged pockets. Lognormal with log output looks like ordinary busy FBm, as the maths says (log of a product is a sum), so that mode adds nothing.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3 with a fixed rotation per level, z-continuity max 0.0220 for dz=1e-3, vol rendered
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D path; only source calls

multiplicative-cascade.range: Density -1.000 .. 0.963 over 8 seeds, mean -0.386, by construction of R/(R+knee). Multifractal -0.984 .. 0.973, mean 0.002, by soft limit v/sqrt(1+v^2).
multiplicative-cascade.artifacts: Creases at the floor edge because Max(0, ...) is C0, seen as sharp void outlines, which suit the look. Mean is far from 0 in Density (-0.386), since voids dominate. Simplex inner is too dusty at the same settings; Perlin was the best inner. Value with rot=0 and lac 2 gives blobby clumps in large voids, not visibly better. Lognormal with Density output is almost black because the median of R is tiny.
multiplicative-cascade.node_shape: MultiplicativeCascade : Generator. Source, Levels (int), Lacunarity, Intermittency (hybrid), Intermittency Decay, Knee, Output enum (Density, Multifractal), Gain (Multifractal), VariableRange. Drop the lognormal model and the Log output.
multiplicative-cascade.port_notes: Fixed loop, Max and multiply per level, one divide at the end; Multifractal doubles source evals. A generic Source input works; Perlin as default. Keep R as float32v; R can underflow to 0, which is intended. For Density, offer the measured median as a level hint in the docs, because thresholding at 0 lands on the bright side. Rotation per level is a constant, as in the other fractals.
multiplicative-cascade.params_text: plain render is lev=6,model=0,inner=2 (Perlin),I=3,idecay=0.8,knee=1,f0=0.5,lac=2,rot=1, Density output. Multifractal: out=2,I=2.5,idecay=1,gain=0.7,fmul=1.5. Log lognormal: model=1,sigma=1.2,out=1,loglo=-6,loghi=3,idecay=1. Vol: f0=1 --iso -0.6

master.one_liner: Mandelbrot/Schertzer-Lovejoy multiplicative cascade as a node: the field is a running product of per-level weights that can hit zero, producing intermittent clumps and hard voids nested at all scales, optionally used as a spatially varying gain for FBm (multifractal terrain).
master.look: Density mode: sparse bright clumps separated by large empty regions, with voids of all sizes carved out of clumps (Intermittency>1 gives true zero floors, so the void set is the union over scales). Reads as rain cells, galaxy filaments, lichen colonies, ore veins, population density. Multifractal mode: terrain where roughness itself is patchy and inherited hierarchically (smooth basins next to very rough massifs, rough patches containing rougher sub-patches), unlike FBm's uniform roughness.
master.algorithm:
R=1; freq=1; F=0; amp=1
  for i in 0..Levels-1:
    w = noise(p*freq, seed+i)                          // Value (cell-shaped voids) or Simplex (round voids), enum
    W = Select(Model==PModel, Max(0, 1 + Intermittency*w),   // can be exactly 0 -> hard voids
                               Exp(Sigma*w - 0.5*Sigma*Sigma)) // lognormal, never zero
    R *= W
    // Multifractal mode: also accumulate a signal octave gated by the cascade so far
    F += amp * R * noise(p*freq, seed+i+1000)
    amp*=Gain; freq*=Lacunarity
  Density mode: out = ScaleOutput( R / (R + Knee) , 0, 1 )  // Knee ~ 1 maps the heavy tail into [0,1); or out = Log(R+eps) remapped (enum)
  Multifractal mode: out = F / sum(amp)
master.why_new: exp(FBm) alone is a trivial graph (PowFloat of FBm) and is NOT this: the p-model with max(0,...) kills regions at each level, so voids are not expressible as a function of the FBm sum. Weighted Strength in FractalFBm is a cousin (gain modulated by the previous octave's own value), but it cannot zero out, uses the signal octave as the weight, and has no lognormal/intermittency control. One loop replaces N Multiply+Remap+noise nodes.
master.simd_plan: Branch-free (Max, Exp, Select). No window beyond the inner noise. Density mode ~Levels x noise; Multifractal mode 2x that. 6 levels of Simplex 2D ~7-8 ns/sample AVX2 estimate; 2D/3D/4D free via GenT since it is just noise calls.
master.continuity: Same as the inner noise (C2 Simplex) except at the p-model zero floor where Max(0,.) is C0; the product stays continuous.
master.params: Levels int, Lacunarity, Model enum {PModel, Lognormal}, Intermittency hybrid (p-model, 0..3), Sigma hybrid (lognormal), Inner noise enum {Value, Simplex}, Output enum {Density, Log, Multifractal}, Gain hybrid (multifractal), Knee float, Seed Offset.
master.risks: Heavy-tailed range: normalisation must be by knee/log remap, not by measured max. With Value inner noise and Lacunarity exactly 2 the voids align to a quadtree (desirable for a Cantor look, but visibly axis aligned).
master.cost_note: 6 levels of Simplex 2D ~7-8 ns/sample AVX2 estimate; 2D/3D/4D free via GenT since it is just noise calls.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: Density 8.37x perlin2 (437.6 ns vs 52.3 ns) for 6 levels. Multifractal 16.93x (867.3 ns vs 51.2 ns), which evaluates 12 noises. Numbers include about 18 std::map param lookups per sample.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: Density 2D about 7.5 ns, 3D about 14 ns, 4D about 27 ns at 6 levels of Perlin; Multifractal about double.
measured.c0_note: 5.83 at default scale from steep octaves and the floor creases. With f0=0.05 (features 10x larger than the step) it measures 7.98, so no jumps. Multifractal: 6.94 and 8.00.

order-stat-fractal.look: Max: big smooth blobs over a floor of mid blobs, with tiny blobs in their troughs, sizes clearly separated at lac 2.6. Creased where blobs meet. Reads as lumps on lumps; the relief shows smooth mounds rising out of a rough floor, stylised and not natural terrain. Min: the same inverted, with smooth pools in a rough plateau. Min volume at iso 0.54 is the best image: smooth swiss cheese with holes inside holes, a clean karst look I have not seen from FBm. Max volume at low iso: rugged dusty zones, less attractive. Median: low contrast fine grit with faint rings, dull, close to a busy FBm. Hybrid rank: a morph from pools to mounds across the map through a gritty middle.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3, z-continuity max 0.0115 for dz=1e-3, vols rendered
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D path; only source calls and the same network

order-stat-fractal.range: Max -1.039 .. 0.872, mean -0.453. Min -0.902 .. 1.004, mean 0.452. Median -0.597 .. 0.591, mean 0.000. Hybrid rank -1.039 .. 1.001, mean -0.013. All over 8 seeds. Centre and scale follow the bound, raw Max is -0.1 .. 1, so Max spends its range unevenly: the median sits well below zero.
order-stat-fractal.artifacts: Creases along every octave tie, as predicted; visible in hillshade, they are the character of the look. At lac 2 the lumps run together, so 2.6 or higher is better, which differs from the FBm default. Near a Perlin lattice point all octaves tend to 0 together at lac 2 with no rotation; the rotation avoids that. Weighted Strength is implemented in the prototype (ws) but not evaluated, because Max already gives what it was for.
order-stat-fractal.node_shape: OrderStatFractal : Generator. Source, Octaves (int, up to 8), Gain, Lacunarity, Rank (hybrid, 0 = Min, 1 = Max), Octave Rotation (bool), VariableRange.
order-stat-fractal.port_notes: Octave loop writing to a fixed float32v array, then a compile time compare exchange network chosen by Octaves outside the lanes. A hybrid Rank needs a Select chain over the sorted values, which is N selects. A constant Rank is one lerp. Centre per lane = 0.45 * (2r - 1) with a global scale 1.8 keeps the morph centred; this constant is for gain 0.62 and lac 2.6, and other gains need a measured value. A graph can build Max or Min from about 3N nodes, so the node's value is one parameter, a morph, and a rank that a graph cannot reach. Max and Min are worth it; Median alone would not be.
order-stat-fractal.params_text: plain render is Max: oct=5,gain=0.62,lac=2.6,f0=0.5,rank=1,centre=0.45,scale=1.8 with golden angle octave rotation. Min: rank=0. Median: rank=0.5. Hybrid rank: rank=0.5,rvar=1.3,rf=0.2. Vols: f0=1 --iso -0.648 (Max), f0=1,rank=0 --iso 0.54 (Min).

master.one_liner: Fractal that combines octaves by order statistic instead of sum: Max, Min, Median or any fractional rank of the scaled octaves via a fixed sorting network, bounded in [-1,1] for any octave count, giving blobs-within-troughs and karst-like nesting.
master.look: Max: the base octave shapes dominate where they are high, and in its troughs the finer octaves poke through, so there are blobs at every scale nested inside each other (cumulus cauliflower, piles of stones, lichen on lichen); the superlevel set at any threshold is the union of the per-octave superlevel sets, so small islands are guaranteed to exist between big ones. Min: pits inside pits, sponge or karst. Median: a smooth, scale-balanced field with fewer extremes than FBm and a distinct 'plateau and gully' texture. Fractional rank morphs continuously between these.
master.algorithm:
v_i = gain^i * S(x * lacunarity^i, seed + i), i = 0..N-1 (N = Octaves, int member, same for all lanes; N <= 8).
Sort the N lanes-parallel values with a fixed compare-exchange network (odd-even merge; N=5: 9 CEs, N=8: 19 CEs; CE(a,b) = (Min(a,b), Max(a,b))).
Rank r = Rank parameter in [0, N-1] (float): out = lerp(v_(floor r), v_(floor r + 1), frac r) (Mode Max = r = N-1, Min = r = 0, Median = r = (N-1)/2). Fractional rank gives a continuous blend between order statistics.
Range: each v_i is in [-gain^i, gain^i] subset of [-1,1] so every order statistic is in [-1,1] without renormalisation; subtract a per-(N, gain, rank) measured median constant to centre (Centre option), VariableRange for the rest.
Weighted Strength as in FBm (amplitude of octave i scaled by the previous octave's value) applies before sorting.
master.why_new: Expressible only as a chain of ~3N nodes for Max and not at all for the median; the sorting network makes rank selection as cheap as FBm's sum. Statistically, the output range does not shrink with octave count (FBm's 1/sum(gain^i) normalisation changes variance and therefore coverage whenever Octaves changes), and the max-union topology of level sets is a property no additive fractal has.
master.simd_plan: Fractal.inl octave loop writing to a small fixed array of float32v (N <= 8), followed by the compile-time sorting network for the current N (switch on N outside the lane loop, 5 networks). Cost = N x source + ~2N log^2 N Min/Max ops (negligible): same as FBm.
master.continuity: C0 (min/max of smooth functions have kinks along the loci where two octaves tie); fractional rank is C0 too.
master.params: Source; Octaves (int); Lacunarity; Gain; Weighted Strength; Rank (float, hybrid possible); Mode enum (Max, Min, Median, Rank); Centre (bool).
master.risks: Kinks everywhere where octaves cross (fine for terrain, visible in hillshade as creases). Max mode is strongly biased positive; needs the centring constant. A hybrid Rank makes the per-lane lerp index vary, requiring a Select chain over the N sorted values (still branch-free, N Selects).
master.cost_note: Cost = N x source + ~2N log^2 N Min/Max ops (negligible): same as FBm.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 7.15x perlin2 (362.0 ns vs 50.6 ns) for 5 octaves with an insertion sort standing in for the network. Includes about 12 std::map param lookups per sample.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D about 6 ns, 3D about 12 ns, 4D about 22 ns at 5 octaves of Perlin plus 9 compare exchanges.

region-spectrum-fractal.look: Style 2 with warp and wide fade: rough massifs beside smooth green plains with soft borders, a province look; it holds up in relief. Style 1: patches of different material, fine grit next to smooth hills; with no warp and a narrow fade the borders are straight Voronoi lines and it looks artificial. Style 0 (the catalogue's independent octave weights) is subtle and reads as slightly uneven FBm, so it fails to deliver the promise. Volume: smooth walls next to gritty ones. The style 2 look is very close to what fractal-spectrum's Detail hybrid gave, which is why I call this merged.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3 with a 3x3x3 region window, z-continuity max 0.0056 for dz=1e-3, vol rendered
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D path; the region search would be 81 points

region-spectrum-fractal.artifacts: The catalogue blend has jumps along F2 = F3 lines near every Voronoi vertex, because the second region's identity changes at nonzero weight; the catalogue called this a tiny kink and it is a real seam. Fixed here by weighting every window point with sat(1 - (d - F1) / Fade)^2 and averaging octave weights, which is one weighted sum instead of two. In 2D a point outside the 3x3 window can still matter at wide fade and high jitter; no jump was measured at fade 0.5 and jitter 0.85.
region-spectrum-fractal.node_shape: As a node of its own it would be: RegionSpectrumFractal : Generator. Source, Octaves, Lacunarity, Region Scale, Jitter, Fade, Style enum (Roughness, Band), Gain Low, Gain High, Region Warp, VariableRange. Preferred instead: give fractal-spectrum its hybrids and provide a soft cell value source.
region-spectrum-fractal.port_notes: Hash per window point gives one or two parameters by bit field, averaged by weight (9 points in 2D, 27 in 3D), so the octave weights come from one or two values instead of N per region. Measured cost of the fix is near zero against the two region form. Finding worth carrying to any other idea with F2-F1 blending: the swap of the second nearest makes a seam unless the weight goes to zero first. The average of bell parameters instead of bell weights was not tested; I averaged weights in the prototype.
region-spectrum-fractal.params_text: plain render is style=2 (hashed gain per region, 0.3 to 0.9),oct=7,f0=0.5,rs=0.33,jitter=0.85,fade=0.5,warp=0.35,wf=0.6,blend=1. Materials: style=1. Catalogue weights: style=0. Catalogue blend for comparison: blend=0,warp=0. Vol: f0=1,rs=0.7
region-spectrum-fractal.merged_into: fractal-spectrum (hybrid Center, Width or Detail fed by a soft edged cell value, such as a biome-blend style sparse convolution of hashed constants)

queue.name: RegionSpectrumFractal
queue.reason: Octaves evaluated once and reweighted per Voronoi region: cheap biome spectra at FBm plus one coarse Cellular. Check the kink at Voronoi vertices.

master.one_liner: One fractal whose per-octave amplitudes are hashed per Voronoi region of a coarse cellular lattice, so adjacent regions have different spectra (smooth plain, grainy plateau, mid-band hills), blended across region borders with an F2-F1 fade.
master.look: Patchwork landscapes: each cell-shaped region has its own character (one is smooth rolling hills, its neighbour is all fine grain, another is mid-frequency bumps), with soft borders. Reads as geological provinces / biome tiles, the thing FBm never gives because its roughness is spatially stationary. Compared with multiplying by a cellular mask this changes the *spectrum* per region, not just amplitude.
master.algorithm:
coarse cellular 3x3 search at RegionScale -> nearest two points, hashes h1,h2, distances F1,F2
  for region r in {h1,h2}: per-octave weights a_r[i] = Base^i * Select(bit_i(h_r) ...)  more usefully a_r[i] = Base^i * Lerp(1, rnd01(Hash(h_r, i)), Variation)  (so Variation 0 = plain FBm everywhere) ; n2_r = sum a_r[i]^2
  evaluate octaves ONCE: v_i = noise(p*freq_i, seed+i) for i < Octaves  (uniform loop, store in registers/stack array of MaxOctaves)
  F_r = sum a_r[i] v_i / Sqrt(n2_r)   for r = 1,2
  m = smoothstep(0, Fade, F2 - F1)   -> out = Lerp(F_2, F_1, 0.5 + 0.5*m)  (Fade in region-space units)
  Optional per-region hashed overall gain and a per-region 'roughness exponent' instead of independent weights (Variation controls spread). Optional sharpening of the region mask with Terrace-like hashed region 'height' offset so regions also differ in base elevation (biome plateaus).
master.why_new: A graph would need one fractal per region type plus a region-selection blend (N fractals evaluated); here octaves are evaluated once and reweighted twice, so N 'biomes' cost one FBm plus a small cellular search. Not aware of any library offering per-region spectral coefficients inside one fractal.
master.simd_plan: Branch-free: cellular window for F1/F2 (existing code), octave loop with values kept in a fixed-size array indexed by compile-time unrolled loop (MaxOctaves template or 8 slots), two weighted sums. Cost ~ FBm(Octaves) + CellularDistance(coarse, 2D 3.9 ns) + 2*Octaves FMAs; 3D/4D via the cellular window costs (41 ns in 4D), acceptable since region search is at coarse scale.
master.continuity: Same as the source inside regions; C1 across borders via smoothstep fade (the two blended fields share the same octave values, so the blend is a smooth reweighting rather than a crossfade of unrelated fields, which keeps features aligned across the border).
master.params: Source, Octaves int, Gain, Lacunarity, Region Scale, Variation hybrid, Fade, Region Height Variation, Jitter, Seed Offset.
master.risks: Needs MaxOctaves slots (fixed 8 or 12); with 3 or more near-equidistant regions at a Voronoi vertex only two are blended (tiny kink at vertices, same as other F1/F2 blends).
master.cost_note: Cost ~ FBm(Octaves) + CellularDistance(coarse, 2D 3.9 ns) + 2*Octaves FMAs; 3D/4D via the cellular window costs (41 ns in 4D), acceptable since region search is at coarse scale.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 13.31x perlin2 (675.8 ns vs 50.8 ns) with warp, 7 octaves plus a 3x3 region search. Without warp 12.52x (624.9 ns). Catalogue two region blend without warp 12.44x (620.8 ns). Includes about 20 std::map param lookups per sample.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D about 14 ns (7 octaves at 1.1 plus a 3x3 cellular at 3.9 plus weights), 3D about 32 ns, 4D about 75 ns because of the 3x3x3x3 region search.
measured.c0_note: With f0=0.05, so only region transitions can show: this blend measures 7.99 (8.00 before warp); the catalogue F2-F1 blend measures 1.00 with both 3x3 and 5x5 windows, and 1.58 with this style and no warp, so it has real jumps.

sparse-octaves.look: Default: weathered plaster or pitted stone. Smooth pale and dark blobs carry fine pits and scratches, with crumbled zones between them. Hillshade: smooth rocky domes dotted with small craters, in a crust of rough detail. Threshold is a rough but bold coast. Histogram is bimodal, with a low dip at zero, unlike FBm. It reads closer to a natural material photo than any fractal in the existing set. Sharp 2 to 3: crisper bright and dark plates with gritty gaps between, more stylised; the sharp 2 volume shows rounded boulders sitting in rubble. Relief at sharp 2: domes with spikes between them, less usable as terrain. The sweep confirms Gain has to be high: at 0.65 the base octave wins almost everywhere.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3, z-continuity max 0.0210 for dz=1e-3, slice viewed on the sheet, vols rendered
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D path; only source calls

sparse-octaves.range: -0.943 .. 0.921 over 8 seeds, mean 0.002, with no normalising constant: the output is bounded by the largest |v_i|. 3D slice -0.628 .. 0.476, std 0.229.
sparse-octaves.artifacts: Detail lands where the base octave crosses zero, since it wins elsewhere, so the structure follows the base contour and overlaps a little with iso-focus-fractal at level 0, though here detail replaces instead of adding. Sharp 4 with Gain 0.65 gives a flat gray floor with crisp blobs on it; that floor is the 1e-20 eps swamping v^32, an accident and not a designed feature. At Sharp 4 w underflows, so denormals are a real concern in a port.
sparse-octaves.node_shape: SparseOctaves : Generator. Source, Octaves (int), Gain, Lacunarity, Sharpness (int, 0 to 4), Floor (eps as a real parameter, for the stencil look), Octave Rotation (bool), VariableRange.
sparse-octaves.port_notes: FBm loop plus Sharp+2 multiplies per octave and one divide at the end, branch free. To make the floor independent of amplitude, divide v by the largest possible amplitude or by a running Max first, then use a relative eps; not tested. Set FTZ or clamp w at a small minimum to avoid denormals on older CPUs. Rotation per octave is a constant.
sparse-octaves.params_text: plain render is oct=6,sharp=1,gain=0.85,lac=2,f0=0.5 with golden angle octave rotation. Crisper plates: sharp=2,gain=0.8. Stencil accident: sharp=4,gain=0.65. Reference FBm: plain=1. Vol: f0=1

master.one_liner: A soft winner-take-all between octaves: at each point one scale dominates, which gives clean smooth regions broken by patches of rough detail.
master.look: Crisp blobs with sudden pockets of grit, heavier-tailed and more natural-image-like than FBm, where every scale is active everywhere. Reads like weathered stone or lumpy plaster.
master.algorithm: For i: v_i=a_i*Source(seed+i,p*Lac^i). w_i=v_i^2 squared Sharp times by repeated multiply (Sharp=3 gives v^16). Output=sum(w_i*v_i)/(sum(w_i)+eps). Sharp 0 is a mild magnitude-weighted average; a large Sharp tends to the single largest |v_i|. Branch free, no Exp. Output is bounded by max |v_i|, so it stays in range for a_0=1.
master.why_new: Every octave in a Gaussian-style sum is active everywhere; real textures are sparse across scales. This couples all octaves per point, which no chain of two-input blends can do with low node count. It is not Weighted Strength, which only feeds forward and only in amplitude.
master.simd_plan: FBm plus Sharp+2 multiplies per octave and one divide total. Fixed octave loop. Dimension agnostic. Cost about 1.15 x FBm.
master.continuity: C-infinity for smooth sources thanks to eps, measured c0ratio 4.44, driven by steep values and no jumps seen. Higher Sharp makes switching regions steep.
master.params: Source, Octaves, Gain, Lacunarity, Sharpness (int; 2-4 useful).
master.risks: An exp-based version overflowed to NaN at high beta, so keep the power form. Sharp at 3-4 with Gain below 0.6 leaves the top octave always winning, so it needs Gain 0.75-0.9. Close to plain FBm at low Sharp. Denormal risk when all v are near 0; eps covers it.
master.cost_note: Cost about 1.15 x FBm.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 7.35x perlin2 (374.4 ns vs 50.9 ns) for 6 octaves. Plain 6 octave FBm in this prototype (plain=1) measured 397.1 ns in the same run, so the cost above FBm is below timing noise. Includes about 8 std::map param lookups per sample.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D about 8 ns, 3D about 15 ns, 4D about 29 ns at 6 octaves of Perlin (about 1.15x FBm).
measured.c0_note: 6.15 at default scale from steep switching. With f0=0.05 it measures 8.00, so no jumps. Sharp 2: 4.94 and 8.35. Sharp 3: 3.55 and 7.88. As Sharp rises the switching lines get steep enough to read as hard edges at image resolution.

flow-watershed.look: Flat plates with curved, slightly irregular borders and a wide size spread, each at its own grey level. Terrain view reads as a patchwork of provinces. Interiors are mottled because the second octave makes sub-basins. A few high areas break into messy blobs with bright halos where small pits sit on high ground. The 3D slice shows the same plates, cleaner. Oct=1 sweep: Edge output gives a clear crack network with faint step-contour lines inside each cell, Rings gives target nests bounded by watersheds, LocalPosition gives equal-height hills with occasional seams, HeightAboveDrain gives soft dark blobs with seams. Oct=3 turns to salt-and-pepper grain in every output.
flow-watershed.dims: 2D and 3D measured; 4D not prototyped (same loop with d+1 taps)
flow-watershed.range: [-1,1] after a measured recentre and clamp of the landing value (8 seeds min -1, max 1, mean -0.04); high plateaus clip at 1
flow-watershed.artifacts: Real jumps at watersheds (c0ratio 1.04, slope 1739), by design. Grain in unconverged areas, worse with octaves: oct=3 at gain 0.4 is unusable. Step-contour ripples show in Edge. Vol at iso 0 is torn shards with grainy faces, so the 3D form works but is not an attractive solid. delta and decay barely changed the look in the sweep.
flow-watershed.node_shape: Covered by DomainWarpFlow at angle 0 (Potential, Steps, Length, Direction, Normalise, Step Decay, Output). Worth adding to its Output enum from this prototype: Edge (3 traces in 2D, 4 in 3D), Rings, LocalPosition (down and up trace), HeightAboveDrain.
flow-watershed.port_notes: Fixed N loop, forward differences, no masks. Keep Field at 1 to 2 octaves or grain takes over. Basin Id by floor(q*cs) needs good convergence or it fragments, seen in the out=2 sweep. Why merged: this is the same descent loop that domain-warp-flow already measured as its watershed mode, and the plates here match that description. The look itself is keeper quality.
flow-watershed.params_text: out=0,oct=2,gain=0.25,steps=8,h=0.5,decay=0.8,delta=0.15 (plain render). Other outputs: out=7,oct=1 edge network; out=3,oct=1 rings; out=5,oct=1 local position

master.one_liner: Gradient-descent the sample position N steps down a smooth source and read something at the landing point: lake-filled basins, slope-length, catchment ids.
master.look:
Organic polygonal plates whose borders are the actual ridge lines of the source: varied cell size, curved walls, each floor at its own depth, optional agate-like ripple interiors. Looks like dried mud, giraffe patches, cloisonne or basin terrain. With 2-3 octave sources it gives plates carrying inner detail. Good for terrain basins, cracked ground, biome regions and masks.
[Catchment, dynamics-iteration] Verified in prototype. Flat-coloured patches with curved borders and a wide natural size distribution, no convexity and no grid. Multi-octave sources give fractal or irregular borders. Distance gives pitted bowls with curved walls. Rings gives agate, orbicular lichen or target nests, each bounded by a watershed. Edge gives branching crack networks with fractal tufts. Good for biomes, plates, drainage basins, stone, lichen, tectonic provinces.
master.algorithm:
Inputs: Field F (GeneratorSource, smooth), Steps N (int, 4..12), StepLen h (hybrid, sampled once at p0), Direction (enum Descend/Ascend), Normalise (bool), Output (enum BasinValue / Travel / BasinId / BasinSource), CellScale (float, BasinId only), Basin B (GeneratorSource, BasinSource only).

  p = p0
  for k in 0..N-1:                       // same N for all lanes
      g = grad F(p)                      // central differences: 2d extra F evals at p +- eps*e_i (eps ~ 0.02 feature), or forward diffs d+1 evals; or analytic if F is the built-in gradient Perlin/Simplex
      if Normalise: g *= InvSqrt(dot(g,g) + 1e-6)    // constant-speed descent, branch-free
      p = p - dir * h * g
  Travel  : out = |p - p0| / (N*h)  (or path length sum of |h*g|)
  BasinValue: out = F(p)              // every point takes the value N steps downhill
  BasinId : out = rnd11(hash(floor(p*CellScale)))   // piecewise-constant catchment mosaic
  BasinSource: out = B(p)             // any node evaluated at the landing point
As a DomainWarp-family node (DomainWarpFlow) the vector p - p0 is simply added to the positions, so any downstream graph is 'gathered' into the pits.

[SlopeSlide, graph-meta-filters] Simplex stencil v_i (triangle in 2D, tetrahedron in 3D, 5-cell in 4D), with sum v_i = 0. q = p. Repeat N times (int member, 1 to 6): g = D/((D+1)h) * sum S(q + h v_i) v_i; q -= a * g / sqrt(1 + c*|g|^2). Output Target(q), where Target defaults to S. a is the step and c softens the step on steep ground. Regimes seen in the prototype with single-octave Perlin: a=0.05-0.12 gives bright ridge network around dark rounded basins; a=0.25-0.5 overshoots the minimum, so plate interiors fill with parallel ripple bands; a<0 gives fat pillow plates with thin dark seams and ripple rings. N=3-4 at a=0.1-0.2 gives flat basin floors with crisp watershed lines. Extra outputs: HeightAboveDrain = S(p) - S(q_down), and LocalPosition = (S(p) - S(q_down)) / (S(q_up) - S(q_down) + e), which equalises every hill to 0..1.
master.why_new: No node can move a position along a field's own gradient for several steps; a one-shot DomainWarp by a single gradient has no convergence so cannot produce catchments or lake floors. The output is the flow map of the field, which a graph cannot express (it needs the gradient at each successive position). Shares one 'FlowEngine' with StirAdvect, StretchFTLE and StreamlineLIC.
master.simd_plan:
Dimension-agnostic GenT<P...> over a pack: fixed loop of N, inside it d+1 (forward) or 2d (central) source evaluations and FMA updates; no per-lane branching at all. If a built-in gradient-aware Perlin/Simplex is added internally (PerlinD, ~1.6x Perlin), use it when Field is left empty. Costs (AVX2 est.): 2D N=6 forward diffs, Perlin field: 18 Perlin = ~20 ns (18x Perlin); 3D: 24 Perlin3D = ~53 ns; 4D: 30 Perlin4D = ~130 ns. With FBm-5 Simplex field multiply by 5. 4D works and tiling via GenTileable2D is preserved because the moved position stays a function of the 4D input point. Far-coordinate safety: clamp per-step |h*g| to 1 feature with FS::Min.
[SlopeSlide, graph-meta-filters] No lattice of its own and no branches. Taps: N*(D+1)+1, so 4/5/6 at N=1 and 10/13/16 at N=3 for 2D/3D/4D. On Perlin at N=1 about 4.4/11/26 ns (scalar prototype measured 4.4x perlin2), comparable to CellularDistance in 2D and cheaper in 3D and 4D. Dimension agnostic via a GenT stencil table.
master.continuity: Mathematically C0 (composition of continuous steps), numerically a step at watersheds: measured c0ratio 1.0..1.2, max slope about 2400 per unit. Inside a basin it is smooth.
master.params: Field (GeneratorSource); Steps int; StepLen hybrid (sampled at p0 only, so spatially varying descent length is free); Epsilon float for finite differences; Direction enum; Normalise bool; Output enum; CellScale float; Basin GeneratorSource (optional). Seeded + ScalableGenerator mixins.
master.risks:
Cost scales with N x field cost; FBm fields get expensive (use GeneratorCache-style thinking, or let the field be a cheaper noise than the terrain). Large h overshoots pits and oscillates (Normalise + h <= 0.25 feature avoids it). BasinId has lattice edges where flow has not converged.
[Catchment, dynamics-iteration] Unconverged areas near flat maxima or saddles show hatched grain (fixed-step limit cycle); decaying step fixes most of it, and it worsens beyond 3 octaves. Basins are not guaranteed to reach the minimum in N steps on big features, so Step*N should match the source's feature scale. Border aliasing is unavoidable at the output level.
[BasinFlow, distribution-topology] Comb-shaped artifacts and rippled patches appear where trajectories bounce along narrow ridges and do not converge in N steps, visible even at N=14. Plateau values retain faint rings. Cell ID by rounding fails unless convergence is good. Expensive; smooth 1-octave sources only. The histogram is spiky by nature. This is the riskiest idea on the list.
master.cost_note: Costs (AVX2 est.): 2D N=6 forward diffs, Perlin field: 18 Perlin = ~20 ns (18x Perlin); 3D: 24 Perlin3D = ~53 ns; 4D: 30 Perlin4D = ~130 ns.
master.variant_notes: Fixed-count gradient descent then read something at the landing point. Regimes: N=1 small step gives ridge-network plates, overshoot gives ripple interiors, N=3-4 gives flat basins, decaying N=12 gives true watershed cells. Outputs merged from Catchment, SlopeSlide, BasinFlow, FlowDescentBasin and DomainWarpGradientDescent: value, distance, rings, height-above-drain, label, path min, or a Warp() displacement.

measured.scalar_note: Measured on the default out=0 before the recentre, which adds no taps; out=7,oct=1 measured 57.31. Both include a param map lookup per sample.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, tap count x handbook Perlin cost: default 50 taps ~55 / 3D 66 taps ~145 / 4D 82 taps ~350 ns; oct=1 halves it

implicit-warp.look: Overlapping folded sheets: broad smooth facets bounded by crisp scalloped hairline creases, with small tight swirl pockets where creases meet. Reads as folded satin, foil or layered petals, and the threshold panel shows hooked marble shapes. The fbm source adds soft streaks inside each facet. The sweep runs from a mild curled inverse (A=0.6) through crumple (A=1) to torn foil (A=2.2, damp=0.6), then white static at damp=1 with A>=1.5. The 3D slice shows the same creases. Vol shows sharp-edged folded shells. The relief and the extra thumbs were rendered but not inspected individually.
implicit-warp.dims: 2D and 3D measured; 4D not prototyped (one more Perlin per step)
implicit-warp.range: [-1,1] follows the source, clamped (8 seeds min -1, max 1, mean 0.003)
implicit-warp.artifacts: c0ratio 2.8, slope 450 per unit: steep creases at the probe scale, continuous by construction since it is a composition of continuous steps. I did not confirm that by bisection. The FFT has straight rays from long creases. Wide view shows an even petal scale because V is single octave. The regime change is abrupt: damp=1 with A>=1.5 is static, so damp needs a sensible default.
implicit-warp.node_shape: DomainWarpImplicit: Warp Amplitude (hybrid), Damp (float), Iterations (int), Warp Frequency (via ScalableGenerator), Seed Offset; Warp() returns q-p so it composes with any source and with the warp fractals
implicit-warp.port_notes: No masks, fixed N loop of d noise evals and a lerp, using one noise with seed offsets per axis. A graph cannot do this because each step needs the original p as well as the moved q. Needs fnlab seams to confirm the creases are steep and not true jumps. Sample Damp once at p if it becomes hybrid.
implicit-warp.params_text: A=1.5,damp=0.4,N=6,wf=1,src=3,of=1.2,so=3 (plain render). src=1 stripes and src=0 single Perlin also read well. A=1,damp=0.6 is a calmer crumple.

master.one_liner: Domain warp by damped fixed point q = p + A*V(q) rather than one forward step, which produces crumpled-foil creases and folded sheets instead of the smeared look of forward warps.
master.look: Verified in prototype. A=1: triangular crumpled paper facets with crisp creases. A=1.3: folded satin or foil with sharp ridges and swirl pockets. A=2: chaotic torn foil with fine detail in small regions and smooth elsewhere. Good for crumpled materials, rock folds, cloth and metal textures, alien terrain.
master.algorithm: q=p; repeat N (6..10): V=(n1(q), n2(q)[, n3(q)[, n4(q)]]); q=lerp(q, p+A*V, Damp). Return Source(q) as a generator, or implement Warp() so q-p is the warp displacement. Below A*Lipschitz<1 this is the exact inverse of a forward warp; above it, the iterates oscillate and period-double, which is where the creases appear. Prototype: dyn_lens mode=20,N=6,A=1.3,damp=0.6,of=1.2 and N=10,A=2,damp=0.4.
master.why_new: Forward warps stretch into streaks; the inverse compresses where forward stretches, so the visual vocabulary is flipped into creases and facets. Known nested warps f(p+fbm(p+fbm(p))) use a few undamped levels and do not reach this crease regime; Damp is the key control, and it goes from a smooth inverse through to period-doubling folds.
master.simd_plan: N x D noise evals + source. 2D 12 evals about 14 ns; 3D 18 evals about 40 ns; 4D 24 evals about 100 ns. Fits the DomainWarp base class and Warp() interface, so it composes with DomainWarpFractal. Reuse one noise with offset coordinates rather than separate nodes.
master.continuity: C0 always (continuous composition). Slope up to (1+A*L)^N in the chaotic regime; measured c0ratio 5 at A=1.3, max slope about 320 per unit. Not a smooth function along creases.
master.params: Warp Amplitude (hybrid), Damp float, Iterations int, Warp frequency, Source.
master.risks: Regime change is abrupt in A; above about 2 it becomes grainy in patches. Low Iterations combined with low Damp just looks like a weak warp.
master.cost_note: 2D 12 evals about 14 ns; 3D 18 evals about 40 ns; 4D 24 evals about 100 ns.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, tap count x handbook Perlin cost: default 15 taps ~17 / 3D 21 taps ~46 / 4D 27 taps ~116 ns

impulse-warp.look: Clean spiral whorls and comma curls of several sizes on otherwise undisturbed soft fbm, in a clear Van Gogh style. Arms stay coherent at 7 radians. Threshold panel shows crisp curled paisley shapes. Where kernels overlap, the arms link into knots and broken rings, and that gets busy from amp=14 or at density=1 with R=1.05. On stripes it gives loops hanging off straight bands. Displacement magnitude shows ring-shaped kernels. 3D slice shows the same whorls, softer, and the vol of warped stripes shows curled slabs with spiral cut faces.
impulse-warp.dims: 2D and 3D measured (random rotation axis per eddy); 4D not prototyped (plane form from the catalogue)
impulse-warp.range: [-1,1] follows the source, clamped (8 seeds min -1, max 1, mean 0)
impulse-warp.artifacts: No seams (c0ratio 7.31, slope 53.5; amp=14 gives 6.27, slope 116). Knots where kernels overlap, because rotations are summed and not composed. FFT shows faint petal lobes from long arcs. The wide view is even, with no visible lattice at jitter 0.9.
impulse-warp.node_shape: Kernel = Impulse on the sparse warp in DomainWarpCurl: Warp Amplitude (hybrid), Radius, Radius Variation, Density (hybrid via smooth gate), Grid Jitter, Mode {Vortex, Lens}
impulse-warp.port_notes: Window fits: R <= 1.5 - 0.5*jitter in lattice units for a 3x3 or 3x3x3 window, and R=0.9 at jitter 0.9 is inside that. Sin and Cos per point, all points evaluated, weight zero outside.
