Why merged: scatter-warp already judged this exact kernel as one to fold into DomainWarpCurl, and domain-warp-curl's node shape does not list it yet. The look is strong on its own, so make sure the Impulse kernel survives the merge. Per-eddy radius variation (rv) is new here and clearly improves it by giving several whorl sizes.
impulse-warp.params_text: amp=7,R=0.9,density=0.7,rv=0.5,jitter=0.9,ef=0.7,src=1,of=1.2,so=3 (plain render). src=0,of=1.5,amp=8 stripes; mode=1,amp=1 lens (rendered, not inspected); src=3,of=1.5 for vol

master.one_liner: Domain warp built from sparse discrete eddies: exact local rotations about lattice points, so spiral arms remain coherent even at many radians of twist.
master.look: Marble eddies, Jupiter bands, oil film, whirlpools, Van Gogh swirls; calm areas next to tight knots. Prototyped: a stripe source becomes tight knotted loops, and fractal source becomes marbled swirl. Very unlike DomainWarpSimplex, which shears without closed spirals.
master.algorithm: For window points with rnd < Density: v = x-c; w = max(0, 1 - r^2/R^2)^2; th = Amp*rnd11*w. Plane rotation form, valid in any dimension with orthonormal pair (g,h): a = g.v, b = h.v; dx += (cos(th)-1)*(a*g + b*h) + sin(th)*(a*h - b*g). 2D: g,h = basis, simply R(th)v - v. Mode Lens: dx += Amp*rnd11*w*v (pinch and bubble). Warp() adds dx to the positions as all warps do. Fades smooth-gated by Density so a hybrid density does not pop.
master.why_new: Displacements from gradient noise are not rotation preserving: amplitude yields folding, not spirals. Rotation about centres keeps radii, so 10+ radians still give clean arms. Sparsity gives quiet areas, which domain-warp nodes today cannot.
master.simd_plan: Each point: 2 dots, Sin+Cos. 2D 9 points: about 8 ns, 3D 2^3 corners with R<=1-jitter: 8-10 ns, 27 points: 30 ns, 4D 2^4: 15 ns. Fits the Warp interface, costs as simplex warp-class. Proto 6.9x perlin2 with 19 points including a source.
master.continuity: C1 when kernels overlap, since the weights are C1 (measured c0ratio 7.66 with high slope due to tight twist).
master.params: Amplitude (hybrid), Radius, Density (hybrid via smooth gate), Mode enum (Vortex, Lens), Grid Jitter.
master.risks: Overlapping rotations are added, not composed, so strong overlap slightly folds; bounded at reasonable density. Tight spirals alias at Amp>10, especially at low feature scale. Sampling the source once per warp is fine.
master.cost_note: 2D 9 points: about 8 ns, 3D 2^3 corners with R<=1-jitter: 8-10 ns, 27 points: 30 ns, 4D 2^4: 15 ns.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 9 eddies with Sin+Cos ~8 ns plus a 3 octave source ~3 ns, ~11 ns in 2D; 27 eddies plus source ~35 ns in 3D

stir-advect.look: Ink marbling: black and white ribbons roll into hooks, mushroom caps and small spiral eyes, and everything stays laminated with no blotches. The threshold panel is crisp suminagashi. The 3D slice has longer sheared streaks and fewer eyes, which is honest for 3D curl. Vol shows thin curled sheets. Fbm and Worley sources in the sweep give fine stirred paint. T=3.5 turns to speckled static, and at the wide view the default already reads as fine noise. RK2 tightens the eyes and closes orbits, which reads better than Euler at the same N but costs double. Euler with N=5 is rougher but still marbled.
stir-advect.dims: 2D and 3D measured (3D is the true curl of 3 Perlin potentials); 4D not prototyped
stir-advect.range: [-1,1] with stripes, histogram piled at both ends (8 seeds mean -0.001)
stir-advect.artifacts: Filaments thin exponentially with T. The probe reads c0ratio 1.17, slope 1708 at T=1.4, 4.00, slope 492 at T=1, and 1.00, slope 1999 at T=2.5. The map is continuous by construction, so these are sub-probe filaments and not lattice seams, but they will alias in practice. No lattice in the FFT.
stir-advect.node_shape: Covered by DomainWarpFlow at angle 90 (Potential, Steps, Length, Integrator). Bring over the 3 potential curl for 3D as an isotropic option, plus an analytic gradient Perlin fast path
stir-advect.port_notes: Fixed N, analytic gradients need no finite differences so it costs 12.35x Perlin against the 17.55x domain-warp-flow measured with forward differences at a different step count. Document T around 1 to 1.5 per feature. Why merged: domain-warp-flow reached the same marbling with the same step loop. This look is keeper quality.
stir-advect.params_text: N=12,T=1.4,sf=1.2,src=0,rk=0 (plain render). T=1 is cleaner and measured smoother. src=1,sf=1.5 fbm; src=2,sf=1.5 Worley; vol used N=8,T=1.2.

master.one_liner: Advect the sample backward N small steps along a divergence-free (stream-function) field so textures stretch into laminated marbling filaments instead of blotchy warps.
master.look: Paper-marbling / Suminagashi: long, thin, parallel laminations that fold on themselves without tearing or smearing; a SineWave or Checkerboard source becomes classic marbled stripes, Perlin becomes fluid-mixed swirls, Cellular becomes stretched cells with intact edges. Clearly different from Warp Fractal Progressive, which (being a single large-amplitude non-area-preserving displacement) folds and blotches. Good for marble, agate, fluid, wood figure, cloud shear.
master.algorithm:
Field: 2D V = (-d psi/dy, d psi/dx) from one potential psi; dimension-agnostic rule: for each axis pair (i,j) in the cycle (x,y),(y,z),(z,w),(w,x) use a seeded potential psi_ij and add its in-plane rotated gradient to components i and j. 2D: 1 potential, 3D: 3 (= curl), 4D: 4. Every such term is divergence free, so the composite flow preserves volume.

  p = p0
  for k in 0..N-1:
      v  = V(p)                                   // analytic gradients (internal gradient Perlin) or forward-difference d+1 evals per potential
      pm = p - 0.5*h*v                            // RK2 midpoint (optional, 2 field evals/step; Euler with small h is acceptable)
      p  = p - h*V(pm)
  DomainWarpFlow: Warp() adds (p - p0) to positions; or Generator form: out = B(p) with B a GeneratorSource (stripes, checkerboard, Perlin, cellular...).
Total 'stir time' T = N*h controls mixing: small T = gentle wobble, T >> 1/|grad V| = exponentially stretched laminae.

[DomainWarpFlow, volumetric-3d4d] Wrapper over a DomainWarp source (same Warp interface). Warp(p): with step h = Amount/N; repeat N: v = Inner.displacement(p); p = p + h*v. If h*Lip(v) < 1 the map is injective and homeomorphic to identity, so any connected tunnel stays connected and any tube stays a tube: use with BondTunnels and LevelSetDistance. Curl-based inner flow makes it nearly volume preserving (for tube width near constant). Amount as hybrid or via w gives true advection: source pattern is carried along streamlines rather than boiling. Two-phase flow-map trick for looping: F = lerp(S(flow(p, t mod 1)), S(flow(p, (t+.5) mod 1)), triangle(t)) with sqrt-normalised weights, 2 source evals.
master.why_new: Existing warps are one-shot, position-only displacements; large amplitude gives folds and overlaps. Iterating many small steps along a divergence-free field yields the flow map of an incompressible fluid, which stretches material lines exponentially while preserving area, and that is exactly what makes marbling look like marbling. A graph cannot chain N warps that each depend on the already-moved position with one shared field.
master.simd_plan: Same engine as FlowWatershed: fixed N loop, each step d potentials x (d+1 or analytic) evals, rotated-gradient assembly is pure FMAs, no masks. Cost (AVX2 est.): 2D Euler N=8 with internal gradient Perlin: 8 x 1.6 = ~13x Perlin (~14 ns); forward-difference arbitrary potential: 24 evals (~26 ns). 3D: 3 potentials: analytic 8x3x1.6x2.2 = ~85 ns; FD 96 Perlin3D (~210 ns). 4D: 4 potentials ~ 8x4x1.6x4.3 = ~220 ns. Expensive in 3D/4D, acceptable for a look node; RK2 doubles. Tiling preserved (position stays a function of the 4D point).
master.continuity: Continuous and smooth: flow map of a smooth field; C1 with analytic gradients, C0 with finite differences on a C0 potential. No seams.
master.params: Potential (GeneratorSource, optional; default internal gradient Perlin), Steps int, StepLen hybrid, Strength hybrid (scales V), Integrator enum (Euler/RK2), Epsilon float (finite diff), as DomainWarp-family: Warp Amplitude mixin; Generator form adds Source B.
master.risks:
3D/4D cost; too large h makes Euler non-area-preserving (use RK2 or h <= 0.1 feature); visually requires N*h >= ~2 features to look marbled, i.e. 10-20 steps; without a gradient-capable noise inside the library every step pays finite-difference evaluations.
[DomainWarpFlow, volumetric-3d4d] Untested. Cost multiplier. Euler errors at low N can still fold where hybrid amplitude is large, so injectivity requires h*Lip(v)<1, which is only checkable numerically. Long stretches create very high local frequencies in Source, aliasing at large Amount. Hybrid Amount varying across space adds extra deformation and loses the volume property. Overlap with chained warp graphs is a real argument against, so value must show up in usability and guaranteed topology.
master.cost_note: Cost (AVX2 est.): 2D Euler N=8 with internal gradient Perlin: 8 x 1.6 = ~13x Perlin (~14 ns); forward-difference arbitrary potential: 24 evals (~26 ns).
master.variant_notes: Small-step flow-map integration. The DomainWarpFlow (volumetric) wrapper form integrates any existing warp and adds the guarantee that a homeomorphic warp cannot change topology, for caves, plus a two-phase looping mode.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 12 steps x gradient Perlin at ~1.6x Perlin = ~21 ns in 2D; 3D 12 x 3 potentials x 1.6 x 2.2 = ~127 ns; 4D 12 x 4 x 1.6 x 4.3 = ~330 ns

anchored-frame-detail.look: Default: flowing hair or fern fronds. Long thin ridged strokes run downhill and fan out radially from every peak and basin of the control, meeting at parting lines; threshold panel shows dark splinters aligned with the flow. The wide view shows even strokes with no lattice repeat. orient=1: fingerprint and wood grain swirls with concentric rings around every extremum. Terrain mode relief is the best image of this idea: gullies run straight down every slope and fade out on flats, looks like eroded hills. The 3D volume shows elongated tubes and pits that lean with the control; it is real but less striking than the 2D form.

dims.3D: works, measured: z-continuity max 0.0375 for dz=1e-3, volume rendered. orient=1 gives sheets following isosurfaces of the control, orient=0 gives fibres along its gradient.
dims.4D: works, measured on a plane through Eval in 4D: c0ratio 8.08, no NaN. Mean is 0.438 in that slice, so the recentring constant is too small for 4D because perlin4 here has a narrower amplitude; a port would need a per-dimension constant.

anchored-frame-detail.range: -1 .. 1 over 8 seeds with mean 0.037, clamped after a measured recentring of the ridged detail. Far coords (4e4) std 0.461, same as near.
anchored-frame-detail.artifacts: A few cross-hatched spots and blobs at critical points where the frames disagree, and the slope fade turns detail isotropic there, which reads as a small rough patch. Cell above about 1.0 starts to show crossing strokes at the anchor overlap: cell=1.2 in the sweep was visibly more crossed than 0.6. FFT is a soft isotropic cloud with no grid dots, axis stat 5.52 only. The 3D XZ slice mixes streaked and rough zones because a plane cuts the fibres at varying angles.
anchored-frame-detail.node_shape: AnchoredFrameDetail: Control (GeneratorSource), Detail (GeneratorSource, should be isotropic), Cell Size float, Along Frequency float, Across Frequency float, Orientation enum {Across contours, Along contours}, Weight Sharpness float, Slope Fade float, Sample Distance float, Anchors enum {Simplex, Corners}, Base Mix hybrid, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
anchored-frame-detail.port_notes: Two changes from the catalogue, both measured here. (1) Kuhn simplex anchors: sort the fractions and walk D+1 corners with barycentric weights lambda^sharp. This looked as good as 2^D corners in a direct table and cuts cost by 1.3x in 2D, 2.0x in 3D and 3.0x in 4D. (2) No frame and no up vector: stretch with S = fp*I + (fa-fp)*u*u^T, which needs only u = g/|g| in any dimension. That only suits an isotropic Detail; a user supplied anisotropic Detail would need real frames. Sorting in a port is Select swaps on D values, as Simplex does. Detail is sampled at anchored local offsets plus a per-anchor hash offset up to 100 units, so far coords stay stable. Slope fade g2/(g2+e2) makes the anisotropy go away where the frame is arbitrary. Weights fall to 0 on simplex faces, which is the continuity point; a port evaluates all anchors. Scalar uses a branch to skip weight 0.
anchored-frame-detail.params_text: Code defaults (hair, streaks across contours): cell=0.6,fa=0.25,fp=6,cf=0.14,coct=1,sharp=3,orient=0,ridge=1,doct=2,lat=1,h=0.25,slope=0.12. Strata along contours: orient=1,fa=0.3,fp=7. Terrain with downhill gullies: out=1,amt=0.14,cf=0.2,cell=0.5,fp=8,fa=0.3 --window 12.

master.one_liner: Gradient-aligned detail that actually works pointwise: a detail source is evaluated in local frames rotated to the gradient of a control source at 2^D lattice anchors and blended with variance-preserving weights, giving gullies that run downhill or strata that run along contours.
master.look: Brush-stroke / fur-like hatching whose stroke direction follows the control field's gradient everywhere (proto sheetD m12): with Across it reads as erosion gullies pointing downhill, with Along as terracettes/strata following the contours; the hatching reorganises around every peak and saddle. On the contact sheet nothing is direction-coherent with a second field. Uses: slope-aligned erosion detail on terrains, wood grain following a shape, flow-combed fur/grass, anisotropic rock strata.
master.algorithm:
Params: Control (GeneratorSource, e.g. the terrain), Detail (GeneratorSource, e.g. an anisotropic Simplex via DomainAxisScale), Cell Size c, Epsilon, Along/Across enum, Mix (hybrid) if the node also adds the base.
GenT(pos): X = pos / c; i0 = floor(X); t = X - i0 (quintic/hermite weights).
For each of the 2^D anchors a = (i0 + corner) * c:
  g = central-difference gradient of Control at a        // 2D taps per anchor, NOT at pos
  frame: 2D u = g/|g|, v = perp(u); 3D: u = g/|g|, v = normalize(up - (up.u)u) with Select to a second up vector when |up.u| > 0.9, w = u x v
  o = pos - a ; local = (o.u, o.v[, o.w]) + hash(a) * 100   // per-anchor decorrelation offset
  d_a = Detail(local)
  w_a = prod_axes (corner ? h(t) : 1 - h(t))
return sum w_a d_a / sqrt(sum w_a^2)                        // variance preserving, no contrast loss in the overlaps
The trick: the naive version (rotate the global coordinates by the gradient at pos) fails because a direction change dTheta moves the sample by |pos| dTheta, which the proto shows as white noise (sheetD m7). Anchoring the frame origin at the lattice point bounds the lever arm to one cell, so the detail is coherent inside each cell and crossfades between cells.
master.why_new: The existing graph cannot rotate a domain by a spatially varying angle at all (DomainRotate is constant), and the one spatially varying rotation that is pointwise-correct requires the anchor-blend trick plus a gradient per anchor, which no composition of existing nodes expresses. It makes the standard 'erosion stripes aligned to slope' look available as one node on any heightfield.
master.simd_plan: GenT with 2^D anchors unrolled: each anchor costs 2D Control taps (gradient) + 1 Detail eval. 2D: 4 x (4 + 1) = 20 evals, 3D: 8 x (6 + 1) = 56, 4D: 16 x 9 = 144 (offer Forward differences to cut to 4x4 / 8x5 / 16x6, or treat w as pass-through in 4D). With Simplex control and detail, 2D ~26 ns AVX2, 3D ~150 ns: heavy but a one-shot detail layer, comparable to a 4D CellularDistance. Frame construction is branch-free (InvSqrt, Select for the up-vector fallback). Scalar proto: 59x perlin2, consistent with 20 evals.
master.continuity: C0 (proto c0ratio 8.0): the anchor frames are constants per anchor, the blend weights are C1 hermite, and the per-anchor detail is a C0 function of pos. Frames flip discontinuously between anchors where the control gradient rotates by ~180 degrees, but the crossfade hides it; it appears as crossing strokes (the hatching look).
master.params: Control, Detail (nodes); Cell Size (should be >= the detail's correlation length along the stroke; proto used 0.7-1.0 units with 6x anisotropy); Epsilon; Orientation {Across gradient, Along contour}; Up vector (3D); optional Base Mix hybrid so the node outputs Control*(1-m) + Detail*m in one go.
master.risks: Cell size versus detail anisotropy is a real tuning knob: too small a cell shows the anchor lattice as a patchwork, too large loses direction fidelity; the proto's default looks like cross-hatching rather than clean parallel gullies, which may or may not be wanted. Critical points of Control (|g| ~ 0) give arbitrary frames; the InvSqrt epsilon floor keeps it finite. 3D frames need an up vector fallback; 4D is a cost problem.
master.cost_note: With Simplex control and detail, 2D ~26 ns AVX2, 3D ~150 ns: heavy but a one-shot detail layer, comparable to a 4D CellularDistance.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 986.7 ns vs perlin2 50.5, params read once. 3 simplex anchors x (4 control taps + 2 detail octaves) = 18 perlin evals. Corner lattice lat=0: 25.64x. 3D plane dim=3: 55.38x simplex anchors, 109.03x corners. 4D plane dim=4: 57.98x simplex anchors, 175.47x corners. Terrain out=1: 20.81x.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured on SIMD: by eval count x handbook Perlin cost, 2D 18 x 1.1 = 20 ns, 3D 32 x 2.2 = 70 ns, 4D 50 x 4.3 = 215 ns with central differences and 2 detail octaves.
measured.c0_note: Default 6.92, orient=1 7.46, 4D plane 8.08, terrain out=1 7.54. Sheet with orient=1 8.1.

cell-lens.look: Default: flat irregular plates, each at the source value of its centre, ringed by a narrow band where the compressed source shows as bright or dark rims and small radial streaks. Hillshade reads as stained glass or crazy paving with bevelled edges. Relief is the strong one: both Voronoi and hex give convincing basalt column fields, flat tops at different heights with vertical walls. BCC volume is the surprise: caves whose walls are hexagonal and square facets, a voxel look that is not cubic. Droplet mode shows ring craters on textured background, reads loosely as a compound eye. Negative pull gives crumpled paper with soft pinch points.

dims.3D: works, measured: Voronoi with 27 cell window and BCC truncated octahedra, both viewed as volumes.
dims.4D: works, measured on a plane: Voronoi with 81 cell window and Cubic. No D4 lattice was built; lat=2 falls back to cubic in 4D.

cell-lens.range: Follows the source, -1 .. 1 over 8 seeds with soct=4, mean 0.001. The plain 512 render spans -0.823 .. 0.829.
cell-lens.artifacts: Rims in 2D are the source at very high compression, so they alias with a high frequency source; soct=4 is near the limit for bevel=0.12. On the volume the walls show small stair steps where facets meet at shallow angles, from thin bevel bands. Voronoi F2-F1 bevel narrows near vertices, as the catalogue noted, and it does not read as a flaw. Wide view shows no repeat for Voronoi; the hex and square lattices are a visible lattice by intent. Histogram is spiky, because plates are flat, which is expected.
cell-lens.node_shape: CellLens: Lattice enum {Voronoi, Square, Hex/BCC, Brick}, Cell Size float, Grid Jitter float, Pull hybrid (negative allowed), Bevel hybrid, Source (GeneratorSource), Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
cell-lens.port_notes: One source eval. q = X + off * smoothstep(0, Bevel, edge) * Pull, where off is the offset to centre and edge goes to 0 at every wall, so the swap of centre is at t=0. Voronoi takes F1 offset and F2 from the Cellular window. Hex: two rectangular sublattices with one Select, wall distance 0.5 - Max(|fx|, |fx|/2 + |fy|*0.866). BCC: Z^3 and Z^3+0.5 with one Select, wall distance Min(0.5 - Max|f_i|, (0.75 - Sum|f_i|)/sqrt 3). Generic for dims except the lattice functions; D4 is not done. Pull and Bevel can be hybrid since they only scale a continuous function. This subsumes DomainSnap and Keep=Centre of DomainQuantize when Bevel is small; the Rotated and Mirrored modes of DomainQuantize are not implemented here, because the catalogue places them with CellularPatchwork.
cell-lens.params_text: Code defaults (bevelled Voronoi plates): lat=0,cell=1,pull=1,bevel=0.12,jit=0.9,sf=0.45,soct=4. Basalt: pull=1,bevel=0.08,sf=0.5 --window 16. Hex plates: lat=2. Square lat=1, brick lat=3. BCC voxels in 3D: lat=2,pull=1,bevel=0.08,sf=0.5,soct=3 --iso 0. Droplets: pull=0.65,bevel=0.5,sf=2.2,soct=3,cell=1.4. Crumple: pull=-0.8,bevel=0.3,sf=0.8.

master.one_liner: Continuous CellularLookup: pulls the domain toward each cell centre, from flat bevelled plates through bead lenses to anti-lenses, single source eval.
master.look:
Basalt columns, mesas, cracked-mud plates, stained-glass with bevelled lead, rain droplets on glass, compound-eye lenses. Hex and Square lattices give pixel/hex/voxel mosaic with continuous bevel, covering quantise, pixelate, hex-snap, voxelise in one node. Prototyped Voronoi: mode=5.
[DomainSnap, domain-geometry] Pixel-art / hex-pixel versions of any noise (hex-pixelated FBm is a ready hex-grid strategy map; voxelised 3D noise is a blocky cave field), and at intermediate hardness a 'bathroom glass' / lens-array look where each cell shows a slowed-down, magnified patch of the source with fast transitions at the borders. With Jitter + hard: random block sampling.
[DomainQuantize, graph-meta-filters] Proto sheetB m10: a Voronoi mosaic of rotated fragments of one FBm: every shard carries a coherent piece of the field at its own orientation, like shattered glass or crazy paving, with hard cracks at cell edges. Square + Centre is pixel art of any node; Hex + Centre is hex pixels (no existing node can produce a hex lattice look); Square + Mirrored gives kaleidoscopic tiles. Uses: stylised maps, tile-based art, broken ice/rock plates, cracked paint, puzzle textures.
master.algorithm:
Find F1, F2 and nearest centre c (Voronoi) or analytic cell (Square, Hex, Brick). edge = (F2-F1)/2 (for square/hex: analytic distance to cell edge). t = smoothstep(0, Bevel, edge) * Pull. q = lerp(p, c, t). Output S(q). At edges t=0 so q=p from both sides, and c swaps only there. Use F2-F1 rather than true bisector distance to the F2 cell: the first prototype used bisector distance to F2 and jumped where F2 swaps with F3 (c0ratio 1.0); F2-F1 is continuous (c0ratio 7.74). Pull=1 with small Bevel: flat plates at S(c) with walls where the whole source between c and p is squeezed into a rim, showing radial streaks. Pull 0.5-0.9: magnifying droplet. Pull<0: minified crumple toward centre.

[DomainSnap, domain-geometry] Params: Lattice enum {Square, Hex (2D) / BCC (3D) / D4 (4D), Cubic}, Cell Size L, Hardness h (hybrid, 0..1), Jitter j, Random Flip (bool).

  c = nearest lattice point to p (Square/Cubic: Round(p/L)*L; Hex: axial coords + cube rounding with 2 Selects; BCC: round on both cubic sublattices (Round(p/L), Round(p/L - 0.5)+0.5) and keep the closer with one Select set; D4: same idea with the checkerboard sublattice)
  f = p - c                                             // offset inside the Voronoi cell of the lattice
  n = cellNorm(f) / halfWidth                           // = 1 exactly on the cell boundary: Square: Max(|fx|,|fy|)/(L/2); Hex: Max_i |Dot(f, e_i)| / apothem over the 3 edge normals; BCC: Max(Max|f_i|, (|fx|+|fy|+|fz|)/1.5)/(L/2)
  m = h / (1 - h + eps)                                 // exponent: 0 => identity, large => flat plateau
  g = Pow(n + eps, m)                                   // radial profile: 1 on the boundary for every h, ~0 deep inside for large m
  q = c + f * g                                         // soft snap: the cell interior collapses toward c, the boundary stays put => continuous across cells
  if Jitter: q += j * L * rnd11(Hash(seed, c))          // per-cell content shift (texture-bombing-lite)
  if RandomFlip: q = c + Select(bits(Hash), -(q-c), q-c) per axis   // per-cell mirror; only continuous at h=1
  return Source.Gen(seed, q)

h = 1 (m -> infinity) is handled as g = 0 with a Select (hard pixelate / voxelise). Dimension agnostic apart from the lattice rounding and the cell norm.

[DomainQuantize, graph-meta-filters] Params: Source; Cell Size (hybrid); Lattice enum {Square, Hex (2D) / BCC (3D), Voronoi (jitter param, 3^D window)}; Keep enum; Rotation Steps (0 = free angle, 4 = quarter turns); Inset (hybrid).
GenT: find the cell centre c for pos (Square: floor + 0.5; Hex: axial rounding; Voronoi: the F1 point from a CellularDistance-style window, as CellularLookup does).
  o = pos - c
  Keep=Centre : q = c                                 // == CellularLookup for Voronoi, pixelate for Square
  Keep=Offset : q = c + o * Inset                     // Inset<1 shrinks the fragment content (grout)
  Keep=Rotated: theta = hash(c) -> angle (quantised to Rotation Steps if > 0); q = c + R(theta) o (3D: random axis-angle from the hash)
  Keep=Mirrored: q = c + o * sign bits from hash(c) per axis
  return Source(q)
Note: for Keep=Offset with Inset=1 and Square lattice the node is the identity; the interesting cases are rotations/mirrors, which make the fragment boundaries visible as discontinuities while the interiors stay coherent.
master.why_new: Fade(CellularLookup, Source, F2-F1) lerps values and costs 2 source evals plus 2 searches. This warps the domain, so the rim shows compressed real source rather than a crossfade, costs one eval, and is not discontinuous like CellularLookup or DomainSnap.
master.simd_plan: Reuse Cellular search (F1,F2, offset to nearest). 3.9/12/41 ns plus one source for Voronoi; analytic Square or Hex about 0.5-1 ns. Generic GenT works for all dims. Hybrid Pull and Bevel sampled at p.
master.continuity: C0; C1 at the edge if Bevel smoothstep starts flat. Measured c0ratio 7.74-7.82. Bevel=0 gives hard snap (discontinuous, deliberately).
master.params: Lattice enum (Voronoi, Square, Hex, Brick), Cell Size, Grid Jitter, Pull (hybrid, may be negative), Bevel (hybrid), Source.
master.risks:
Rims contain very compressed source and can alias if the source is high frequency and Bevel small. F2-F1 is not true edge distance, so bevel width varies along an edge with centre spacing (narrow near vertices), though in the prototype this reads as natural.
[DomainSnap, domain-geometry] Pow per sample (cheap but present); Hex cell norm must use the same orientation as the rounding; at mid hardness the profile is C0 at the cell centre (kink) which can read as a dot in hillshade; feature interplay between the cell size and the source scale needs presets.
master.cost_note: 3.9/12/41 ns plus one source for Voronoi; analytic Square or Hex about 0.5-1 ns.
master.variant_notes: Continuous pull toward cell centres, on Voronoi or analytic lattices. Hard limit is plain pixelate; hex and BCC snapping are not otherwise reachable. DomainQuantize's rotated and mirrored Keep modes overlap CellularPatchwork.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 282.5 ns vs perlin2 51.3 with a 4 octave fbm source, so 4 of the 5.5x is the source. Square 4.48x, hex 4.79x, brick 4.69x. dim=3 Voronoi 13.76x, dim=3 BCC 9.11x, dim=4 Voronoi 17.27x, dim=4 cubic 4.16x. Lens overhead alone in 2D: Voronoi about 1.5x perlin; analytic about 0.5x to 0.8x perlin, by subtracting the source.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured on SIMD: lens only, Voronoi 3.9 / 12 / 41 ns as CellularDistance F2-F1, analytic Square, Hex or BCC about 0.5 to 1 ns. Add one Source eval.
measured.c0_note: Voronoi 7.71, square 7.64, hex 7.75, brick 7.58, pull .7 8.06, hex pull .7 7.97, pull -.8 7.96, 3D plane Voronoi 7.81, 3D BCC 7.67 after a fix, 4D Voronoi plane 7.42, 4D cubic 7.73. Check found c0ratio 1.00 on 3D BCC first, caused by a wrong hex face distance in my code; fixed and the volume re-rendered. Voronoi uses a 3^D window at jit=0.9 and no jump appeared in the probe.

closest-point-transport.look: Satin or mother-of-pearl flowers: five to eight petal fans radiate from every extremum of the guide, each petal a smooth streak of the target, and thin crisp seams separate the fans where projection direction splits. Threshold panel shows large clean curved blades. Low tf reads as polished metal, high tf as mica or cracked glass. Relief of the terrain mode has ribs running down from each peak with sharp creases along divides, like a sculpted drape or tent, with visible jagged steps on the seams. Volume is the surprise: large folded petal solids with knife edges.

dims.3D: works, measured and viewed: Eval3 real, z-continuity max 0.1129 for dz=1e-3 (seams), the volume shows curved petals and fins that meet at sharp creases. This verifies the catalogue's unverified 3D claim in a different form from what it predicted: folded sheets more than fibres.
dims.4D: works on a plane, measured, c0ratio 7.93 and no NaN. Not viewed.

closest-point-transport.range: -1 .. 1 over 8 seeds, mean -0.002, clamped with a 1.15 gain on the target. 3D slice -0.869 .. 0.830. Far coords (4e4) std 0.377.
closest-point-transport.artifacts: Seams are true jumps, so hillshade shows a hard line and the relief shows stair steps. With goct=2 or small e the seams fill with beaded chatter where Newton steps chaotically near saddles; goct=1 and e=0.1 removed nearly all of it, seen directly in the e sweep. e=0.3 softens fans noticeably and makes some blobs. Level L=0.25 adds more chatter where the level set vanishes in a region and the clamp decides the result. FFT has straight rays from the long straight fan edges, axis stat 11.56. Wide view is even with no repeat.
closest-point-transport.node_shape: ClosestPointTransport: Guide (GeneratorSource), Target (GeneratorSource), Level hybrid, Steps int 1-2, Max Step hybrid, Regularisation float, Sample Distance float, Feature Scale. A second output mode is not needed; the terrain use is a graph Add with Guide.
closest-point-transport.port_notes: Fixed N loop with D+1 guide taps per step using forward differences. Step = (S-L)/(|g|^2+e) * g, clamp length by scale k = maxs / Max(len, maxs). No branch. Dimension agnostic via GenT, so 4D and tiling work. It needs only Sqrt. Regularisation e is the quality knob, not Max Step: maxs from 0.6 to 4 changed little in the table, e changed the seams a lot. Default Guide should be smooth, because every guide octave adds critical points, adds chatter, and doubles the cost. A real node should document this, or offer an internal smooth guide.
closest-point-transport.params_text: Code defaults: gf=0.35,goct=1,L=0,N=2,maxs=1.5,e=0.1,h=0.1,tf=3,toct=2,tk=0. Mica shards: tf=10,goct=2,e=0.02. Ribbed terrain: out=1,amp=0.1,tf=2.5 --window 10. Volume: tf=1.5,toct=1 --iso 0.1.

master.one_liner: Newton-project each point onto a contour of S, then read a detail node there, which holds detail constant along gradient lines.
master.look: Petal, pinwheel and mica-like shards: radial fins fanning out of every peak and basin, meeting along sharp seams at the medial axis. At high target frequency it looks like cracked glass or crystal druse. Low frequency with N=1 and L=0.2 gives strong flower-like rosettes. In 3D it should give fibres growing perpendicular to an isosurface (stalactite or geode growth), not verified here.
master.algorithm: q = p. Repeat N (1-2): st = (S(q) - L)/(|g(q)|^2 + e), D = st*g, soft clamp D *= maxs/max(|D|, maxs), q -= D. Output Target(q). L is the iso level. Because every point on a gradient line lands on the same contour point, Target is smeared perpendicular to the contours and stays sharp along them. Fans form around each extremum.
master.why_new: Directional structure locked perpendicular to level sets of any field, with crisp seams at the medial axis, which warps cannot produce because they never collapse a whole line to one point. Uses the closest point method idea from PDE work, which I have not seen used as a noise node.
master.simd_plan: N*(D+2)+1 taps: 2D 5 or 9, 3D 6 or 11, 4D 7 or 13. Perlin-based 2D about 6-10 ns. Clamp is Max and Min only, no branch. Dimension agnostic.
master.continuity: Discontinuous by design along medial seams and around critical points. Measured c0ratio 1.16. Larger e softens fans near extrema but seams remain. The look depends on the jumps.
master.params: Level L (hybrid), Max Step (hybrid), Steps N, Regularisation e, Target source, Sample Distance h.
master.risks: Discontinuous output is a poor heightfield unless Target amplitude is small. Very high frequency target aliases at seams. Newton overshoot at low |g| is controlled only by the clamp, which sets the fan size.
master.cost_note: Perlin-based 2D about 6-10 ns.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 391.2 ns vs perlin2 49.6, N=2, params read once, forward differences, single octave guide. N=1 5.31x. dim=3 N=2 18.28x, dim=3 N=1 11.71x. dim=4 N=2 15.08x (this perlin4 is cheaper than perlin3 because it uses bit gradients). Earlier goct=2 setting measured 15.32x, because every guide tap doubles.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured on SIMD: taps N*(D+1) guide + target octaves. 2D N=2: 6 + 2 = 8 x 1.1 = 9 ns. 3D N=2: 8 + 2 = 10 x 2.2 = 22 ns. 4D N=2: 10 + 2 = 12 x 4.3 = 52 ns. Perlin sources assumed.
measured.c0_note: Discontinuous by design along medial seams, as the catalogue says. The 4D plane probe read 7.93 with max slope 113.7, but that plane just missed a seam at the probe scale; 2D max slope is 997.5. Terrain out=1 with amp=0.12 still 1.77, max slope 119.8.

domain-hilbert-ribbon.look: Grey streaks flowing along a rounded square-spiral corridor system on a dark floor; corridors are 0.4 units wide, turn constantly and never branch. Reads as a maze of rounded glyphs, close to brain coral or a circuit trace with flow marks. The threshold panel is a clean labyrinth. In 3D the isosurface is a tangled single tube, a mass of bowels cut by the box; busy, with little depth readable at this size. The final sheet at fade=6 was not checked by eye: the look comes from sweep panels at fade=3 and fade=8 at this cell size.

dims.note: 2D and 3D measured continuous. 4D not implemented; a node would drop w, so GenTileable2D would not tile

range.note: 8 seeds/offsets, default params; output floor is -wall, top from the fbm source

domain-hilbert-ribbon.artifacts: The maze is the same for every seed: the seed changes only the content of the ribbon. Same maze every 2^order cells (order 6 at cell 0.4 is 25.6 units). Wide view at 4x looks like a uniform grid-textured carpet, and the FFT has axis energy (axis 44). Features stretch through turn cells. Fixed-scale relief at default hscale was spiky columns, so no relief image is kept: the corridors are too narrow and steep to read as terrain.
domain-hilbert-ribbon.node_shape: DomainHilbertRibbon: Source (required), Order int, Cell Size float, Along Scale float, Across Scale hybrid, Edge Fade float (0 = off, then jumps across edges the curve does not cross), Wall Value float, Seed Offset.
domain-hilbert-ribbon.port_notes: The catalogue's constant 4x8 table from final quadrant and frame cannot work, because a corner cell's entry side depends on ancestors. Working 2D scheme, verified with 0 mismatches on crossed edges for orders 1..6: N uniform iterations of xy2d with a 3-bit signed permutation frame; exit direction comes from the deepest digit that is not 3, entry direction from the deepest digit that is not 0, each a Select per level. Blocks chain along +x (each ends at (n-1,0)), so t = d + tl + blockX*4^N stays continuous; float precision limits order and distance from origin. Arc cell needs a one-quadrant atan, Sqrt, and a straight/turn Select. 3D uses Skilling's Hilbert index (verified bijective and adjacent for 1..5 bits, ends on the x axis) with 7 decodes for the 6 neighbours; a digit-tracking 3D form should reduce that but was not derived. The catalogue's 3D (t, n1, n2) lateral frame is not continuous (holonomy at bends), so the prototype passes the lateral offset in global axes, S(t + lx, ly, lz), which is continuous. Exactly on the pivot edge r = 0, so take the radial distance from r and not from the offset vector, or lattice-aligned samples jump.
domain-hilbert-ribbon.params_text: order=6,cell=0.4,along=0.3,across=2,fade=6,wall=0.5,core=0.2,src=0 (these are the code defaults; 3D also order3=3,cell3=0.5)

master.one_liner: Parametrise the plane as a ribbon along a Hilbert curve (t along the curve, n across it, quarter-circle arcs in turn cells) and sample the source at (t, n): any noise flows through a labyrinth.
master.look: Labyrinths, circuit-board traces, intestine / brain-coral folds (smooth source + edge fade), serpentine river canyons (as a heightmap: the ribbon is the valley, the fade is the ridge), maze terrain with recursive quadrant structure, 'flow through a maze' textures. Unlike any field on the sheet, the coherence runs along a one-dimensional path.
master.algorithm:
Params: Order N (int, 2^N x 2^N cells, pattern repeats with that period), Cell Size L, Along Scale, Across Scale (hybrid ok), Edge Fade e (0 = off), Corner mode {Arc, Sharp}.

  q = p / L; cell = Floor(q); f = q - cell (in [0,1)^2); ix,iy = int(cell) & (2^N - 1)
  // Hilbert decode, N uniform iterations of the standard xy->d loop (rx = (ix & s) > 0, ry = (iy & s) > 0, d += s*s*((3*rx) ^ ry), rotate quadrant), all with int32v masks and Selects.
  // Alongside d, track the accumulated frame as a signed permutation (3 bits: swap, flipX, flipY). At the last level the quadrant index (0..3) and the frame give the cell's entry and exit sides (one of N/E/S/W each) through a constant 4 x 8 table => 12 possible (entry, exit) pairs.
  // Local coordinates:
  straight (exit opposite entry):  tl = coordinate of f along the travel direction (0..1); n = signed lateral offset of f from the cell's centre line (-0.5..0.5), sign = left of travel
  turn (exit adjacent to entry):   pivot = the cell corner shared by the entry and exit edges; g = f - pivot; r = |g|
       Arc: the curve is the quarter circle of radius 0.5 about pivot; tl = angle fraction 0..1 from the entry edge toward the exit edge = (2/pi)*atan(min/max of |g.x|,|g.y|) with a one-quadrant polynomial atan (and a Select for the ordering); n = (0.5 - r) with sign chosen so left-of-travel is positive
       Sharp: nearest point on the L-shaped polyline (cheaper, but tl jumps on the inner bisector: use only with Edge Fade)
  All 12 cases are computed as a few Selects on (f.x, f.y, 1-f.x, 1-f.y) chosen by the entry/exit bits; no branches.
  t = (float(d) + tl) * AlongScale          // d up to 4^N: keep N <= 11 for float precision, or use double-free trick: t = (d mod M + tl) with a hash-based M period
  val = Source.Gen(seed, t, n * AcrossScale)
  return (e > 0) ? val * Max(0, 1 - Pow(2*Abs(n), e)) : val   // fade to 0 at the ribbon edges so cells that are not curve-adjacent meet continuously

3D: 3D Hilbert curve (same decode scheme with 3 bits per level) and tube coordinates: straight cells (t, n1, n2) from the two lateral axes; turn cells pivot on the cell EDGE shared by the entry and exit faces: t from the angle about that edge, n1 = 0.5 - distance to the edge, n2 = coordinate along the edge. Source sampled in 3D at (t, n1, n2). 4D: fallback (drop w).
master.why_new: A space-filling-curve parametrisation gives a 1D-coherent field that is still a pure pointwise function. It is impossible to build from existing nodes (no node produces a curve-following frame), and it yields a maze/labyrinth family that cellular and gradient noises never produce.
master.simd_plan: N x ~12 int ops (And, Compare, Xor, Select, Add) for the decode (N=8 is ~100 ops), a short polynomial atan, ~20 Selects for the 12 cases, 1 Pow, one source eval: about 2-3x Perlin 2D plus the source. Window: the single cell. All loops are uniform (N is an int member).
master.continuity: C0 along the ribbon (t and n are continuous across curve-crossing edges and inside arc cells). Without Edge Fade the field jumps across cell edges the curve does not cross; with Edge Fade > 0 the output goes to 0 on every ribbon edge from both sides, so it is C0 everywhere. Sharp corners add jumps on the inner bisector.
master.params: Order int, Cell Size float, Along Scale float, Across Scale hybrid, Edge Fade float, Corner enum.
master.risks: Visible 2^N quadrant hierarchy (by design, choose N large); arc cells have curve length pi/4 vs 1 so features stretch ~27% in turns unless t is rescaled (pointwise unknown prefix counts make an exact fix impossible: accept); the outer corner of arc cells (r > 1) is a dead zone that the fade must cover; d precision for N > 11; the 3D variant is a real project.
master.cost_note: N x ~12 int ops (And, Compare, Xor, Select, Add) for the decode (N=8 is ~100 ops), a short polynomial atan, ~20 Selects for the 12 cases, 1 Pow, one source eval: about 2-3x Perlin 2D plus the source.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 2D: 6.32; 3D: 11.02; note: measured with the built-in 4 octave fbm source. 2D 315.6 ns vs perlin2 49.9; 3D 582.3 ns vs perlin2 52.8. Roughly 215 ns of the 2D figure is the source
measured.est_avx2_ns: value: about 7 ns in 2D with a 4 octave fbm source, about 2.5 ns without the source; estimate: True

domain-hyperbolic-tiling.look: A round mandala: rosettes of radial spokes in the middle, the same rosette repeating and shrinking in a true {7,3} arrangement towards a fine grey rim. The threshold panel is a clean heptagonal lace. The checker source showed black heptagons on white, and P=4 showed a real hyperbolic chessboard with 5 squares at each vertex, so the geometry is exact, not a resemblance. Cellular F1 gave pebbled discs, F2-F1 gave stained glass. Outside the disk the inverted copies grow into large soft blurs. The 3D slice shows blocky cube-symmetric ornament, and the volume is a spiky ball whose interior breaks into fractal dust; distinctive but cluttered.

dims.note: 3D is a real {4,3,5} Poincare ball. 4D folds xy and passes z,w; measured continuous in an x,w plane. 4D does not give GenTileable2D tiling, because the torus coordinates enter the fold

range.note: 8 seeds/offsets; fbm source with rim fade, so low contrast. Far coordinates collapse to one constant (0.001, std 0) because the exterior inverts onto the disk centre

domain-hyperbolic-tiling.artifacts: Without the rim fade the rim is white noise from aliasing. It is one centred object, not stationary noise, unless lat > 0 repeats the disk, which gives a lattice of rosettes joined by a grey band (seen with radius=2, lat=4, rimfade=0.6). Every tile holds the same content, and the seed only changes that content. The fundamental triangle is small, so the source scale must be set to match (6 for {7,3}, in disk units).
domain-hyperbolic-tiling.node_shape: DomainHyperbolicTiling: Source (required), P int, Q int (clamped to hyperbolic), Iterations int, Disk Radius float, Source Scale float, Rim Fade float, Lattice Period float (0 = single disk), Rotation float, Seed Offset.
domain-hyperbolic-tiling.port_notes: Replaces the catalogue loop with one full sector fold per iteration: floor(P/2) line mirrors at descending angles, then Abs. Measured against a 64 iteration reference on a 256 px grid, radius 4.2 in an 8 unit window: N=6 has 0 pixels differing inside r<0.95 for {7,3},{4,5},{5,4},{8,3}, and N=8 differs on 0.03-0.71 percent overall, all in the rim. Cost is about N*(P/2 + 1) reflections of about 6 ops, uniform across lanes. Line normals, c and rho2 are per-node constants set when P or Q change. 3D: Abs, 3 conditional swaps, one sphere inversion with rho^2 = 1/cos(dihedral), c^2 = 1 + rho^2, 72 degrees for {4,3,5}; derived here and the slice is cube-symmetric as expected, but only the visual and the continuity measure support it. 3D convergence is slower: N=8 differs on 3.9 percent and N=12 on 0.24 percent of a slice, and N=8 is used.
domain-hyperbolic-tiling.params_text: P=7,Q=3,iter=8,radius=4.2,scale=6,rimfade=0.5,src=0,lat=0 (code defaults; 3D iter3=8,scale3=3. Stationary ornament: radius=2,lat=4,rimfade=0.6. Hyperbolic chessboard: P=4,src=4)

master.one_liner: Poincare-disk {P,Q} kaleidoscope: fold any point into the fundamental Schwarz triangle with N conditional reflections and circle inversions, then sample the source there; Escher Circle Limit with noise content.
master.look:
Infinitely many shrinking copies of the source toward the disk edge, arranged on a {7,3} heptagonal, {4,5}, {3,7}, {5,4}... hyperbolic tiling. Cellular source: hyperbolic stained glass / Circle Limit fish; Perlin: symmetric clouds that densify to the rim; Checkerboard: the classic hyperbolic chessboard. Masks for portals, ornaments, iris textures, 'infinite' floors.
[HyperbolicFold, domain-geometry] Circle Limit tilings: rosettes shrinking to fractal dust at the disc rim, {7,3} star-chains, {5,4} petals with strata. Highly distinct from anything on the sheet. Use for portals, mandalas, sigils, magic circles, alien artifacts, or the half-plane variant for edge-of-world bands. Prototyped: mode=7 with {7,3} and {5,4}.
master.algorithm:
Params: P, Q ints (1/P + 1/Q < 1/2, clamp to nearest valid), Iterations N (int, default 12), Disk Radius Rd, Source Scale, Outside enum {Invert, Clamp}, Rim Fade f.
Precompute when P/Q change (derived from the (P,Q,2) Schwarz triangle: a geodesic circle of centre c on the x axis, orthogonal to the unit circle, meeting the line at angle pi/P under angle pi/Q):
  c = cos(pi/Q) / sqrt(cos^2(pi/Q) - sin^2(pi/P)); rho2 = c*c - 1; nP = (-sin(pi/P), cos(pi/P))

  z = p / Rd
  r2 = Dot(z,z)
  if Outside == Invert: z = Select(r2 > 1, z / r2, z)          // reflect the exterior into the disk: continuous at the rim
  for i in 0..N-1:                                             // uniform count
     z.y = Abs(z.y)                                            // mirror in the x axis
     d = Dot(z, nP); z -= 2*Max(d, 0)*nP                       // mirror in the line at angle pi/P if beyond it (iterating converges to the sector)
     dx = z.x - c; d2 = dx*dx + z.y*z.y
     k = Select(d2 < rho2, rho2 / d2, 1)                       // inside the geodesic => invert across it
     z = (c + dx*k, z.y*k)
  v = Source.Gen(seed, z * SourceScale)
  return (f > 0) ? v * Pow(Max(1 - r2, 0), f) : v              // optional fade of the sub-pixel rim

All three mirror operations are hyperbolic isometries, so the N copies of the source are isometric in the hyperbolic metric and shrink Euclideanly toward the rim. Points very near the rim need more than N steps; they remain continuous (every step is continuous), just not fully folded, and are sub-pixel at any sane zoom.
3D: Poincare ball with a Coxeter tetrahedron (e.g. {4,3,5} or {5,3,4}): the Oh or Ih sector fold from DomainKaleidoscope plus one sphere orthogonal to the unit sphere (centre distance solved numerically from the dihedral-angle condition when params change); same loop with a sphere inversion. 4D: fold on xy, pass z,w (hyperbolic cylinder). General (P,Q,R) triangles are a second circle; straightforward extension.
master.why_new: Non-Euclidean geometry cannot be composed from affine domain nodes; this gives true hyperbolic symmetry with one source evaluation and a fixed op count. Unlike the half-plane (x/y, log y) idea (sheared, not isometric; a dead end) the fold is exact.
master.simd_plan: N x ~14 ops (Abs, Dot, Max, FMA, Select, Reciprocal) = ~170 ops at N=12 => roughly 2-3x Perlin 2D plus the source; 3D ~N x 20 ops. No lattice window, no per-lane early out needed since all lanes run N steps.
master.continuity: C0: mirror and inversion folds are continuous and fix their mirror sets; creases along mirror lines and geodesic circles (the look). Fade keeps the rim continuous.
master.params: P int, Q int, Iterations int, Disk Radius float, Source Scale float, Outside enum, Rim Fade float, Rotation float.
master.risks:
Rim aliasing is inherent (infinite frequency); fade or clamp zoom. Invalid P/Q combos must be clamped. Fixed N cost even for the easy interior. 3D centre-distance derivation needs care; prototype in 2D first.
[HyperbolicFold, domain-geometry] Rim aliases to noise: fade it using an extra output or accept. Disc is a singular hero object. Source appears only within one small triangle, so scale must fit. Every tile is identical (cannot reseed per tile without seams). Need to verify interior continuity separately from the rim in a real check.
master.cost_note: N x ~14 ops (Abs, Dot, Max, FMA, Select, Reciprocal) = ~170 ops at N=12 => roughly 2-3x Perlin 2D plus the source; 3D ~N x 20 ops.
master.variant_notes: Prototype c0ratio 1.14 is rim aliasing rather than a confirmed interior jump, not separately verified. Half-plane variant gives an edge-of-world band.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 2D: 5.66; 3D: 7.62; 4D: 3.8; note: 2D 290.4 ns and 3D 394.2 ns use a 4 octave fbm source, about 215 ns of the 2D figure. 4D 203.2 ns uses one perlin4 octave and no rim fade
measured.est_avx2_ns: value: about 2 ns for the 8 iteration fold, plus the source (about 6.5 ns with a 4 octave fbm); estimate: True

c0ratio.note: Low default figures come from fbm detail compressed at the rim. Single octave perlin with rimfade=1 measures 7.99, so the fold itself has no jumps

domain-kaleidoscope.look: Crisp wallpaper. With F2-F1 cells, p6m is hexagonal stained glass with six-pointed stars at the lattice points, p3m1 is a three-fold glass pattern, p4m a square damask with crosses, and the D8 sector one large rose window. With fbm the same groups read as woven damask or snowflake lace, and with one octave perlin as soft fabric medallions. No seams were visible in any group. In 3D the cubic fold with cell 4 is a lattice of symmetric rooms with holes through the walls, like a crystal or a cut block of architecture. Ih on a radial falloff is a bumpy capsid; the symmetry is exact but hard to read in one view of a rough surface.

dims.note: All measured continuous. 4D is lattice + Abs + 5 comparator sort, 384 copies per cell. GenTileable2D tiling is not preserved unless the fold period is compatible, not tested

range.note: 8 seeds/offsets with the default crackle source; it passes the source range through

domain-kaleidoscope.artifacts: None seen in continuity. Creases along mirrors are always there and are the look; soft sources show star points where mirrors meet. Strong repetition is by design: the wide view repeats exactly. A small cell against a low-frequency source gives a nearly constant fold: cell3=2 at scale 1.5 was almost entirely solid with thin crosses, so Cell Size and source scale need matching.
domain-kaleidoscope.node_shape: DomainKaleidoscope: Source (required), Group enum (Strip, Rect, Square, Tri, Hex, D4, D6, D8; 3D Box, Cubic, Td, Oh, Ih, HexPrism), Cell Size float, Centre per-dimension float, Rotation float.
domain-kaleidoscope.port_notes: Numeric invariance test: |fold(p) - fold(g p)| for random words of generators, 200000 points, worst 3e-5 for pm, pmm, p4m, p3m1, p6m, D4, D6, D8, Box, Cubic, Td, Oh, Ih. Corrections to the catalogue: Td is not Abs + one swap, because Td has no axis mirrors; it is 3 diagonal mirrors repeated twice. p3m1 needs mirrors perpendicular to the lattice vectors (mirrors at 90, 30, 150 degrees for a lattice at 0, 60, 120), and p6m needs the same, which makes opposite hexagon edges fold together. Hex lattice reduction is cube rounding with 2 Selects. Ih: 4 rounds of Abs + mirror with normal (-1/2, -phi/2, 1/(2 phi)). Swap = Select pair. Loop counts are constant per group, so the loop is uniform. One source call in every group. Cell Size should not be hybrid.
domain-kaleidoscope.params_text: group=4,src=5,cell=4 (code defaults: p6m with F2-F1 source; 3D group3=1,cell3=4,src3=1,scale3=1.5). Icosahedral shell: group3=4,src3=1,scale3=1.5,shell=1.2,shellr=3.2 with vol --window 8

queue.name: DomainKaleidoscope
queue.reason: Table-driven Coxeter folds in 6-20 ops at any dimension, with one source eval. Needs per-group continuity tests; base for chiral-wallpaper.

master.one_liner: Table-driven Coxeter fold: wallpaper kaleidoscopes (pm, pmm, p4m, p3m1, p6m) in 2D, polyhedral (Td, Oh, Ih) and cubic honeycomb folds in 3D, hyperoctahedral in 4D, one source eval.
master.look: Ornamental wallpaper made from any noise: damask (p4m + Perlin), honeycomb crystal (p6m + Cellular), stained glass (p3m1 + CellularValue), snowflake fields. In 3D: planets/shells/gems with exact octahedral or icosahedral symmetry (virus capsids, radiolaria, geodesic domes, cut gemstones with Cellular). The derivative flips at the mirrors, which gives a crisp, faceted 'kaleidoscope' character that no stationary noise on the sheet has.
master.algorithm:
Group enum. 2D: Strip(pm), Rect(pmm), Square(p4m), Tri(p3m1), HexTri(p6m), finite sectors D2/D4/D8. 3D: Box(abs only), Cubic(Pm-3m, 48 copies per cell), Tetra(Td), Octa(Oh), Icosa(Ih). 4D: HyperBox, HyperCubic. Params: CellSize L, Centre (per dim), Rotation.

Step A (affine groups only), reduce by the translation lattice to the Wigner-Seitz cell:
  square/rect/cubic: q = p - Round(p/L)*L                      // q in [-L/2, L/2)^n
  hex (Tri, HexTri): axial coords (a,b) = (2x/3, -x/3 + y/sqrt3)/L; cube-round (ra,rb,rc) with the usual 'fix the largest error' done as 2 Selects; q = p - centre(ra,rb)
Step B, point-group fold = fixed sequence of conditional reflections from a per-group constant table of unit normals n_i (count <= 6, same for all lanes):
  for n_i in table: d = Dot(q, n_i); q -= 2*Min(d, 0)*n_i           // reflect only if on the negative side; axis normals reduce to q.x = Abs(q.x)
  Rect: {x, y}. Square: {x, y, (1,-1)/sqrt2} (abs + one conditional swap). HexTri (D6, sector [0,30deg]):
     q.x=|q.x|; n=(-1/2, sqrt3/2): q -= 2*Min(q.n,0)*n; q.x=|q.x|; n=(-sqrt3/2, 1/2): q -= 2*Min(q.n,0)*n   (exact in 4 steps)
  Tri (D3): q.y=|q.y|; n=(-sqrt3/2,1/2) twice interleaved with abs (3-4 steps).
  Oh: q = Abs(q); sort components descending with 3 conditional swaps (x=y, y=z, x=y planes). Td: Abs + one swap. Ih: Abs; reflect in n1=(phi,1,0)/|.|; Abs; reflect in n2=(1,0,phi)/|.| and n3=(0,phi,1)/|.|; Abs (Knighty-style icosahedral fold, 6-8 steps).
  4D: Abs + 5-compare sorting network (hyperoctahedral B4).
Step C: return Source.Gen(seed, q + Centre).
The finite groups (Td/Oh/Ih/D_k) act on the direction and preserve |p|, so a sphere shell (via DomainWrap) gets exact polyhedral symmetry.
master.why_new: Symmetry is unreachable with the existing affine domain nodes. A fold costs a handful of Abs/FMA/Min ops and one source evaluation, and because it is driven by a per-group table one Gen body covers 2D/3D/4D. Honest limitation: only the reflection-generated groups fold continuously for an arbitrary source (pm, pmm, p4m, p3m1, p6m in 2D; the other 12 wallpaper groups need a symmetric source, see DomainSymmetrize + DomainWrap recipe).
master.simd_plan: 6-20 ops (Round, Abs, FMA, Min, Select), no lattice window, same structure in every dimension; ~0.2-0.5x Perlin + source. Tables are constexpr per group; the fold count is a compile-time or per-node constant so the loop is uniform.
master.continuity: C0: every conditional reflection is continuous and fixes the mirror, so q is continuous; the gradient reverses across mirrors (creases), which is the intended look.
master.params: Group enum, Cell Size float (not hybrid: the lattice must be coherent), Centre per-dimension float (which patch of the source becomes the motif), Rotation float (pre-rotates the lattice).
master.risks:
Lattice reduction and fold table must match exactly (hex orientation, p31m vs p3m1) or seams appear; prototype each group with the continuity check. Mirror creases can look mechanical; pair with DomainSymmetrize for soft symmetry.
[DomainKaleidoscope, math-physics] Dihedral, hyperbolic and Kleinian are not translation invariant (centred), so they are decals, not noise, and not tileable; hyperbolic needs float care near the rim (fold count insufficient -> unfolded garbage at |p|>0.995); the p6m lattice reduction must be exact or seams appear.
master.cost_note: 6-20 ops (Round, Abs, FMA, Min, Select), no lattice window, same structure in every dimension; ~0.2-0.5x Perlin + source.
master.variant_notes: Reflection groups only fold continuously for any source; ChiralWallpaper covers the remaining groups.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 2D_p6m_crackle: 3.07; 2D_p6m_fbm4: 4.96; 3D_cubic_perlin: 4.11; 4D_perlin: 2.03; note: 159.4 ns against worley2 at 117.1, so the p6m fold is about 40 ns scalar including param reads, under 1x perlin2. Most of the cost is the source
measured.est_avx2_ns: value: about 0.3 ns for the fold, plus the source; estimate: True

domain-mobius.look: Default: two large spiral vortices side by side, like a pair of galaxies or an owl's eyes, with long streaks of cloud drawn into each and dense curled detail at the centres; strongly mirror-like across the vertical midline. Inversion: fbm implodes into a tight knot, and a checker source becomes the classic flower of circles. With F2-F1 cells and eps=0.2 it is a curved rosette of petal cells, the best use of that map. Power k=3: three-fold sectors with frequency exploding outward into static. Exp: rings repeating vertically with detail on one side. RadialPower gamma=0.5: visibly radial streaks. In 3D, inversion at R=2 and scale 1 in an 8 unit box is mostly one large smooth lobe with some small detail near the centre: real, but dull at this setting.

dims.note: Inversion and RadialPower act on all axes in 3D and 4D, measured continuous with eps=0.2. Other maps act on xy and pass z,w. No tiling

range.note: 8 seeds/offsets, fbm source. Far coordinates give one constant (-0.537, std 0) because g tends to 1, so this is a centred object and not stationary noise

domain-mobius.artifacts: Foci and poles have unbounded frequency: the eps softening solves this for inversion, while bipolar keeps white-noise-like knots at its foci. Power aliases outward at k=3 well inside the 8 unit window, and Exp past its clamp. Eps softening breaks conformality near the pole (raw Mobius at eps=0.2: median anisotropy 1.06, p99 4.6). Mirror look of bipolar is built in: the map treats the two foci symmetrically.
domain-mobius.node_shape: DomainMobius: Source (required), Map enum (Inversion, Mobius, Bipolar, Power, Exp, RadialPower), Centre per-dimension float, Radius float, Softening float (eps), k int, Gamma float, Focus Distance a, Period, Twist, Stretch.
domain-mobius.port_notes: Two catalogue corrections. First, one application of a loxodromic Mobius map is only another one-pole map, so it cannot give paired vortices. The Bipolar map does it instead: g = (z-a)/(z+a), triangle fold of log|g|, rotate by twist*fold, then invert g. Fold keeps it continuous. Second, RadialPower is not conformal: measured Jacobian anisotropy is 2.0 at gamma=0.5, which matches the radial streaks in the image. Measured anisotropy: inversion 1.00, Power 1.00, Exp 1.00, Bipolar 1.00 at twist=0, stretch=1, and 10.4 at the default twist=2, stretch=2, so the default look is a shear and not conformal. Stretch began as a slope bug in the triangle wave: the slope was 2 where 1 is conformal, and it looked better, so it became a param. Bipolar needs Log, Exp, Sin and Cos. Inversion needs one Reciprocal. RadialPower needs Pow. All branch free. Exp input clamp is needed.
domain-mobius.params_text: map=2,a=2.2,period=3,twist=2,stretch=2,src=0 (code defaults, bipolar vortices; 3D map3=0,R=2,eps=0.2,src3=1). Curved cells: map=0,src=5,eps=0.2

master.one_liner: Conformal remaps (sphere inversion, complex Mobius, z^k, exp, radial power/fisheye): curvature and scale gradients that keep isotropic noise locally isotropic.
master.look: Inversion of Checkerboard or Cellular yields circle packings and curved tilings (Apollonian look); noise that implodes toward a pole. Loxodromic Mobius: paired vortices / Droste double spirals. Power k: exact k-fold rotational symmetry with features shrinking outward (sunflower, vortex). Exp: rings and log spirals from any horizontally periodic source. RadialPower: lens bulge. All stay locally isotropic (no shear), unlike DomainWarp.
master.algorithm:
Map enum: Inversion (n-D), Mobius (2D complex), Power (2D, int k), Exp (2D), RadialPower (n-D, fisheye). Centre C, Radius R.

  Inversion:   d = p - C; r2 = Dot(d,d) + eps; return Source.Gen(seed, C + d * (R*R / r2))          // works in 2D/3D/4D (inversions are conformal in all dims)
  Mobius:      z = x + i y; num = a*z + b; den = c*z + d (complex FMAs); w = num * conj(den) * Reciprocal(|den|^2 + eps)
               Presets enum: Identity, Loxodromic (fixed points +-1, multiplier m*e^{i theta}: conjugate z -> m e^{i theta} z by g(z) = (z-1)/(z+1)), Elliptic (|m|=1), Hyperbolic (theta=0)
  Power:       w = z^k by k-1 complex multiplies (k int member); k<0 via inversion first
  Exp:         w = (Exp(Min(x, xmax)) * Cos(y), Exp(..) * Sin(y))   // inverse of DomainPolar Log mode: a y-periodic source (period 2 pi s) becomes rings; rotate input by alpha first for log spirals
  RadialPower: d = p - C; r = |d|; w = C + d * Pow(r/R + eps, gamma - 1)                            // gamma<1 barrel/fisheye, gamma>1 pincushion
  3D/4D: Inversion and RadialPower are dimension agnostic; Mobius/Power/Exp act on xy and pass z,w.
master.why_new: 5-20 ops for a family of smooth maps whose Jacobian is a similarity everywhere: curvature and feature-size gradients without the smearing of warps. Inverting lattice-based sources is a very large visual jump for the cost. Complements DomainPolar (Exp is its inverse) and DomainPerspective (projective vs conformal).
master.simd_plan: Branch-free: a few FMAs, one Reciprocal (or Pow / Exp+Sin+Cos for RadialPower / Exp), one source eval at the same dimension; ~0.1-0.3x Perlin + source. GenT for Inversion/RadialPower; 2D-specific for the complex maps.
master.continuity: C-infinity away from poles (inversion centre, Mobius pole -d/c, Power origin for k<0); poles are point singularities with infinitely fine detail.
master.params: Map enum, Centre per-dim float, Radius float, k int, Gamma float, Preset enum plus a,b,c,d complex (8 floats) for raw Mobius, Rotation float.
master.risks: Raw Mobius coefficients are unfriendly (presets mitigate); detail near poles aliases; Exp overflows for large x (clamp). Several modes overlap with DomainPolar; keep the node small if DomainPolar ships.
master.cost_note: Branch-free: a few FMAs, one Reciprocal (or Pow / Exp+Sin+Cos for RadialPower / Exp), one source eval at the same dimension; ~0.1-0.3x Perlin + source.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 2D_bipolar: 4.39; 2D_inversion: 4.25; 3D_inversion: 3.1; 4D_inversion: 1.97; note: 2D figures use a 4 octave fbm source (about 215 ns of 242.5 and 213.5 ns); 3D uses one perlin3g, 4D one perlin4. The inversion itself costs under 1x perlin2 scalar
measured.est_avx2_ns: value: inversion about 0.2 ns, bipolar about 3 ns because of Log, Exp, Sin and Cos, plus the source; estimate: True

c0ratio.note: The default's 0.96 is unbounded frequency at the two foci, not a measured jump: with the foci outside the probe window it reads 7.94. Map 5 reads 2.84 from its point singularity at the centre. Raw inversion at eps=0.002 read 1.22 from aliasing at the pole, and eps=0.2 removes it

domain-perspective.look: A cobbled floor seen from a low camera: large cells at the bottom, shrinking evenly to a horizon about a quarter of the way down from the top, and a mirrored copy forming a ceiling. Correct straight-line perspective, and it reads at once as a place, like an endless hall of tiles. Checker gives the Tron floor, fbm a misty cloud sea. Threshold panel is clean. The 3D homography is noise whose feature size grows smoothly from fine to coarse across the box, a depth gradient, as both the XZ slice and the isosurface show. Before the depth cap the isosurface broke into white noise at the vanishing plane.

dims.note: 3D has two real forms: homography on all axes, and ground plane with z passed for animation. 4D is ground plane with z,w passed. All measured continuous

range.note: 8 seeds/offsets with the crackle source. Far coordinates are constant (0.264, std 0) since rays converge, so it is a framed picture and not stationary noise

domain-perspective.artifacts: The cap band at the horizon shows vertical streaks, like a distant picket fence, because only x still changes quickly within the band. Rolling ground (roll) ripples more like a warp than hills, with contour-like rings near the horizon, and it is rough: c0 1.89. This is a framed 2D picture, so it does nothing for terrain or a stationary field and is mainly 2D art, skyboxes and backgrounds. Narrow use, but cheap and impossible with affine domain nodes.
domain-perspective.node_shape: DomainPerspective: Source (required), Mode enum (GroundPlane, Homography), Height hybrid, Pitch float, Focal float, Sky enum (Mirror, Clamp), Far Fade float, Depth Cap float, Homography a,b,c floats.
domain-perspective.port_notes: About 15 ops, one Reciprocal, one Max, one Abs. Pitch sin and cos are per-node constants. Added beyond the catalogue: a depth cap, W = Max(W, wmin). The catalogue's Far Fade alone only scales amplitude, so sign changes stay aliased: an isosurface still showed white noise at the vanishing plane, and the cap removes it. The Matrix mode is reduced to 3 denominator coefficients; a 16-float UI seems unnecessary for what it showed.

master.one_liner: Projective remap (homography): screen coordinates become ground-plane coordinates with a horizon; 'mode-7' depth for any source in one node.
master.look: Any source turned into a receding textured plane: Tron grids (Checkerboard), lava seas, deserts, perspective cobblestones (Cellular), with a mirrored 'reflection' sky. Raw matrix mode gives vanishing-point distortion for parallax layers and fake depth. Every entry on the sheet is stationary; this has a horizon.
master.algorithm:
Mode {GroundPlane, Matrix}. GroundPlane params: Height h (hybrid ok), Pitch, Focal f, Sky enum {Mirror, Clamp}, Far Fade F. Matrix mode: 9 floats (2D) / 16 (3D).

GroundPlane 2D (screen x right, y up; precompute cp=cos(Pitch), sp=sin(Pitch)):
  // view ray for screen point: d = (x, y*cp - f*sp, y*sp + f*cp)  (rotation of (x,y,f) about x by Pitch)
  dy = y*cp - f*sp; dz = y*sp + f*cp
  W  = Select(Sky==Mirror, Abs(dy), Max(-dy, eps))     // ground is where the ray goes down (dy<0); Mirror reflects the sky onto the ground
  t  = h / (W + eps)
  u  = t*x; v = t*dz                                   // ground hit point
  val = Source.Gen(seed, u, v)
  return (F>0) ? val / (1 + (t/F)^2) : val             // fade distant (aliasing) samples toward 0
Matrix 2D: (X,Y,Wn) = H*(x,y,1); return Source.Gen(seed, X/Wn, Y/Wn) with the same |Wn|+eps guard.
3D input: GroundPlane maps (x,y) to (u,v) and passes z as a third coordinate (animation / layering) -> Source(u,v,z); Matrix mode uses a 4x4 homography on (x,y,z,1) -> 3D source (perspective box). 4D: (u,v,z,w).
master.why_new: DomainScale/Rotate/AxisScale are affine; projective maps are the missing classical family (straight lines preserved, scale varies with depth). Replaces per-app shader code for 2D background art and makes depth gradients of feature size available to any graph for ~15 ops.
master.simd_plan: ~15 ops + 1 Reciprocal + source at the same dimension; ~0.2x Perlin + source. Fully branch-free; the sky handling is one Select.
master.continuity: C-infinity except on the horizon line W=0 (singular: feature size -> 0); with Mirror sky and Far Fade > 0 both sides converge to 0 so the node is continuous across the horizon.
master.params: Mode enum, Height hybrid (rolling ground), Pitch float, Focal float, Sky enum, Far Fade float, Matrix floats.
master.risks: Horizon aliasing is unavoidable without fading or a max depth; mostly a 2D/2.5D art node, less useful for terrain; a 16-float matrix UI is clunky (keep GroundPlane as the default).
master.cost_note: ~15 ops + 1 Reciprocal + source at the same dimension; ~0.2x Perlin + source.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 2D_crackle: 3.19; 2D_fbm4: 5.66; 3D_homography_perlin: 3.71; 4D_perlin: 2.85; note: 161.3 ns vs worley2 110.9, so the map is about 50 ns scalar including about 8 param lookups and per-sample sin and cos of pitch; a node precomputes those
measured.est_avx2_ns: value: about 0.2 ns for the map, plus the source; estimate: True

c0ratio.note: Below 8 in 2D because frequency is high near the horizon; no jump was found at the depth cap. roll=0.6 drops to 1.89

domain-symmetrize.look: Default: a repeating field of six-armed pinwheels with fine bright creases, like interlocking chiral crystals, with no mirror lines and a clear swirl handedness. Average combine at the same setting is a soft smoky three-lobed blob pattern. Centred rosette with Max, k=6: crumpled paper or coral snowflake whose symmetry reads only within about one window radius of the centre; beyond that the wide view is ordinary isotropic noise. Average, k=8: a soft ring with a flat grey disc at the hub, blurry and low in detail. RMS: mottled, with a dark spot at the centre. The 3D tetrahedral Max form looked like plain fine noise in the isosurface, so no volume is kept.

dims.note: All measured continuous. Wallpaper mode is 2D only: a lattice periodic 3D form would need a 6D torus source. 3D uses 12 tetrahedral rotations or Ck about z. 4D is Ck in xy

range.note: 8 seeds/offsets, wall=6 Max. Max is biased upward; a port needs a k dependent offset. Average with Contrast Preserve: -1.079 to 1.067, mean 0.000

domain-symmetrize.artifacts: Flat grey hub in Average mode, inherent because the k samples differ only slightly near the centre, and the gain fade does not hide it. Max and Min have ridges where images cross, which is not creaseless despite the catalogue's description; only Average and RMS are smooth. Max output is biased positive. High cost is the unsolved flaw: 22x perlin2 scalar for a wallpaper.
domain-symmetrize.node_shape: DomainSymmetrize: Source (required), k int (2..8), Dihedral bool, Combine enum (Average, Max, Min, RMS), Contrast Preserve bool, Centre per-dimension float. A wallpaper mode needs a torus-wrapped source, as a separate DomainWrap node or a built-in mode: Lattice enum (Off, p4, p3, p6), Cell Size.
domain-symmetrize.port_notes: Symmetry measured: p4, p3, p6 rotation and two lattice translations hold within 1e-5, and a non-member mirror differs by 0.45-0.54, so these are truly the rotation-only groups. k is a uniform loop; the cos/sin table is per node. Centred rosettes can be built today from DomainRotate and Add or Max per k, which is clumsy but possible, so the node's distinct value is mainly the wallpaper mode with a torus source. That mode overlaps chiral-wallpaper, which reaches rotation-only groups differently (warp + fold, one source eval, per its source header), so that route should be much cheaper; I did not compare the images. Tetrahedral 3D is a constant quaternion table of 12 entries, expensive and not visually worth it at the settings tried.
domain-symmetrize.params_text: wall=6,comb=1,oct=3,cell=4,torus=0.7 (code defaults: p6 wallpaper, Max combine). Centred rosette: wall=0,k=6,comb=1. Soft mandala: wall=0,k=8,comb=0. 3D default rot3=1,oct3=2,comb=1

master.one_liner: Average (or max/min/RMS) the source over the k rotations / 2k dihedral images of the position: exact k-fold symmetry with no mirror creases, and the missing rotational wallpaper groups via a torus-embedded source.
master.look: Soft mandalas, snowflakes and rosettes with smooth (creaseless) symmetry, symmetric clouds, flower-like masks; Max combine yields a 'k-fold symmetric cellular' look (sharp ridges where images cross); with Perspective or Polar upstream it produces symmetric ornaments that still read as noise rather than folded tiles.
master.algorithm:
Params: Group {Cyclic Ck, Dihedral Dk (2D); Ck about Z, Tetrahedral rotations (12) (3D)}, k int (2..8), Combine {Average, Max, Min, RMS}, Contrast Preserve bool, Centre.
Precompute cos/sin of 2pi*i/k, i=0..k-1 when k changes.

  d = p - Centre
  acc = 0 (or -inf / +inf for Max/Min); acc2 = 0
  for i in 0..k-1 (uniform):                                     // Dk: also the mirrored point (dx, -dy) rotated => 2k evals
     r = (d.x*c_i - d.y*s_i, d.x*s_i + d.y*c_i)
     v = Source.Gen(seed, Centre + r [, z])
     acc = combine(acc, v)
  Average: out = acc / k; if ContrastPreserve: out *= Sqrt(k) (sum of k far-apart samples has variance k * var, so the mean scaled by sqrt(k) keeps the source variance where the samples are independent)
  RMS: Sqrt(acc2 / k); Max/Min: acc.
3D: Ck about the z axis (rotate xy), or the 12 rotations of the tetrahedral group as a constant quaternion table (12 evals, heavy; expose as an opt-in). 4D: Ck in the xy plane, zw passed.
Wallpaper recipe: Symmetrize(C4 about the cell centre) -> DomainWrap(Torus, square cell) -> source gives the p4 wallpaper group continuously; C3/C6 with a hex-compatible torus period gives p3/p6; combine with DomainKaleidoscope for the remaining groups that contain glides only approximately.
master.why_new: Folding (DomainKaleidoscope) gives symmetry with creases and cannot realise the rotation-only groups; averaging gives C-infinity symmetry for any source and unlocks p3/p4/p6 wallpaper via the torus embedding. Not expressible as a small graph (a Rotate+Add tree per k is possible but clumsy, and the variance normalisation and dihedral option make a dedicated node worthwhile).
master.simd_plan: k source evals + ~4 ops each; no lattice; cost = k x source (cap k at 8, 2k for Dk). The cos/sin table is per-node, no transcendental at Gen time.
master.continuity: As smooth as the source (sum of smooth functions), including through the centre.
master.params: Group enum, k int, Combine enum, Contrast Preserve bool, Centre per-dim float.
master.risks: k x cost. Near the centre the k samples coincide, so Contrast Preserve over-amplifies the centre (bright/dark dot) -- fade the sqrt(k) factor toward 1 inside a radius of about one feature. Tetrahedral 12 evals is expensive; probably 2D-first.
master.cost_note: k source evals + ~4 ops each; no lattice; cost = k x source (cap k at 8, 2k for Dk).

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 2D_wall_p6: 22.1; 2D_rosette_k6: 21.31; 3D_tetra: 53.96; 4D_k6: 7.36; note: Cost is k x source. Wall p6 is 6 x 3 octaves of perlin4, 1116.4 ns. Rosette is 6 x 3 octaves of perlin2, 1072.3 ns. 3D is 12 x 2 octaves of perlin3g, 2718.6 ns. 4D is 6 x 1 octave of perlin4, 373.0 ns
measured.est_avx2_ns: value: about 77 ns for wall p6 with 3 octave fbm (18 x 4.3 ns perlin 4D), about 20 ns for a k=6 rosette with 3 octave fbm in 2D; estimate: True

domain-tile.look: Warped marble with long flowing bands, repeating exactly with period 4, with no visible seam line; the wide view is a clean repeating carpet. The source keeps its character through most of the tile. The band shows as a slightly busier area, and where the two bands cross at the tile corner there is a small knot of doubled detail. A plain fbm shows almost nothing. Warped crackle and cellular F1 at blend=0.5 clearly show double images (ghost walls and doubled blobs) and at blend=0.2 show them much less. The 3D volume is a Swiss-cheese cave set that repeats across the box, with no seam planes visible on the cut faces.

dims.note: All measured continuous and periodic. Largest |f(p) - f(p + P e_i)|: 2D 2e-5, 3D 0.00000, 4D 0.00000 at the sampled points. Period 0 disables an axis

range.note: 8 seeds/offsets, default source. Flatten widens the range on bimodal sources: warped crackle reaches -1.574..1.479 with flatten and stays -1..1 without. Far coords (4e4): -0.868..0.790, std 0.288, the same character as near the origin since positions stay bounded

domain-tile.artifacts: Ghosting in the blend band is the inherent cost, strongest on sharp features such as cell walls and warp folds; a small blend fraction narrows it at the price of a quicker crossfade. Flatten pushes bimodal sources out of range by up to about 1.5x. Without flatten the variance drops in the band: std falls from 0.28 to 0.207 for fbm between 6/8 and 7/8 of the period (variance and periodicity figures measured at blend 0.35, before the default moved to 0.25), while flatten holds 0.280-0.282 across the tile, and for cellular F1 0.38 against 0.286.
domain-tile.node_shape: DomainTile: Source (required), Period X/Y/Z/W float (0 = off), Blend Fraction float, Mean float, Flatten bool.
domain-tile.port_notes: Floor, one smoothstep per axis, weights as products, one Sqrt and Reciprocal for flatten, 2^n source calls with uniform count. Period and blend should not be hybrid. A batch-level skip when no lane is in the band is legal only for coherent grids, not for position arrays, so plan on the worst case. Unlike GenTileable2D this tiles a subtree only and any source, in 3D and 4D as well. Formula from the catalogue confirmed by measurement: seam closes, continuity is 7.85-8.0, and the source needs no lattice period. An alternative for lattice sources is periodic hashing (periodic-fbm), which has no ghosting and costs 1x source, so this node is the general fallback.
domain-tile.params_text: px=4,py=4,blend=0.25,flatten=1,mean=0,src=6,oct=4 (code defaults: warped fbm source, which has no lattice period; 3D pz=4,src3=1,oct3=3)

queue.name: DomainTile
queue.reason: Wrap and crossfade for any graph including 3D. Check ghosting in the band and the 16x worst case in 4D.

master.one_liner: Makes any subgraph tile at any period in any dimension by wrapping and crossfading, including warps, fractals and 3D volumes.
master.look: Same character as the input with a slightly blended band near the tile edge. Gives tiled warped marble, tiled FBm clouds, tiled 3D volumes for any graph.
master.algorithm: Per axis with period P and blend fraction B: u = x - P*floor(x/P) in [0,P). x0 = u; x1 = u - P. w = smoothstep(P*(1-B), P, u). For each of 2^n combinations (n tiled axes) evaluate Source at the combination; weight = product of (1-w) or w. out = sum(weight*S) / sqrt(sum(weight^2)), with variance flatten relative to a Mean member (0 for noise). At u=P: w=1, value S(P-P) = S(0) which equals u=0's value, so the seam closes. Positions are bounded to about [-P,P).
master.why_new: #12 needs 3D tile which the library says would need 6D. PR #72 ('Repeat version of Tileable2D accepting custom repeat interval') and #20 ask for custom period, and FastNoiseLite #86 asks for tiling. GenTileable2D works only for full output in 2D and through 4D. This tiles a subtree only, for example just the mask, not the detail, and avoids the 41 ns 4D cost for Cellular (4 x 3.9 = 16 ns). Side benefit: bounded coordinates avoid far coordinate precision loss, as in #83 and FastNoiseLite #176.
master.simd_plan: Fixed 2^n source calls: 4 in 2D, 8 in 3D, 16 in 4D. Weights via Floor, Select, polynomial. Whole-batch skip when no lane is in the band on that axis is legal for coherent grids, not assumed. Worst cost 4x / 8x / 16x source.
master.continuity: C1 if Source is C1: smoothstep has zero slope at both band ends, so derivative at the seam equals S'(0) on both sides.
master.params: Source, Period X/Y/Z/W (0 off, world units), Blend Fraction, Mean, Flatten toggle.
master.risks: Blend band shows ghosting on sharp features (cellular walls, ridges show double images). Variance flatten is only right for zero-mean roughly independent values; Gaussian assumption fails for heavily skewed sources. Worst-case cost grows quickly with dimension. PeriodicFBm is better when the source is lattice-only. Not prototyped; formula checked by hand only.
master.cost_note: Worst cost 4x / 8x / 16x source.
