measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 2D_warped_fbm: 20.19; 2D_fbm4: 15.33; 2D_perlin: 4.39; 3D_3oct_perlin3g: 11.53; 4D_perlin4: 14.67; note: Exactly 2^n source calls: 4 in 2D, 8 in 3D, 16 in 4D. 2D perlin: 223.5 ns, about 4x perlin2 plus weights
measured.est_avx2_ns: value: 4 x source plus about 0.5 ns: 4.9 ns for 2D perlin, about 18 ns for 2D 4 octave fbm; 8 x source in 3D, 16 x source in 4D (about 70 ns for 4D perlin); estimate: True

gradient-smear.look: Contour mode: fingerprints or marbled smoke, closed whorls around each extremum with smooth flow lines between them, very clean threshold panel of ridges and bifurcations. Along mode: radial streak bursts between basins. Terrain with contour mode gives terracettes wrapping around hills, a look that is rare and read at once as sheep tracks or strata. Terrain with along mode gives downhill gullies, less crisp than anchored-frame-detail because a line integral softens across as well. 3D volumes show twisted struts for contour and blade-like shards for along.

dims.3D: works, measured: contour via grad A x grad B, along via one gradient, both viewed as volumes with elongated struts and blades.
dims.4D: along mode only, measured on a plane, c0ratio 7.98. Contour needs a generalised cross and was not built.

gradient-smear.range: -1 .. 1 clamped over 8 seeds, mean 0.000. Std 0.352 at the measured gain 2 for M=5; M=3 at the same gain gives std 0.436, so gain must follow M and a.
gradient-smear.artifacts: Hillshade of the fine default shows a faint dotted bead grain along flow lines, which comes from the discrete tap spacing, even though a*df is 0.6. Ridged detail beads worse, seen directly in the table. Step a=0.24 at df=5 shows a strong beaded lattice. M=3 slightly beads at a=0.12. Mismatched tap count is the main user trap, a*df near 0.6 and M at least 5 looks clean. Near vortex centres the straight segment cuts across curved lines, which reads as small tight eyes and is acceptable. FFT is a soft central disc with a low contrast outer square; no grid dots. beta 6.93 is high: strong low pass, as expected.
gradient-smear.node_shape: GradientSmear: Guide (GeneratorSource), Detail (GeneratorSource), Second Guide (optional source, 3D contour), Step hybrid, Taps int M, Mode enum {Contour, Along}, Regularisation float, Sample Distance float, Gain float (or auto by table), Feature Scale.
gradient-smear.port_notes: Forward differences for g, t = g or R90 g over sqrt(|g|^2+e), then a fixed loop of 2M+1 Detail taps with squared triangular weights. No per-lane control flow. 3D contour takes a second D+1 taps. A step that is hybrid can fade to no smear where wanted. Direction is computed once, so cost is flat in streak length. Compared to anchored-frame-detail and steered-bank in 2D: it gives softer, closed flow lines rather than ridged strokes, and costs 14x vs about 20x. The look is different, so all can coexist, but only this gives real low-passing. related: line-integral-noise.
gradient-smear.params_text: Code defaults (contour, fingerprints): mode=0,a=0.1,M=5,df=6,gain=2,doct=1,ridge=0,gf=0.2,goct=1,h=0.1,e=0.003. Radial bursts: mode=1. Terracettes: df=8,out=1,amt=0.1,mode=0 --window 12. Gullies: same with mode=1. Volumes: df=2.5,a=0.25 (mode 0 or 1) --iso 0.

master.one_liner: Streamline-like streaks at about 10 taps: one gradient at p sets a direction, then a short weighted line integral of detail runs along it.
master.look: Swirling closed flow lines, hair, wood grain, fingerprint whorls, marbled smoke, with vortices at extrema and saddles of the guide. Along mode gives radial streak bursts between basins. Good for fur, wood, wind streaks, fluid-like textures.
master.algorithm: g from stencil of guide S at p. t = R90(g)/sqrt(|g|^2+e) (contour mode) or g/sqrt(|g|^2+e) (along mode). Output sum_{k=-M..M} w_k Detail(p + k a t) / sum w_k, with w_k = (1-|k|/(M+1))^2, then multiply by a measured gain to restore variance. 3D contour mode: t = cross(grad A, grad B)/(norm+e) using two guides, which has no hairy-ball seam and fades where the two are parallel. 4D: along mode only, or a generalised cross of three gradients. The direction is not re-evaluated along the segment, which is what keeps the cost flat.
master.why_new: True directional low-pass filtering. Warps stretch features but keep them sharp across the flow, while this removes energy along the flow only, which yields actual line structure. It was a surprise that this straight-segment version looks better than true curved LIC at the same budget: curved LIC at N=3 showed beads, and needed 49 taps at N=6.
master.simd_plan: Taps 2D 3+7=10 (M=3), 3D 8+7=15, 4D 5+7=12 along only. Perlin detail about 11/33/52 ns (scalar 2D prototype 12.4x perlin2 using fbm wrapper overhead). Direction is computed once for all lanes, then a fixed loop.
master.continuity: C0, C1 with a C2 guide, thanks to e in the normalisation. Measured c0ratio 7.76 with max slope about 103 per unit at detail frequency 8.
master.params: Guide, Detail, Step a (hybrid; length of streak, 0 fades to no smear), M (int), Mode enum, Sample Distance h. Keep a below half the detail feature size or beads appear.
master.risks: Contrast drop requires a measured gain per M and a. Detail sampling along a straight segment wrongly crosses tight curvature near vortices, though it looks acceptable. 3D requires a second guide and has more cost. Known cousin: line integral convolution, not seen as a noise node.
master.cost_note: Perlin detail about 11/33/52 ns (scalar 2D prototype 12.4x perlin2 using fbm wrapper overhead).

kaleido-stamp.look: 2D: an instantly ornamental scatter of mandalas, snowflakes, rosettes and dark or light flowers on a gray ground, each stamp different, with overlaps fading softly. FFT is a clean isotropic disc. Threshold shows crisp little snowflake outlines. It reads as designed, not random, as the catalogue said. Rorschach folds=1 with low zoom fbm was dull. 3D is less convincing: dense stamps lose the symmetry entirely, and only isolated stamps show it.

dims.2D: works, measured, D2^n, D6 and D3.
dims.3D: works, measured: box, octahedral, icosahedral chains. Dense settings looked like rock clumps with no visible symmetry. Isolated sparse settings give faceted symmetric boulders with star patterns at the facing axes, viewed.
dims.4D: works, measured on a plane: abs and sort of 4 axes, with an 81 cell scan. Not viewed.

kaleido-stamp.range: -1 .. 1 clamped over 8 seeds, mean -0.121 at K=3. Dim 3 mean 0.108, dim 4 mean 0.091. Mean is not centred, because the ridged source minus a fixed offset is measured roughly and stamps sit on a 0 background.
kaleido-stamp.artifacts: Gray background is flat where no stamp reaches, because R is capped by the window at 1.5 - 0.5*jit. Stamps with large R show a faint rim where the mask fades into the background. Overlapping stamps partly hide each other. A 3D stamp needs a dome term or it is an irregular blob. My first D3 fold chain was wrong and was fixed: abs x, then mirrors at lines -30 and 30.
kaleido-stamp.node_shape: No new node. Graph: StampScatter(K=3, Size, Jitter, Rotation, Stamp Zoom, Source=DomainKaleidoscope(Group=D6 or D8 or Ih, Source=FractalRidged(...))). If that graph proves awkward, a Fold enum on StampScatter would do the same with no extra source eval.
kaleido-stamp.port_notes: Mirror is p -= 2*Min(0, p.n)*n, cheap, with a constant table. Power of two dihedral mirror lines at 0, pi - pi/2, pi - pi/4...; each halves the kept wedge. The catalogue formula th/=2 starting from pi with n=(-sin th, cos th) does not halve the wedge correctly, so I used this table instead. D6: abs x, abs y, lines at 60 and 30. Ih: 3 x (abs of all axes, reflect across normalize(-phi, phi-1, 1)). Offset local coordinates by a per-stamp hash before the Source, because Perlin is 0 at the origin and every rosette would otherwise have a gray centre; a real graph gets this from a DomainOffset, or by a Source with no zero at the origin.
kaleido-stamp.params_text: Code defaults (D6 snowflakes): sym=1,K=3,jit=0.7,R=1.15,Rmin=0.65,zoom=3,src=1,soct=2,sharp=1.25,scale=0.5. Mandalas with 16 sectors: sym=0,folds=4,zoom=3.5. D3: sym=2,zoom=2.5. Isolated 3D gems: scale=1,sym=2,dome=1.2,zoom=2,sharp=0.4,dens=0.45,jit=0.5,R=0.95,Rmin=0.95,K=1,soct=1,src=1 --window 3 --iso 0.05.
kaleido-stamp.merged_into: stamp-scatter with a finite group domain-kaleidoscope as its Source. StampScatter already evaluates Source once per stamp in the stamp's rotated local frame with a per-stamp seed, and a finite sector fold around the origin is this idea's fold. The prototype runs exactly that sequence: rotate, fold, Source. Not tested on real nodes: integ.dll has StampScatter, but no real DomainKaleidoscope exists yet, and that idea is still a prototype.

master.one_liner: Scatter rosettes of any node: N-fold symmetry by O(log N) mirror folds in stamp-local coordinates, with no trig or atan2.
master.look: Prototype: each stamp becomes a symmetric mandala, snowflake, or insect-face-like Rorschach blot from plain Perlin. With R around 1.3, the field densely covers with overlapping symmetric motifs. Instantly reads as designed instead of random; ornament, flowers, snowflakes, crystal cross-sections.
master.algorithm: Choose top K stamps as in StampScatter (rank-subtract fade). For each winner, local l = (p-c)/r rotated by hash angle. Fold: th = pi; for q in 0..Folds (constant): th /= 2; n = (-sin th, cos th) from a precomputed table; dn = min(0, dot(l,n)); l -= 2*dn*n. Reflection is continuous (it maps across its own mirror exactly), so fold seams cannot jump. This gives 2^(Folds+1)-fold mirrored rosettes. v_k = Source.Gen(h_k, l*Zoom). Output sum(w_k v_k). 3D: fold across chosen octahedral or icosahedral mirror sets (constant table of 3-6 planes), for crystal-symmetric solids. Also useful as K=1 Scatter-free node: DomainKaleido around a single origin or hybrid-free lattice.
master.why_new: No node has mirror folding, and DomainAxisScale or abs of coordinates only offers a single global axis fold. Local per-instance mirror groups with per-stamp seeds provide endless non-repeating motifs from any existing graph.
master.simd_plan: Scan as StampScatter (5 ns in 2D, 15 ns in 3D, 50 ns in 4D), plus K*(Folds dot-and-subtract + Source). Folds table computed at param set. 3D mirror table cost ~ number of planes. K=2 Folds=3 in 2D: about 8 ns + 2 Source.
master.continuity: C0 verified: c0ratio 8.17 at K=2, Folds=2. Reflection folding is C0 with mirror kinks in the source's image, visible as creases when Source has gradient across a mirror (which is the look).
master.params: Folds (int), Source, K, Size, Zoom, Rotation (per stamp), Density, Mirror Set enum in 3D
master.risks: Reads as ornamental, so its niche is decorative textures and props rather than terrain. Pareidolia (faces) with low octave sources. Fold count per-lane is impossible; it is a member. Could overlap with a generic Kaleidoscope domain modifier from another lens, but per-stamp local fold is the distinct part.
master.cost_note: Scan as StampScatter (5 ns in 2D, 15 ns in 3D, 50 ns in 4D), plus K*(Folds dot-and-subtract + Source).

measured.scalar_note: Measured 495.5 ns vs perlin2 50.8, K=3, 2 octave source, so 6 of the 9.76x is the source. K=2 7.45x, K=1 4.60x, 16 sectors 10.21x, D3 9.64x. dim=3 octahedral 20.51x, icosahedral 20.37x, box 19.63x. dim=4 22.88x with 81 cell scan. Params read once.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured on SIMD: scan as StampScatter 5 / 15 / 50 ns in 2D / 3D / 4D as in the catalogue, plus about 1 ns per stamp for the mirrors, plus K x source.

local-frame.look: Rotate: flowing fur or wind-combed grass, long ridged strokes turning smoothly across the image with whirls and partings. Threshold panel shows clean tapered blades. It looks better than I expected for 2 evals. bins=4 gives a sharply different look: straight strokes in angular patches, like woven or herringbone shards. Scale: fine grain to broad blobs across the image, same isotropic character at each scale, FFT smooth with a soft ring. Terrain with hu=0.9: large mountains in one area, small foothills in another, with no shear. Naive forms confirmed side by side: moire eye loops for rotation and swirling shear bands for scale.

dims.3D: works, measured: rotation in the xy plane about a constant z axis (axis=1 rotates xz), scale in full. Scale volume viewed. A rotation about one constant axis is the limit: it cannot orient along a 3D vector field; see anchored-frame-detail for that.
dims.4D: works, measured on a plane: rotation applied in xy and zw planes, scale in full.

local-frame.range: -1 .. 1 over 8 seeds, clamped, mean 0.028 rotate and -0.001 scale. Scale with hu=0.9: -0.941 .. 0.847. The ridged recentring constant is measured in 2D: means rise to 0.307 at dim=3 and 0.323 at dim=4, so a port needs a constant per dimension.
local-frame.artifacts: A faint double exposure in the blend band where the control is slow, which reads as short crossing strokes rather than a flaw at bins=10. bins=24 is busier, not smoother, because bands get so thin that strokes are chopped. band below 1 cuts zipper arcs along control contours, seen directly in the band sweep, so band=1 stays. Scale step=2 shows visible patches of a different size with a soft edge; step 1 and 0.5 are clean. Scale relief with equal amplitude is needles in the fine zones, which led to hu. Scale values far from origin lose precision by 2^k, as the catalogue warned; far coords at 4e4 had no NaN and std 0.363. Angle is a scalar control, so there is no radial fan around a peak as anchored-frame-detail gives.
local-frame.node_shape: LocalFrame: Mode enum {Rotate, Scale}, Source (GeneratorSource), Control hybrid, Angle Range float or Scale Range float, Bins int (rotate) or Step float (scale), Plane enum for 3D, Amplitude Follows Scale float (scale mode), Contrast Preserve bool. Anisotropy is left to the source, through DomainAxisScale.
local-frame.port_notes: Always 2 source evals and 1 control. k = Floor(ctl*range/dl); t = hermite(frac); two rotations by k*dl and (k+1)*dl via FS::Sin and Cos on 2 angles, or a permute table when Bins is a power of two. A rotation by pi maps a stretched isotropic source to itself statistically, not exactly, so wrap does not matter because the control is continuous. Blend lerp(A,B,t)/sqrt(t^2+(1-t)^2). Scale uses 2^k by writing exponent bits for integer steps, FS::Pow otherwise. hu multiplies each slot by 2^(-k*hu), so its jump is hidden at t=0 or t=1. GeneratorCache as source would miss heavily.
local-frame.params_text: Code defaults (rotate, fur): mode=0,cf=0.14,coct=1,arange=3,bins=10,band=1,ani=9,sf=1.3,soct=2,ridge=1. Scale: mode=1,ridge=0,soct=3,sf=1,srange=3,step=1. Scale for terrain: mode=1,ridge=0,soct=4,sf=0.35,srange=3,hu=0.9,cf=0.12 --window 16 --hscale 110. Geometric shards: bins=4,arange=3.5,cf=0.22,coct=2,ani=7. Naive comparisons: mode=2, mode=3.

queue.name: LocalFrame
queue.reason: Binned scale and rotation crossfade removes origin shear when scale varies by mask, 2x source. Earlier proto beats naive scaling; watch the ghosting band.

master.one_liner: Spatially varying scale and rotation without swirl artifacts: quantise the control into bins, evaluate the source at the two adjacent frames, and contrast-preserving blend them.
master.look:
Scale: noise whose feature size changes smoothly across space with stable statistics. Rotate with an anisotropic source: fur, wind-swept grass, wood-like streaks flowing along an angle field. Look-tested (modes 4, 5): naive p*2^s shows large moire swirls and naive R(th)p shows tight moire loops, while both quantised versions are clean. The rotate result is one of the most striking looks from this lens.
[ScaleField, signal-phase] Tested. Noise goes smoothly from fine grain to broad blobs across the image, with the same isotropic character at each scale. The naive noise(f(p)*p) on the same field gives violent swirls and shear (rendered side by side). Uses: terrain roughness zones, gravel to sand transitions, detail focused near a mask, biome-dependent roughness.
master.algorithm:
VariableScale: s = Scale(p) (log2 units); k = floor(s/Step)*Step; t = quintic((s-k)/Step); A = Source(p * 2^k); B = Source(p * 2^(k+Step)). VariableRotate: th = Angle(p); dl = pi/Bins; k = floor(th/dl); t = hermite(th/dl - k); A = Source(R(k*dl)*p); B = Source(R((k+1)*dl)*p). Both: out = lerp(A, B, t) / sqrt(t^2 + (1-t)^2). k needs no wrap for a continuous scalar control. Combining both controls would need 4 evals (bilinear), so ship as two nodes or a mode switch. Anisotropy comes from the source, e.g. DomainAxisScale(X=0.25, Y=3, Perlin).

[ScaleField, signal-phase] L=Range*(ScaleSource(p)*0.5+0.5), the log2 of the frequency.
ra=2*Round(L/2) is the even slot; rb=2*Round((L-1)/2)+1 is the odd slot.
wa=1-|L-ra|; wb=1-wa; optionally smoothstep wa.
fa=Exp(ra*ln r), fb=Exp(rb*ln r).
Out=(wa*S(seed+ra, p*fa)+wb*S(seed+rb, p*fb))/Sqrt(wa*wa+wb*wb).
Each slot jumps only at the L where its weight is zero, so there are no seams. The source gets per-lane positions and seeds, which the execution model already allows because lanes may be spatially unrelated. Sibling mode Rotate: the same two-slot scheme on rotation angle, which gives oriented anisotropic sources (DomainAxisScale noise, SineWave) a spatial orientation field.
master.why_new: A hybrid DomainScale or DomainRotate would have shear proportional to |p|*|grad control|, so artifacts grow with distance from the origin, which is why people avoid it. Quantisation removes the origin dependence with exactly 2 source evals regardless of range or bin count. Feature size or orientation as a spatial input is otherwise unavailable, and DomainScale's Scaling is a constant float today.
master.simd_plan: Branch-free, always 2 source evals + 1 control. Floor, Convert. 2^k by writing the float exponent bits (integer steps) or FS::Pow (fractional Step). Per-lane cos/sin of two angles (4 FS::Sin/Cos), or a small permute table when Bins is a power of two. About 2x source + ~1 ns in all dimensions. 3D rotates in a plane or about a constant axis (R built by the same Sin/Cos); 4D rotates xy and zw planes.
master.continuity: C0: at a bin change t reaches 0 or 1, so only one frame has weight. Measured c0ratio 8.0 for both.
master.params: Source, Scale (hybrid, log2), Step (float), Angle (hybrid, radians), Bins (int), Axis enum, Contrast Preserve (bool).
master.risks:
Ghosting in the blend band (two unrelated patterns as a double exposure), especially when the control changes slowly or the source is strongly anisotropic. Mid-blend amplitude can reach sqrt2 x source on correlated values, so clamp if range matters. An angle from atan2 of a direction field wraps and would jump, so use a continuous scalar (or map the wrap via multiples). Large scale ranges lose float precision at far coordinates.
[ScaleField, signal-phase] The mid-blend zone shows two scales overlaid, which is mild for r=2 and worse for larger ratios. Sources must honour per-lane seed and positions; GeneratorCache would miss heavily. GPU-style lane coherence assumptions in sources would break. Rotate mode has only been reasoned through via the SteeredStripes test, and with stripes it gives herringbone (see that entry).
sources: Flow-map two-phase blending (Vlachos, Valve, from memory, not consulted)
master.cost_note: About 2x source + ~1 ns in all dimensions.
master.variant_notes: Six proposals: vary scale or rotation by quantising per lane and blending exactly two evals. The odd/even slot form (ScaleField) keeps a single source pair for any range. Rotate mode with stripes gives herringbone at low bin counts.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 303.6 ns vs perlin2 49.7, 1 control + 2 frames x 2 octaves = 5 perlin plus Sin/Cos. Scale with 3 octave source 8.31x. dim=3 rotate 11.81x, scale 15.89x. dim=4 rotate 6.30x, scale 8.28x (this perlin4 is cheap). Naive rotate 3.84x, naive scale 5.45x. Scale terrain 4 octaves plus hu pow 10.81x.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured on SIMD: about 2x source + 1 control + 1 ns. With 1 octave control and 2 octave Perlin source, 2D about 7 ns, 3D about 13 ns, 4D about 25 ns.
measured.c0_note: Rotate 7.93, scale 7.76, rotate dim=3 7.93, scale dim=3 7.38, rotate dim=4 7.84, scale dim=4 7.43, scale terrain with hu=0.9 8.01. Naive rotate mode=2 5.81 with max slope 259.4, against 38.3 for the quantised form. Naive scale mode=3 7.48 with max slope 68.6, against 28.0.

log-polar-vortex.look: A field of crisp logarithmic spirals, one per Voronoi cell, packed edge to edge: like Van Gogh's sky, marbled paper or a floor of whirlpools. Clockwise and anticlockwise spirals mix, with arms tightening smoothly into each centre. The hillshade looks like swirled green glass. Cell borders are soft grey seams between neighbouring spirals, and the threshold panel shows they are straight polygon edges. At twist=0 the arms vanish, leaving rosettes of concentric rings, and low zoom gives radial star bursts. The 3D form is real: cut faces of the isosurface show rose-like spirals in every direction, and the XZ slice shows whirls as well.

dims.note: 2D and 3D measured continuous. 4D needs a 5D source and is not implemented, so GenTileable2D would need the catalogue's dropped-component fallback

range.note: 8 seeds/offsets, far coords (4e4) min -0.700 max 0.657 std 0.203

log-polar-vortex.artifacts: Straight cell borders show as thin grey bands, most visibly in the threshold panel and in cells without enough arms. Centres have fine detail at the 512 px sheet. Histogram has a spike at 0 from the fade. Neighbouring spirals do not connect: this is a packing, not a flow field. All cells have the same statistics, so at the wide view it becomes an even carpet.
log-polar-vortex.node_shape: LogPolarVortex: Source (required, sampled one dimension up), Cell Size via Feature Scale, Zoom Rate float, Angular Scale float, Twist hybrid, Mix Spin bool, Min Radius float, Edge Fade float, Background float, Jitter float, Seed Offset.
log-polar-vortex.port_notes: Uses a 3x3 window (3x3x3 in 3D), matching CellularDistance. lab's worley2 is 5x5, so a local 3x3 search replaces it; c0 was identical. Costs: cellular F1 and F2 tracking the nearest vector and hash; Log, Sin, Cos, InvSqrt; one source call one dimension higher, plus one for the centre blend. Inside Min Radius the direction is a pinwheel point, so the prototype blends to Source(0, 0, L) between 0.5 and 2 Min Radius. To save the second source call a port could accept a small pinwheel, not tested. Per-cell random offset to L (rnd01 * 37) keeps cells different; per-cell spin sign from one hash bit; 3D twist about a hashed axis with Rodrigues (no atan2). float precision: L stays small, but the source is sampled away from origin by the hash offset, which is harmless.
log-polar-vortex.params_text: cell=1.8,zoom=1.1,angular=1.1,twist=3,rmin=0.04,fade=0.2,jitter=0.8,oct=3,mixspin=1,bg=0 (code defaults; 3D oct3=2). Rosettes without arms: twist=0,zoom=2.2

master.one_liner: Each Voronoi cell becomes a self-similar zoom into its centre: the Source is evaluated in (log radius, unit direction) coordinates with optional spiral twist, giving whirlpools/galaxies/rosettes whose detail density grows toward the centre, packed seamlessly by a cell-edge fade.
master.look: Fields of whirlpools, galaxies, rosettes, tree rings with ever-finer rings toward the centre, drain/vortex surfaces; with Twist the Source's features become logarithmic spiral arms. Nothing on the sheet is scale-covariant around points. Good for magical/alien terrain, shells, eyes, fluid vortices, spiral galaxies in space skyboxes, and as a warp when used inside a DomainWarp graph on its output.
master.algorithm:
cellular 3x3 search -> nearest point c (hash h), F1, F2 (reuse Cellular code)
  d = p - c ; r = Max(|d|, MinRadius) ; u = (d / r)               // unit direction, no atan2
  L = Log(r) * ZoomRate + rnd01(h)*Period                           // log-radius coordinate
  twist: (cs, sn) = (Cos(Twist*L), Sin(Twist*L)); u' = rotate(u, cs, sn)   // spiral arms; 3D: rotate u about a hashed per-cell axis
  2D node: v = Source3D(u'.x * Angular, u'.y * Angular, L)          // Source sampled one dimension up (as AddDimension does)
  3D node: v = Source4D(u'.x*Angular, u'.y*Angular, u'.z*Angular, L)
  m = smoothstep(0, Fade, F2 - F1)                                   // cell-edge fade so neighbouring vortices meet without a crack
  out = Lerp(Source(p) * Background, v, m)   or  v*m
Because the direction lives on the unit circle/sphere the angular coordinate is automatically periodic (no seam at 2pi); the radial coordinate is logarithmic so each factor of e in radius maps to a fixed noise distance: structure repeats statistically under zoom (Droste effect) down to MinRadius.
master.why_new: Requires evaluating a Source in a log-polar frame per cell with a dimension lift; a graph has no log, no per-cell centre, no unit-direction coordinates. Combines multi-scale self-similarity (literal) with cellular packing.
master.simd_plan: Branch-free: Cellular F1/F2 window + Log, InvSqrt, Sin/Cos + one Source call one dimension higher (+ optional second Source call for background). Cost ~CellularDistance + Source(D+1) + 20 ops. 2D and 3D exact; 4D requires a 5D Source (not available): 4D falls back to using (u.xyz, L) and dropping the 4th direction component (tiling then imperfect; acceptable, document it).
master.continuity: C1 inside a cell where the Source is C1 (log and normalisation are smooth for r>0; MinRadius caps the singularity, leaving a flat disc); across cell edges continuity comes from the Fade (C1 with smoothstep).
master.params: Source (required), Zoom Rate, Angular Scale, Twist hybrid, Min Radius, Fade, Background, Jitter, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
master.risks: Near the centre the Source is sampled at extreme frequency in angle terms; aliasing inside MinRadius is avoided by the cap but the ring at MinRadius is a visible disc; blend to Source(c) there. 4D story is weak.
master.cost_note: Cost ~CellularDistance + Source(D+1) + 20 ops.

steered-bank.look: 2D default: feathers or big leaves. Ridged strokes fan out from every extremum and meet at sharp partings, with threshold panel showing clean blades. orient=1: Van Gogh swirls around peaks. 3 octaves gives a plumage-like texture. Terrain relief looks very similar to anchored-frame-detail: gullies running downhill, fading at flats. 3D volume shows slits and blades in a few fixed directions.

dims.3D: works, measured, flawed look. Six fixed icosahedron diagonals show directly: a P sweep from 2 to 8 on a 3D plane shows straight parallel stripe patches and blobby zones. Low P adds crosshatch and does not hide the patches.
dims.4D: works, measured on a plane: 12 axes of the 24 cell, c0ratio 7.80. Not viewed. Same limitation expected.

steered-bank.range: -1 .. 1 over 8 seeds clamped, mean -0.050. 3D plane mean -0.006 and 4D plane mean -0.088 after per dimension constants.
steered-bank.artifacts: FFT shows a clear 16 ray star from the 8 fixed axes, axis stat 7.92; this does not read as a lattice in the image but does at low K. Below P=6 there is obvious crosshatch, and at P=16 sector boundaries get sharper. Zero mean detail is needed before the variance preserving sum, otherwise K=12 at low P saturates white: seen in the first sweep and fixed. In 3D the direction quantisation is the unsolved flaw, and it is why this is promising and not keeper. 12 or more axes in 3D would help at linear cost; not tried.
steered-bank.node_shape: SteeredBank: Guide (GeneratorSource), Detail (GeneratorSource), Anisotropy float, Axes int (2D) with fixed tables for 3D and 4D, Sharpness int, Orientation enum {Along Slope, Along Contours}, Sample Distance hybrid, Fade float, Feature Scale.
steered-bank.port_notes: Fixed loop over K axes. Forward differences for the guide, then per axis two Dots, an integer power, and one Detail. Stretch is a fixed linear map, so shear does not grow with distance: far coords (4e4) had std 0.452. In 2D this competes with anchored-frame-detail, 20.69x vs 19.54x at similar quality; anchored has no axis star and works in 3D without direction quantisation, but needs a lattice and per-anchor taps. With doct=1 SteeredBank is cheaper at 12.60x. If only one of the two ships, anchored-frame-detail is the better choice because of 3D; SteeredBank wins only on a 2D budget, and because its orientation follows the guide at full resolution, not at anchors.
steered-bank.params_text: Code defaults: K=8,P=8,ani=10,df=4,doct=2,ridge=1,gf=0.2,goct=1,h=0.1,e2=0.01,orient=0. Swirl along contours: orient=1. Woven: K=4,P=2,df=4,ani=8,doct=1. Gullied terrain: out=1,amt=0.14,df=7,ani=12,gf=0.2 --window 12. Volumes: df=1.5,ani=6,doct=1 --iso 0.

master.one_liner: Orient detail along a sampled gradient by crossfading a small bank of fixed-direction stretched noises, so there is no rotation and no far-from-origin shear.
master.look: K=6 and sharpening P=6 give feather and leaf-like fans, with sector boundaries that resemble plumage or shell ridges. Multi-octave detail with larger K looks like brushed, Van Gogh-style flow. K=4 and low P looks woven or herringbone. Good for feathers, foliage masses, brushed metal, strata following terrain, fabrics.
master.algorithm: K axes a_k mod 180 degrees (2D K=4-6; 3D 6 icosahedron diagonals; 4D 12). Stretch without frames: q_k = p + (1/ani - 1)(p.a_k)a_k + offset_k, n_k = Detail(q_k). Orientation weight from the guide's gradient, with no atan: o_k = ((g.a_k)^2/(|g|^2+e) - 1/D) scaled by |g|^2/(|g|^2+e2). w_k = (0.5 + 0.5 o_k)^P via integer power. Output sum(w_k n_k)/sqrt(sum w_k^2), which preserves variance. Enum selects streaks along contours or along the slope by flipping the sign of o_k.
master.why_new: Hybrid rotation of a domain shears without bound far from the origin, so spatially varying anisotropy is not achievable today. The bank is a linear blend of linear domains, so shear cannot grow with distance and the node stays correct at any coordinate. A graph would need K+D+1 hand-wired nodes, and it could not get the double-angle weights.
master.simd_plan: Taps (D+1) guide + K detail: 2D 3+6=9, 3D 4+6=10, 4D 5+12=17. On Perlin-based detail about 10/22/73 ns. A guide may be a cheap low-frequency single octave. Could skip detail evaluation when all lanes have w_k=0, which does not alter results.
master.continuity: C0 and generally C1 when the guide is C2 with the fade at |g|=0. Measured c0ratio 7.32 with the fade, 1.9 without it, so the fade term is essential.
master.params: Guide source, Detail source, Anisotropy ani (float), K (enum), Sharpness P (int), Orientation enum, Sample Distance h (hybrid). Sharpness could be hybrid at the cost of Pow.
master.risks: Crossfade between two directions shows crosshatching in between unless P is large, and large P makes sector seams (which is the feather look but may not be wanted). The stretch and K are compile-style choices for the axis tables. Related to Goldberg et al. anisotropic noise, which uses a precomputed texture bank; this is the pointwise form.
master.cost_note: On Perlin-based detail about 10/22/73 ns.

measured.scalar_note: Final build: 1053.4 ns vs 50.9, K=8 with 2 octave detail, 3 guide + 16 detail = 19 perlin. dim=3 33.30x, dim=4 33.04x. Measured on the build before the mean constant edit, which only changed a constant: doct=1 12.60x, K=6 P=6 doct=1 10.33x (the catalogue form), dim=3 doct=1 20.76x, dim=4 doct=1 20.68x.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured on SIMD: taps x handbook Perlin cost: 2D K=6 1 octave 9 x 1.1 = 10 ns, 3D 10 x 2.2 = 22 ns, 4D 17 x 4.3 = 73 ns, agreeing with the catalogue.
measured.c0_note: Default 7.81, doct=1 8.00, K=6 P=6 doct=1 7.97, orient=1 7.85, dim=3 7.96 and dim=4 7.80 on the final build. Without the fade e2=0: 4.57, max slope 291.4, so the fade is essential, as the catalogue says.

truchet-flow.look: Default: agate or marbled ribbons. Plain fbm stretched along the paths makes concentric bands that follow closed loops and small rounded square rings, with a calm thick and thin variation. src=1,band=2 is brain coral or wet fingerprint loops. Without pre warp it reads as op-art tiles with an obvious square grid, like koru patterns. Plain isotropic source without anisotropy (ku=kv) looks stamped and mirrored, which is not good; anisotropy is needed. Relief is dark with sharp contour ploughed terraces, more graphic than natural. Tube volume is the surprise: a real pipe network with continuous curved tubes and fine ribbing, immediately recognisable as a 3D Truchet.

dims.3D: works, measured and viewed. A true tube tile, which the catalogue did not prototype: three quarter tori in a cube, reflected by 3 hash bits, makes a closed tube network, and nested tubes come out with a generic source.
dims.4D: works as pass-through S(U, V, z, w), measured on a plane. A true 4D tile is not built.

truchet-flow.range: -1 .. 1 over 8 seeds, clamped, mean 0.013. Default render -0.941 .. 0.902. 3D plane default -0.908 .. 0.876.
truchet-flow.artifacts: The wide view of the default has vertical column banding: source x is mostly drift*x and source y is dominated by 5*V, so the noise looks like slow columns at large scale. An untested idea is to feed the warp noise values into the source offset instead of linear drift, with no extra evals. Square lattice is still faintly present at warp=0.6, as rounded square rings. Tubes show faint ribs from the source and small stair steps near arc swaps, where U is faded. FFT has a faint cross and axis stat 23.7.
truchet-flow.node_shape: TruchetFlow: Source (GeneratorSource), Cell Size float, Along Scale float, Across Scale float, Drift hybrid, Output 3D enum {Extrude, Tubes}, Feature Scale, Seed Offset. A pre warp can stay a graph job through a domain warp node.
truchet-flow.port_notes: 2D is 1 hash, 1 sqrt after comparing squares, atan poly, Selects, no neighbours. 3D tube: 3 arcs per cube with sqrt each, hash bits reflect axes, each face centre is used by exactly one arc. Two seams were found by check and fixed. First, on a cube face another arc can be nearest beyond distance .5, so V is capped at .5, since other arcs stay at least .5 from that face. Second, U swaps at the medial surface between arcs inside a cube, so U is multiplied by smoothstep(0,.08,d2-d1) and by 1-smoothstep(.35,.5,d1). This makes U equal 0 on every face. Both took c0ratio from 1.09 to 7.95. The catalogue's 3D note asked for its own seam proof, and this is it. Anisotropy needs ku small and kv large: isotropic settings look mirrored.
truchet-flow.params_text: Code defaults (agate ribbons from plain fbm): cell=2,ku=0.4,kv=5,drift=0.25,sf=1,soct=3,warp=0.6,wf=0.3,src=0,tube=1. Brain coral: src=1,band=2. Plain tile lattice: warp=0,src=1,band=3,ku=2,kv=2,drift=0.15. True 3D tubes: cell=1.6,src=1,warp=0,ku=2,kv=2,drift=0.15 --iso 0.

master.one_liner: Feeds the source arc-ribbon coordinates (along-path, across-path) of a random Truchet tiling, so any noise flows along closed meanders with one eval.
master.look: Brain-coral and labyrinth meanders: bands of source follow closed curves and rings around tile corners. With strata it looks like agate worm tracks, wet fingerprint loops, river meanders or Maori koru. Prototyped: mode=3, src=1 gives the clearest result.
master.algorithm: cell = floor(p*s). (u,v) = frac; if hash bit, u = 1-u. Pick nearest arc corner: r1 = |(u,v)|, r2 = |(1-u,1-v)|, (dx,dy) = nearer corner offset, r = min(r1,r2). th = atan(min(dx,dy)/max(dx,dy)) by polynomial on [0,1], in [0,pi/4]. U = th*r, V = abs(r-.5). Output S( ku*U/s + drift*x, kv*V/s + drift*y ). Continuity proof: on every tile edge th=0 so U=0, and V = |edge offset - .5| matches both sides for either flip; on the anti-diagonal r1=r2 and the min/max form makes th equal from both corners; at corners r=0 so U=0 (the first prototype used th*.5 and had a jump there, th*r fixes it). Fold means source is mirrored at each tile edge and arc midpoint; drift adds slow variation to break repetition.
master.why_new: Puts texture along a path network rather than just drawing the network. No cell or warp node can route a source along curved channels, and a graph cannot since it needs local arc coordinates.
master.simd_plan: 1 hash, 2 sqrt (or 1, comparing squares first), atan poly, Select. About 1.5-2 ns (estimate) plus source. Lattice 1x1, no neighbours. 3D: pass z through as S(U,V,z), or true tube form using a hash-picked set of 3 quarter tori in a cube with V = tube radius, U = arc angle*r (needs its own seam proof). 4D: S(U,V,z,w).
master.continuity: C0 with creases along edge and mid lines; measured c0ratio 8.07 after the fix.
master.params: Cell Size, Along Scale ku, Across Scale kv, Drift (hybrid), Source.
master.risks: With no drift the tile content repeats and looks stamped. Very anisotropic stripe sources show star-shaped mirror junctions at corners (seen with ku=.3,kv=1.2 on a sine source), so anisotropy needs limits. True 3D tubes were not prototyped. The square lattice remains faintly visible; pre-warping helps.
master.cost_note: About 1.5-2 ns (estimate) plus source.

measured.scalar_note: Measured 314.5 ns vs perlin2 51.3 with 3 octave source and 2 Perlin evals of pre warp. warp=0: 3.73x, so the mapping alone is about 0.7x perlin. Coral 6.52x. dim=3 tubes 13.56x, with params for tubes 13.65x, dim=3 extruded 12.84x. dim=4 3.44x with pass-through z,w and no warp, 3 octaves of cheap perlin4.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured on SIMD: mapping 1.5 to 2 ns in 2D as in the catalogue, 3D tubes about 4 ns for 3 arcs with sqrt per arc. Add one source eval, plus 2 to 3 low frequency evals if a warp is wanted.
measured.c0_note: Default 7.92, warp=0 7.99, coral 7.88, 3D plane default 8.04, 3D tubes src=1 7.48, 3D extruded tube=0 7.96, 4D 7.97. First true tube version read 1.09 because of two seam sources, both fixed; see port_notes. These are plane probes, not a full seam scan of 3D.

blend-mode.look: Overlay of a slow fbm and a cellular F1: round bubbles that are bright and full-contrast inside light regions of the base and fade into dark regions, keeping the full [-1,1] range (std 0.60). The same pair through a [-1,1] Multiply is measurably flatter (std 0.23, grey with sign flips, visible in the mode table). SoftLight is a softer Overlay. HardLight and VividLight nearly threshold the bubbles. Burn leaves isolated bright blobs on black. With fbm in place of cellular, Overlay looks like another contrasty fbm, nothing distinctive. Ridged input saturates to white in Dodge, LinearLight and Screen because ridged has a high mean, so Input Min/Max must be tuned per source.

dims.3D: works, measured (check and XZ slice)
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D; the node is output-only math so a GenT form is dimension agnostic

blend-mode.artifacts: None in Overlay, SoftLight, HardLight, Screen, Exclusion, Linear, Pin (Pin c0ratio 8.00). Dodge c0ratio 6.55, max slope 67.5; Vivid c0ratio 5.58, max slope 130.8: these two are steep at the guarded division, not true jumps at eps 0.02. Clipped plateaus at the histogram ends (spikes at -1 and +1) because inputs saturate at Input Range 0.6.
blend-mode.node_shape: BlendMode: Base, Blend (generators); Mode enum (Overlay, SoftLight, HardLight, Screen, Dodge, Burn, Vivid, LinearLight, PinLight, Exclusion); Opacity (hybrid); Input Min, Input Max.
blend-mode.port_notes: Generic GenT, enum switch once per Gen, per-lane Select on the compares, guarded division. No lattice. Keeper on authoring ability rather than a new noise: Overlay and SoftLight need a per-lane compare, which a graph could only imitate by duplicating both source subtrees through Min and Max. Could drop Vivid and Pin to trim the enum, but Pin gave the most unusual look.

master.one_liner: Photoshop and W3C separable blend modes in a normalised space: Overlay, SoftLight, HardLight, Screen, ColorDodge, ColorBurn, Vivid, Linear and Pin Light, Exclusion, with an opacity hybrid.
master.look: Overlay: large-scale FBm modulates the contrast of detail while keeping range and mean. Look-tested (mode 20): Multiply of two [-1,1] fields is flat grey with sign flips, while Overlay/SoftLight stay contrasty. Dodge and VividLight with cellular produce blown-out bubbly plates; Burn gives isolated bright blobs on black.
master.algorithm: b = 0.5 + 0.5*Base; s = 0.5 + 0.5*Blend (W3C naming: Cb = backdrop, Cs = source). HardLight: s <= 0.5 ? b*2s : b + (2s-1) - b*(2s-1). Overlay = HardLight(s, b). Screen: b + s - b*s. SoftLight: s <= 0.5 ? b - (1-2s)*b*(1-b) : b + (2s-1)*(D(b) - b), with D(b) = b <= 0.25 ? ((16b-12)b+4)b : sqrt(b). ColorDodge: min(1, b / max(1-s, eps)). ColorBurn: 1 - min(1, (1-b)/max(s, eps)). Exclusion: b + s - 2bs. LinearLight: sat(b + 2s - 1). VividLight: s <= 0.5 ? Burn(2s) : Dodge(2s-1). PinLight: s <= 0.5 ? min(b, 2s) : max(b, 2s-1). out = lerp(b, B(b,s), Opacity) * 2 - 1.
master.why_new: Multiply in [-1,1] is a sign-flipping operation, whereas the common intent (modulate) needs Remap + Multiply + Remap. Overlay and SoftLight additionally need a per-lane compare with no graph form except duplicating sources. These modes are what texture artists reach for first, so authoring gets far faster from Substance and Photoshop habits.
master.simd_plan: Two source evals; enum selects code path once per Gen; per-lane Select on compares; guarded division. About sum of sources + under 1 ns. No lattice, dimension agnostic.
master.continuity: C0 for Screen, Overlay, HardLight, SoftLight, Exclusion, Linear, Pin. Dodge, Burn and Vivid have a corner discontinuity at (s=1, b->0) softened by eps; measured c0ratio 7.7 on Dodge with cellular.
master.params: Base, Blend (generators), Mode enum, Opacity (hybrid), Input Min, Input Max (default -1, 1).
master.risks: Mathematically not novel, so value is entirely in convenience and frequency of use. Assumes normalised inputs; out-of-range inputs clip. Dodge and Burn saturate large areas (test panel mostly white). Enum count may be trimmed to Overlay, SoftLight, HardLight, Screen, Dodge, Burn, Linear Light.
master.cost_note: About sum of sources + under 1 ns.

measured.scalar_note: Measured with the built-in sources included (4 octave fbm + 3x3 cellular) and per-sample map lookups of 6 params, so nearly all of it is source cost, not node cost.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: sources + under 1 ns; about 9 ns with these built-in sources (4 x 1.1 Perlin + 3.9 cellular + 1)

combine-ops.look: Default is Stairs on two crossing vein fields (|noise|): rounded pods separated by dark channels, with ribs that run parallel to the crease and fan out into star-like knots where the veins cross. Hillshade shows strong dark ribbing on every flank. The 3D isosurface gives separated rocks with stepped, ribbed bevels along their edges, which reads as carved or wave-cut stone. On smooth fbm height fields the same operators are far quieter: plain Chamfer and Round barely differ from Min at this scale, Tongue, Groove and Engrave draw thin lines along one field's zero set, Stairs is a few faint ripples. Pipe gives a different bright ridge network. So the distance-like vein input is what makes this node worth having.

dims.3D: works, measured (check, XZ slice, vol)
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D; output-only math so a GenT form is dimension agnostic

combine-ops.artifacts: Spectrum has a diagonal X because the a,b mod runs along a-b; visible only as directional ribs. Threshold panel shows small ribbed notches where a level cuts stair treads. Stair width depends on local field slope, so ribs widen on flat ground. Output range is not analytic: default outScale and outBias are measured fits and other ops reach further (Columns measured [-1.07, 1.25], Engrave without rescale up to 1.73). Catalogue's gated Columns form jumped (c0ratio 1.08, max slope 185); the clamped index form I wrote instead measures c0ratio 8.00.
combine-ops.node_shape: CombineOps: A, B (generators); Operation enum (Chamfer, Round, Stairs, Columns, Pipe, Engrave, Groove, Tongue); Side enum (Union, Intersection, Difference); Radius (hybrid); Step Count (int); Tongue Radius (hybrid). Soft dropped, it is MinSmooth.
combine-ops.port_notes: Generic GenT, enum once per Gen, 2 source evals plus Min, Max, Sqrt, floored Modulus. FS::Modulus must be floored for stairs on negative values; check against Blends.inl. Columns here is branch free: clamp the column index so no a<r && b<r gate is needed. Formulas came from the catalogue entry and were not fetched; check the hg_sdf licence before citing it in a real node.
combine-ops.params_text: op=4,side=0,r=0.5,n=5,srcMode=1,freq=0.5,inScale=1.4,octaves=1,outScale=1.7,outBias=-0.65 (these are the code defaults); vol uses --iso -0.33

queue.name: CombineOps
queue.reason: Chamfer, stairs and groove combiners under 1 ns. Fillet radii are only true on distance-like inputs, so pair with iso-distance.

master.one_liner: hg_sdf distance-field combiners for two noise fields: chamfer, round fillet, stairs, columns, groove, tongue, engrave, pipe.
master.look: Look-tested (mode 10). Stairs: rippled terraces in the crease where fields meet. Chamfer: flat planar facets. Round: clean fillet that keeps sharp elsewhere. Tongue and Engrave: raised or cut line following one field's zero set across the other, like roads with embankments or ditched rivers. In 3D, these give bevelled cave junctions.
master.algorithm: With a, b and min convention. Chamfer: min(a, b, (a+b-r)/sqrt2). Round: max(r, min(a,b)) - length(max(r-a,0), max(r-b,0)). Soft: e = max(r-|a-b|, 0); min(a,b) - e^2/(4r). Stairs: s = r/n; u = b - r; min(a, b, 0.5*(u + a + |mod(u-a+s, 2s) - s|)). Columns: if a<r and b<r place n-1 circular columns of radius r*sqrt2/(2(n-1)+sqrt2) along the diagonal, else min(a,b). Pipe: sqrt(a^2+b^2) - r. Engrave: max(a, (a+r-|b|)/sqrt2). Groove: max(a, min(a+ra, rb-|b|)). Tongue: min(a, max(a-ra, |b|-rb)). Max-family by negation of inputs and output; Difference by max(a,-b) form. Use mod floored (hg_sdf uses GLSL mod).
master.why_new: MinSmooth and MaxSmooth have a single fillet shape. Crease shaping with steps, chamfer or inlaid lines is unavailable, and a graph version needs repeats of a and b, each an expensive subtree evaluated several times.
master.simd_plan: 2 source evals + few Min/Max/Sqrt/FS::Modulus ops, under 1 ns extra, one enum dispatch per Gen. Columns uses Select instead of a branch. Generic GenT, all dimensions.
master.continuity: C0: measured c0ratio 8.0 for Stairs and Tongue; hg_sdf operators are piecewise smooth with continuous joins. Columns may have a slope break at the column boundary.
master.params: A, B (generators), Operation enum, Radius (hybrid), Step Count (int), Tongue Radius (hybrid), Side enum (Union, Intersection, Difference).
master.risks: Operators are built for true distance fields, and on raw noise the fillet width depends on local slope, so pairing with IsoDistance gives better results. FS::Modulus must match floored mod semantic or stairs break for negatives; check against Blends.inl. Niche compared with BlendMode and HeightBlend, and Columns and Soft may not earn enum slots (Soft is close to MinSmooth).
master.cost_note: 2 source evals + few Min/Max/Sqrt/FS::Modulus ops, under 1 ns extra, one enum dispatch per Gen.

measured.scalar_note: Includes 2 Perlin source evals and per-sample map lookups, so node overhead alone is small.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 2 x source + under 1 ns, about 3.2 ns on single octave Perlin

contrast-fade.look: Default render: patches of smooth fbm and sharp ridged veins grading into each other through a slow Perlin mask, with no grey band in the transition. In the split image (left half lerp, right half ContrastFade, bands along y) hillshade relief is a bit stronger on the right and the split line is visible, but side by side panels of the whole image look nearly the same, and on 5 octave sources I could not reliably tell them apart by eye. A real numeric win that reads as subtle in a still image. Ghosting of both sources in the band remains.

dims.3D: works, measured (check and XZ slice)
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D; output-only math

contrast-fade.artifacts: None. Slight overshoot at t=0.5 (std 0.318 against 0.305). With fbm and ridged sources the means differ (ridged mean 0.121 at gain 1), so the mean drifts across the fade, as the catalogue warned; a Mean param would be needed for exact preservation. Range is not analytically bounded, gain 0.85 is a measured fit.
contrast-fade.node_shape: Add to Fade: Preserve Variance (bool or interpolation variant), Correlation rho (float, -1 to 1).
contrast-fade.port_notes: One InvSqrt and one multiply after the existing Fade lerp, guarded by the fact that wa^2 + wb^2 stays at or above 0.5 when rho is 0. Merged because the catalogue's own variant note and the measurements agree: there is no new look, only a better Fade. It is cheap and worth doing as that option. Not a keeper as a separate node.
contrast-fade.params_text: srcKind=1,fadeSrc=0,maskFreq=0.22,band=0.5,freq=0.9,octaves=3,gain=0.85,rho=0 (these are the code defaults). Comparison image: split=1,fadeSrc=2,maskFreq=0.125,srcKind=0,octaves=2
contrast-fade.merged_into: Fade (real node): an interpolation or normalise option, not a new node

queue.name: ContrastFade
queue.reason: Variance-preserving lerp with one InvSqrt that fixes washed-out fades. Likely a Fade option rather than a new node.

master.one_liner: Variance-preserving crossfade: ((1-t)A + tB) / sqrt((1-t)^2 + t^2 + 2 rho t(1-t)) with hybrid t, so the transition zone between two noises keeps full contrast instead of the washed-out band that Fade/lerp produces; exact histogram preservation when inputs are Gaussianised.
master.look: Same two sources, but the transition band keeps peaks and valleys rather than turning into low-contrast mush. Look-tested (mode 7): hillshade across the fade retains full relief while plain lerp visibly flattens in the middle.
master.algorithm:
a = A(x), b = B(x), t = clamp(Fade(x), 0, 1) (hybrid), rho = Correlation (float, 0 for independent sources, measured for correlated ones).
wa = 1 - t, wb = t (optionally t = smoothstep(t) first).
norm = InvSqrt( wa^2 + wb^2 + 2 rho wa wb )
out = (wa a + wb b) * norm
Mean handling: if Mean != 0, subtract Mean from a and b, blend, add back (keeps the mean fixed and the std fixed).
N-way variant via chaining: StatBlend(StatBlend(A,B,t1), C, t2) is still variance preserving when the sources are independent.
With A, B passed through ExactGaussianNoise/CdfRemap (Gaussian) first and CdfRemap (target) after, the blend preserves the full histogram, not just variance (the Heitz-Neyret operator applied to procedural noise).
master.why_new: Plain lerp of two uncorrelated zero-mean fields has std/sqrt2 at t=0.5, and this is visible around every biome boundary and in all crossfade animation. The fix needs a per-lane sqrt of the fade value, which cannot be done on Fade's internal value from a graph. It is an obvious quality win that I did not see offered in other noise libraries consulted here. Small change, large benefit, so a dedicated option is worthwhile.
master.simd_plan: Inside Fade after interpolation: one InvSqrt and a multiply, under 0.2 ns, no extra source evals. Dimension agnostic because it only touches outputs.
master.continuity: C-infinity in t, because W stays at or above 1/sqrt2. Output continuity equals sources.
master.params: A, B (GeneratorSource); Fade (hybrid 0..1); Correlation rho (float, -1..1, default 0); Mean (float); Smooth Fade (bool).
master.risks:
Variance preservation assumes both inputs have the same variance (scale them first or use CdfRemap to Gaussian); with very different inputs the normalisation slightly over-boosts the transition. Only the second moment is preserved unless the Gaussianise/de-Gaussianise sandwich is used; the full pipeline is 3 nodes.
[ContrastFade, libs-modifiers] Statistically right only for uncorrelated sources of similar variance. Correlated A and B overshoot up to 1.41x, so output can leave [-1,1] (Burley uses a soft-clip for that). Not meaningful when A and B have very different means (flat plain vs mountain), where a Mean per source would be needed. Ghosting persists, only contrast is corrected.
sources: Heitz & Neyret, 'High-Performance By-Example Noise using a Histogram-Preserving Blending Operator', HPG 2018 (variance-preserving blend of Gaussianised textures; cited from memory, not fetched in this task)
master.cost_note: Inside Fade after interpolation: one InvSqrt and a multiply, under 0.2 ns, no extra source evals.
master.variant_notes: Could be an enum on Fade. Full histogram preservation needs the Gaussianise and de-Gaussianise sandwich via CdfRemap.

measured.scalar_note: Almost all source cost (2 x 3 octave fbm + mask Perlin) and map lookups. With compare=1 (plain lerp) the same run measured 445 ns against 424 to 426 ns here, so the InvSqrt did not rise above timing noise.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: Fade + under 0.2 ns

slope-projected-detail.look: Relief: thin strata lines wrap around every hill along its contours and ring the lake basins, fading out on flat tops and floors. Terrain reads as layered sedimentary hills, with no terrace steps cut into the shape. Detail alone: a marbled pattern of nested contour loops following the terrain, with blobs on flats, which is the clearest view of what it does. Tilt=5: bands cross the contours at an angle, giving tilted bedding. Volume: rock with clear horizontal ledges and layers on its side walls; the best 3D image for rock, more convincing than the 2D. Mesa source (cliff=0.85): rough tops and dark walls, whose strata alias to vertical streaks, as the catalogue warned. Cellular detail: almost nothing visible at mixD=0.05, worse than strata.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3, triplanar with y as the strata axis, finite difference slope; z-continuity max 0.038 for dz=1e-3; vol seen
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path

slope-projected-detail.artifacts: Band frequency in plan is kH times slope, so very steep faces alias in a heightfield, seen on the mesa walls. Gentle to moderate slopes are the working range; a kH clamp by 1/s would be needed for cliffs. c0ratio 6.44 is lower than 8 from steep thin bands, not a jump. A finite difference step fd=0.06 keeps the mask from following the finest octave. Rendering at window 8 with 5 or more octaves and low kH hides the bands, so kH=18, along=0.12 and a lower terrain gain matter.
slope-projected-detail.node_shape: SlopeProjectedDetail : Generator. Height (GeneratorSource), Detail (GeneratorSource), Height Scale kH, Detail Scale, Along Scale, Tilt (hybrid), Slope Min and Max (hybrids), Blend Sharpness, Slope Epsilon fd, Mix hybrid onto height, VariableRange.
slope-projected-detail.port_notes: All FMA and Select, no lattice window. 2D is 5 Height taps plus 3 Detail evals; 3D is 7 plus 3; 4D would be 9 plus 4 and was not tried. Pow(k) for k=2 is a square. Bands alone are possible in a graph, using DomainOffset with a hybrid offset on Height, so the value here is the slope gate and per-axis blend, which need a gradient the graph does not have. The 3D strata coordinate is a world axis; in a port offer the up axis as an enum. Overlaps in purpose with the strata-terrace prototype, which steps the height: this one only textures it.
slope-projected-detail.params_text: hf=0.5,oct=4,gain=0.45,kH=18,ds=3,along=0.12,doct=3,smin=0.2,smax=0.5,k=2,mixH=1,mixD=0.06,mixD3=0.18,ky3=0.3,fd=0.06 (these are the code defaults). Tilted bedding: tilt=5. Mesa test source: cliff=0.85. Detail alone: mixH=0,mixD=1

master.one_liner: Triplanar-style cliff texturing for heightfield graphs: on flats the detail is sampled in the plane, on steep flanks it is sampled as a function of (along-contour position, height), so sedimentary strata appear exactly along the contours of steep faces and fade out on flats.
master.look: Proto sheetA m5: blobby detail in the valleys and flats, switching to thin banded layers on steep slopes whose bands follow the iso-height lines (cliff strata), with the transition following the slope mask. Different from anything on the sheet: band orientation is dictated by the terrain rather than by a global axis. Uses: canyon walls, sedimentary cliffs, basalt columns (use a Cellular detail), snow lines (bands at fixed heights).
master.algorithm:
Params: Height (GeneratorSource), Detail (GeneratorSource, 2D-ish texture), Height Scale kH, Detail Scale, Slope Min/Max (hybrids), Epsilon.
2D node: h = H(pos); g = central gradient of H (4 taps);  s = |g|; steep = smoothstep(SlopeMin, SlopeMax, s)
  wx = |g_x| / (s + eps), wy = |g_y| / (s + eps)
  top   = Detail(x * ds, y * ds)
  sideX = Detail(y * ds * 0.5, h * kH)   // face normal mostly +-x: vary along y and with height
  sideY = Detail(x * ds * 0.5, h * kH)
  side  = (wx * sideX + wy * sideY) / (wx + wy + eps)
  out   = Lerp(top, side, steep)  (optionally Add to h with a Mix hybrid)
3D node (volume): planes are the three axis planes of the position, weights |n_i|^k from the gradient of H, which is the classic triplanar blend; the 'height' coordinate is the third axis of each plane.
4D: dimension-agnostic version with D planes; or fall back to the 3D blend on xyz and pass w into the detail.
master.why_new: The graph can almost do it: DomainOffset/AddDimension chains could feed h into a detail's second axis, but the slope-dependent per-axis blend needs the gradient components, three detail evaluations and a normalised blend, i.e. 15+ nodes with a SourceGradient. The node bundles the technique engines use for cliff texturing, which is what people actually want from 'detail where the terrain is steep'.
master.simd_plan: 2D: 1 + 4 taps of Height plus 3 Detail evals; 3D: 1 + 6 + 3; 4D: 1 + 8 + 4. With FBm Simplex x3 height and Simplex detail: 2D ~ 5x4 + 3x1.3 ~ 24 ns, 3D ~ 7x8 + 3x2.6 ~ 64 ns. All Select/FMA, no lattice window.
master.continuity: C0 (proto c0ratio 7.7): smooth weights, continuous taps. The axis-weight normalisation needs the eps floor at |g| = 0 where 'side' is undefined but also unused (steep = 0).
master.params: Height, Detail (nodes); Height Scale kH; Detail Scale; Slope Min / Max (hybrids, so a biome mask can decide where strata appear); Blend Sharpness k for the axis weights; Mix hybrid to add onto the height.
master.risks: Strata density depends on kH times the local slope, so very steep faces get aliased bands; a SuperSample wrap or a kH clamp by 1/s helps. The height coordinate makes strata horizontal in world terms, which is right for sediment but wrong for tilted bedding (add a Tilt param that mixes a world axis into the height coordinate). In 3D the volume version is just triplanar and less novel.
master.cost_note: With FBm Simplex x3 height and Simplex detail: 2D ~ 5x4 + 3x1.3 ~ 24 ns, 3D ~ 7x8 + 3x2.6 ~ 64 ns.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 30.8x perlin2 with finite difference slope, as a generic port would do it (1565 ns vs 50.8 ns: 5 x 4 octave height + 3 x 3 octave detail); 17.8x with the analytic low octave slope (906 ns)
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D about 32 ns on a 4 octave Perlin height and 3 octave Perlin detail; 3D (1 + 6 height taps, 3 detail) about 90 ns

cdf-remap.look: Same fbm shapes with a designed height histogram. Bimodal default: a flat sea floor, sharply defined coastlines, then land rising to mountains. In relief: real looking islands in a flat blue sea from a plain 5 octave fbm, without any mask graph. Uniform target: much higher contrast fbm with large white and black regions, full use of the range (source was -0.50 to 0.54, target -0.98 to 0.99). Beta(0.5,0.5): plateaus and basins with steep connecting slopes, no terraces. Gaussian target on fbm looks identical to the source, as expected, since fbm is already near Gaussian.

dims.3D: works, measured (check, XZ slice); the 2D-calibrated table was used for 3D, and uniform target still gave range -0.977 to 0.907
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D; output-only math, calibration should run in the dimension in use

cdf-remap.artifacts: c0ratio 7.47, max slope 21.9 at the steep coast; continuous. 8 and 16 knots soften the coast and flatten the highest tips, with no hard banding on a 2 octave source; 64 keeps the coast crisp and bright peaks. Peak tops clip into small flat white caps in hillshade at 64 knots on a 2 octave source (probably because the top quantile is a single segment; not verified). Table is calibrated on a fixed seed and goes stale if the source subtree changes.
cdf-remap.node_shape: CdfRemap: Source; Input Distribution enum (Measured, Gaussian, Range); Sigma, Range Min, Range Max; Target enum (Uniform, Gaussian, Beta, Bimodal); Alpha, Beta, Sea Fraction, Separation; Knots (int, 16 to 64); Strength (hybrid). Optional Calibrate Seed.
cdf-remap.port_notes: Gen is two sums of clamped segments with no gathers, tables broadcast from node members. Calibration must happen off the Gen path, with fixed positions, when the source is set, 16384 samples here. Staleness when a child node changes is the unsolved API question in real use: needs a Recalibrate or an editor-driven rebuild. Could become a preset of a spline remap node if that lands. Quantile table costs real time per stage, offer Knots.
cdf-remap.params_text: input=0,target=3,sea=0.62,sep=0.42,knots=64,srcKind=0,octaves=5,freq=0.5,strength=1 (these are the code defaults). Other looks: target=0 uniform, target=2,alpha=0.5,beta=0.5 plateaus

queue.name: CdfRemap
queue.reason: Threshold X means X percent coverage. Start with the analytic Gaussian stage, since Measured mode holds stale state across subtree edits.

master.one_liner: Monotone histogram transform: pushes a source through its (assumed or auto-measured) CDF to a uniform, then through a chosen inverse CDF (Gaussian, Beta(a,b), bimodal hypsometric), so threshold X covers X percent and the height histogram is designed.
master.look:
Same shapes as the source, redistributed tones. Uniform target: flat histogram, every threshold meaningful (coverage = threshold). Beta(0.5,0.5) target: U-shaped histogram, terrain splits into plateaus and basins with steep connecting slopes (two-level look without Terrace's steps). Bimodal hypsometric: Earth-like, most area near two heights (abyssal plain, continental shelf) and little in between: continents with well-defined coasts from any noise. Gaussian target: normalises any weird source (cellular, warped) to a Perlin-like tone distribution.
[Equalize, libs-modifiers] Flat histogram, full contrast regardless of octave count. Look-tested numerically (mode 28, 64-unit window, 3-octave Perlin FBm): source std 0.198-0.202 across seeds; with Sigma 0.207, threshold 0.2 gave mean -0.200 (expected -0.200) and threshold 0.6 gave -0.585 (expected -0.6), so coverage error is about 1% area at the tails.
master.algorithm:
Stage A (to uniform) by InputDist:
  Gaussian: u = 0.5(1+erf(v/(sigma sqrt2)))  (Sigma float, e.g. measured once for Perlin/Simplex/FBm presets)
  Range:    u = clamp((v - lo)/(hi - lo), 0, 1)
  Measured: table q[0..64] of source quantiles computed when Source (or Calibrate Seed/Extent) is set: evaluate the source on 65536 fixed pseudo-random positions in a box of side CalibrateExtent, sort, q[k] = value at rank k/64. At Gen, gather-free piecewise-linear CDF:
     u = (1/64) * sum_{k=0..63} clamp( (v - q[k]) / (q[k+1] - q[k]), 0, 1 )   // 64 FMA + clamp, all lanes same table
Stage B (uniform to target) by TargetDist:
  Uniform: out = 2u - 1
  Gaussian: out = PhiInv(u)/3 (Acklam rational approx, 1 Log + 1 Sqrt in the tails, or central polynomial)
  Beta(Alpha,Beta) / Bimodal(SeaFraction, Separation) / any preset: inverse-CDF table T[0..64] built at param-set time by numeric integration, then gather-free: out = T[0] + sum_k (T[k+1]-T[k]) * clamp(64u - k, 0, 1)
Strength (hybrid): out = lerp(v, out, Strength(x)).
Topology note: the map is monotone, so every level set of the source is a level set of the output; only the value attached to each level set changes.

[Equalize, libs-modifiers] q = 1.702*(Source(p) - Mean) / Sigma; out = 2/(1 + exp(-q)) - 1 (logistic approximation of the Gaussian CDF; same form as ANL's sigmoid node with centre and ramp, but parameterised by distribution). With a flat output, threshold T selects area (1-T)/2. Optional Calibrate() helper outside Gen: evaluate the source at a fixed 4096-point pseudo-random pattern with a fixed seed, and set Mean and Sigma, or fill a 16-knot empirical CDF table for skewed sources (ANL AutoCorrect idea, but producing stored parameters so Gen stays pure).
master.why_new: Users ask for this constantly: gamedev.stackexchange biome-selection answers suggest histogram equalisation, and a Minetest forum thread asks what thresholds divide a world into 3 biomes equally. FN2 #57 asks to normalise to a guaranteed range; #121 and #212 ask about predictable ranges; Godot proposal #11001 asks to expose min and max. No graph has the erf-shaped map; Remap is linear. Could be a preset on SplineRemap if that lands, so judge it after that node exists.
master.simd_plan: Source eval + two 64-segment piecewise-linear evaluations done as sums of clamps (no gathers, tables are node members broadcast per segment): roughly 2 x 64 x 3 ops ~ 1-1.5x Perlin per stage; analytic Gaussian stages are 1 Exp or 1 Log + poly (~0.5x Perlin). Dimension agnostic (GenT). Calibration runs on the scalar/SIMD path once at SetSource time with a fixed seed and positions (deterministic).
master.continuity: Monotone C0 map (piecewise linear tables, C1 for the analytic erf/PhiInv stages); preserves the source's continuity class up to the table knots.
master.params: Source; InputDist enum (Gaussian, Range, Measured); Sigma, Range Min/Max; Calibrate Extent, Calibrate Seed; TargetDist enum (Uniform, Gaussian, Beta, Bimodal); Alpha, Beta / Sea Fraction, Separation; Strength (hybrid).
master.risks:
Measured mode holds state derived from the source subtree: if the user edits a child node after calibration the table is stale (fine in the NodeEditor where the tree is rebuilt, a footgun in the C++ API; needs a Recalibrate trigger or calibrating lazily on first Gen behind a flag). Calibration cost ~65k source evaluations at setup. 64 knots make the output slightly piecewise linear (visible as faint banding in hillshade of smooth sources; use 128 knots or C1 monotone cubic segments if it shows).
[CoverageRemap, distribution-topology] Not automatically updated when the upstream graph changes, so the table can go stale; an editor warning would help. Coverage is exact only for the calibrated law, and finite sampling gives about 1 percent error. Metadata would have 9 extra floats on a small node. Not prototyped since it is a straightforward table; numbers above are design estimates. Hybrid-varying source params shift the law.
master.cost_note: One source eval plus two table stages at about 1-1.5x Perlin each, or about 0.5x Perlin per analytic Gaussian stage.
master.variant_notes: Thresholds as area percent. Calibration must stay off the Gen path, stored as plain members, and goes stale if the subtree changes, so it needs tooling. Measured about 1% area error at tails for the logistic approximation.

measured.scalar_note: Includes a 5 octave fbm source. The source alone measured 293.9 ns; with 64 knot tables 378 to 383 ns; with 16 knot tables 329.4 ns. So the node itself is about 85 ns (1.7 x perlin2) at 64 knots and 35 ns (0.7 x perlin2) at 16 knots, in the gather-free sum-of-clamps form, scalar.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: source + about 1.5 to 3 ns for two 64 knot sum-of-clamps stages

contour-snap-landforms.look: Aggrade: real fans sitting on the chosen contour around each mountain, spilling into the blue valley, with radial grooves, merging in places. In relief they read as seashell or scallop discs: the idea works and is unmistakable, but they look stamped rather than deposited. In gray the discs are visible as round overlapping patches. Excavate: at the earlier scale, rounded amphitheatres cut into mountain flanks with a curved rim wall and a floor with terrain detail, like cirques or calderas; bowls with a small bowl constant give big flat pans. At d=0.85 on the rescaled terrain the carve is subtle. Knife-edge aretes between neighbouring bowls did not appear; bowls rarely overlapped at the densities tried.

dims.3D: runs, measured: real Eval3 with a 3x3x3 window on iso-surfaces of a 3D placement, z-continuity max 0.0077 for dz=1e-3 (aggrade), 0.0011 (excavate). The excavate volume looks like rough fBm rock; no landform reads in it.
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path

contour-snap-landforms.range: -0.954 .. 0.884, mean 0.007 over 8 seeds (aggrade); excavate -0.954 .. 0.884, mean -0.013, c0ratio 7.85
contour-snap-landforms.artifacts: Fans are near circular with regular grooves, which is the unsolved flaw. Fan toes form a short bank where the valley is deep. Reach is limited to 0.75 cell by the 3x3 window, and validity fade plus random size only partly hides the lattice. Before the fine term (df) bowl floors looked like plastic; the fine term fixed this at one extra placement eval. No seams were seen and c0ratio is near 8 in both modes.
contour-snap-landforms.node_shape: ContourSnapLandforms : Generator. Source, Placement Source, Level (float), Mode enum (Aggrade, Excavate), Slope or Bowl (hybrid), Apex Offset, Groove Amount, Groove Warp, Fine Detail, Toe, Lattice Frequency (Feature Scale), Newton Steps int, Jitter, VariableRange.
contour-snap-landforms.port_notes: Candidates are pure functions of the cell: 9 x (Newton steps) x (D+1) placement evals, then cone or bowl per candidate; Min or Max, Select for the clamp. Window bound with jitter 0.5 and clamp 0.5: safe radius 0.75 cell. Toe must exceed the deepest valley below Level or the window edge can show. Atan seam is safe because groove counts are integer per fan. Fine term h - P(p) needs one placement eval at p. To reduce the stamped look, untested: an elongated downhill cone using the placement gradient at the apex, which is already computed.
contour-snap-landforms.params_text: mode=0,d=0.7,hf=0.3,L=-0.03,s=0.14,e=0.06,gr=0.02,gn=10,gw=2,df=0.5,toe=0.8,oct=5,poct=2,ns=1,jit=0.5,clamp=0.5,Rmax=0.75,kS=0.03,amp=1.4 (aggrade fans, the code defaults). Excavate: mode=1,d=0.55,L=0.08,a=0.09,kS=0.015

master.one_liner: Stamps whose apexes snap onto a chosen contour of the terrain, then use Max with a cone for alluvial fans or Min with a paraboloid for cirques, so the terrain itself cuts the landform's outline.
master.look: Aggrade: fans spilling from a mountain front into a valley, merging as bajadas. Excavate: alpine amphitheatres with knife-edge aretes and horn peaks above an elevation line, or sinkholes on a limestone bench.
master.algorithm:
For each lattice cell in the 3x3 window: start at jittered a; evaluate placement source P and its gradient; one or two Newton steps a'=a-(P(a)-L)*gradP/|gradP|^2, displacement clamped to 0.5 cell. Validity v=smoothstep on |P(a)-L|/|gradP| vs max displacement; cells with no nearby contour fade out.
Aggrade mode (fans, talus cones): cone_i(p)=L+e-s*r_i, minus radial distributary grooves, minus a large v-based sink. out=SmoothMax(h(p), max_i cone_i). Uphill the cone lies below the terrain and disappears; in the valley it buries the floor, so the fan's outline follows topography without any angular mask or flow calculation.
Excavate mode (cirques, sinkholes): bowl_i(p)=L+a*r_i^2 (or a superellipse), plus sink for invalid. out=SmoothMin(h(p), min_i bowl_i). Adjacent bowls intersect in sharp curves, which produce aretes and pyramidal horns automatically.
master.why_new: Stamps usually ignore terrain. Here placement comes from any source and the shape is resolved by min/max against it, turning a simulation-looking landform into a few lines of math. A graph cannot place features on a level set.
master.simd_plan: 9 candidates x (dim+1) x Newton steps of Placement evals, plus 1 Source eval. 2D with one Newton step is 27+1 evals. Estimate at a 1-2 octave Perlin placement: 40-80 ns. In 3D and 4D keep the lattice in the XY plane (9 candidates, 4 or 5 evals each) because 27 or 81 candidates is too costly; a full 3D option can place on iso-surfaces at 108 evals. 4D tiling therefore does not hold unless the search goes 4D.
master.continuity: C0 via validity fade, radius cutoff smoothing and SmoothMin/Max. Newton displacement must be continuous across p, which it is since each candidate is fixed per cell.
master.params: Source, Placement Source (often a low-octave version of Source), Level (float), Mode (enum), Slope s or Bowl a (hybrid), Radius (float, must fit window), Groove Amount, Newton Steps (int), Jitter.
master.risks: Not tested. An apex's fade-out may show as pop-in-like shapes when the contour leaves the cell. Max cone radius limited to about 1 cell, so big fans require coarse lattice and sparse density. Mismatch between Placement and full Source can float apexes above or below the visible terrain.
master.cost_note: Estimate at a 1-2 octave Perlin placement: 40-80 ns.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 43.6x perlin2 for aggrade (2161 ns vs 49.6 ns), includes atan and groove noise per candidate; excavate 34.4x (1716 ns); aggrade with 2 Newton steps 68.6x (3416 ns). All with a 5 octave terrain and 2 octave placement.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D with 1 Newton step and analytic Perlin gradients for a 2 octave placement about 25 ns plus 5 ns for the terrain; on a generic placement source (27 evals of 2 octaves) about 65 ns, in line with the catalogue's 40 to 80 ns

feigenbaum-remap.look: Mostly calm gently mottled gray, with sharply delimited patches where the source is high. Each patch is ringed by white and black contour bands that follow its outline, and its core is a dense zebra maze of tightly nested fine lines, a fingerprint look. Hillshade: green rolling land with crinkled dark patches. Relief: smooth low ground with rugged spiky rock outcrops, and the detail really does appear only on the highs. XZ slice and vol: hollow blobs with nested concentric shells on the cut faces, agate or geode like. Start frequency matters most: f2 0.5-1 gives the coherent maze, f2 1.7 gives speckle, f2 4 gives near white noise. N=12 is speckle. Start=0 gives hard black centres, because r=4 from v=0.5 falls to 0 and stays there. avg=1 (mean of the last two iterates) cancels period 2: flat pale ground with thin black ink contours around the patches.
feigenbaum-remap.dims: 2D and 3D measured. A pointwise modifier, so 4D works with any 4D source; no 4D harness run.
feigenbaum-remap.range: -1 to 1, guaranteed by r <= 4 and v in [0,1] if Start stays in [0,1] (0.5 +- 0.2 x noise does). Measured -1.000 to 1.000 over 8 seeds, mean 0.015, 0 NaN. Sharp histogram peak at the calm fixed point.
feigenbaum-remap.artifacts: c0ratio 1.67, max slope 1191: continuous polynomial by construction, but the slope is very high in the core, and at wide view (the 4x panel) the maze aliases into black and white speckle. Relief peaks are spiky. Calm areas keep faint source texture only, the ground is low contrast.
feigenbaum-remap.node_shape: Modifier. Members: Source, R Min, R Span (hybrid), Gain, Iterations, Start (hybrid: constant 0.5 or second source), Start Amplitude, Average Last Two (bool).
feigenbaum-remap.port_notes: Trivial: GenT over the pack, source + N x FNMulAdd, r clamped with Min. Must clamp r at 4 (an FBm source beyond its nominal range would diverge). The Start hybrid is what stops it being a 1D LUT of the source, and it carries the look. Output needs no normalisation in the raw form; avg=1 has measured range -1 to 0.56 and would need a scale.
feigenbaum-remap.params_text: rmin=2.8,rspan=1.5,gain=1.3,N=8,st=0.2,f2=0.8,sf=0.25,oct=4 (all code defaults; source = 4 octave fbm of perlin2, Start = 0.5 + 0.2 * perlin) at --window 12. avg=1 gives the ink contour variant.

master.one_liner: Modifier that iterates the logistic map with growth rate from the source: flat calm where it converges, period-doubling contour rings at the transition, and lacy chaos at peaks, all for a few multiplies.
master.look: Verified in prototype. Plateau-like calm gray areas (fixed point), abruptly hugged by nested ring contours around high regions (period 2,4,8), with white-speckled lace in the cores (chaos). With a perturbed start the lace gets coherent 2D grain. With FBm source: lichen or corroded metal patches with crisp outlines. Good for corrosion, lichen, foam edges, alien coasts, detail masks that only fire at high values.
master.algorithm: r=Min(4, Rmin + (0.5+0.5*Source(p)*Gain)*Rspan); v=0.5 (or Source2-perturbed start: 0.5+0.2*Source2(p)); repeat N (6..12): v=r*v*(1-v). Output v*2-1, range guaranteed because r<=4 and v in [0,1]. Prototype: dyn_lens mode=33,N=8; mode=33,N=12,v0=1,rr=1; mode=33,N=8,oct=4,rr=1.
master.why_new: PingPong and Terrace are regular across the value range; this has three distinct behaviours partitioned by value, from one cheap node. Detail is added selectively where the source is high, with hierarchical contour doubling that no single remap of Remap, Terrace or PingPong gives.
master.simd_plan: Source + N x 2 mul-adds, under 1 ns extra. GenT over pack, all dimensions, trivially tileable. Optional Source2 hybrid. Much cheaper than a fractal for detail creation.
master.continuity: C0 and piecewise polynomial; slope grows like up to 4^N in chaos; N<=12 stays numerically sane. Measured c0ratio 7.7 at N=8 and max slope about 125 per unit, i.e. Lipschitz.
master.params: Rmin, Rspan (hybrid), Gain, Iterations int, Start hybrid (constant 0.5 or second source), Source.
master.risks: High N in chaos is sample-rate dependent aliasing, effectively white in the core. Needs clamp at r=4 or it diverges (hit in test with FBm source, fixed with Min). Its behaviour is a 1D function of value, so it can also be a LUT, but the Start hybrid breaks that and is the better look.
master.cost_note: Source + N x 2 mul-adds, under 1 ns extra.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: the node itself under 1 ns (8 x 2 mul-adds plus clamp), on top of its sources. 7-8 ns with this test graph of a 4 octave fbm and one Start Perlin. Scalar 318.3 ns with Start, 301.2 ns without, nearly all of it source Perlins.

hopf-lax-envelope.look: Better than the catalogue describes. Erode: dark round bowls of very varied size separated by a thin bright web of sharp crests, each bowl at its own depth. Relief reads as a field of craters or bubbles with knife-edge rims. Volume reads as open foam: spherical cavities meeting in sharp edges. Dilate (sweep): pale pillows or cobbles with dark creased joints. Sweep over t morphs from the source at t=0.1 through cells at 0.25 to 0.5. Unlike CellularDistance there is no lattice and cell depth varies, since the cells are the source's own minima. 3 octave sources give smaller cells mixed with big ones and rough webs. K=1 M=3, a single descent from p, gives harder cracked walls for about a quarter of the cost; it has no real min, so its walls are steep slopes from diverging trajectories rather than true creases.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3 with K=7 and M=4, z-continuity max 0.0034 for dz=1e-3, volume seen before the amp and bias change
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path

hopf-lax-envelope.range: -0.873 .. 1.063, mean -0.003 over 8 seeds at the defaults (amp 1.5, bias 0.27, chosen from the raw -0.762 .. 0.528, mean -0.182). Constants depend on t; output shrinks towards the source minimum as t grows.
hopf-lax-envelope.artifacts: Hatch patch of a few pixels on a volume wall, not explained. K=3 uses two opposed ring starts and K=5 and K=7 soften the web progressively compared with K=1; axis bias at K=3 was not checked.
