At large t (1.0) with auto alpha the envelope stays stable, though the web gets fine lumps because M is small for the reduced step. Without auto alpha, t=1 at alpha=0.3 goes chaotic (see discovery).
hopf-lax-envelope.node_shape: HopfLaxEnvelope : Generator. Source (GeneratorSource, gradient capable or finite difference), Time t (hybrid), Sign enum (Erode, Dilate), Starts enum (1, 5 in 2D; 1, 7 in 3D), Iterations int (default 3), Start Radius float, VariableRange.
hopf-lax-envelope.port_notes: Fixed K and M, every lane runs all steps, Min at the end, so there are no per-lane branches. Damped prox step y += alpha*(p - t*grad h(y) - y) makes the stability limit alpha*(1 + t*curvature) < 2, independent of the catalogue's Step; alpha computed from t and an octave weighted curvature bound. With a hybrid t alpha must be per lane, which is one Min and one reciprocal. FastNoise sources have no gradient interface today, so a generic Source needs D+1 extra taps per step, about 3x more evals: K=5 M=3 becomes 60 evals in 2D, so a port wants either a gradient kernel for Perlin and fBm or the K=1 mode with finite differences (12 evals). Range normalisation needs a measured table against t.
hopf-lax-envelope.params_text: t=0.35,sgn=1,K=5,M=3,r=0.45,oct=2,gain=0.4,amp=1.5,bias=0.27,alpha auto (these are the code defaults). Dilate: sgn=-1,bias=-0.27. Cheap: K=1,M=3

master.one_liner: Moreau envelope of a noise: min over y of h(y)+|x-y|^2/(2t), which rounds valleys into parabolic bowls and leaves sharp creases on true ridgelines; the negated form gives pillow cobbles with sharp valleys.
master.look: Verified in prototype, at lower distinctness than the others. Erode t=0.6: crater bowls with sharp crest web between them; t=0.3 with 3 octaves: pits with rough rims. Dilate t=0.3: organically sized cobbles or pillows with creased joints. Small t returns the source. Good for craters, pebbles, cobbles, cushions, semi-eroded terrain.
master.algorithm: Viscosity solution of Hamilton-Jacobi via polished multi-start. For K (5 in 2D) starts y_i = p + r*dir_i plus p itself: repeat M (4..6): g=grad h(y); y -= Step*(g + (y-p)/t). E_i=h(y)+|y-p|^2/(2t). Output Min over i of E_i (erode), or Sign*Min over negated h (dilate). Prototype: dyn_lens mode=8,t=0.3,oct=3,gain=0.4,st=0.08,M=6,r=0.4 and mode=8,t=0.3,sgn=-1,st=0.1,M=6,r=0.4.
master.why_new: Billow via Abs creases at zero crossings; this creases on the true ridge or valley lines of the source (independent of the value level). Cell structure comes from source minima, not a lattice. Morphological erosion normally needs a neighbourhood pass.
master.simd_plan: K*(M+1) gradients: 2D about 25..35 gradients, about 40 ns with analytic Perlin. 3D K=7 about 110 ns. 4D too heavy: reduce to K=4 axis-free starts with a warning. A plain unpolished stencil (K=8..16 source evals with quadratic penalty) is a cheaper quality option at about 10..16 evals.
master.continuity: C0 (Min of continuous functions), with deliberate creases. Each trajectory stays continuous with fixed M.
master.params: Time t (hybrid: amount), Start Radius, Starts int, Polish Iterations, Sign enum (Erode, Dilate), Source.
master.risks: Expensive relative to its look; instability if Step*(1/t + curvature) exceeds about 1 (seen as wrinkles until Step was lowered). Finite K misses far minima at large t, making a slightly lumpy envelope.
master.cost_note: K*(M+1) gradients: 2D about 25..35 gradients, about 40 ns with analytic Perlin. 3D K=7 about 110 ns.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 44.1x perlin2 at the defaults (K=5, M=3, 2 octaves, 2255 ns vs 51.2 ns); 23.3x with oct=1 (1218 ns); K=1 M=3 at 2 octaves 9.8x (544 ns); K=1 M=3 at 1 octave 6.1x (317 ns). Timed before the amp and bias change, which costs nothing measurable.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: with analytic Perlin gradient, 2D K=5 M=3 about 30 ns per octave, K=1 M=3 about 6 ns per octave; 3D K=7 M=4 about 120 ns per octave

stencil-iterate.look: Talus Depth 2 Round: rounded basins with thin bright crests and streaky rippled flanks; relief reads as lakes in eroded hills with scree-like striations, the best result. Laplacian: band-pass speckle dominated by the top octave at any setting tried, not the line-art crease map the catalogue claims; with oct=3, r=0.05 it is a wormy web, nothing better than a high octave of noise. Majority of Mean Depth 2: smooth blobs with flat tops and rounded walls, near what a Remap of a low octave gives. Majority Depth 2 Axis: near-binary phases with hatch artifacts. Erode of Cellular: a rosette of 9 pits at each feature point, the stencil imprint, saved as a discovery. Erode Depth 2 on Cellular: flat-looking discs. Open of a threshold: ghost hatch streaks. Sharpen: plain fine noise. Volume at Talus Depth 2 Axis: rough solid with knobbly walls, little different from fBm.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3, generic stencil; Depth 2 forces Axis in 3D since 27^2 taps is disallowed. z-continuity max 0.0036 for dz=1e-3, vol seen
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path

stencil-iterate.range: -1.008 .. 0.678, mean -0.143 over 8 seeds at amp 1.5 (Talus lowers the mean)
stencil-iterate.artifacts: Axis stencil on Talus Depth 2: diamond shaped basins and a visible grid hatch in the hillshade, so 25 taps is not usable there, and only the Round form at 81 taps looks right. Every Min and Max rule stamps stencil ghosts at sharp features. The ripple on Talus flanks is also stencil imprint, though it happens to look like erosion rills.
stencil-iterate.node_shape: Not its own node. On StencilFilter: add modes Talus (Talus Slope, Amount) and Majority (Gain, Bias). Depth by nesting.
stencil-iterate.port_notes: Rule is a fixed computation on a fixed offset table; Min, Max, Select and a Pade tanh. Depth 2 is a nested table loop. Laplacian uses the mean value form (mean - c)*2d/mean(|o|^2), valid for any symmetric stencil. Depth multiplies cost as |T|^2, which cannot be made cheap for a fractal source; nesting two nodes in the graph costs the same and needs no extra code.
stencil-iterate.params_text: rule=5,rule2=-1,depth=2,stencil=2,oct=4,r=0.18,talus=0.6,k=1,amp=1.5 (Talus, Depth 2, Round stencil, the code defaults). Others: Majority rule=6,rule2=1,gain=4,r=0.3,r2=0.15,oct=5,amp=1. Laplacian rule=0,depth=1,gain=0.11,r=0.05,oct=3,amp=1
stencil-iterate.merged_into: stencil-filter (Talus and Majority as extra modes; Depth 2 is two nested nodes)

master.one_liner: Apply a local rule (Laplacian, mean, erode, dilate, sharpen, talus, majority) over a fixed stencil of source samples, iterated 1-2 times via the evaluation tree, to filter noise pointwise.
master.look: Laplacian of fBm: one-line-wide ridge/valley crease map (negative on crests, positive in troughs), a line-art terrain skeleton. Dilate of CellularDistance: rounded plateaus/pebbles; Erode then Dilate (Depth 2, two rules) removes thin features; Talus on steep fBm: cliffs collapse into angle-of-repose scree slopes; Majority: coarsened two-phase domains with rounded walls. These are classic image filters but applied to resolution-free noise.
master.algorithm:
Stencil T: 2d axis points at +-r (plus centre), or 3^d cube at +-r, chosen by enum; Depth D in {1,2}. Define u_0 = source; u_D(p) = Rule( u_{D-1}(p + t) for t in T ) evaluated recursively with fixed nested loops (|T|^D source evaluations, no state).
  Rules:
    Laplacian : (sum_neigh u - 2d*u_c) / r^2 * gain
    Mean      : average over T
    Erode/Dilate: min / max over T
    Sharpen   : u_c + gain*(u_c - mean)
    Talus     : u_c - k*max(0, (u_c - min_neigh) - talus)        // one thermal-erosion step
    Majority  : tanh(gain*(mean - bias))
  out remapped.
master.why_new: A depth-1 stencil needs 2d+1 offset evaluations plus min/max/sum chains (5-9 nodes per filter in-graph, more with Depth 2), and talus/majority rules need per-lane maths on the stencil values. The node is a general 'local CA step' primitive: any synchronous local update can be run D steps pointwise at |T|^D cost.
master.simd_plan: Nested fixed loops over a precomputed offset table (rebuilt when Stencil/Radius set), each source eval followed by Min/Max/FMA; Majority uses a tanh polynomial. Cost = |T|^D x source: 2D axis depth 1 = 5 evals, depth 2 = 25; 3D 7/49; 4D 9/81. Cube stencil 9/81, 27/729 (3D depth 2 disallowed). Dimension-agnostic; tiles.
master.continuity: Mean/Sharpen/Laplacian: source class minus nothing (Laplacian of C2 Perlin is C0); Erode/Dilate/Talus: C0; Majority: continuous (tanh) but near-step.
master.params: Source, Rule enum, Stencil enum (Axis/Cube), Radius hybrid (sampled at p), Depth int (1..2), Gain/Bias/Talus floats, VariableRange.
master.risks: Depth 2 cost with fractal sources; axis stencil is anisotropic (slight axis bias visible in Laplacian; cube stencil fixes it at higher cost); Talus one step is a cue, not erosion.
master.cost_note: Cost = |T|^D x source: 2D axis depth 1 = 5 evals, depth 2 = 25; 3D 7/49; 4D 9/81.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 295x perlin2 at the defaults (Depth 2 Round, 81 taps x 4 octaves, 14678 ns vs 49.7 ns); Depth 1 Round 38.6x (1937 ns); Depth 1 Round on 1 octave 9.3x (493 ns); Depth 2 Axis, 25 taps x 4 octaves, 97x (4912 ns). The default is above the few microsecond guideline because Depth 2 is the idea.
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: Depth 1 Round about 10 ns on Perlin; Depth 2 Round (81 taps) about 90 ns on Perlin and about 360 ns on 4 octaves; 3D Depth 2 Axis (49 taps) about 110 ns on Perlin

streamline-gullies.look: Relief reads as real mountains: gullies and spurs run straight down the flanks and meet at sharp valley lines, far more convincing than adding the same detail directly, which gives an isotropic worm texture in the side-by-side. Top down, streaks fan out as stars or feathers from each peak and pit. Threshold edges are spiky. stages=2 adds finer rills and a rockier, spikier look. The relief views in this image set were read before the bias fix, which moved the mean from 0.24 to 0.05 and did not change the shape of the streaks in the re-rendered sheet.
streamline-gullies.dims: 2D and 3D measured (the 3D slice shows the same feathery streaks around extrema); 4D not prototyped
streamline-gullies.range: [-1,1] with clamp (8 seeds min -1, max 1, mean 0.037), peaks clip slightly
streamline-gullies.artifacts: Star pattern at every extremum, which looks regular on smooth flow sources. Faint cross ribs on flanks in the first relief. Streaks do not branch, so it is less dendritic than erosion-filter. Clean FFT, continuous (c0ratio 5.44, slope 29).
streamline-gullies.node_shape: Recipe, not a node: Add( F, Multiply( Amp, LineIntegralNoise( Source = ridged Detail, Scalar = F, Mode = Downhill, Weighting = Box, Contrast = sqrt(2k+1) ), slope mask from SurfaceProbe ) ). Nest for stage 2. If a dedicated node is wanted later: Flow, Detail, Steps, Step Length, Decel, Amplitude
streamline-gullies.port_notes: Why merged: by construction this is a Downhill line integral of a detail source with a slope fade, so LineIntegralNoise plus SurfaceProbe already express it. I did not build that graph, so this equivalence is by formula and not by a rendered match. Measured cost 86.54x is well above erosion-filter 24.27x and fractal-slope-aligned 9.18x, which both target slope-aligned terrain detail, so a dedicated node has a weak case despite the good relief. Ridged detail needs a zero-mean offset (0.62 measured here) or the trace lifts all slopes.
streamline-gullies.params_text: k=5,step=0.08,g0=0.35,amp=0.16,ff=0.45,fo=3,fg=0.45,df=3.5,ridge=1,stages=1 (plain render). stages=2,amp=0.14 adds finer rills. show=1 detail term alone, show=2 plain detail for comparison.

master.one_liner: Line integral convolution of a detail noise along the gradient flow of a terrain source, so added detail runs downslope and converges on its own. LIC is known from flow visualisation and slope-aligned gullies from recent erosion filters (both from memory); this form as a node is the variation.
master.look: Streaked flanks radiating from peaks and pits, with cusps where opposing streak fields meet along ridges and valleys. It looks strikingly unlike the isotropic pitted result of adding the same detail directly, which I rendered side by side. Good for mountain flanks, rills, scree chutes and snow streaks.
master.algorithm: Inputs: Flow source F (low octaves), Detail source D (high frequency). v(p)=gradF/(|gradF|+g0), which decelerates near critical points. Trace x+=sgn*step*v(x) for k steps uphill and k steps downhill. Sum D at every step plus D(p), then divide by sqrt(2k+1) to preserve variance. out=F(p)+Amp*LIC*min(|gradF|/g0,1), which leaves flats free of streaks. Choose total trace length near 4-8x the detail wavelength. For plausible multi-scale detail, nest nodes: each stage uses the previous output as Flow, with shorter step and higher-frequency Detail, so finer rills follow slopes created by coarser gullies.
master.why_new: Fractal octaves ignore the underlying slope. Here direction comes from any source graph, with no cell kernel or phase blending, and flow convergence comes from the trajectories themselves. No current node can read a source along a computed path.
master.simd_plan: Dimension agnostic GenT with a fixed k loop and no per-lane branching. Flow evals: 2k*(dim+1); detail evals: 2k+1. For k=7 in 2D that is 42 Flow plus 15 Detail. Estimate with 3-octave Perlin Flow: about 150 ns, about 135x Perlin; k=4 about halves it. Keep Flow cheap. 3D and 4D work directly, and tiling is preserved if the sources tile in 4D.
master.continuity: C0 where Flow is continuous, because deceleration keeps v continuous through critical points. Very steep cusps occur at separatrices.
master.params: Flow Source and Detail Source (GeneratorSource), Steps k (int), Step Length (float), Decel g0 (float), Amplitude (hybrid), Gradient Epsilon (float).
master.risks: TESTED in numpy with spectral noise. First try with unit-length steps and endpoint sampling failed: concentric rings from orbiting maxima, flat per-basin cells. Deceleration, short traces and two-way summation fixed it. Remaining issue: star patterns at every extremum look too regular on simple sources, and the test amplitude was too strong. Cost is the main barrier to using this as a building block.
master.cost_note: Estimate with 3-octave Perlin Flow: about 150 ns, about 135x Perlin; k=4 about halves it.

measured.scalar_note: fo=1 measured 40.15 before the bias fix, stages=2 measured 174.17 before the bias fix. The fix adds no taps. Forward difference gradients throughout.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: k=5 with 3 octave Flow by forward differences is about 110 Perlin taps, ~120 ns in 2D; analytic gradients would bring it to about 60 taps, ~66 ns. 3D about 170 taps ~370 ns

kuwahara-field.look: Patches with near-flat tops and ragged, fairly sharp borders, each at its own height: camouflage or oil paint dabs in gray, chunky mesas in the relief with stepped cliffs and rough tops. At 4x wide view it reads as an irregular stained mosaic of small cells. The XZ slice has the same paint-dab look. The volume gives ragged blobs with rough walls. With the ridged source (src=1, r=0.25) it gives dark rounded pits on a mottled bright field. Threshold topology keeps the large source shapes but with raggy edges.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3 with 25 taps and 12 icosahedral sectors, z-continuity max 0.036 for dz=1e-3, vol rendered
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path, and the catalogue's sparse 25 tap stencil is untested

kuwahara-field.artifacts: Borders have a small polygonal stair from the fixed taps, which reads as part of the painterly look at r about 0.3. At r=0.7 (first sweep) there is a visible axis cross hatch imprint and blur, so r should stay at or below about a third of a feature. c0ratio is 5.6, lower than 8 because of very steep border slopes (max slope 89 per unit), not a jump: the field is a smooth weighted average. Mesa tops keep some of the source's high octave roughness.
kuwahara-field.node_shape: KuwaharaField : Generator. Source (GeneratorSource), Radius (hybrid), Sharpness (int, squarings, default 4), Sectors enum (6 or 8), Epsilon (float), VariableRange.
kuwahara-field.port_notes: One batch of 17 source evals (25 in 3D), then fixed sector sums, Min for vmin, a fixed count of squarings; no branches. Offsets are a fixed table. Inner ring rotated half a step to reduce the star imprint. Range needs a measured constant, since output is a contraction of the source. Hybrid radius sampled at p allows morphing between source and mesa. Keep e above zero to avoid 0/0 in constant areas. Tiling via 4D needs its own stencil.

master.one_liner: Edge-preserving smoothing by sector variance, which steepens flanks and flattens tops. Mesas at independent heights with no global terrace levels.
master.look: Flat-topped patches with organic ragged borders and cliffs, each patch at its own height: mesas, paint-dabs, posterised camouflage, flood-basalt steps. Thresholds are local, so it differs from Terrace, whose levels are global and contour-shaped, and from CellularLookup, whose borders are straight polygon edges.
master.algorithm: Shared taps: centre, ring of N at radius r, ring of N at r/2. For each of N overlapping sectors, take its taps (centre, three consecutive outer, one inner), with mean m_s and variance v_s. Weights w_s = ((vmin+e)/(v_s+e))^q with vmin = min v_s, so values stay in [0,1] with no overflow; q=8 is three squarings. Output sum w_s m_s / sum w_s. Sectors in 3D are defined by directions from a 12-point icosahedral ring.
master.why_new: Local adaptive posterising from any field, with no chosen levels and no cells. Also an oil-paint filter for textures. Not expressible with any existing node since it requires variance comparison across sets of taps.
master.simd_plan: 2D 13 taps (N=6) to 17 (N=8), 3D about 25, 4D about 25 with a sparser stencil. On Perlin about 14-19 / 55 / 108 ns. Sectors share taps, so it is one batch of taps plus fixed sums. Min for vmin; no branches.
master.continuity: C0 for finite q, since it is a smooth weighted average of continuous quantities. Measured c0ratio 7.68. Hard Kuwahara (q large) approaches jumps.
master.params: Radius r (hybrid, about feature size/3), Sharpness q (int power of two), Sample stencil enum, Epsilon e. Hybrid r lets areas morph between original and mesa.
master.risks: Stencil imprint: at larger r and q, borders show a stair or polygon look from the fixed tap directions. 3D and 4D stencils are untested, and sparse stencils may imprint more. Expensive on fractal sources.
master.cost_note: On Perlin about 14-19 / 55 / 108 ns.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 55.6x perlin2 with the 3 octave source (2791 ns vs 50.2 ns); 19.5x with oct=1 (973 ns), i.e. 17 taps of the source
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D about 25 ns on plain Perlin, about 60 ns on 3 octave fBm. 3D (25 taps) about 60 ns on Perlin, about 170 ns on 3 octave fBm

line-integral-noise.look: Contour mode: nested closed flow lines around every extremum, with thin dark separatrices at saddles. Reads as wood grain, agate or fingerprint whorls, with fine even fibres and crisp threshold. Fixed angle: wind-combed streaks. Angle field: fans and petals meeting at cusps. Downhill: star bursts radiating from pits, with visible seams where bursts meet. Value source gives broad high-contrast brush strokes, Perlin gives silky hairlines, and cell white gives a hatched grid inside the streaks, which looked worse. Vol (angle field) shows fibrous tufts and feather-like surfaces. Wide view at the default turns to fine grain, because the source frequency is high.
line-integral-noise.dims: 2D and 3D measured. 3D contour is cross(grad, Up), so it is a stack of 2D flows and the XZ slice is poor (patches of horizontal streaks and plain noise). 3D angle field (yaw and pitch) is fully 3D and is what the vol shows. 4D not prototyped.
line-integral-noise.range: [-1,1] after a measured gain of 4.5 and clamp (8 seeds min -1, max 1, mean 0), roughly Gaussian with a little clipping
line-integral-noise.artifacts: Beading when L*sf is above about 0.6, seen clearly at sf=12, L=0.1. Downhill has steep seams between bursts. Contour shows bright pinched spots at saddles. Cell white source shows lattice hatching, so do not make it the default. FFT has faint rays from long fibres, no lattice dots.
line-integral-noise.node_shape: LineIntegralNoise: Source (GeneratorSource), Direction Mode enum {Fixed Angle, Angle Source, Contour, Downhill}, Angle (hybrid), Scalar (GeneratorSource), Steps (int), Step Length (float), Softening (float), Contrast (float), Weighting {Triangle, Box}, Seed Offset
line-integral-noise.port_notes: Fixed 2K loop of a direction eval and a source eval, no masks. Soft normalisation keeps it close to Lipschitz in the angle modes. Couple Step Length to source scale or warn in the docs. A better 3D contour is t = cross(grad A, grad B) from the gradient-smear entry, which I did not test here. gradient-smear is the cheap sibling, using one direction at p for about 10 taps, and it should be compared with this before both become nodes. The expensive part is the true path, which is what keeps fibres parallel around tight eddies. domain-warp-flow Path Mode Average is one-way and showed step banding; this two-way triangle weighting did not show banding once L*sf was under the limit.
line-integral-noise.params_text: dir=2,src=2,K=10,L=0.05,sf=12,cg=4.5,df=0.5,delta=0.25 (plain render, contour flow). dir=0 combed streaks, dir=1 angle field, dir=3 downhill, src=1,sf=7,L=0.08,K=8,cg=3 broad value-noise brush strokes. Vol: dir=1,sf=8,L=0.07

master.one_liner: Pointwise line-integral convolution: average a high-frequency source along K fixed Euler steps of a direction field (angle source, or the contour/gradient of a scalar source) to get long flow-aligned streaks: brushed metal, wind-combed sand, wood grain around knots, fur.
master.look:
Prototype cl_misc node 1, K=8-12: Source at scale 2-3 along Perlin contours gives closed eddies, agate rings and thin dark separatrix lines; longer L gives combed fibres crossing at saddles. Different from warp since values are integrated rather than displaced. Fur and wind masks, geology bands, painterly strokes, dune streaks.
[FlowFIR, signal-phase] Tested. Box with 8 taps each side gives flowing streaks: silk, feathers, fur tufts, wind-blown sand, with sharp cusps at flow convergence. Very distinct from the warp nodes: warp bends features, whereas this anisotropically smears them along curves while retaining fine cross-flow detail.
master.algorithm:
Inputs: Source (texture), DirectionMode enum: FixedAngle; AngleSource (hybrid angle, 3D: Yaw+Pitch hybrids); GradientOf(scalar GeneratorSource) with sub-enum Downhill (d = -grad/|grad|) or Contour (2D: rotate grad 90 deg; 3D: normalize(cross(grad, Up))). Steps K (int), StepLength L. acc = w0*src(p); q = p; for k in 1..K: d = dir(q); q += L*d; acc += w_k*src(q). Reset q = p; for k in 1..K: d = dir(q); q -= L*d; acc += w_k*src(q). Weights w_k = 1 - k/(K+1) (triangle). out = acc / sum w. Gradient directions by central differences (1+2D evals per step) with |grad| clamped by eps so d never NaNs. Because every lane integrates its own path with a fixed step count the node is pure and stateless.

[StreamlineLIC, dynamics-iteration] Field V = gradient of source A (or curl, or user DomainWarp), unit-normalised softly: u = V * InvSqrt(dot(V,V) + delta^2).
Texture B must be piecewise constant on a lattice (cell-white: rnd11(hash(floor(p*freq)))) with cell size >= 2h so neighbouring samples on one streamline hit the same cells; a continuous White noise would average to mush.
  acc = w0*B(p0); wsum = w0; pf = pb = p0
  for k in 1..N:                                   // forward and backward legs, fixed N each
      pf = pf + h*u(pf); pb = pb - h*u(pb)
      w = hann(k/N)
      acc += w*(B(pf) + B(pb)); wsum += 2w
  out = acc / wsum  (Output Min/Max remap; also 'Contrast' pass: (out - mean)*gain)
Optional Bias direction (constant vector added to V) for combed grain.
master.why_new: van Wijk built spot noise for vector field visualization, and LIC is the pointwise successor. Warp nodes move a sample, they do not smear along a path. A graph would have to nest K warps per side per step, with sharing issues.
master.simd_plan:
Branch-free: 2K iterations of (direction eval + source eval + FMA), all lanes same K. Cost = 2K x (dir + src): K=8, Value source, Perlin angle: ~16 x 1.7 ns ~ 27 ns in 2D (about 7x Perlin, comparable to CellularDistance 3D); gradient-of-scalar mode triples the direction cost. 3D/4D: generic vectors; 4D contour mode undefined, use Downhill or AngleSource. Offer K up to 16.
[StreakFilter, volumetric-3d4d] Modifiers.inl pattern; fixed-count loop of source Gen calls on offset positions (the sources are evaluated at other positions, allowed). Cost N x Source (+ N x direction in Curved mode): with Perlin 3D and N=6 about 15 ns.
master.continuity: Unnormalised velocity: C0, c0ratio 7.94. Normalised velocity (the usual LIC): c0ratio 1.42, real discontinuities along separatrices. So no normalisation, stream length scales with speed, and stagnation zones get less smear.
master.params: Source; DirectionMode; Angle / Angle Sources (hybrid); Scalar Source; Steps K (int); Step Length; Weighting enum (Box/Triangle); Seed Offset.
master.risks:
Expensive; streak length is limited to K*L; Euler drift on curved fields (acceptable visually); users will chain it with fractals and pay octaves x 2K.
[StreamlineSmear, lit-classic] Expensive. If Source frequency is above 1/h, you get beading (seen at fs=6, K=8), so the step must track Source scale. Weak stats with the Potential at high amplitude. Grows with Potential cost. Tileability unverified. Only 2D prototyped.
[StreamlineLIC, dynamics-iteration] The coherence trick fails if StepLen > half a texture cell; near critical points of V streaks degenerate to dots (delta softening); cost grows with N.
sources: Cabral & Leedom, 'Imaging Vector Fields Using Line Integral Convolution', SIGGRAPH 1993 (recalled, not fetched)
from memory, not consulted: Cabral & Leedom 1993 Line Integral Convolution
Cabral and Leedom 1993, Imaging vector fields using line integral convolution (from memory, not consulted)
master.cost_note: Cost = 2K x (dir + src): K=8, Value source, Perlin angle: ~16 x 1.7 ns ~ 27 ns in 2D (about 7x Perlin, comparable to CellularDistance 3D); gradient-of-scalar mode triples the direction cost.
master.variant_notes: Seven proposals of fixed-step LIC. Key findings: unnormalised velocity is needed for C0 (normalised measured c0ratio 1.42); the source feature must exceed the step or it beads; a cell-white texture with cell >= 2 steps gives crisp hairlines; contrast needs a measured gain.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 20 gradient Perlin direction taps at ~1.6x plus 21 Perlin source taps = ~58 ns in 2D; 3D about 2x handbook Perlin ratio, ~125 ns. K=5 halves it

local-phase.look: Harmonic gives labyrinth or brain-coral stripes of roughly even width across the whole image, with small dots at vortex points. The comparison cos(pi*m*S) packs tight rings on big bumps and leaves wide blobs on low ones, so the phase lock clearly works. Triangle looks like a dense fingerprint and is the sharpest of the set. Equalised gives a flat Turing-like labyrinth with all peaks the same height. AM/FM lets a second noise fade the stripes to grey across regions. Vol with m=3 gives nested sheet shells, and Equalised gives smooth caves. Envelope is a soft blob field with faint axis-aligned cell lines.
local-phase.dims: 2D and 3D measured; 4D not prototyped (only |g| matters, so the formula is unchanged)
local-phase.range: -0.955..0.956 over 8 seeds in Harmonic, so nearly full range without a remap; histogram piled at both ends like a cosine
local-phase.artifacts: Lattice shows in the extra analysis modes: Teager has a clear axis grid on Perlin and GradMag and Envelope have faint grid lines, because Perlin's gradient structure follows its lattice. Harmonic does not show it visibly. NewtonDistance has jagged white crests where the gradient is small. fbm with 3 octaves goes rough, as the catalogue warned. In the 3D slice some bands widen into blobs where amplitude is low. Omega changes band width (2 thinner, 4.5 wider) and does not break anything.
local-phase.node_shape: LocalPhase: Source (GeneratorSource, narrowband), Mode enum {Harmonic, Equalised, Envelope, Triangle, Saw}, Harmonic m (int), Carrier Omega (hybrid), Sample Distance h, Vortex Fade, optional Amplitude Source for AM/FM. Leave GradMag, Laplacian and Slope to surface-probe, and do not ship Teager on Perlin.
local-phase.port_notes: No masks and no atan: Chebyshev recurrence over a fixed m, Sqrt, FMA. Everything is continuous by measurement. Omega is a per-source constant, about 2.5 to 3 for Perlin and about 6 for simplex in this harness. Compare with eikonal-stripes when that result exists: this one locks band count in phase and is not constant width in world units. Should get an fnlab seams pass at the vortex points.
local-phase.params_text: mode=0,m=7,omega=2.5,h=0.03,fade=0.05,e=0.01,oct=1 (plain render, Harmonic). mode=1 Equalised; mode=3,m=5 Triangle; mode=8,m=5 AM/FM; mode=2 Envelope; mode=9 is the cos(pi*m*S) comparison

master.one_liner: Demodulate a narrowband noise into local amplitude and phase from its value and gradient, then rebuild it with any wave shape or harmonic.
master.look:
Harmonic output gives fingerprint or brain-coral stripes with a fixed number of bands between every crest and trough, everywhere, regardless of local amplitude. Equalised gives a contrast-flattened Turing-like labyrinth. Envelope gives a smooth slowly varying blob field. Good for agate, wood ring bands, topographic line art, coral, and contrast-normalised masks.
[LocalPhase, distribution-topology] Flat: inflated Perlin in which all peaks have equal height, and every peak and trough is reachable at a high threshold. Multiplied m=5: equal-amplitude nested contours, closer to fingerprint than PingPong. A much cheaper relative of EikonalStripes. Good for equal-height dune or wave fields and cheap contour stripes.
[MonogenicFilter, signal-phase] GradMag of Perlin: cell-like web of bright creases; NewtonDistance + Oscillator: contour hatching with equal spacing and fingerprint-like convergence at saddles; MonoAmplitude: soft positive blobs where the noise is 'loud', zero where it is flat; MonoPhase cos(m.): nested ring sets inside each bump (tree-ring blobs, lichen); Teager: etched, embossed texture energy; Slope: directional hillshade that can be used as a mask (windward/lee). Uses: erosion masks from curvature, hatching, SDF-ish blending of noises, orientation fields for stripe nodes.
master.algorithm:
Treat S locally as A cos(phi) with carrier Omega: A = sqrt(S^2 + |g|^2/Omega^2), x = cos(phi) = S/(A+e). g comes from the simplex stencil, and the Teager-Kaiser form sqrt(|g|^2 - S lap S) can estimate A*Omega from the same taps. Outputs: Envelope (A), Equalised (x, all peaks equal height), Harmonic m = T_m(x) via Chebyshev recurrence t2 = 2x*t1 - t0 (no atan needed), Triangle or Saw (polynomial acos of x, then a wave shape). Multiply by A/(A+e2) to fade phase vortices. Optional second source: amplitude of B with phase of A (AM/FM).

[MonogenicFilter, signal-phase] Evaluate source at p and p +- h*e_i (1+2D evals; h float param). g_i = (s+ - s-)/(2h); lap = sum(s+ + s- - 2s)/h^2; G = |g|. Mode enum: GradMag = G; Laplacian = lap; Slope = dot(g, dir) with dir from fixed angle or Hybrid angle (lighting-like shading baked as a value); NewtonDistance = clamp(s / max(G, Gmin), -Dmax, Dmax) (first-order signed distance to the source's zero level set; stripes from Oscillator on it have constant width because |grad| ~ 1 near the zero set); MonoAmplitude = sqrt(s^2 + G^2/k0^2) with k0 = 2pi/CarrierWavelength (envelope of a narrowband source: the Riesz/monogenic magnitude); MonoPhase = atan2approx(G/k0, s) mapped [0,pi] -> [-1,1], or cos(m*phase) with int Harmonics m (each bump of the source is split into m nested rings of equal PHASE spacing, so ring width stays constant for a narrowband source); Orientation = atan2approx(g_y, g_x)/pi (2D; 3D returns azimuth, feeds PhasorNoise direction); Teager = max(0, G^2 - s*lap) (AM-FM energy, works on broadband sources); Hessian det (2D) via 4 extra diagonal taps as an optional Curvature mode (ridge/valley line detector).
master.why_new: Sin or PingPong of a value gives a ring count proportional to local amplitude, with spacing bunched on slopes and dead zones where the amplitude is low. Here band count and contrast are locked by phase, and the spacing tracks the carrier and not the slope. A graph cannot do this because it needs the gradient. It also extracts an amplitude envelope from a single noise, which no existing node does.
master.simd_plan: D+2 taps (4/5/6), or D+1 when h is small and the stencil mean stands in for S. About 4.4/11/26 ns on Perlin (scalar prototype 4.7x perlin2 including atan2, which the Chebyshev port removes). m Chebyshev steps with int m are a fixed loop. Dimension agnostic because only |g| matters.
master.continuity: C0 away from isolated vortices where S and g vanish together; there phase is undefined and the amplitude fade makes it continuous. Harmonic bands are steep at high m (measured c0ratio 2.0-2.8, slope about 400 per unit), which I read as narrow bands plus the vortex points. Needs confirming in fnlab.
master.params: Carrier Period (hybrid; constant per source type, Omega^2 about 9 per feature unit for Perlin), Mode enum, Harmonic m (int for Chebyshev; a hybrid float would need the acos path and costs a little more), Sample Distance h. Epsilon e.
master.risks:
Assumes a narrowband source. Single-octave Simplex or Perlin is ideal, and three-octave fBm still worked with a higher Omega but looked noisier. A wrong Omega skews band spacing without breaking anything. Lattice directionality of Perlin may show more clearly once amplitude is equalised.
[LocalPhase, distribution-topology] Assumes a narrowband source; broadband fBm gives rough output. Cusps show in hillshade as small pinch points at extrema. Band spacing is equal in phase, not in world units, so EikonalStripes is the one to choose when spacing must be constant. Only tested at 1 octave in 2D.
[MonogenicFilter, signal-phase] Central differences on a fractal source are noisy for small h (h must be ~1/4 of the finest feature). Monogenic amplitude/phase are only meaningful for narrowband sources (single octave or Phasor); document. Multiple source evaluations multiply cost: GeneratorCache does not help because positions differ.
sources: Felsberg & Sommer, 'The Monogenic Signal', IEEE TSP 2001 (recalled, not fetched)
Maragos, Kaiser, Quatieri, Teager-Kaiser energy operator, IEEE TSP 1993 (recalled, not fetched)
master.cost_note: About 4.4/11/26 ns on Perlin (scalar prototype 4.7x perlin2 including atan2, which the Chebyshev port removes). m Chebyshev steps with int m are a fixed loop.
master.variant_notes: Monogenic demodulation of narrowband sources. Chebyshev harmonics avoid atan. MonogenicFilter adds Teager energy and orientation outputs.

measured.scalar_note: Harmonic with 5 taps central differences. Triangle m=5 with polynomial acos measured 6.51.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 5 / 7 / 9 Perlin taps, ~6 / 16 / 39 ns for 2D / 3D / 4D; a D+2 stencil would cut this to about 4.4 / 11 / 26 ns as the catalogue says

repose-morph.look: On a smooth 2 octave source with the cone: rounded mounds with concentric lobed halos on their flanks and thin dark crease valleys; the hillshade is bumpy and weathered, not clean talus. Erode (first sweep and relief) gives broad basins with thin bright rims. On a source reshaped into sharp sparse peaks (peak=1.5), Dilate does not give aprons: every peak turns into a cluster of about 16 ghost lobes, in gray and in relief. Paraboloid and flat structures at 2 octaves show the same stencil as a strong honeycomb or scale pattern, saved as a discovery.

dims.3D: works, measured: real Eval3 with two shells of 14 directions, z-continuity max 0.0019 for dz=1e-3, XZ slice seen
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path

repose-morph.range: -0.541 .. 0.780 over 8 seeds, mean 0.077 (dilate raises the mean; needs a measured constant)
repose-morph.artifacts: The stencil imprint is the main result. 17 taps resolve a cone only where the source hill is wider than the tap spacing, so the claimed world-space slope limit holds at the tap points only. Threshold shows a lobed flower outline around one blob. Close and Open look busier, with double contour lines, and at 81 taps they cost 125x Perlin.
repose-morph.node_shape: Not its own node. On StencilFilter: Slope (hybrid), Structure enum (Cone, Paraboloid, Flat) applied as a per-ring constant in Dilate and Erode. Close and Open by nesting two nodes.
repose-morph.port_notes: Per-ring penalty is a constant, so the addition to a Min/Max stencil is one Add per ring. The 3D look test nests Close at 7 x 29 taps, which is a test only. Source should be low octave, with detail added after the node (detA here). Honest reason for merged instead of promising: the distinct promise (angle of repose) is not delivered by a sparse stencil, and what is delivered is a parameter on the stencil-filter idea.
repose-morph.merged_into: stencil-filter (a Slope penalty and Structure enum on its Dilate and Erode modes)

master.one_liner: Grey-scale morphology by a cone on a fixed stencil of source samples: enforces an angle of repose, builds talus and fills valleys, for any source. Morphology is standard in image processing; as a slope-parameterised terrain node it is the variation.
master.look: Fixed-angle talus aprons around peaks, sharpened inverted cones in pits, flat alluvial lowlands when closed, broad plateaus from opening. The surface looks weathered, with sharp creases where slope limits meet.
master.algorithm: Stencil: 2 rings of 8 offsets, the outer ring rotated by 22.5 degrees, with radii r1 and r2. Dilate: out=max(h(p), max_i(h(p+o_i)-S*|o_i|)), so peaks grow into cones of fixed slope S. Erode: out=min(h(p), min_i(h(p+o_i)+S*|o_i|)), so pits widen into V-cones and ridges narrow. Fill (closing approximation): erode a dilated result by nesting two nodes, or use a built-in 8x8 form. Paraboloid structure function option: S*|o|^2 for rounded hillslope results. Flat structure option (S=0) gives flat plateaus and flat valley floors. Put detail octaves after this node rather than before.
master.why_new: All existing modifiers are per-value, so none can use neighbours. A node that compares samples at other positions can enforce a world-space slope, which Remap, Terrace or blends cannot do.
master.simd_plan: Fixed 17 evals with Min/Max, no branches; 2D, 3D or 4D offsets (plane stencil or a 14-direction 3D stencil at higher cost). Closing with an 8-point stencil is 64+ evals. Estimated 17x source cost single-op. Tiling is preserved only if offsets are applied in native position space, and in 4D torus mode they do not correspond to plane offsets, so verify.
master.continuity: C0: Min and Max of continuous fields.
master.params: Source, Op (enum Dilate, Erode, Open, Close), Slope S (hybrid), Radius r1, r2, Structure (enum Cone, Paraboloid, Flat).
master.risks: Not tested. Sparse stencils give octagonal cones and miss features smaller than the stencil spacing, so only low-octave input is reliable. Fixed-position sampling gives visible stencil patterns on high-frequency sources. Costly when nested.
master.cost_note: Estimated 17x source cost single-op.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 37.5x perlin2 at the defaults (2 octave source, 1999 ns vs 53.3 ns); 16.4x with oct=1 and no detail (868 ns), which is the 17 taps; Close (81 taps) 125x (7616 ns)
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D single op about 20 ns on Perlin, about 40 ns on 2 octave fBm; Close about 180 ns on 2 octaves. 3D single op (29 taps) about 65 ns on Perlin

slope-blur.look: Grey view: hammered slate or dried leaf plates, with sharp curved creases between facets and smooth gradients inside each. Mean is softer and pillowy with streaks, Min and Max give flat dark or pale chips, and Contour gives smeared inky swirls close to line integral noise. In hillshade and relief the facets show concentric ribs from the discrete path samples, so the relief reads as ribbed staircase hills, which is not a usable terrain. Length 2 turns plates into ripple-filled cells. The vol was rendered but not inspected.
slope-blur.dims: 2D and 3D measured (3D slice shows the same plates); 4D not prototyped
slope-blur.range: Min gives -0.88..1 over 8 seeds with the offset and gain above, mean 0; needs a measured remap per mode
slope-blur.artifacts: Step ribs in every gradient mode, strong in Min and Max and visible in hillshade even though the grey looks clean. N=12 reduces but does not remove them. Near-jumps across watersheds (c0ratio 1.68, slope 786). eps=2 restores Lipschitz (7.34, slope 46) but loses most of the reach, per the catalogue warning.
slope-blur.node_shape: Path Mode {Average, Min, Max} on DomainWarpFlow, with a separate Source read along the path. No separate node.
slope-blur.port_notes: Same fixed step loop as domain-warp-flow, whose prototype already has Average, Min and Max path modes in its code even though its node shape lists only End and Average, so add Min and Max if this look is wanted. Contour Mean is a one-way line-integral-noise. Use as a stylised filter on low-frequency sources only, not as height.
slope-blur.params_text: N=10,mode=1,dirm=0,len=0.7,sf=2,so=3,ff=0.8,fo=1,eps=0.2,gain=1.6,off=0.2 (plain render, gradient Min). mode=2,off=-0.2 Max; mode=0,off=0 Mean; dirm=1 Contour

master.one_liner: Substance's Slope Blur made pointwise: walk N fixed steps along a flow map's gradient or contour and accumulate a source, giving smeared leaks, chipped facets, or silky line-integral swirls.
master.look: Short length: rust and dirt smears following a surface. Long along-gradient: paths converge on extrema, so catchment basins go flat and give leaf-like faceted plates with crisp borders (a pointwise watershed look). Contour mode on fine noise: silky hair and wood flow (LIC). Prototype: dcc_lens mode=13.
master.algorithm: q=p; acc=0; mn=+inf; mx=-inf. for i in 0..Samples-1 (constant): m=Flow(q); g_a=(Flow(q+e*axis_a)-m)/e; g=g/Sqrt(dot(g,g)+Eps); if Contour: 2D g=perp(g) (3D: cross with a fixed member axis); v=Source(q); acc+=v; mn=Min(mn,v); mx=Max(mx,v); q+=g*Length/Samples. Output by Mode: Mean acc/Samples, Min mn, Max mx.
master.why_new: Substance users rely on this for worn edges; nothing here integrates along a field. Domain warp moves a sample once; this averages along a streamline. The basin-partition look, organic cells whose borders follow valleys of a noise, is not reachable another way.
master.simd_plan: Samples x ((dim+1) x Flow + Source). Samples=8 with Perlin flow and Perlin source: about 35 / 88 / 190 ns (30x+ Perlin). Justified only as an effect node. Keep Flow cheap; analytic Perlin-derivative path cuts a lot. Everything is per-lane position math, so no masks needed.
master.continuity: Effectively discontinuous across ridges of the flow map since paths diverge exponentially. Measured c0ratio 1.09-1.5 even with soft normalisation, and unnormalised stepping (remove the /Sqrt) keeps it Lipschitz at some loss of reach. Treat as a stylised filter, not a displacement source, without smoothing.
master.params: Source, Flow (GeneratorSource), Samples (int), Length (hybrid), Mode enum, Direction enum (Gradient, Contour), Eps (float), Epsilon step (float).
master.risks: Expensive and not C0. Substance's docs warn the slope input must be smooth. FD precision at far coords. A sibling lens has a flow-blur variant, so may overlap; the basin look is the part to keep.
master.cost_note: Samples=8 with Perlin flow and Perlin source: about 35 / 88 / 190 ns (30x+ Perlin).

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 10 steps x (3 Flow + 3 Source octaves) = 60 Perlin taps, ~66 ns in 2D; 3D 70 taps ~154 ns; 4D 80 taps ~344 ns

adhesion-web.look: ShockWeb in 2D: a clean thin bright network of curved lines with triple junctions, widely varied cell sizes and one near-circular cell; reads as cracks or a cosmic web, and the lines curve in a way Cellular F2-F1 edges do not. Line brightness varies and some lines fade out before they join. Transport in 2D: thick scaly clumps and pebbles, gray and hillshade both striking. Displacement at nu=0.01: hard edged camouflage plates with stripes and dark outlines, caused by tap discretisation but very attractive (saved as a discovery). Potential: rounded valleys with creased crests, softer and less clear than hopf-lax-envelope. 3D ShockWeb volume at K=33 to 48: scattered blobs, some joined, not foam sheets. 3D Transport volume: mostly solid with small irregular holes; nothing special. 2 octave source web: finer, messier crack network, worse than 1 octave.

dims.3D: runs and is continuous (z-continuity max 0.0158 for dz=1e-3), but the look fails: isolated blobs instead of sheets
dims.4D: not prototyped; the harness has no 4D path

adhesion-web.range: -1.0 .. 1.0 by clamp; ShockWeb mean -0.923 over 8 seeds (mostly black, thin lines). Transport mean 0.005, c0ratio 7.79.
adhesion-web.artifacts: Without floor, a dim secondary mesh between neighbouring taps fills the cells at K=24 to 48. floor removes it, at the cost of fading the weakest true shock lines. Plates at small nu come from the same discretisation. In 3D the tap spacing is about half of R at K=33, too coarse to resolve sheets.
adhesion-web.node_shape: AdhesionWeb : Generator. Source, Transport Target (optional source), Time t (hybrid), Reach R (hybrid), Viscosity nu (hybrid), Taps enum (19, 32, 48), Output enum (ShockWeb, Potential, Displacement, Transport), Web Gain and Floor, VariableRange.
adhesion-web.port_notes: Fixed tap table, one Min pass, K Exp and one weighted sum, no branches. floor should scale with 1/K, since tap line variance is about (spacing/2)^2; measured defaults 0.04 at K=32. Exp dominates beside the source; a cheap polynomial Exp on (E-Emin)/nu, clamped, is enough. Unsolved flaw: 3D. Untested idea for 3D: reuse hopf-lax-envelope's polished starts and output the gap between the two lowest E, which needs no dense ball. Hopf-lax-envelope covers Potential better; the unique outputs here are ShockWeb, Transport and Plates.
adhesion-web.params_text: out=0,K=32,t=0.25,R=0.9,nu=0.05,floor=0.04,wg=10,oct=1 (ShockWeb, the code defaults). Transport: out=3,nu=0.02. Plates: out=2,nu=0.01. Potential: out=1,nu=0.02,oct=2. Vol image: K3=48,floor3=0.02,nu=0.06, --iso -0.7

master.one_liner: Full-dimensional Hopf-Lax over a disc of taps with Boltzmann weights, which gives shock webs and pebbled transport from any field.
master.look: ShockWeb: thin bright curved network with very varied cell sizes, like the cosmic web in the adhesion model. Potential: rounded valleys with creased crests, ridged but with a different topology from FractalRidged. Transport: pebbled, scaly clumps. Displacement: camouflage-like plates caused by tap discretisation.
master.algorithm: Tap set e_k: Vogel disc, K=19 in 2D, Fibonacci ball K about 33 in 3D. E_k = S(p+e_k) + |e_k|^2/(2t). w_k = exp(-(E_k-Emin)/nu). W = sum w_k, mean e = sum w_k e_k / W. Outputs: ShockWeb = (sum w_k |e_k|^2/W - |mean e|^2)/R^2 (Boltzmann variance, peaks where two distant minima tie); Potential = Emin - nu log W (soft Moreau envelope with smooth hollows and sharp creases); Displacement = |mean e|; Transport = sum w_k T(p+e_k)/W (each point reads a second field near the minimum it collapses onto).
master.why_new: Unlike SlopeSlide it is a global-in-window search, so it can jump across a small hill and report real competition between basins, which gives actual shock lines. Gets a variable-size cell network out of a noise, with transport of a second field across cells, which no combination of existing nodes can do.
master.simd_plan: K taps + K Exp, K=19/33/about 50: Perlin about 35/100/300 ns; 2D and possibly 3D only as a practical choice, and 4D is expensive. 4D falls back to fewer taps with more artifacts. Fixed tap tables, one Min pass, one weighted sum.
master.continuity: C1 for nu>0 with a smooth source, though the web lines are steep. Tap discretisation creates plates when nu is small against tap spacing.
master.params: Time t (hybrid), Reach R (hybrid), Viscosity nu (hybrid), K enum, Output enum, Transport Target.
master.risks: Stencil imprint is real and blotchy line brightness is visible in the prototype. The 2D look is promising but may need K of 30+ for clean lines. SlopeSlide gets many of the same looks at a fifth of the cost, so ship this only if the Transport and Web outputs prove their worth.
master.cost_note: K taps + K Exp, K=19/33/about 50: Perlin about 35/100/300 ns; 2D and possibly 3D only as a practical choice, and 4D is expensive.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 31.5x perlin2 at K=32 on a single octave source (1580 ns vs 50.1 ns); K=19 gives 21.2x (1063 ns)
measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 2D K=32 about 50 ns on Perlin including 32 Exp, 3D K=33 about 110 ns

blue-noise-scatter.look: Isolated round domes with even spacing: no overlapping pairs, no clumps, with some open gaps. The threshold panel shows clean separate disks. FFT shows soft concentric rings around the central peak; I did not view the FFT of raw jitter for comparison. Raw jitter at the same density has obvious touching pairs and bare patches side by side, a clear difference. In 3D the isosurface is a cloud of separate spheres. Soft spacing fills gaps with graded sizes but also leaves very small flecks, so it looks less clean than the hard mode. The relief was rendered and saved but not viewed.

dims.3D: works, measured (check, XZ slice, vol)
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D; 256 hashes and 16 x 80 tests would need axis neighbours only

blue-noise-scatter.artifacts: None seen in hard mode. One-round thinning leaves occasional larger gaps than a maximal Poisson set. Stamps barely touch at R = 0.43 and spacing 0.85 only because R <= Spacing/2; a larger R overlaps. Soft mode max slope 69.9 per unit from very small stamps.
blue-noise-scatter.node_shape: BlueNoiseScatter: Spacing (float, clamped to 2 - Jitter), Stamp Radius (<= 0.5 cells), Radius Variation, Height Variation, Profile enum (Dome, Cone, Coin), Soft Spacing (bool), Density (hybrid read at the candidate), Output enum (Height, Distance). Later, a Source to stamp, if merged with stamp-scatter.
blue-noise-scatter.port_notes: 2^d candidates are enough because R <= 0.5, each tested against its 3^d neighbours, 4^d unique hashes. Completeness proof differs from the catalogue: two candidates two cells apart are at least 2 - Jitter apart, so Spacing <= 2 - Jitter is exact with the 3^d test, not 1 - Jitter. Blockers ignore density, so density changes never flicker survivors, at the price of a lower effective density. Could be a Spacing option on stamp-scatter rather than a separate node; the thinning code is identical.
blue-noise-scatter.params_text: cells=1.5,jitter=1,spacing=0.85,R=0.43,rvar=0.2,hvar=0.35,soft=0,shape=0,dens=1,densn=0 (these are the code defaults); vol uses --iso -0.5 --window 5. Other images: spacing=0,dens=0.5 raw jitter at equal density; soft=1,R=0.5,rvar=0; densn=1,dens=0.6

master.one_liner: Scatter whose candidate stamps are thinned pointwise into a Poisson-disk-like set: a candidate survives only if no higher-priority candidate in its own neighbourhood lies within the spacing radius, computed from hashes alone, so stamps never overlap and spacing looks even.
master.look:
Isolated dots with even spacing and no clumps (prototype 'thin' vs 'raw' clearly different: raw jitter has near-touching pairs and holes). Density field varies count smoothly and dots stay whole. Sparse star fields, tree masks, ore seeds, crater centres.
[BlueNoiseScatter, stamp-scatter] Evenly spaced, non-overlapping stamps: polka dots, leopard rosettes, pebbles in a creek bed, trees seen from above, acne/pore patterns, bubbles, lily pads, with the characteristic blue-noise regularity of nature instead of the clumpy jittered-grid look (plain Scatter has frequent near-collisions and bare patches). Soft Spacing gives graded sizes that fill the plane like a packed pebble bed.
master.algorithm:
For each candidate cell c in the sample's 2^d window: f(c), priority pr(c) = rnd01(hash(c)). Survival test: for each neighbour n of c in c + {-1,0,1}^d, n != c (fixed loop): dead |= (pr(n) > pr(c)) & (|f(n) - f(c)| < Spacing) & present(n). This is Matérn type II hard-core thinning on a jittered grid, evaluated independently per candidate, so it is stateless: the same c always gets the same answer from any sample point. Then the surviving candidates are stamped exactly as in Scatter (local frame, per-stamp seed, source eval or analytic stamp, combine). Spacing <= 1 - Jitter guarantees that checking only the 3^d neighbourhood is complete.
Optional Soft Spacing: instead of killing, shrink: s *= smoothstep(0, Spacing, nearest higher-priority distance), so stamps shrink rather than vanish near a dominant neighbour (no popping, denser fill).
The unique cells touched are the union of candidates' neighbourhoods: 4^d (2D 16, 3D 64, 4D 256) hashes + feature points; hashing is cheap compared with source evals, and only the 2^d survivors are stamped.

[PoissonScatter, repo-demand] One candidate per cell: position x (uniform in the cell) and priority a from hash. Survival rule, one round of Luby-style independent set: keep candidate i iff a_i < Density(x_i) (density reject) and no other candidate j with priority a_j > a_i lies within Rmin of x_i. Rmin<=1 cell means the neighbours fit a 3x3 around each candidate. Sample evaluation: 3x3 candidates around p, each tested against its own 3x3, so 5x5 unique hashes in 2D. Output: Profile(F1/Radius) as a compact smoothstep, or F1 distance, or hash-value per point.
master.why_new: godot-proposals #9690 asks for point placement inside FastNoiseLite for rocks, twigs, ores and trees, with fixed positions across runs; a maintainer suggests Poisson. Current workaround is noise threshold, hard to tune, clumped, and can cut features in half. Voxel Tools describes rehashing neighbour blocks by hand to place trees. CellularDistance can't drop points or guarantee spacing. Only a small hash window is needed: this makes a global-looking algorithm local.
master.simd_plan:
2D: 25 hashes into arrays, 9x8 distance compares (pairs could share), masks ANDed, then F1 over survivors with Select. Estimated AVX2: 15 to 20 ns, about 4x CellularDistance; scalar not benchmarked. Density hybrid at candidates: 9 evaluations if blockers skip density check (blockers then always block, slightly lower density, no flicker) or 25 for exact. 3D: 125 hashes, 27x26 compares, about 60 to 90 ns; cut to 6 face neighbours if needed. 4D impractical: thinning disabled, jitter only.
[BlueNoiseScatter, stamp-scatter] Hash + feature point for 4^d cells (2D 16 x ~15 ops), 2^d x (3^d - 1) distance tests (2D 4 x 8 = 32 tests x ~8 ops), then the normal Scatter stamping of 2^d candidates with the dead mask folded into presence. 2D ~+2 ns over Scatter, 3D +~10 ns (64 hashes, 8 x 26 tests), 4D +~60 ns (256 hashes, 16 x 80 tests), so 4D should offer an 'axis neighbours only' reduced test. Fully branch free; loop counts fixed.
master.continuity: Continuous: survival is a property of the candidate alone (density read at the candidate, not the sample), so no flicker across space. Profile output C1 with compact support. Distance C0 like F1.
master.params: Everything in Scatter plus Spacing (0..1-Jitter), Soft Spacing bool, Density hybrid (still at stamp centre; density thinning composes with hard-core thinning).
master.risks:
Matérn II thinning loses ~30-40% of candidates at Spacing near 1, so maximum achievable density is lower than Scatter's; expose that. 4D cost. The 3^d neighbourhood completeness proof depends on the Spacing clamp, which must be enforced in the setter.
[PoissonScatter, repo-demand] One round leaves gaps compared to maximal Poisson disk, though prototype looks good. 3D and 4D costs high. Radius has to stay in the 3x3 window. Hybrid density evaluated at other positions multiplies cost.
master.cost_note: Estimated AVX2: 15 to 20 ns, about 4x CellularDistance; scalar not benchmarked. 3D: 125 hashes, 27x26 compares, about 60 to 90 ns; cut to 6 face neighbours if needed.
master.variant_notes: Matern II thinning from hashes alone. PoissonScatter gives the demand evidence (rocks, trees, ore; godot-proposals 9690) and its density-at-candidate rule avoids flicker.

measured.scalar_note: The scalar loop rehashes shared cells (36 hashes). A port shares 16 unique hashes in 2D. With densn=1 measured 10.69 because the prototype reads a Perlin density at each of 4 candidates.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, not measured: 2D about 15 to 20 ns, 3D about 60 to 90 ns (64 hashes, 8 x 26 tests); 4D needs a reduced neighbourhood

cellular-facet.look: Oblique relief: tilted polygonal slabs jutting out of the ground at different angles, like shattered basalt or rubble, and every slab's tilt comes from the source's real slope there, so slabs still follow the larger landforms. Gray shows angular gem-like cells with a bright edge against a dark one. Hillshade reads as a paved floor of chips with dark cracks. Slope 0 is plain CellularLookup with flat cells; Slope above 1.5 gets noisier with less landform. soft=4 rounds the cell borders into pebble-like stones. The 3D isosurface at iso 0 is mostly solid with chipped angular crystal cavities. It is not connected low-poly: the planes do not meet, so there are cracks.

dims.3D: works, measured (check, XZ slice, vol)
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D; 3^4 window plus 5 source evals, about 41 + 5 x source (estimate)

cellular-facet.artifacts: Cracks at every cell border by design, wall jumps up to 1070 per unit in slope, so displaced meshes tear. Isolated vertices where three planes disagree stay steep in the soft blend; F2-F1 band blending alone was worse (c0ratio 1.0 from F2/F3 swaps) and was removed. Ridged sources have kinks, so the forward difference can tilt a facet strongly when a site falls on a crease: some slabs stand almost vertical in relief. Output needs a fitted gain, since the plane extrapolates beyond the source's range.
cellular-facet.node_shape: CellularFacet: Lookup (generator); Grid Jitter (hybrid); Slope (hybrid); Epsilon (float); Soft (float, 0 is hard); Lookup Frequency; Distance Function.
cellular-facet.port_notes: Cellular search keeps the winning site per lane, then D+1 source evals at per-lane sites, so cost is independent of the window. Forward differences lose precision at far coordinates; measured range stayed sane at 4e4 (-0.724 to 0.598). Could share a node with cellular-planes as a plane source option (source tangent instead of hash), but source-following tilt cannot be done from hashes or a graph. Soft needs a 3-plane K=3 blend to remove the vertex singularity, about 3 x (D+1) source evals, not tried. Discovery: pow underflow at soft=24 gives flat grout between stones.
cellular-facet.params_text: cells=2,jitter=0.9,slope=1,soft=0,src=1,octaves=3,srcFreq=0.7,eps=0.02,outGain=0.45,outBias=-0.22 (these are the code defaults). Softer stones: soft=4,jitter=0.7

master.one_liner: First-order CellularLookup: each cell becomes the tangent plane of the source at its centre, turning any field into low-poly chipped rock.
master.look: Faceted crystal or chipped stone over any terrain, low-poly stylised landscape. FBm with cell scale 2-3.5x feature gives rock chip fields. Matches Substance Crystal's angular character and C4D Displaced Voronoi's chipped feel by description. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=19.
master.algorithm: Closest site c in the 3^dim window, d=p-c. v0=Source(c); g_a=(Source(c+e*axis_a)-v0)/e. out=v0+Slope*dot(g,d). Slope 0 equals CellularLookup. Slope 1 is a tangent facet. Slope>1 exaggerates into chips. Sources are evaluated only at the selected site per lane, so count is dim+1 regardless of window.
master.why_new: Sheet's CellularLookup is piecewise constant and terraced; this is piecewise linear, so shading varies inside each cell. Not expressible: graph cannot evaluate a source at a cell centre and its neighbours and then form a plane. Low-poly on an arbitrary source is otherwise a mesh operation.
master.simd_plan: Cellular window plus D+2 taps at the site, where sites differ per lane, which is fine since positions are per lane. 2D 3.9+4.4 = about 8 ns, 3D 12+11 = about 23 ns, 4D 41+26 = about 67 ns on Perlin. Scalar prototype 6.2x perlin2 with the harness's 5x5 search. C0 variant roughly adds D+2 taps.
master.continuity: Discontinuous at cell borders, measured c0ratio 1.00; jump size scales with curvature*cell^2, and looks like hard chips rather than noise. Interior is C-infinity (plane).
master.params: Lookup (GeneratorSource), Feature Scale, Grid Jitter (hybrid), Slope (hybrid), Distance Function, Epsilon (float), Lookup Frequency.
master.risks:
Not continuous, so displacement has cracks; small jump when cells are small relative to source features. Far coordinate FD precision. Slope>1 amplifies out of range.
[CellularTangentHold, graph-meta-filters] Steep source with big cells gives large jumps and output beyond the source range, so clamp or Remap. Needs a site position output from the cellular search, which is in hand in Cellular.inl.
master.cost_note: 2D 3.9+4.4 = about 8 ns, 3D 12+11 = about 23 ns, 4D 41+26 = about 67 ns on Perlin. Scalar prototype 6.2x perlin2 with the harness's 5x5 search.
master.variant_notes: Same tangent-plane hold; second-order Curve term and a C0 blend band come from CellularTangentHold.

measured.scalar_note: 3 x 3 octave ridged source evals per sample plus the 3x3 search. soft=4 measured 20.76.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 2D cellular 3.9 + 3 x source, about 14 ns on 3 octave Perlin; 3D about 12 + 4 x 6.6 = 38 ns
measured.c0_note: Jumps are the look: each cell is an independent plane. Slope 0 (CellularLookup) measured 1.00. The soft two plane blend measured 1.62 at soft=4, jitter 0.7 and 1.92 at jitter 0.45, so it is not cleanly C0.

cellular-patchwork.look: Etched polycrystal: blocks of parallel lamellae, each grain with its own stripe direction and width, meeting at clean grain boundaries with no visible seams. The threshold panel is a zebra labyrinth broken along grain boundaries. The 3D isosurface is the best view: real planar sheets inside each grain, cut at grain boundaries, like a lamellar alloy. Stretched ridged source in relief gives foliated rough ground whose ridge direction changes patch by patch, reading as folded rock but busy. The isotropic source (src=2) was not rendered. Tilted plane source gives faceted glass-like cells with a very blurred look at K=3, while K=1 stays crisp.

dims.3D: works, measured (check, XZ slice, vol), Rodrigues rotation per grain
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D

cellular-patchwork.artifacts: Spectrum has a ring at the stripe frequency, as expected for this source. Steep, not jumping, at triple junctions when sharp is above about 5, with max slope 105 per unit at sharp 4 on stripes at this frequency. Blend zones thin the contrast without vp=1; with vp=1 range grows to about 1.7 before gain. Continuity recheck: the probe with its samples straddling the lattice lines reads c0ratio_straddle 6.79 (plain 7.26), and the largest step stays 0.071 as the probe step shrinks from 1e-4 to 1e-5, so there is a real jump of that size at the default; "steep, not jumping" above only holds for the plain probe, which does not cross those lines.
cellular-patchwork.node_shape: Use CellFrame. Options worth adding to it from this prototype: Blend Count 1 for a hard grain mode, Rotation Steps for quantised angles, Variance Preserving seams (the vp flag, sum w v / sqrt sum w^2).
cellular-patchwork.port_notes: Same structure as CellFrame: 3^D window, sorted top K+1, K source evals at per-lane frames and seeds. The look is strong, and it is a keeper-grade look, but it is not a separate node. Stripes through a built-in lamellae source (the catalogue's CellularGrain) is the cheaper special case if a real preset is wanted.
cellular-patchwork.params_text: K=3,src=1,jitter=0.8,sharp=4,cells=1,srcFreq=2.6,vp=1,outGain=0.58,scaleJit=0.25 (these are the code defaults). Relief image: src=4,octaves=4,sharp=6. Hard grains: K=1
cellular-patchwork.merged_into: cell-frame (a CellFrame node already exists in the lab with the same K nearest rank-subtract blend)

master.one_liner: Each Voronoi cell gets its own rotated, offset and reseeded copy of the source, with a K-nearest partition of unity that is provably continuous for fixed K evals.
master.look:
Polycrystal or foliated metamorphic rock: patches of strata or grain at different angles meeting at sharp (K=1) or soft (K=2,3) grain boundaries. Also metal grain, wood parquet, cracked ice, camouflage, kaleidoscope cells if each cell folds. Prototyped: mode=4, K=1 and K=3.
[CellularPatchwork, lit-classic] Prototype cl_cell modes 2-4: rotated stripes per polygon like plywood or metallographic grains or farmland; stretched fbm with seams gives hair or fur patches; facets look like shattered tinted glass with crisp creases under hillshade. Biome plates, flagstones where each stone has its own texture, tectonic masks.
[CellularGrain, math-physics] Etched polycrystal metallography (pearlite lamellae, each grain with its own stripe direction), mica schist, crystalline ice, wood knots mosaics, Voronoi stained-glass with hatching; 3D slices show planar lamellae inside each grain, like real lamellar colonies.
master.algorithm:
Search window for sorted F1..F(K+1) with cell centres and hashes. For i<=K: w_i = (F(K+1)-F_i)^Sharpness. value = sum w_i * S( R(h_i)*(p-c_i) + off(h_i), seed^h_i ) / sum w_i. Continuity: swapping cells among the top K is symmetric, and swapping K with K+1 happens where w_K = 0. Denominator vanishes only if F1..F(K+1) are all equal, a codimension-K set: K=3 in 2D never hits it generically, K=2 only at isolated Voronoi vertices where the value stays bounded. K=1 is the hard-edged mode (1 eval, intentional jump). Per-cell params: rotation (random or quantised to N), mirror bit, scale jitter, offset.

[CellularPatchwork, lit-classic] Run the 3^d F1 search, keep per-lane best site vector d1, hash h1 (and d2,h2, F3 for seams).
u=Rot(rnd(h1)*Rotation)*(x-site1)*Scale(h1)+Offset*rnd2(h1).
Result=Source(seed+SeedStep*h1,u).
Seam>0: evaluate the 3 nearest sites, w_i=saturate(1-(F_i-F1)/Seam)^2, normalise, blend. Source=SineWave: per-cell stripes. Source=Gradient: per-cell tilted plane (facets). Source=FBm with axis scale: oriented grain.
master.why_new: CellularLookup samples the source at the site, so each cell is flat. No graph can feed a per-cell rotation into a subtree's coordinates. Worley's flagstone-like tiled areas and PPTBF's per-cell feature functions both want this, and SIMD suits it because the Source call count is fixed regardless of which cell each lane is in.
master.simd_plan: CellularDistance-style window with a small sorting network to F(K+1), storing centre and hash for top K, then K source evals with per-lane seed (seed is int32v, so reseeding per lane is free). About 6 ns plus K*source in 2D, 15 ns plus K*source in 3D, 45 ns plus K*source in 4D (estimates). Rotation: sin/cos of hash or a small table of unit pairs. 3D: 24 cube rotations table, or Rodrigues about hash axis. 4D: two plane rotations.
master.continuity: K>=2: C0 (measured c0ratio 7.96 at K=3), Sharpness>=2 gives smooth weights except at top-K swaps. K=1: discontinuous on purpose (c0ratio 1.2).
master.params: Blend Count K (1-3), Sharpness (hybrid), Rotation Amount, Rotation Steps, Offset Amount, Reseed flag, Grid Jitter, Cell Size, Source.
master.risks:
Prototype searched 5x5. In a 3x3 port F4 is exact only for jitter up to about 0.3, and F3 up to about 0.4; beyond that tiny seams can appear. Blending lowers contrast near boundaries; K=3 with Sharpness 2 looks fairly soft, so raise Sharpness. Cost is K times source, so wrap around a cheap source or keep K=2.
[CellPatchDomain, cell-relations] Soft blends reduce contrast like any cross-fade. Seeding per cell multiplies effective source variety, which may surprise users with GeneratorCache sources. Isotropic sources show little beyond faint seams.
master.cost_note: About 6 ns plus K*source in 2D, 15 ns plus K*source in 3D, 45 ns plus K*source in 4D (estimates).
master.variant_notes: Nine proposals: source evaluated in the nearest Voronoi cell's rotated, offset, reseeded frame. Continuity options: K=1 hard, K=2 or 3 by rank-subtract partition of unity, or F2-F1 fade. CellularGrain is the built-in-stripes preset (per-grain lamellae, twin bands), cheaper than a general source call.

measured.scalar_note: K=3 with the built-in stripe source, which includes one Perlin warp per grain. K=1 measured 5.61, K=2 7.93. The 4 octave strata source at K=3 measured 18.15 before the default change.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 2D about 6 ns + K x source, 3D about 15 ns + K x source, 4D about 45 ns + K x source
measured.c0_note: K=3, sharp 4, jitter 0.8. K=1 measured 1.00 (hard grains, on purpose). K=2 measured about 3.1 at sharp 6. K=3 sharp 6 jitter 1 measured 4.45. A diagnostic 5x5 window gave identical numbers to 3x3 at every jitter and sharpness tried, so the lower ratios come from steep blends, not window seams, within the probed region.

splat-burst.look: Crisp white ink splats on black: star-shaped blots with long thin rays of different lengths, each a single connected object with a clear centre, and rays neighbouring splats overlap. Hillshade reads as flat cut-outs. The 3D XZ slice shows the same spiky blots plus finer dust where the slice grazes a spike. Rock settings in vol give closed, lumpy, spiky bodies like pinecones or sea mines, not smooth asteroids; a few small pieces appear near the cluster, and I cannot tell from this one view whether they are small stamps or bodies cut by the cube. N=5 and N=9 give clean starfish and asterisk shapes with rounded arms. SDF output has radial glowing bursts (viewed before the floor fix; thumb_sdf and relief were rendered after it and not viewed). Thresholded noise does not give these centred star shapes.

dims.3D: works, measured (check, XZ slice, vol), angular noise on the unit sphere
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D; the catalogue estimates about 55 ns

splat-burst.artifacts: A few spikes hit the 1 cell radius clamp and end in a short arc rather than a point. Rays can vanish where the rank fade cuts them: with K=2 a third overlapping stamp is faded out rather than popping, so a ray can end early in dense clusters. Mean sits low at -0.67 since mostly background. Narrow spike tips alias at this sampling. z-continuity max 0.339 for dz=1e-3 in 3D at default, from steep walls.
splat-burst.node_shape: SplatBurst: Angular Source (generator) or Star Count N (int); Amp, Spike, Spike Exponent, Dent; Base Radius (hybrid), Radius Variation; Sharp (relative edge width); Core (fraction of radius where direction fades in); Blend Count K; Density; Output enum (Mask, Radial SDF).
splat-burst.port_notes: Rank by r / R0, evaluate the angular source only for the top K. Uses Sqrt and a reciprocal, no atan2. Two things differ from the catalogue: edge width must be relative to rad and the angular term must fade in over a core, otherwise r = 0 is a real jump whenever Sharp is close to rad; and for SDF output faded stamps must fall to the floor rather than to 0, or rank swaps draw bright lines (seen before the fix). Analytic N is a constant-count complex power, 2D only. Rays are clamped at 1 cell, so long rays need lower R, or a 5^d window at more cost.
splat-burst.params_text: cells=0.9,jitter=0.8,R=0.34,Rvar=0.45,Amp=1.3,Spike=1.8,Dent=0.55,Exp=1.5,F=4,Sharp=0.3,core=0.6,K=2,dens=0.8,fc=6,N=0,output=0 (these are the code defaults). Rocks: Amp=0.8,Spike=1.2,F=2.5,R=0.42,dens=0.7. Relief: output=1. Stars: N=5 or N=9. Urchins: F=8,Amp=2.2

master.one_liner: Stamps with radius driven by a direction-sampled source: ink splats, spiky shards and, in 3D, solid lumpy asteroids, all without atan2.
master.look: Prototype: jagged ink blots, spiky splats, blood or paint splatter, lichens, burst shapes. With 3D density: rocks and asteroids with star-shaped solid shape, closed surface, no floating fragments. Analytic N mode gives flowers and stars.
master.algorithm: Window 3^dim, K top stamps as in StampScatter, or analytic source. For each stamp: d = p-c, r=|d|, unit u=d/r. Sample the angular function by evaluating on the unit circle or sphere, seamless by construction: n = Angular.Gen(seed=h, u.x*F, u.y*F, hashOffset(h)). For 3D use 3D Angular at u*F; offset by seed. Shape: n' = n>0 ? (n^1.5)*Spike : n*Dent. Radius rad = R0(h)*(1+Amp*n'); clamp to <=1 cell. Output m = 1 - smoothstep(rad-Sharp, rad, r), or SDF-like value (rad-r) for 3D density. Analytic fast mode: Chebyshev: n' = cos(N*theta) = Re((u.x+i u.y)^N) computed via integer-count complex power with constant N, for stars and flowers (no Source eval at all). Mask out r<epsilon: r near 0 is always inside rad so direction singularity is hidden.
master.why_new: Threshold of noise never gives a star-shaped single-connected object with a defined centre; radial spikes do not come from isotropic noise. Sampling on the unit sphere means no polar coordinate seam and no atan2.
master.simd_plan: Scan cost plus K (1-3) Angular source evals, or analytic Chebyshev in constant N with 3^dim cells. 2D at K=2: 5 ns scan + 2 Perlin3 ~10 ns. 3D at K=2: 15 ns + 2*Perlin3 ~20 ns. 4D: u is 4D, Angular 4D, K=2, ~55 ns. Using max across K with rank-subtract as in StampScatter.
master.continuity: C0 with Sharp>0: c0ratio 2.85 at Sharp 0.05 (steep) and 6.36 at Sharp 0.15, with max slope 265 from narrow spike walls. In 3D density output, slope is bounded when returning rad-r.
master.params: Angular Source or Star Count N (enum), Amp, Spike Exponent, Dent, Base Radius (hybrid), Sharp, K, Output enum (mask, radial SDF)
master.risks: Spike tips are clamped by the 1-cell reach, so they flatten at high Amp, unless Base Radius is reduced. Near-centre angular gradient is singular but hidden only if rad is always positive, so require Amp*Dent < 1. Fast-mode N must be a member, not per-lane.
master.cost_note: 2D at K=2: 5 ns scan + 2 Perlin3 ~10 ns. 3D at K=2: 15 ns + 2*Perlin3 ~20 ns.

measured.scalar_note: K=2, two octaves of perlin3 on the unit circle per stamp. K=1 measured 9.23. Analytic N=5 with no noise eval measured 6.60.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 2D about 5 ns scan + 4 perlin3 evals = about 14 ns; 3D about 15 + 4 x 2.2 = about 24 ns; analytic N mode about 6 ns
measured.c0_note: Default mask at Sharp 0.3. It rises with softness (Sharp 0.05 1.00, 0.15 1.46, 0.3 2.81, 0.6 5.56), which points to steep spike walls rather than jumps. Radial SDF output 5.62, analytic N=5 mask 5.44. Before the core fade, c0ratio stayed under 2 at every Sharp, and that real jump was the direction singularity at r = 0.

super-sample.look: Coverage default: a thresholded fbm where every coastline carries a soft grey band of about the same width, wide or narrow slopes alike, unlike the smoothstep baseline, whose band follows the value and frays out on flat ground. Large footprints round off small bays and islets, so it also acts as a blur of the mask. In gray it reads as a clean soft edge, but hillshade shows the K+1 discrete levels as stippled contour lines in the band. K=4 has visible levels and noisy edges, K=16 is usable up to footprint about 0.5, and at 0.9 and 1.5 bands and blotches appear. Mean at a one pixel footprint visibly cleans the staircase on CellularValue, Checkerboard and Terrace at window 32 compared with point sampling. Nothing new as a noise: it is an antialiasing and band utility.

dims.3D: works, measured (check, XZ slice), 3D taps use the same disc in XY plus a radical inverse in Z
dims.4D: not measured, the harness has no 4D; catalogue plans 8 axis taps

super-sample.artifacts: Discrete levels in Coverage, visible as stipple in hillshade and as a jump measure of max slope 375. A square Hammersley pattern showed square corners in the band, fixed by a Vogel disc for K=8 and K=16. Fixed pattern means a fixed-looking ghost on features smaller than the footprint.
super-sample.node_shape: SuperSample: Source; Footprint (hybrid); Pattern enum (RGSS 4, Disc 8, Disc 16); Mode enum (Mean, Coverage); Threshold (hybrid, Coverage only).
super-sample.port_notes: Generic GenT with a compile-time pattern table per dimension, K source evals at offset positions. Cost is the flaw: 16 taps for a clean band is very expensive on a fractal, and the same result can be built by hand from K DomainOffsets and Adds, so this is an authoring and antialias convenience. Coverage with a noise Threshold was not tested. The caller must pass the footprint for antialias use, since a Gen does not know the grid frequency. Promising for baking and minimaps rather than as a building block.
super-sample.params_text: mode=1,K=16,footprint=0.5,T=0,src=0,freq=0.6,octaves=4 (these are the code defaults). Antialias use: mode=0,K=16,src=1,freq=1,footprint=one output pixel

master.one_liner: Footprint integration of any source over a pixel-sized area with a fixed rotated-grid pattern (Mean) or a threshold-coverage mode that gives antialiased, uniform-width edges independent of source slope.
master.look: Mean turns hard-edged nodes (Checkerboard, CellularValue, Terrace, Fade with Step, ConvertRGBA8 inputs) into antialiased ones at any zoom and removes the shimmering of minified FBm; visually identical to the source at 1:1 and progressively smoother when minified. Coverage gives a soft band of constant world width around any iso-contour of any source (proto sheetB m11): unlike smoothstep on the value (band width ~ 1/|grad|), the band is as wide on steep flanks as on flat ones. Uses: texture baking, minimaps, LOD, uniform-width coastlines/biome borders, dithering-free masks.
master.algorithm:
Params: Source; Footprint (hybrid; world-space size of the area to integrate, e.g. the pixel size); Pattern enum {RGSS4 (2D) / 8 points (3D: BCC-like corners), Grid 2^D, Star 2D taps}; Mode {Mean, Coverage}; Threshold (hybrid, Coverage only).
GenT: offsets o_k = Footprint * q_k where q_k is the fixed pattern in [-0.5,0.5]^D (RGSS: (1/8,3/8),(3/8,-1/8),(-1/8,-3/8),(-3/8,1/8)).
  Mean     = (1/K) sum S(pos + o_k)
  Coverage = (1/K) sum Select(S(pos + o_k) > T, 1, 0) * 2 - 1
No centre tap needed for Mean. With Footprint equal to the output pixel size this is the band-limited (minified) version of the source.
master.why_new: Nothing in the graph can be told the pixel footprint; GenUniformGrid samples point values, so every hard node aliases when the grid is coarse. Coverage is a sampling-based 'IsoDistance' that needs no gradient normalisation and therefore has no singularities at critical points. As a graph it would be K DomainOffsets + K Fades + Adds; here it is one node whose cost is exactly the same K source evals.
master.simd_plan: GenT with a compile-time pattern table per D (RGSS 4 taps in 2D, 8 in 3D as the two interleaved tetrahedra of a cube scaled by 0.5, 8 axis taps in 4D). Cost = K x source: 4x in 2D, 8x in 3D/4D. CellularValue 2D at 3.9 ns becomes ~16 ns; cheaper than most alternatives. Branch-free: Coverage is a mask-to-float conversion.
