master.continuity: Mean: C0 when the source is C0 and still C0 for piecewise-constant sources only in the integral sense: with 4 taps the output is piecewise constant with 4x finer steps, i.e. a sparse approximation; true continuity needs the footprint to be the pixel size so steps fall below one output level. Coverage is a step function with K+1 levels (discontinuous) by construction; at pixel footprint that is exactly what antialiasing wants.
master.params: Source; Footprint (hybrid: pass a constant from the caller or a DistanceToPoint-based function for perspective-correct LOD); Pattern; Mode; Threshold (hybrid: a noise threshold gives a dithered-looking but still antialiased border).
master.risks: Fixed K=4/8 patterns are visible as 4-level staircases on hard edges when the footprint is larger than a pixel; offer K=16 (two rotated RGSS sets) as an expensive option. Not a substitute for a true band-limiting filter of fractals (only removes the worst aliasing). Users must supply the footprint; document the GenUniformGrid relation (footprint = frequency step).
master.cost_note: Cost = K x source: 4x in 2D, 8x in 3D/4D. CellularValue 2D at 3.9 ns becomes ~16 ns; cheaper than most alternatives.

measured.scalar_note: K=16 on a 4 octave fbm. K=4 measured 17.56; the bare source measured 5.37, so cost is K x source as planned (2930.9 against 272.6 ns is 10.8x, part of the source cost is shared map lookups). Mean K=4 on CellularValue measured 3.06.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: K x source: K=4 CellularValue about 16 ns, K=16 on 4 octave Perlin fbm about 70 ns
measured.c0_note: Coverage is stepped by design (K+1 levels). Mean K=16 on fbm with footprint 0.5: c0ratio 8.00. Mean K=4 on CellularValue at pixel footprint: c0ratio 1.50.

low-discrepancy-dither.look: Thresholding the fbm gives a fine even stipple whose local density follows the source, with no clumps or bald patches. Side by side with White in the comparison table the difference is obvious, especially on the ramp row: White has clusters and voids, IGN and R2 ramp smoothly like a halftone. Raw dither is a fine woven gray grain with a slight tilt. IGN midtones show short horizontal dark streaks; R2 is more of an even dashed hatch. The 3D XZ slice: IGN shows clear parallel diagonal stripes even though its block statistics are good; R3 is a woven hatch without the long stripes.
low-discrepancy-dither.dims: 2D and 3D measured (IGN with the frame offset on z, R3 with the plastic constants). 4D not written; R4 constants exist from x^5 = x + 1, same one line form.
low-discrepancy-dither.range: Threshold output is exactly -1 or 1. Raw dither: -1 to 1, uniform (measured in numpy: std 0.2886 for IGN, 0.2887 for R2, uniform is 0.2887).
low-discrepancy-dither.artifacts: Not blue noise: FFT is a regular lattice of bright spots for both modes, so it reads as ordered when looked at as a texture. It is a mask source, not a texture. The optional block shuffle (XOR of the cell by a block hash) made visible square seams every 32 cells and was left off. Discontinuous by design, piecewise constant per cell. The check's far coordinate run was clean, but float precision of the first frac at wrap 2^16 is about 2.4e-4, multiplied by 53 in IGN; the shader original has the same limit.
low-discrepancy-dither.node_shape: Members: Mode {IGN, Plastic}, Feature Scale (cell size), Phase (hybrid, animates), Threshold Source (optional hybrid; output is Source > dither mapped to +1/-1), Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
low-discrepancy-dither.port_notes: Trivial: floor, integer mask to 16 bits, convert, 2-4 FMAs, 2 fracs, no hash per sample. Seed only shifts x by 8 bits of a hash, so seeds are translations of one pattern: acceptable for a mask, say so in the docs. Threshold mode is a one line Select. Needs nothing from a lattice window.
low-discrepancy-dither.params_text: mode=0,src=1,sc=16 (code defaults: IGN thresholding a 3 octave fbm) at --window 8. mode=1 is R2/R3, src=0 is the raw dither, src=2 a ramp.

master.one_liner: Pointwise low-discrepancy grids: Interleaved Gradient Noise (Jimenez 2014) and the R2/R3 plastic-constant grids (Roberts 2018) as a dither/threshold generator whose values are evenly spread within every small neighbourhood, unlike White noise (Wolfe 2022 analysis).
master.look: Fine, extremely even 'ordered-but-random' grain; thresholded against a smooth field it yields stipple/halftone-like scatter masks (vegetation placement, pebble sprinkle, decal density, stochastic transparency, dithered terracing) with no clumps or voids. White noise thresholded shows clusters; this does not.
master.algorithm:
Params: Mode enum {IGN, R2, Bayer-like via R2 rounding}, CellSize (Feature Scale; positions are floored to integer cells), Frame/Phase (hybrid, animates by offsetting), Threshold Source (optional hybrid: output a binary mask Source > dither).
IGN (2D): i = floor(p); v = frac(52.9829189 * frac(0.06711056*i.x + 0.00583715*i.y)); animated: i += 5.588238 * (frame mod 64).
R2 (2D): v = frac(0.5 + 0.7548776662*i.x + 0.5698402910*i.y) (plastic constant g=1.32471795724: a1=1/g, a2=1/g^2). R3 (3D): a = (0.8191725134, 0.6710436067, 0.5497004779) from the 'plastic-3' root of x^4 = x+1. R4: 4 constants from x^5 = x+1. Output 2v-1.
ThresholdMode: out = Select(ThresholdSource(p) > v, 1, -1): a binary scatter/stipple mask whose local density equals the source value exactly (within every 3x3 block the 9 dither values are ~k/9).
Optional 'xor-shuffle' of i by a hash of floor(i/64) to de-periodise the R2 grid at large scales (R2 is exactly periodic only in the limit; IGN is quasi-periodic).
master.why_new: White is the only stochastic point-pattern source in FastNoise and it clumps; a blue-ish low-discrepancy grid gives visually uniform coverage for placement masks and dithering at ~20 ops with no tables (true blue-noise tables are not allowed by the rules). The threshold mode makes 'density field -> uniform scatter' a one-node operation.
master.simd_plan: Trivial: floor, 2-4 FMAs, 2 frac; < 0.3x Perlin in any dimension. Branch-free.
master.continuity: Discontinuous by design (piecewise constant per integer cell), like White/Checkerboard.
master.params: Mode (enum), CellSize (Feature Scale), Phase (hybrid), Threshold (hybrid source), Dimension constants chosen per Gen dim.
master.risks: IGN/R2 have visible diagonal micro-structure when viewed as an image; fine for masks, not as a texture. Precision of frac for huge coordinates (use integer cells and a periodic wrap of 2^16).
master.cost_note: Trivial: floor, 2-4 FMAs, 2 frac; < 0.3x Perlin in any dimension.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: raw dither about 0.3 ns in any dimension. The scalar 57.8 ns raw is mostly param reads and hash calls for the seed. 196.9 ns with threshold includes the 3 octave fbm source, which is not part of the node's own cost.

triaxial-weave.look: Immediately reads as woven cane or a kagome basket: hexagonal black holes, flat ribbons with fine fibre streaks, every ribbon visibly going over then under, each strand a slightly different tone with slight wobble. Hillshade and relief both read as a real woven mat with rounded over-crossings. Sweep: hw 0.14 is open kagome with small triangles, 0.24 hexagon holes only, 0.33 small holes, 0.43 nearly closed and soft in height mode. TopFamily at hw 0.33-0.43 is a clean tumbling block pattern with a strong 3D illusion. Lookup mode (rattan) has a metallic twisted strip look with sharper fibre detail. FFT is the expected six pointed star.
triaxial-weave.dims: 2D and 3D measured (3D is a thin sheet Height - z repeated every zs = 3 units). 4D would pass through, not run. Pattern is 2D by nature; a genuinely 3D weave is a different idea.
triaxial-weave.range: Height -1 (hole) to 1 by clamp, measured -1.000 to 1.000 over 8 seeds, mean 0.15, 0 NaN. Histogram: spike at the hole level plus a broad upper range.
triaxial-weave.artifacts: Regular by design, so the wide view repeats exactly apart from tone and wobble. Height mode at hw above about 0.33 loses the weave read and looks like soft pillows; use TopFamily there. Vol shows stacked sheets breaking into small fragments at this resolution, clearly a 2D pattern in a slab, not an impressive 3D result. Threshold at P50 gives broken jagged strand pieces because of the grain.
triaxial-weave.node_shape: Members: Half Width (hybrid), Thickness, Lift Amp (hybrid), Width Jitter, Wobble, Grain, Tone, Edge, Chirality (bool), Density (broken cane), Mode {Height, TopFamily, Lookup}, Source for Lookup, Period for tiling, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
triaxial-weave.port_notes: Branch free as described: 3 dots, 3 floors, 3 hashes, 3 Sqrt, 3 Cos, Select to the hole level. Half width must keep hw*(1+wj)+wob below 0.5, or strands get cut at the cell boundary and a seam appears. Chirality flip, density and tiling period are not rendered here (flip and dens are coded, period is not). Grain as coded is 3 Perlins; a 1D value noise across the strand would be cheaper and probably as good, not tried.
triaxial-weave.params_text: hw=0.2,th=0.5,amp=0.4,wj=0.1,wob=0.03,wf=0.7,tone=0.15,grain=0.3,edge=0.25,mode=0 (all code defaults) at --window 8. mode=2 is the rattan ribbon texture; mode=1,hw=0.43 is the tumbling block three colour pattern.

master.one_liner: Three families of strands at 60 degrees with a provably consistent cyclic over-under rule and no trig per strand, giving the hexagonal-hole kagome basket, rattan cane webbing and closed 'mad weave' looks that a two-family weave cannot.
master.look: A regular lattice of hexagonal holes bordered by six-pointed star overlaps, every strand clearly passing over then under its neighbours, chair cane webbing, kagome baskets, rattan, and at full width the dense three-way 'mad weave' with its tumbling-block illusion. Visibly different from the two-family plain/twill weaves already prototyped and from any hex cellular pattern.
master.algorithm:
Three unit normals 120 degrees apart: n0=(0,1), n1=(-sqrt3/2,-1/2), n2=(sqrt3/2,-1/2) so n0+n1+n2=0 and s0+s1+s2=0 for s_a = p.n_a. Strands of family a are centred on half-integer s_a with pitch 1. For each a: k_a=floor(s_a), f_a=s_a-k_a-0.5 (across coordinate, |f|<=0.5), per-strand hash h_a=hash(a,k_a), half-width hw_a = HW*(1+WidthJitter*rnd11(h_a)) with HW<=0.5 (HW<1/6 keeps the small triangles open, HW=0.5 closes the hexagons into mad weave), crown_a = sqrt(max(0, 1-(f_a/hw_a)^2)) * Thickness.
Interlace (cyclic rule 0 over 1, 1 over 2, 2 over 0): because s0+s1+s2=0, where strand centres of families a and a+1 cross (both half-integers) s_{a+2} is an integer, i.e. the third family passes exactly between its strands: no triple points, and along any strand the crossings alternate between the other two families, so the cyclic rule is automatically alternating over/under and pairwise consistent (checked: at an a/(a+1) crossing a says over, a+1 says under its a-1=a). Lift without any crossing bookkeeping: lift_a = Amp*(cos(2 pi s_{a+2}) - cos(2 pi s_{a+1}))/2, which evaluates to +Amp at crossings with a+1 and -Amp at crossings with a+2 and interpolates smoothly between (3 cosines total, shared by all three families).
height_a = crown_a + lift_a where crown_a>0 else -1 (hole). Output Height = max_a height_a (ScaleOutput). Modes: Height; Lookup = Source(seed^h_top, t_a, f_a/hw_a) with t_a = p.d_a along the top strand (ribbon texture, Strata on k_a gives coloured cane); TopFamily (0,1,2 as -1,0,1 for three-colour patterns); Wobble: f_a += W*n1d(t_a, k_a) (1D value noise along the strand, 2 hashes) for hand-woven irregularity.
3D: Height - z gives a solid woven sheet (iso-surface), or z selects layers; 4D passes through. Explicit integer Period on the hashes makes it tile.
master.why_new: A two-family weave node cannot produce three-directional interlacing; the existing hex nodes give cells, not strands with over-under. The identity s0+s1+s2=0 is what makes the interlace rule and lift closed-form, so the node is as cheap as a plain weave.
master.simd_plan: Branch-free: 3 dot products, 3 floors, 3 hashes, 3 sqrt, 3 cos, a few selects, max of three. Roughly 2-3x Perlin in 2D; 3D/4D cost identical plus passthrough. GenT over the pack works since only (x,y) are used for the pattern.
master.continuity: Height is C0 (max of continuous terms; crown goes to 0 at strand edges and the hole level -1 is below any strand). Lookup and TopFamily are discontinuous at strand edges and crossings by design.
master.params: HalfWidth (hybrid), Thickness, LiftAmp (hybrid), WidthJitter, Wobble, Mode enum, Source, Period, optional Chirality flip (swap the cyclic rule) and per-strand presence (rnd01<Density, broken cane).
master.risks: The cyclic rule yields one chirality; the physical kagome exists in both, so expose a flip. Lift amplitude versus crown height must be tuned so an under-strand is never visible through an over-strand at the crossing centre (Amp >= Thickness*(1-cos(pi*hw)) roughly; proto to confirm). Verify the no-triple-point claim numerically for the chosen normals.
master.cost_note: Roughly 2-3x Perlin in 2D; 3D/4D cost identical plus passthrough.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: about 3-4 ns without grain, 7-8 ns with grain and wobble (a port must run all 3 grain Perlins and 6 wobble hashes; the scalar 220.9 ns skips strands that do not cover the sample). Without grain, scalar measured 185.7 ns.

queue.name: FlowNoise
queue.reason: Perlin-Neyret rotating gradients for looping animation at 1.6x base, static look same as Perlin. Belongs as a Phase member; only a loop check is needed.

master.one_liner: Flow noise: a hybrid phase on Perlin, Simplex and Cellular that rotates gradients or orbits features, giving seamless looping animation with no extra dimension. Looping 3D volumes become possible at all.
master.look:
A still frame looks like the base node. In motion: Perlin swirls in place with features neither translating nor fading, and Cellular cells jostle and return. Band-pass stays intact, unlike slicing 3D noise (Cook & DeRose, Gustavson). Boiling water, fire, looping clouds, breathing cells.
[FlowNoise, dcc-tools] A still frame looks like Perlin. In time it churns and swirls rather than crossfading or sliding. With pseudo-advection the fractal gains veiny, fluid lines (dcc_lens mode=3 adv=0.35). Good for fire, clouds, water surface, looping VFX.
master.algorithm:
Gradient nodes: at each corner g(alpha)=u*cos(alpha)+v*sin(alpha), u,v orthonormal from hash (2D: v=Ju, so v.d=dot(u,(d.y,-d.x)); 3D per Gustavson: per-corner axis, or a 12 gradient table with a perpendicular table).
cos(alpha), sin(alpha) are computed once per lane; alpha=Phase(x).
Equivalently N(x,alpha)=N_u(x)*cos(alpha)+N_v(x)*sin(alpha).
Cellular: site_c(alpha)=c+.5+j1(h)*cos(alpha)+j2(h)*sin(alpha), j1,j2 two jitter vectors in one hash; elliptical orbit with no per-cell trig; orbit bound must fit the window.
A hybrid alpha varying in space is also seamless because alpha is sampled at x.

[PhaseSpinPerlin, volumetric-3d4d] Standard Perlin lattice (4/8 corners). Per corner hash h: gradient g = Grad[h & 15], axis a = Axis[(h>>4) & 15] (table of 16 unit vectors), phase phi = ((h>>8) & 15) * 2pi/16 -> cphi, sphi from a 16-entry table.
 theta = Omega * (w + Phase(p))  (Phase is a hybrid; in 2D/3D w = 0)
 S = Sin(theta), C = Cos(theta) once per lane
 per corner: s_i = S*cphi + C*sphi, c_i = C*cphi - S*sphi   // sin/cos(theta + phi_i)
 3D Rodrigues: g_i(theta) = g*c_i + (a x g)*s_i + a*(a.g)*(1 - c_i)   (precompute a x g and a(a.g) per table pair -> 256 x 3 vectors, or 6 muls on the fly)
 2D: g_i(theta) = (gx c_i - gy s_i, gx s_i + gy c_i)
 n = quintic-interpolated dot products as Perlin; same normalisation (rotated gradients stay unit length).
Period in w is exactly 2pi/Omega.
master.why_new: Looping a 2D image needs 4D (torus in t) and looping a 3D volume needs 5D, which does not exist here; the phase gives both with no extra dimension. Looping 2D Cellular would otherwise cost 41 ns (4D). The graph form cos*NoiseA+sin*NoiseB covers gradient noise statistics but not Cellular, needs a per-frame user sin/cos, and has twice the hashing.
master.simd_plan:
Gradient: 2 gradient dots per corner, 1 sincos per lane: ~1.6x base. 2D ~1.8 ns; 3D ~3.5 ns; 4D ~7 ns. Cellular: +1 jitter pair: ~1.15x: 4.5/14/47 ns. So 2D loop at 4.5 ns vs 41 ns in 4D, a 9x saving.
[FlowNoise, dcc-tools] 2D estimated 1.7 ns (1.5x Perlin), 3D about 3.5 ns, 4D about 7 ns, with one sincos per lane plus Select per corner instead of per-corner trig. Time can be hybrid since the sincos is per lane. Same GenT layout as Perlin. Scalar proto 2.2x perlin2 with per-corner trig.
master.continuity: Same as base node in x (C2 Perlin, C0 Cellular F1). Smooth and 2pi periodic in alpha. Not prototyped; formulas are straightforward from the sources.
master.params: Hybrid: Phase (radians or turns). Added member on existing nodes, or new FlowPerlin, FlowSimplex, OrbitCellular. Orbit Radius for cellular.
master.risks:
Static look adds nothing, so it needs a video-capable eval. Fixed period of 2pi means all features share the same cycle, which reads as pulsing unless octaves use different speeds (a Fractal phase-speed member is needed). Cellular orbit plus jitter must fit the seam bound. 3D gradient pair table quality untested.
[PhaseSpinPerlin, volumetric-3d4d] Perlin's zeros at lattice corners are pinned, so under animation a faint stationary grid of zero-crossings can show (standard Perlin has it too, but motion makes it visible); mitigations: use inside FBm, or add a small per-corner oscillating value offset. High Omega reads as flicker rather than flow.
[SpinGradient, volumetric-3d4d] Untested. Perlin zero at lattice points remains, so iso-surfaces in animation stay pinned to the lattice corners, a visible artifact; mitigate through Simplex base or per-octave offset. Same 4.5 ns cost as 4D Perlin, so only worthwhile if looping or motion quality win. Well known concept (flow noise) with an exact loop as the new part. Tiling via 4D mapping feeds w as an ordinary coordinate, which does tile but is meaningless as time.
sources: from memory, not consulted: Perlin & Neyret 2001 'Flow Noise' (rotating gradients + pseudo-advection)
master.cost_note: Gradient form about 1.6x base: 1.8 / 3.5 / 7 ns. Orbiting Cellular about 1.15x: 4.5 / 14 / 47 ns, so a looping 2D Cellular is 9x cheaper than going through 4D.
master.variant_notes: Rotating gradients with integer speeds give an exact loop. Included: orbiting Cellular sites (LoopPhase), per-corner phase to remove pulsing (PhaseSpinPerlin), Gustavson 3D axes. Value shows only in animation, so a video-capable eval is needed to judge it.

queue.name: PeriodicFBm
queue.reason: No new look: wrapped lattice indices give true tileable 3D and ~3.5x cheaper 2D tiling (J4 top pick). Should land as a Period member on lattice nodes. Only tiling needs checking.

master.one_liner: Lattice noises that wrap by integer period per axis, giving tileable 2D at a quarter of the cost and tileable 3D, which FastNoise cannot do today.
master.look: Normal Perlin or Worley, but periodic. PerlinWorley gives billowy cauliflower cloud masses, new on the sheet. For bakes: tiling terrain textures, 3D cloud volumes, tile materials.
master.algorithm: Hash uses wrapped lattice indices: ix' = ix - P*floor(ix/P) (AND mask when P is a power of two), per axis, P=0 disables. The offset vector still uses unwrapped ix so gradients and distances are correct. Built-in octave loop: P doubles with lacunarity 2, seed changes per octave. Kernel enum: Perlin, Value, Cellular F1, Cellular inverted, PerlinWorley (Perlin remapped by inverted Worley FBm, the cloud base shape). Cellular wraps neighbour cell indices in the 3^d window the same way. Output tiles exactly at world size P*Feature Scale.
master.why_new: On Auburn's list: #2 says '3D periodic noise using modulus grid coordinates, probably only valid for value, perlin and cellular noise'. #12 asks for tiled 3D volumes especially cellular; Auburn replied it would need 6D via the hypertorus. FastNoiseLite issues #4, #20, #33, #53, #74, #86, #87 all ask for tiling; #53 links a fork doing 2^N periods and #86 asks for tileability again. Can't be a domain op since fractal parents don't pass period information to sources.
master.simd_plan: Same as Perlin or Cellular plus a mask or float floor per axis per lattice lookup, about +10%. Estimated AVX2 per octave: Perlin 1.2 / 2.4 / 4.8 ns, vs 4.3 ns for tiling via 4D, so about 3.5x cheaper in 2D with no hypertorus stretch. Cellular costs the same as CellularDistance.
master.continuity: Same as the kernel (Perlin C2 interpolant). Seam fully continuous since hash values match. Non-integer Feature Scale relative to the tile size breaks the tile, so period is the defining parameter.
master.params: Kernel enum, Period X/Y/Z/W (int), Octaves, Gain, Lacunarity (int), Jitter, Feature Scale derived or checked.
master.risks: Simplex family cannot use it because of the skewed lattice (Auburn notes this). Period and Feature Scale need clear UI. Duplicates some kernels unless Perlin/Value/Cellular kernels are shared. Warps above it break the tile; see DomainTile for those.
master.cost_note: Estimated AVX2 per octave: Perlin 1.2 / 2.4 / 4.8 ns, vs 4.3 ns for tiling via 4D, so about 3.5x cheaper in 2D with no hypertorus stretch.

queue.name: AlligatorNoise
queue.reason: Houdini alligator: top-2 weighted domes in the Cellular loop at 1.4x. Proven look; just needs a measured remap.

master.one_liner: Houdini's alligator: weighted compact domes per site, output is the gap between the two strongest, giving raised scales of varied height with flat creased gaps.
master.look: Scaly hide, blistered paint, cobbled skin. Domes of different heights separated by creases, with black dead zones where two weak sites meet. Fractal version reads as cauliflower or lichen. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=0, fractal mode=16 which=1.
master.algorithm: Per the SideFX HDK reference. cell=floor(p); m1=m2=0. For each cell in the 3^dim window: h=hash(cell); c=cell+jitter(h); w=rnd01(mix(h)); d=Sqrt(dot(p-c,p-c)); t=Max(0,1-d/R); f=w*t*t*(3-2t); mask=f>m1; m2=Select(mask,m1,Max(m2,f)); m1=Max(m1,f). Return ScaleOutput(m1-m2, 0, 1). The HDK uses R=1 and a 3x3x3 search. Fractal use in other tools: lacunarity 2.2-2.5 with high persistence.
master.why_new: Not reachable from CellularDistance: F2-F1 has no per-site weight and no compact falloff, and top-2 selection on weighted values cannot be expressed by a graph. SideFX docs say it cannot be simulated with their Worley functions. Height varies per cell, unlike F2-F1 where every cell peaks at a similar level.
master.simd_plan: Same 3^dim loop as CellularDistance, plus one hash mix, Sqrt and a cubic. No Sqrt avoidance possible because the falloff needs d. Estimated 5.5 / 17 / 58 ns, 1.4x CellularDistance. Scalar proto 113 ns vs 50 for perlin2 and 109 for the harness worley2.
master.continuity: C0 everywhere: R=1 means any site outside the window is at distance >=1 and contributes 0, at any jitter <=1 inside the cell. C1 except on the creases where m1 and m2 swap. Measured c0ratio 8.0 at jitter 1 and 0.7.
master.params: Grid Jitter (hybrid), Weight Jitter (hybrid; 0 reduces to a smoothstep F2-F1), Radius (float, <=1), Output Min/Max.
master.risks: Mean is low (about -0.34 after 2x-1), so a measured remap may be nicer than the [0,1] bound. 4D is costly like all cell nodes.
master.cost_note: Estimated 5.5 / 17 / 58 ns, 1.4x CellularDistance. Scalar proto 113 ns vs 50 for perlin2 and 109 for the harness worley2.

queue.name: CellularSmooth
queue.reason: Smooth voronoi plus voronoise, a well-known gap and cheap to fill. Clamp k and guard Exp underflow; Power mode avoids Exp.

master.one_liner: Smooth Voronoi (exp-smin of all cell distances) and Voronoise (kernel-weighted cell values) in one node: blobby metaball cells and the continuous family between cell noise, Perlin-like noise and Voronoi.
master.look:
Soap-film / metaball cells with rounded junctions instead of sharp creases, melting Voronoi; the voronoise path gives soft random-blob textures and bevelled rounded plates. All continuous, none of it on the contact sheet, and the Smoothness slider morphs continuously from F1 to a smooth bump field.
[SoftCellular, lit-classic] Prototype cl_kens. Value k=12: soft-edged polygon mosaic, airbrushed stained glass; k=40: crisp with rounded lobes; k=6: blurry patches. Distance k=4-10: dark wells that merge into peanut shapes, with smooth ridges and no cusps, unlike the F1 sheet. Soft biome masks, cells under membrane, droplets.
master.algorithm:
Window 3^d, centred jitter J <= 0.5, kernel reach R <= 1 cell so the window is exact (iq uses 5x5 because his jitter is 1 and reach sqrt(2)).
For each cell: h = hash(c); q = c + 0.5 + J*(rnd01(h)-0.5); d = |p - q| (or d2 to skip the sqrt in the Value mode); v = rnd11(h>>8).
Mode SmoothDistance (iq smooth voronoi):
  acc += Exp(-k * d)         // k = 1/Smoothness, Smoothness in (0, 1]
  out = -Log(acc) / k        // exact n-ary exponential smin of all distances; Smoothness->0 recovers F1
  (alternative Power mode: acc += 1/d^8, out = acc^(-1/8); needs d>eps guard; cheaper on hardware without fast exp)
Mode SmoothValue (iq voronoise): 
  w = (1 - smoothstep(0, R, d))^k with k = 1 + 63*(1-V)^6 (V = value smoothness 0..1); Wsum += w; Vsum += w*v
  out = Vsum / Wsum          // V=0: hard cell values (CellularValue), V=1: smooth blobby value noise on a jittered grid, J=0 V=1: a Perlin-like lattice noise
  Integer k path: k rounded to an int member, pow via repeated squaring (branch-free, k same for all lanes); fractional k via Exp(k*Log(.)).
Mode SmoothDistanceMinusF1: out = F1 - smoothF1 (iq/Blender 'bevelled cells', needs F1 from the same loop: free).
master.why_new: MinSmooth exists only as a binary blend of two sources; an n-ary smin over the 9/27 cell distances cannot be expressed in the graph. Voronoise is a well-known 2-parameter family (cell/Perlin/Voronoi) that FastNoise cannot reach today.
master.simd_plan: One fixed loop, per cell: hash, distance, Exp (or pow via integer squaring), 2 FMAs. 2D: 9 Exp ~ CellularDistance 2D x 1.5 (~6 ns). 3D: 27 Exp ~ 20 ns. 4D 81 Exp ~ 65 ns (document). Log once at the end. Reuse CellularDistance's lattice/jitter machinery; dimension agnostic.
master.continuity: C-infinity for value mode with the subtraction (c0ratio 8.00 at k=6). Distance mode has a tiny window seam for k below ~6, visible as faint straight lines in hillshade at k=2-4.
master.params: Feature Scale, Jitter (<=0.5), Smoothness (hybrid, distance mode), Value Smoothness V (hybrid), Kernel Reach R (<=1), Mode enum {SmoothDistance, SmoothDistancePower, SmoothValue, Bevel}, Distance function enum (Euclidean, Manhattan: still C-inf smin), Output Min/Max.
master.risks:
Exp(-k d) underflow for small Smoothness: clamp k <= 64 and compute relative to the min distance (acc += Exp(-k*(d - dmin)) with dmin from a first min pass, or just clamp). Output range depends on k; normalise by measured constants per k or expose VariableRange.
[SoftCellular, lit-classic] k<6 needs a 5^d window or shows lattice seams. Very large k underflows (Clamp k or normalise by the smallest d2 first). Distance range shifts with k, so ScaleOutput needs a k-aware offset.
master.cost_note: 2D: 9 Exp ~ CellularDistance 2D x 1.5 (~6 ns). 3D: 27 Exp ~ 20 ns.
master.variant_notes: Exp smin distances and Voronoise-style weighted values. SoftCellular adds the window-seam subtraction and a hybrid Sharpness that morphs from soft blobs to crisp mosaic.

queue.name: DomainMap
queue.reason: Cylinder, torus and sphere embedding per sub-graph, so you tile the base rather than the Terrace. Plumbing with very high utility; costs one dimension.

master.one_liner: Per-node cylinder / torus / lat-long sphere / cube-sphere mapping: 2D input sampled on an embedded 3D or 4D surface, so seamless tiles and planets become composable inside the graph.
master.look: No new look by itself; it makes hard things easy: seamless strips and tiles per sub-graph (tile the base noise but not the Terrace after it, or tile two branches with different periods), equirectangular planet heightmaps without pole pinching, cube-map faces that match across edges, and shells with altitude. Combined with DomainKaleidoscope Icosa or DomainSymmetrize it also gives symmetric planets.
master.algorithm:
Params: Mode {CylinderX, Torus, SphereLatLong, CubeSphere, SphereShell3D}, Period X, Period Y (world units), Radius (3D), Face Layout {Strip 6x1, Atlas 3x2}.

  CylinderX:     R = PeriodX/(2pi); a = x / R; return Source.Gen(seed, R*Cos(a), R*Sin(a), y)                           // 2D -> 3D, seamless in x
  Torus:         R1 = PeriodX/(2pi), R2 = PeriodY/(2pi); return Source.Gen(seed, R1*Cos(x/R1), R1*Sin(x/R1), R2*Cos(y/R2), R2*Sin(y/R2))   // 2D -> 4D: GenTileable2D as a node
  SphereLatLong: u = 2pi*x/PeriodX, v = pi*y/PeriodY (v in [-pi/2, pi/2]); cv = Cos(v); return Source.Gen(seed, R*cv*Cos(u), R*cv*Sin(u), R*Sin(v))  // equirectangular planet, poles converge correctly
  CubeSphere:    face = Floor(x/PeriodX) (Strip) or (Floor(x/Px), Floor(y/Py)) (Atlas); s,t = face-local in [-1,1]; optional equal-angle warp s = Tan(s*pi/4) via Sin/Cos; build the cube point from face with 6-way Select on sign/axis; normalise with InvSqrt; scale by R; return Source.Gen(seed, point)
  3D input:      CylinderX -> 4D (x wraps, y,z pass); SphereShell3D: (u, v, h) -> dir(u,v) * (R + h) (3D source: altitude-aware planet shells). Torus in 3D needs 5D: unsupported (document). 4D: identity.

[ManifoldLift, domain-geometry] Enum of pure maps with dim raise. Torus(Px,Py): 2D input to S4(Px/2pi*cos(2pi x/Px), Px/2pi*sin(2pi x/Px), Py/2pi*cos(2pi y/Py), Py/2pi*sin(2pi y/Py)), flat and no stretching. Cylinder(Px): to S3(cos,sin,y), or 3D input to S4. LatLong: lon=x*2pi/W, lat=(y/H-.5)*pi, to R*(cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat) in S3, seamless at wrap and poles. CubeFace(face): gnomonic plus tan-adjust (u=tan(pi/4*x) with polynomial tan) to unit sphere in S3. Stereographic: (2x,2y,|p|^2-1)/(|p|^2+1), infinite plane to finite sphere. 3D to S^3: same in 4D for bounded-coordinates worlds. OctaFold (reverse direction): 3D direction n = p/|p|_1, feed S2(nx, ny) (lower hemisphere mirrors onto upper). This has creases on the equator but no seams, so any 2D-only source wraps a planet.
master.why_new: Asked repeatedly: FastNoiseLite #53 (torus), #86 (tile plus 'evolution looping' with UI video), gamedev links in #86 about world maps, Unity thread about planets, Reddit Burst erosion port added cubemap sampling for spherical terrain. FN2 can only hypertorus the entire output with GenTileable2D, and users cannot express this in graphs at all: no cos/sin domain, AddDimension only adds a constant or field. It also lets the editor preview planets, which GenPositionArray callers cannot.
master.simd_plan: 2-4 Sin/Cos (or one Sin+Cos pair reused) + source at +1/+2 dimensions: Perlin 2D 1.1 ns becomes Perlin 3D 2.2 / 4D 4.3 ns plus ~0.5 ns. CubeSphere: 6-way Select chain (~20 ops) + InvSqrt. No lattice window.
master.continuity: C-infinity (smooth embeddings) for all modes; CubeSphere is C0 across face edges (the sphere point is continuous, the direction derivative kinks), fine for sampling.
master.params: Mode enum, Period X/Y float, Radius float, Face Layout enum. All constant (not hybrid): a varying period breaks the seam.
master.risks:
Costs a dimension (4D sources for Torus); a user can already tile with GenTileable2D so the value is composability, not novelty; 3D Torus impossible.
[DomainMap, repo-demand] 4D source required for Torus and TimeLoop; node has to reject or fall back when input dim + added dims exceeds 4. Feature scale relationships are confusing: fractals stay seamless, since scaling happens below the map, but scale should be explained in world units. Not prototyped; simple enough.
master.cost_note: 2-4 Sin/Cos (or one Sin+Cos pair reused) + source at +1/+2 dimensions: Perlin 2D 1.1 ns becomes Perlin 3D 2.2 / 4D 4.3 ns plus ~0.5 ns.
master.variant_notes: Per-subtree tiling, wrap and planet projection. OctaFold direction mode (ManifoldLift) lets 2D-only sources wrap a planet, with mirror creases.

queue.name: DomainPolar
queue.reason: Log-polar through a unit-circle embedding into a 3D source, so no atan2 seam. Needs a minimum radius; 4D input drops out.

master.one_liner: Seam-free log-polar / spiral / mandala remap: 2D input becomes a 3D source sample (unit-circle embedding + log radius), no atan2, no theta=pi seam.
master.look: Whirlpools, spiral galaxies, snail shells (Twist), tree rings and ripples (small R so angular variation vanishes), mandalas and snowflakes (m=6 + Mirror), infinite-zoom detail converging to the centre (Log mode). With Cellular source: radial crystal facets; with Checkerboard: log-polar grid (Escher-like zoom tiles). Good for ornaments, vortex masks, planetary storms, radial terrain features (calderas, impact basins) and any 'around a point' structure.
master.algorithm:
2D input, 3D source. Params: RadialMode {Log, Linear}, RadialScale a, AngularRadius R, Twist k (hybrid), Symmetry m (int >= 1), Mirror (bool), MinRadius rmin.

  r2 = x*x + y*y; r = Max(Sqrt(r2), rmin); inv = 1/r
  ux = x*inv; uy = y*inv                       // unit direction = (cos th, sin th) without atan2
  rho = (Log) ? Log(r)*a : r*a                 // Log => features scale with r (scale invariant zoom)
  phi = k*rho                                  // twist angle grows with rho: log spiral (Log) / Archimedean (Linear)
  c = Cos(phi); s = Sin(phi)
  (ux,uy) = (ux*c - uy*s, ux*s + uy*c)         // rotate the direction by phi
  // m-fold symmetry by de Moivre: (ux + i uy)^m, m-1 complex multiplies (m is an int member => uniform loop)
  (vx,vy) = (ux,uy); repeat m-1: (vx,vy) = (vx*ux - vy*uy, vx*uy + vy*ux)
  if Mirror: vy = Abs(vy)                      // dihedral symmetry; folding the circle onto a half circle is continuous
  return Source.Gen(seed, vx*R, vy*R, rho)     // circle of circumference 2*pi*R in source space, rho along the third axis

3D input: Cylindrical mode = same on (x,y), z passed through -> Source.Gen(seed, vx*R, vy*R, rho, z) (4D source). Spherical mode: d = p/|p| (3 comps), rho = Log(|p|)*a -> Source.Gen(seed, dx*R, dy*R, dz*R, rho); m-fold about z applies de Moivre to (dx,dy)/h with h = sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) and rescales by h, so poles stay continuous.
4D input: cylindrical on xy with z passed and w dropped (documented), or spherical on xyz.
No lattice; range unchanged (passes the source's range through).

[DrosteLift, domain-geometry] r2 = |p-c|^2 + e^2. r = sqrt(r2). L = .5*log(r2). Unit vector u = (p-c)/r needs no atan. Spiral: rotate u by Twist*L via sin, cos. Cylinder form: S3(K*L, K*ux, K*uy): locally conformal, features scale with r, seam-free because the angle is a circle in the source space. Droste form with log-period T: a = 2*pi*L/T, S4( (T/2pi)*K*cos a, (T/2pi)*K*sin a, K*ux, K*uy ), exactly repeating at each scale factor e^T when Twist*T = 2*pi*m, otherwise self-similar with rotation. N-fold: replace u by u^N through repeated complex multiply (fixed int count). 3D input: S4(K*L, K*nx, K*ny, K*nz) with n = unit direction; 3D Droste would need 5D, so drop it there.
master.why_new: Nothing in the graph can produce radial, spiral or scale-invariant structure; DomainWarp only bends locally. The classic obstacle (polar mapping has a seam at theta = pi unless the source is periodic) disappears by sampling the source on an embedded circle instead of an angle, the same trick GenTileable2D uses, and the m-fold symmetry comes from complex powers so arbitrary m is exact and continuous. One source evaluation.
master.simd_plan: Branch-free: Sqrt/Reciprocal, Log, one Sin+Cos, m-1 complex multiplies (uniform int loop), one Abs/Select. ~25-30 ops + the source at one dimension higher. 2D cost ~0.3x Perlin + Perlin3D (2.2 ns) => ~2.5 ns; 3D ~0.4 ns + Perlin4D (4.3 ns). GenT works for the shared part; per-dimension overloads choose cylindrical vs spherical.
master.continuity: C-infinity wherever the source is, except the single centre point (log diverges, direction undefined; MinRadius clamps it). Mirror adds C0 creases along the m mirror lines by design.
master.params: RadialMode enum, RadialScale float, AngularRadius float, Twist hybrid (spatially varying twist gives swirls that stay seam-free), Symmetry int, Mirror bool, MinRadius float, Mode3D {Cylindrical, Spherical}. Centre via DomainOffset upstream.
master.risks:
Log mode aliases near the centre (features below pixel size): clamp with MinRadius or fade. Large m compresses angular features; users must raise R. 4D input cannot be made tileable in all four axes.
[DrosteLift, domain-geometry] Hero object, not stationary. Features at the core shrink below pixel size: control by e. Requires a higher dimension source and 3D Droste plus 4D input are not supported, so GenTileable falls back to dropping dims or reduces to the cylinder form. Far coords collapse to nearly constant (expected, log compression).
[DomainLogPolar, signal-phase] Needs a D+1-dimensional source (a 2D image needs a 3D-capable source: fine for all lattice noises, not for user 2D-only sources). The seamless Twist constraint is subtle. Centre-dependent, so not stationary: it is a design tool, not a terrain base.
master.cost_note: 2D cost ~0.3x Perlin + Perlin3D (2.2 ns) => ~2.5 ns; 3D ~0.4 ns + Perlin4D (4.3 ns).
master.variant_notes: Circle embedding removes the seam without atan2. Options merged: complex-power p-fold symmetry and mirror, Twist spirals, exact Droste by a torus lift, axis chirps, and an Unwrap mode with true angle so lattice sources wrap as arches and fans.

queue.name: DomainTwist
queue.reason: Axis twist with falloff at ~0.3 ns for helical caves and vortex columns. Trivial and missing from the graph.

master.one_liner: Rotate the plane perpendicular to an axis by an angle that grows along the axis (twist), decays with radius (swirl/vortex column) or grows with w (continuous spin, exact loop): helical caves, tornado funnels, barber poles, spinning fields.
master.look: Twist a TubeNoise or TPMSNoise about Y: helical tunnels and screw-shaped sponge; twist CrystalGrainNoise: twisted columnar crystals; with Radius: a tornado/whirlpool funnel where only the core rotates; Axis=W: slowly rotating cloud banks that loop. 2D: vortex-swirled noise around a point.
master.algorithm:
Axis enum (X/Y/Z/W). Let s = coordinate along the axis, (u,v) the perpendicular pair (for Axis=W rotate (x,y) or a chosen plane), r2 = u^2 + v^2.
 falloff = (Radius > 0) ? Exp(-r2 / Radius^2) : 1
 theta = Rate * s * falloff + Swirl * falloff + Angle(p)   // Angle hybrid, Rate per unit along axis, Swirl constant vortex term
 (u', v') = (u cos theta - v sin theta, u sin theta + v cos theta)
Pass s and remaining coords through. 2D: Axis is implicitly the out-of-plane axis, so only the Swirl/Angle terms act (vortex around origin, or around per-lane Center X/Y hybrids). Axis=W in 4D: theta = Rate*w gives a field spinning about the axis, looping exactly with period 2pi/Rate.
master.why_new: DomainRotate and DomainRotatePlane take constant angles; an angle varying with position cannot be built from existing nodes (hybrid angles would rotate about the origin unboundedly, which the falloff and the axis-relative formulation here avoid). Cost is negligible.
master.simd_plan: One Sin/Cos (+ one Exp with falloff) and 6 FMAs; DomainModifiers pattern with per-dimension Gen. Negligible cost (~0.3 ns).
master.continuity: C-infinity in the warp (so output as smooth as the source).
master.params: Axis enum, Rate, Swirl, Radius (0 = none), Angle hybrid, Center X/Y/Z hybrids.
master.risks: Twist without falloff makes displacement grow with radius from the axis, so far-off-axis features shear into streaks (that is what twist is; document Radius). Modest novelty compared with the other proposals; cheap enough to justify.
master.cost_note: Negligible cost (~0.3 ns).

queue.name: Oscillator
queue.reason: Sine-of-noise with PWM, skew and Chebyshev modes: the common missing modifier at one source plus 1-2 Sin. PWM hatching is the new bit.

master.one_liner: Missing sine-of-noise modifier, with pulse-width modulation for engraving hatches, skew for dune profiles, trig-free Chebyshev mode and a local Nyquist guard.
master.look:
Tested. PWM hatch on warped carrier gives banknote or woodcut line engraving where line width encodes a second noise, and is unlike anything on the sheet. Skew gives asymmetric dune or ripple relief in the hillshade. Sine and Chebyshev give the classic sine-of-noise contour family (Chebyshev T12 is visually near sine-of-noise, its value is cost and exact bounds).
[Oscillator, signal-phase] Oscillator(Add(axis ramp, k*fbm)) = marble; Oscillator(fbm, F=10) = topographic contour hatching; Oscillator(DistanceToPoint) = rings; Pulse with Duty = CellularValue gives per-cell stripe widths; Harmonics on Simplex gives sharper, more 'volcanic' bumps. Also the standard way to render any Phase output as stripes.
master.algorithm:
phi=Freq*S(p)+Phase. Waves: Sine: Sin(phi). Triangle: from fract. Skew: Sin(phi+Skew*Sin(phi)), a one-step Kepler solution that morphs sine toward saw with steep lee and gentle stoss slopes. Pulse: Clamp((Sin(phi)+Duty(p))/Edge,-1,1), so Duty is a hybrid and any node becomes line width: halftone engraving. Chebyshev: T_k(clamp(S)) by recurrence T_{n+1}=2x*T_n-T_{n-1}, with exactly k zero crossings in [-1,1], no trig, and bounded by 1.
Optional Band Guard: forward-difference S, local freq=Freq*|g|, multiply output by Exp(-(freq/limit)^2) to fade instead of alias.

[Oscillator, signal-phase] x = Frequency*src(p) + PhaseOffset(hybrid). t = x - floor(x). Waveform enum: Sine -> sin(2pi t) via FS::Sin or a 5th-order poly on t; Triangle -> 1-4|t-0.5|; Saw -> 2t-1 softened by s = smoothstep(1-Edge,1,t): out = lerp(2t-1, -1, s) (C0 for Edge>0); Pulse -> 2*smoothstep(Duty-Soft, Duty+Soft, t)-1 with Hybrid Duty (PWM: stripe width from another noise) and the symmetric drop at t=1 handled by min(smoothstep up, 1-smoothstep(1-Soft...)); Harmonics -> clamp(src,-1,1)=u, out = a1*u + a2*(2u^2-1) + a3*(4u^3-3u) (Chebyshev T2,T3: adds 2nd/3rd harmonics to any noise without extra evals, sharpening ridges or flattening plateaus). Optional 'Steps' int quantises t before the waveform (quantised phase bands).
master.why_new: Confirmed in sources: FS::Sin appears only in SineWave (position-only) and the tiling map; no node applies a wave to a source. So this family is currently unreachable other than PingPong's fractal fold. A dedicated node is justified by that gap, and by Duty and Band Guard, which a graph cannot do.
master.simd_plan: Branch free. 1 source + 1-2 Sin: about 1x source + 1-2 ns estimated. Chebyshev k=12 is 24 mul-adds. Band Guard adds D source evals and Exp. All dimensions.
master.continuity: C-infinity on smooth sources for Sine and Skew when |Skew|<1; C0 for Triangle and Pulse with Edge>0; a hard square is discontinuous.
master.params: Wave enum. Hybrid: Frequency, Phase, Duty, Skew. Float: Edge, Guard Limit. Int: Chebyshev Order.
master.risks:
Close to a one-liner in its base form, so the argument for it rests on opening the whole family. Stripe width is uneven in base mode (use IsoBands for constant width). Chebyshev bands crowd near +-1 and clip when the source exceeds its range, so the source must be well normalised.
[Bands, dcc-tools] Close to a one-liner for Sine; the case for a dedicated node is the missing primitive plus Strata. High Frequency on steep sources aliases; no constant-width guarantee, which needs a gradient.
master.cost_note: 1 source + 1-2 Sin: about 1x source + 1-2 ns estimated.
master.variant_notes: Enabler for the sin-of-noise family: FS::Sin is otherwise only in SineWave and the tiling map. Bands (dcc) contributes the recipe view: Marble, Wood, Agate.

queue.name: SplineRemap
queue.reason: Minecraft-style Hermite shaper with hybrid knots (J1 top pick), very high demand. Hybrid knots always run for all lanes, so cost must be documented.

master.one_liner: Arbitrary cubic Hermite curve over a source, with knot values that can themselves be subgraphs: Minecraft-style nested terrain shaping and N-way fade.
master.look: Any transfer curve: coast shelf, mesa plateau, plains-to-mountain profile, tiers. As a mixer: smooth interpolation across N biome sources by one control. Not prototyped as it is standard math.
master.algorithm:
Knots i in 0..N-1 (N<=8): Location (float, sorted), Value (hybrid), Slope (float). x = Coordinate(p). Fixed loop over segments, picking per lane with Select: mask_i = x >= loc_i. For the chosen segment: dx = x1-x0, t = (x-x0)*rcp(dx) (reciprocal precomputed at set), dy = y1-y0, a = m0*dx - dy, b = -m1*dx + dy, out = lerp(y0,y1,t) + t*(1-t)*lerp(a,b,t). Outside the range: linear extrapolation with end slopes, or clamp. Nested: Value input can be another SplineRemap with a different Coordinate, giving a multi-parameter table like continentalness x erosion x weirdness.

[SplineBlend, libs-modifiers] c = Coordinate(p). Knots k[0..N-1] are constant floats (sorted when set) and V[i] hybrid. i from masks: for j in 1..N-2: m = c >= k[j]; lo = Select(m, k[j], lo); hi = Select(m, k[j+1], hi), and similarly for values. t = sat((c - lo) / (hi - lo)). Interp: Linear, Smooth (quintic with zero tangents, so plateaus and libnoise Select style falloff are just repeated values), MonotoneCubic (Fritsch-Carlson tangents precomputed when all V are constants; no overshoot, unlike libnoise Curve) or limited Catmull-Rom for hybrid V. out = interpolation of V[i], V[i+1]. Before evaluating a hybrid V[j], test whether any lane uses a segment touching j with FS::AnyMask; if not, skip it. A nested SplineBlend as V[j] gives multi-parameter terrain shaping, e.g. continentalness, then erosion, then ridges.
master.why_new: Remap is linear, Terrace is uniform steps, Fade is one lerp; an arbitrary curve needs many chained nodes and still cannot do Hermite tangents. Minecraft's whole overworld shaper (offset/factor/jaggedness) is nested splines over 3 noises; with hybrid y_i this node reproduces it directly (coordinate = continents, each point's value = a spline over erosion, etc.).
master.simd_plan: Under 8 knots: N compares + Selects, about 1-2 ns constant-value case. Per-batch rather than per-lane skipping, so it honours the data-parallel rule and output is bit-identical to no skip. Up to 2 hybrids per lane matter, but a batch straddling segments evaluates each used hybrid once. GenT dimension agnostic.
master.continuity: C1 across knots by construction when knot values are constant. With hybrid values, smoothness inherits them, still C0 minimum. Loc spacing near zero is guarded at set time.
master.params: Coordinate (source), Knot Count, Knot N Location, Knot N Value (hybrid), Knot N Slope, Extrapolate enum.
master.risks:
Metadata has no dynamic arrays, so 8 fixed slots clutter the node UI. Skip saves nothing on incoherent lanes (GenPositionArray) or lanes straddling knots. Catmull-Rom with hybrid values needs up to 4 values per segment, which reduces the skip gain. Overlaps Remap, Fade and Terrace semantically, so naming should explain why it exists. Knot positions as constants (not hybrid) are needed for tangent precompute and skipping.
[SplineCurve, terrain-tools-engines] Node-editor UI for arrays of points; sorted-x invariant; 16 hybrid sources is a lot of metadata; Extrapolation choice matters because noise outputs exceed [-1,1] after fractals.
master.cost_note: Under 8 knots: N compares + Selects, about 1-2 ns constant-value case.
master.variant_notes: Knot values may be hybrids, enabling Minecraft-style nested splines and N-way mix. Batch-level skipping of unused hybrids keeps output bit-identical.

queue.name: Stamp
queue.reason: Origin-centred analytic profiles, so stamp-scatter and quad-stamp work with no source graph. Dull alone; keep the enum small or split it.

master.one_liner: An origin-centred analytic shape generator (crater, ring, ripple, cone, dome, gaussian, superellipse/boulder, star/polygon, dune, capsule/ribbon, torus) with seed-driven per-instance variation, designed to be the Source of Scatter but usable alone.
master.look: A single crater/ring/boulder/star at the origin; through Scatter these become lunar surfaces with rims and ejecta, raindrop ripple fields, boulder scatters, starfish/sea-urchin patterns, dune fields, broken-rock rubble. The Chebyshev angular term gives spoked craters and n-fold stars without atan2.
master.algorithm:
Input p in local coords, radius 1 = stamp edge. r2 = dot(p,p) in d dims, r = sqrt(r2). Per-instance variation: h = HashPrimes(seed, 0): depth' = Depth*(1 + Variation*rnd11(h)), etc. (the seed differs per instance when driven from Scatter).
Profiles (enum), all defined for any d because they use r only unless noted:
- Crater: bowl = -depth'*(1 - r2/rimR^2) for r<rimR; rim = rimH*exp(-((r-1)/rimW)^2); ejecta = ejH*exp(-(r-1)*ejK) for r>1 (clipped by Scatter envelope); value = Select(r<rimR, bowl, 0) + rim + ejecta. Optional rays: angular term rayA*max(0,cos(n*theta))^8 using cos(n theta) via Chebyshev recurrence from ct = p.x/r, st = p.y/r (no atan2): c1=ct, c2=2ct^2-1, c_{k+1}=2ct c_k - c_{k-1}, n fixed small int; 3D uses the xz or xy plane for theta.
- Ring: exp(-((r-r0)/w)^2). Ripple: cos(2*pi*f*r + phase(h)) * (1-r2)^2. Cone: 1-r. Dome: sqrt(max(0,1-r2)). Gaussian: exp(-k r2).
- Boulder: superellipsoid |x/a|^e + |y/b|^e (+|z/c|^e) via Pow with e in [2,6], then perturb radius by low harmonics: rEff = r*(1 + A*(rnd11 * c2 + rnd11 * c3)) using the same cos recurrence; value = 1 - rEff (an approximate SDF, negative outside). Axis ratios a,b,c from the hash (per instance).
- Polygon/Star (2D plane in any d): regular n-gon SDF: fold angle without atan2 is hard, so use 'cos(n theta) modulated radius' instead: rStar = 1 + Spike*cos(n theta) (star) or the Minkowski-like polygon approximation max_k dot(p, dir_k) over n fixed directions (n <= 8, fixed loop) which is exact and needs no trig at Gen time (dir table built at param set).
- Dune: asymmetric along local x: windward = smoothstep(-1,0,x)-ish slope, slip face = 1 - smoothstep(0,SlipLen,x); multiply by a Gaussian across y (and z).
- Capsule/Ribbon: segment from (-L,0) to (L,0), d = distance to segment, value = 1 - d/w (clamped), or gaussian across. L*s must respect Scatter's rAllow (Scatter can read nothing from its source, so document, or add a 'Max Local Radius' float the artist sets on Scatter).
- Torus (3D/4D): sqrt((rxy - R)^2 + z^2) < w.
Output in [-1,1] by analytic range per profile.
master.why_new: DistanceToPoint gives only a radial distance; everything with a rim, an asymmetric profile, an anisotropic body or an angular lobe needs ~6 nodes of Remap/Abs/Multiply per shape and still has no per-instance variation. A shape library with seed-driven variation is what turns Scatter from 'tiled Perlin blobs' into a crater/rock tool. Standalone it is also the natural 'single feature' node (one volcano, one island) that currently does not exist.
master.simd_plan: Pure arithmetic on p, no lattice, no window: ~20-60 ops depending on profile (Pow/Exp for superellipse and rims). All profiles are enum-switched at the node level (one Gen per profile via a template parameter or a static dispatch when the enum is set) so Gen is branch free. 3D and 4D trivially share the radial code; angular profiles pick a fixed plane. Cost ~0.3-1x Perlin. Combined with Scatter Fast window in 2D: ~4 + 4x0.5 ns.
master.continuity: Profile dependent: Crater/Ring/Ripple/Gaussian/Dome C1 (Dome C0 at the edge), Cone C0 at the apex, Boulder SDF C0 along the superellipse ridge, Polygon via max of dots is C0 at vertices. Variation is per seed so it never changes within one instance.
master.params: Profile enum, Depth, Rim Height, Rim Width, Ejecta Height/Decay, Ring Radius/Width, Frequency (ripple), Exponent (superellipse), Lobes int (star/polygon/rays), Spike, Aspect X/Y/Z, Length (capsule), Slip Length (dune), Variation (0..1, fraction of each parameter randomised by seed). Few should be hybrid: Depth and Lobes could be, the rest are per-stamp constants.
master.risks: Large enum surface; keep each profile's parameter set small or split into 2-3 nodes (StampRadial, StampBoulder, StampAngular). Pow for superellipse is expensive; e=2 and e=4 fast paths. The capsule length and ejecta decay can poke outside Scatter's radius budget: Scatter's envelope clips them (slight truncation), acceptable.
master.cost_note: Cost ~0.3-1x Perlin. Combined with Scatter Fast window in 2D: ~4 + 4x0.5 ns.

queue.name: StreakSmear
queue.reason: One-sided decaying taps for rust runs and drips, K x source along a straight direction. Only banding at long lengths needs a look.

master.one_liner: One-sided decaying multi-tap of a Source along a direction (mean, max or min), the pointwise equivalent of 'directional blur / streaks': rust runs below bolts, water stains, drips, wind-blown snow and brushed smears from any blotchy noise.
master.look: Vertical rusty tails under spots, drip trails that fade, rain-stain streaks on walls, snow or sand drifted onto one side of bumps, motion-blurred noise. The sheet has only isotropic patterns; nothing has one-sided directional structure.
master.algorithm:
Params: Direction per axis (floats; 'down' = (0,-1)), Length L (hybrid, world units), Taps K (int, 2..16), Decay w (0..1), Mode {Mean, Max, Min, Accumulate}, Threshold T (Accumulate), Source.
h = L/K; for k = 0..K-1: s_k = Source(p - k*h*dir) (samples taken upstream along the direction, so a spot at position c influences points downstream of it). Mean: sum w^k s_k / sum w^k (soft smear). Max: max_k (s_k - k*Fall) (a bright spot carries a fading streak below it: drips). Min: symmetric for dark stains. Accumulate: sum_k w^k max(0, s_k - T) normalised (streak intensity from the amount of 'dirt source' above). Output through ScaleOutput.
Use with Direction derived from gravity in texture space; for a terrain, use (0,0,-1) in 3D to streak down slopes of a volumetric field, or feed Direction from DomainRotate upstream. Combining Max mode on CellularDensity Coverage (rivet pits) gives rust streaks whose length is per-spot random when Length is a hybrid CellularValue.
master.why_new: DomainWarp and DomainAxisScale stretch a field symmetrically; a graph cannot sample a Source at a fixed set of offset positions and combine them. The symmetric ring stencil already prototyped (dcc_lens mode 18) blurs/dilates isotropically; the one-sided decaying kernel is what makes gravity effects.
master.simd_plan: Fixed loop of K Source evaluations at offset positions (positions computed by FMA), accumulate with mask-free arithmetic; GenT over the pack. Cost K x Source (K=8 on Perlin 2D: ~9 ns). 2D/3D/4D trivially; tiling is preserved if the offsets are applied before the torus mapping (they are, since it is a Source position offset).
master.continuity: C0 whenever the Source is C0 (finite sum/max of continuous functions).
master.params: Direction (per-axis floats), Length (hybrid), Taps (int), Decay, Fall, Threshold, Mode enum, Source.
master.risks: Visible banding with few taps and long Length (K must grow with L/feature size); Max mode with Fall = 0 produces hard-edged drips (sometimes wanted). Overlaps conceptually with the ring stencil idea; could be merged as a 'Directional' kernel enum on that node.
master.cost_note: Cost K x Source (K=8 on Perlin 2D: ~9 ns).

queue.name: StencilFilter
queue.reason: K-tap blur, sharpen, erode, dilate and peak mask with rotated taps. PeakMargin is the valuable mode; absorbs rank-taps and local-rank.

master.one_liner: K-tap ring/star stencil over any source with modes Mean (blur), HighPass, Sharpen, Dilate, Erode, Range (morphological gradient), PeakMargin / PitMargin (extract local maxima/minima as blue-noise dots), Roughness (variance) and LocalNormalize (local AGC).
master.look:
PeakMargin on a one-octave Simplex gives scattered convex blobs centred on the noise maxima (proto sheetC m2): a Poisson-disk-like scatter mask whose spacing is set by the source frequency and whose blob size by r, with no lattice (local maxima of band-limited noise repel). On FBm it gives summit caps (snow caps, hilltop vegetation); on -CellularDistance it marks cell centres. Range is an edge detector that turns any field into outlines; Mean of Checkerboard/CellularValue is a proper box blur; LocalNormalize flattens the amplitude of a warped or fractal field so its busy-ness is uniform (sheetB m8). Dilate/Erode fatten or thin any mask by r.
[LocalStatistics, signal-phase] Mean of White at R: soft grainy cloud (a true isotropic low-pass of white noise, different in character from any lattice noise); Max of CellularDistance: rounded pebble tops; Min of thresholded fbm: eroded archipelagos with margins; Range of Perlin: crease web; RMS of PhasorNoise: the stripe envelope (blotches where stripes are strong). Band-split: src - Mean(src) isolates the fine band of any graph.
master.algorithm:
Params: Source; Radius r (hybrid); Taps enum {Star 2D taps on the axes, Corners 2^D, Ring8 (2D) / Cuboctahedron12 (3D)}; Rotation (hybrid, 2D angle; 3D: rotate about a fixed axis) to de-lattice the stencil continuously; Mode; Amount; Width.
GenT: v0 = S(pos); for k in 0..K-1: v_k = S(pos + r * R(theta) u_k) where u_k are compile-time unit offsets and R is the per-lane rotation built from (cos,sin) of the hybrid angle.
  Mean      = (v0 + sum v_k) / (K+1)
  HighPass  = v0 - Mean ; Sharpen = v0 + Amount * (v0 - Mean)
  Dilate    = max(v0, max_k v_k) ; Erode = min(...) ; Range = Dilate - Erode
  PeakMargin= (v0 - max_k v_k) / Width, clamp [-1,1]  // > 0 only within ~r/2 of a local maximum of S
  PitMargin = (min_k v_k - v0) / Width
  Roughness = sqrt(mean((v - Mean)^2)) -> VariableRange
  LocalNormalize = (v0 - Mean) / (Roughness + eps) * 0.5
max/min run as FS::Max/Min over the unrolled taps; no per-lane loop count differences.

[NeighbourhoodFilter, terrain-landforms] Stencil: centre plus 2*dim axis points at +-eps (Slope, Laplacian), optionally a ring of S points at Radius (S=8 in 2D, 12-26 in 3D) for Mean/Min/Max/TPI. Slope = |(S(p+eps e_i) - S(p-eps e_i))/(2eps)| over i; Laplacian = sum_i (S+ + S- - 2S0)/eps^2 (negative = convex ridge, positive = concave hollow); TPI = S0 - mean(ring); Range = max(ring) - min(ring); Relative Height = (S0 - min)/(Range) in [0,1]. Output scaled by a user Gain and clamped to [-1,1]. Typical terrain uses: Fade(detail, 0, smoothstep(curvature)) deposits fine 'sediment' noise only in hollows; Multiply(rock texture, slope mask); Remap relative height to carve only upper slopes (free-face/talus split).
master.why_new: Min/max over shifted copies is possible with Max/Min + DomainOffset nodes (8 DomainOffset + 7 Max for one ring), but nobody will build it; the dedicated node is 1 node with a hybrid radius, and the PeakMargin / LocalNormalize modes need the whole tap set at once (variance, max and centre share taps). PeakMargin in particular is a cheap blue-noise scatter generator that needs no point lattice and inherits the correlation structure of whatever source you give it, which no existing node offers.
master.simd_plan: Taps are compile-time constant offset tables per dimension (Star: 2D entries, Corners: 2^D, Ring8/Cubocta12); the rotation is applied with 4 FMAs per tap in 2D. Cost = (1+K) x source: Star 2D/3D/4D = 5/7/9 taps, Corners 5/9/17, Ring 9/13/-. Perlin+Ring 2D ~10 ns, 3D Cubocta ~29 ns; FBm Simplex x5 2D ~60 ns. 4D works with Star/Corners sets. Dilate/Erode of a hard mask at radius r needs at least the Ring set or it looks square.
master.continuity: Mean/HighPass/Sharpen/LocalNormalize: C0 for C0 sources. Dilate/Erode/Range/Margins: C0 (min/max of continuous functions) but C1 breaks where the arg-max tap switches. A rotation hybrid that is itself C0 keeps everything C0; a hashed per-cell rotation would not (so it is not offered).
master.params: Source; Radius (hybrid: distance-dependent blur, or a mask that only dilates in one biome); Rotation (hybrid: feed a low-frequency noise to randomise stencil orientation continuously); Taps; Mode; Amount (Sharpen); Width (margins); Eps (LocalNormalize); VariableRange.
master.risks:
Sparse-tap blur of a high-frequency source aliases (K taps cannot integrate a field with features smaller than the tap spacing); document 'Radius <= 2 x source feature size' or combine with SuperSample. Blur is not Gaussian; an N-fold blur is not affordable (taps^N). LocalNormalize can amplify float noise in flat regions, hence the eps.
[StencilFilter, lit-recent] Cost multiplies the source; Radius must match the feature scale and the intended octave of detail; finite differences on discontinuous sources (Cellular value) give spikes.
sources: World Machine / Gaea / Houdini HeightField Mask by Feature (slope, curvature, TPI style masks; general knowledge, no URL consulted)
master.cost_note: Cost = (1+K) x source: Star 2D/3D/4D = 5/7/9 taps, Corners 5/9/17, Ring 9/13/-. Perlin+Ring 2D ~10 ns, 3D Cubocta ~29 ns; FBm Simplex x5 2D ~60 ns.
master.variant_notes: Fixed-tap neighbourhood statistics: blur, sharpen, erode, dilate, range, RMS envelope, TPI, plus PeakMargin, which extracts local maxima as a blue-noise-like scatter mask with no lattice.

queue.name: RayMarch
queue.reason: N x source march along a direction or added axis. FirstHit turns 3D noise into 2D cliffs; shadow and AO outputs cover horizon-shadow.

master.one_liner: Fixed-count march of a source along a direction (or along an added dimension): projected density, Beer-Lambert transmittance, or soft first-hit depth giving the heightfield of a 3D isosurface (cliffs and mesas).
master.look:
Mean along an in-plane direction: directional smear / motion-blur streaks. Mean/Transmittance along the extra axis: 2D map of the thickness of a 3D cloud volume, with the characteristic smoother-yet-holey cloud layer look and Beer-law contrast. FirstHit along the extra axis with a 3D fBm: the top surface of a 3D isosurface seen from above: flat-topped mesas, vertical cliffs, arches hidden, canyon mazes; a heightfield that 2D noise can never produce because its walls are vertical and organic (Terrace walls are value-aligned, not shape-aligned).
[FirstHitHeight, dynamics-iteration] Verified in prototype. Smooth rolling surfaces cut by vertical drop edges along overhang silhouettes, flat-topped plateaus and floating-island outlines with sharp contour-like cliffs. Low Bias gives more 3D holes, high Bias gets close to plain noise. Good for cliffs and mesas in a 2D heightmap, canyon lands, layered strata with bias stacking, and masks for overhang placement.
master.algorithm:
Source S; Axis enum: Direction (in-plane vector, same dimension) or Extra (march along an added coordinate: a d-dim node evaluates S in d+1 dims, exactly AddDimension semantics; not available for 4D nodes).
  T = 1; acc = 0; depth = 0
  for k in 0..N-1:
      s = S(q_k) where q_k = p + (Start + k*h)*dir  (Extra: (p, Start + k*h))
      Mean          : acc += s
      Transmittance : acc += max(0, s - Thresh)
      FirstHit      : a = smoothstep(Thresh - soft, Thresh + soft, s); depth += T*(k*h); T *= (1 - a)   // expected depth of first crossing
  Mean: acc/N ; Transmittance: exp(-Density*h*acc) ; FirstHit: depth + T*(N*h)  (remapped)
Step lengths may grow geometrically (h*g^k) to reach far cheaply.
master.why_new: N offset evaluations with running products/maxima cannot be built in-graph except by N chained DomainOffset/Add/Multiply nodes. FirstHit in particular turns FastNoise's strong 3D noises into a new class of 2D terrains. One node, three modes, dimension-agnostic in Direction mode.
master.simd_plan: Fixed N loop, one source eval per step plus a few FMAs; FirstHit uses only multiplies (no masks). Cost = N x source: N=16 with Simplex3D as the extra-axis source: ~35 ns for a 2D node; with FBm-4 Simplex ~140 ns; Direction mode 2D Perlin N=8: ~9 ns. Extra mode: implement 2D->3D and 3D->4D overloads; 4D node falls back to Direction mode (document it). Tiling: Direction mode preserves GenTileable2D; Extra mode cannot tile (needs 5D).
master.continuity: Mean/Transmittance: same class as the source (C0+). FirstHit: continuous for finite Softness (product of smooth factors), tending to jump discontinuities at vertical walls as Softness -> 0, which is the intended cliff look.
master.params: Source (GeneratorSource), Mode enum (Mean/Transmittance/FirstHit), Axis enum (Direction/Extra), Direction X/Y/Z/W hybrids, Steps int, StepLen float, StepGrowth float, Start float, Threshold hybrid, Softness float, Density float, VariableRange.
master.risks:
Cost for fractal sources; FirstHit needs enough steps to resolve small features (aliasing of thin walls); Extra mode breaks the 4D/tiling story.
[FirstHitHeight, dynamics-iteration] Pinholes at low Steps; the 3D form needs a 4D source so is costly; a true 4D form changes the semantics. Volumetric lit-cloud output was tested as an alternative and was not visibly worth its N*M cost, so stick to height.
master.cost_note: Cost = N x source: N=16 with Simplex3D as the extra-axis source: ~35 ns for a 2D node; with FBm-4 Simplex ~140 ns; Direction mode 2D Perlin N=8: ~9 ns.
master.variant_notes: FirstHit along an added axis is the distinctive mode: 3D isosurface top as a heightfield with organic vertical cliffs. Cannot tile, because the extra axis needs a 5th dimension in the 4D path.

master.one_liner: Fixed-count ray march of a source treated as a heightfield (2D) or density (3D) along a light direction: cast shadows (horizon test), horizon-based ambient occlusion over M directions, or Beer-Lambert transmittance for clouds.
master.look:
Shadow (proto sheetA m3): hard-edged dark regions trailing every hill in the light direction, length set by elevation; Lit adds the Lambert term and reads like a lit relief map with cast shadows. AO (m4, also with only 4 directions x 5 steps): valleys and the base of slopes darken, crests stay bright: a 'wetness / sediment' mask that is not a slope mask. Transmittance on a 3D FBm gives self-shadowed cloud densities. Nothing on the sheet is non-local in a direction; hillshade is purely local.
[HorizonShelter, graph-meta-filters] Asymmetric masks: flat fully exposed plateaus on one side of each hill and ramped, elongated lee shadows on the other. Used for snow drifts, moss on sheltered sides, tree-line bias, directional weathering, baked hillshade. SkyView gives a soft crevice and hollow mask.
master.algorithm:
Params: Source; Steps N (int, same for all lanes); Step Size s0 (hybrid); Step Growth g (geometric spacing); Direction X/Y[/Z] and Elevation (hybrids); Height Scale a; Softness; Mode {Shadow, Lit (Shadow x Lambert), AO, Transmittance}; Directions M (AO).
Shadow (2D): h0 = a*S(pos); best = -inf; t = s0; repeat N: h = a*S(pos + t*L); best = max(best, h - h0 - t*tanEl); t *= g.  shadow = sat(best / Softness). out = 1 - shadow (or Lit = out * sat(0.5 + 0.5 * dot(grad, L)) using 2D extra taps).
AO: for m in 0..M-1 with directions at angle 2 pi m / M (+ fixed phase): horizon_m = max over N steps of (h - h0)/t ; occ += horizon / sqrt(1 + horizon^2); out = 1 - occ / M.
Transmittance (3D): T = exp(-k * sum_n max(0, S(pos + t_n L)) * dt_n); out = 2T - 1. In 3D the Shadow mode is the same march with max replaced by the sum, so all modes share one loop.
4D: L has a w component of 0; the march is in xyz, so tileable 2D works.
master.why_new: A shadow is a max over many samples displaced along a line; as a graph that is N DomainOffsets + N Subtract + N Max chains per direction and it still would not expose a per-lane direction. Cast shadows and AO are the two masks terrain artists most often bake offline; here they are pointwise, seed-stable and infinite, and the hybrid light direction makes them animatable.
master.simd_plan:
Loop count N (and M) is a member int, so the loop is uniform across lanes; body is 1 source eval + a few FMAs and a Max. Cost = (1 + N*M) x source (+ 2D taps for Lit). Shadow N=8 with FBm Simplex x5: 2D ~ 9 x 6.5 ~ 60 ns, 3D ~ 120 ns. AO 4x5 = 21 taps: 2D ~140 ns, 3D ~280 ns. Geometric step growth (g = 1.5) lets 8 steps cover 25 step sizes so long shadows are affordable. 4D is the 3D march with w fixed.
[HorizonShelter, graph-meta-filters] M+1 taps: 9 at M=8, in any dimension: Perlin 10/20/39 ns. SkyView 19 taps in 2D, only sensible in 2D. Fixed march, max and min only, no per-lane early out.
master.continuity: C0 (proto c0ratio 7.95 shadow, 8.0 AO): max of continuous functions plus a soft clamp; the horizon arg-max switching between steps gives mild C1 kinks that read as shadow terminators. Sparse geometric steps can let a thin ridge slip between samples, producing small gaps in long shadows (a classic sparse-march artefact).
master.params: Source; Steps N; Step Size (hybrid: distance LOD); Growth; Light Dir X/Y/Z + Elevation (hybrids: a time-driven direction sweeps shadows); Height Scale; Softness; Mode; Directions M; VariableRange.
master.risks:
Cost scales with N x M x octaves and users will set N=32; expose a sane max and show cost in the editor. Softness is in height units, so it needs retuning when Height Scale changes (derive Softness from Height Scale x Step Size internally). Shadows from features outside the march range are missing, which is fine for texture work.
[HorizonShelter, graph-meta-filters] Narrow peaks fall between taps at large R, so M should scale with R times source frequency. Output heavily saturates unless gain is matched to the source. It is more of a mask than a shape generator. Tileable direction issue as with other directional nodes.
sources: Max, N. Horizon mapping: shadows for bump-mapped surfaces, The Visual Computer 1988 (recalled, not fetched)
master.cost_note: Cost = (1 + N*M) x source (+ 2D taps for Lit). Shadow N=8 with FBm Simplex x5: 2D ~ 9 x 6.5 ~ 60 ns, 3D ~ 120 ns.
master.variant_notes: Shadow, AO, sky view, and Sx wind shelter, all a horizon march. Geometric step growth reaches far cheaply at the price of possible gaps behind thin ridges.

master.one_liner: Rank filter via a sorting network over taps, with a hybrid rank morphing smoothly from erode through median to dilate.
master.look: On CellularValue: rounded-corner pebble mosaics with plates eating into each other per rank. On FBm: rounded peaks or narrowed crests. On hard masks: corners round and specks vanish, without the blur a soft filter would bring.
master.algorithm: Fixed K=9 stencil: centre plus 4 at r plus 4 at 0.55r rotated by 45 degrees (3D: centre + 12 icosahedral directions). Sort with a min/max network: 25 exchanges for 9 inputs, or Paeth's 19 for median only. q = rank*(K-1); output lerp(v[floor q], v[floor q + 1], frac q), done per lane by sum of masked terms or 8 Selects. Median on a thresholded field approximates curvature motion of the level set (Merriman-Bence-Osher).
master.why_new: The only continuous morph between dilate and erode, painted by a hybrid. The only filter here that handles discontinuous sources gracefully, since its output is always one of the actual values, so cell values stay crisp. Plain Min and Max of taps are the two end ranks.
master.simd_plan: K taps + sorting network of min/max pairs, which is ideal for SIMD. 2D about 10 ns + 6 ns network on Perlin, more on Cellular (9 x 3.9 = 35 ns for rounded cells). 3D 13 taps about 29 ns + 10 ns network. Branch-free and identical across dimensions except for the table.
master.continuity: Inherits the source's class: C0 for continuous sources, since order statistics of continuous functions are continuous, with kinks. On discontinuous sources, jumps move and round but remain.
master.params: Rank (hybrid, 0 to 1), Radius r (hybrid), K enum, Source.
master.risks: Stair or polygon imprint on hard edges with only 9 taps, visible in the prototype. Weak visual effect on smooth single-octave sources. Radii past about half a feature start showing ghost copies at end ranks.
master.cost_note: 2D about 10 ns + 6 ns network on Perlin, more on Cellular (9 x 3.9 = 35 ns for rounded cells).

master.one_liner: Soft rank of the centre value among K fixed-offset probes of the source: a pointwise local histogram equalisation that removes trends, equalises contrast everywhere, and doubles as a scale-selective local-extremum mask.
master.look: On fBm: the large-scale tone is flattened and every region, including formerly dull low-contrast areas, shows full-range detail, like CLAHE on a photo; the output histogram is nearly flat. PeakMask gives a sparse, evenly spaced set of blobs at the local maxima of any source (spacing set by R), a blue-noise-like scatter derived from the terrain itself (trees on local tops, cities on local highs). Contrast mode gives a 'normalised detail' layer that never saturates.
master.algorithm:
Probe offsets o_k, k=1..K: a fixed deterministic set on the unit disc/ball (2D golden-angle spiral radii sqrt(k/K), 3D Fibonacci sphere x 2 shells, 4D 16 fixed points), scaled by Radius R (world units). K = 8 or 16 (compile-time constant or int param).
v0 = S(x); v_k = S(x + R o_k).
u = (1/K) * sum_k smoothstep( (v0 - v_k) / Softness + 0.5 )     // soft empirical CDF of the neighbourhood evaluated at v0
Modes: Rank: out = 2u - 1.  PeakMask: out = smoothstep((u - Threshold)/Edge) (u~1 means x is a local max at scale R).  Contrast: out = (v0 - mean_k v_k) / (std_k v_k + eps) (local z-score, same probes).
master.why_new: No node can see a neighbourhood; local extremum detection, detrending and adaptive contrast are not expressible (DomainOffset+Subtract gives one difference, not a rank). The rank is monotone-local, so it preserves the topology of level sets within a radius while fixing the global statistics; the peak mask gives feature placement that follows the terrain, unlike CellularDistance which ignores it.
master.simd_plan: Modifier evaluating the source K+1 times at fixed offsets (same offsets for all lanes), K smoothsteps and adds; cost = (K+1) x source (K=8 on Perlin 2D ~10 ns). Int K from an enum {8,16} to keep loops lane-uniform. Dimension agnostic apart from the offset tables (one table per dimension).
master.continuity: Same class as the source (smoothstep is C1), continuous because the probe set is fixed per node, not per lane.
master.params: Source; Radius (world units); Softness (source units); Probes enum (8, 16); Mode enum (Rank, PeakMask, Contrast); Threshold, Edge.
master.risks: Expensive (9-17 source evals). The rank marginal is only approximately uniform because the centre is correlated with its probes (not exchangeable). A fixed probe pattern can imprint faint directional bias at scale R; 16 probes in a spiral reduce it. Do not stack on expensive fractals without GeneratorCache-style care.
master.cost_note: Modifier evaluating the source K+1 times at fixed offsets (same offsets for all lanes), K smoothsteps and adds; cost = (K+1) x source (K=8 on Perlin 2D ~10 ns).

queue.name: StochasticPatch
queue.reason: Simplex-vertex local frames with a variance-preserving blend: D+1 evals, the cheapest repetition breaker. Known technique, so a quick port is enough.

master.one_liner: Any node evaluated exactly dim+1 times per lane, in simplex-vertex local frames with variance-preserving or height-based blending: the cheapest way to scatter and to break repetition.
master.look:
SineWave becomes a bent, tangled zebra of rotated stripe patches; a plank pattern becomes herringbone chaos; crackle in Height mode becomes interlocked shard mosaics. Prototype with sine, plank and crackle each looked unlike the input and unlike anything on the sheet. Also the standard fix to a visibly periodic or strongly directional source.
[PatchTuft, texture-materials] Look-tested (m=9, Source = stretched fbm). Crisscrossing clumps of straw or brushed patches, tangle of grain direction. Strongly different from the sheet and stays contrasty because the blend does not wash out. Anisotropic Source sets the material: fibres, wood, wave ripples, sand ripple patches; AngleRange small gives subtle hair-flow variation.
master.algorithm:
skew p onto the simplex lattice (same skew constants as Simplex); find the simplex containing p and its D+1 vertices v_j with barycentric weights w_j (linear, sum 1)
  for j in 0..D: h = HashPrimes(v_j)
     off_j = rnd vector in [-OffsetRange, OffsetRange]^D
     R_j  = rotation from hash (2D: (c,s) = rndDir2(h); 3D: hashed unit quaternion; 4D: two hashed plane rotations), scaled by Rotation in [0,1] via slerp toward identity (precompute formula: angle*Rotation)
     sc_j = 2^(rnd11 * ScaleJitter)
     q_j = R_j * (p - v_j) * sc_j + v_j + off_j     // rotate/scale about the vertex so the patch stays near its lattice site
     X_j = Source(q_j)
  W = Sqrt(sum w_j^2)
  out = Mean + sum_j w_j (X_j - Mean) / W        // variance preserving (Heitz-Neyret), Mean param default 0
  optional Sharpen: out = Lerp(out, sign(out)*|out|^Sharpen, s) to restore contrast for non-Gaussian sources

[StochasticPatch, stamp-scatter] Simplex-skew lattice as in Simplex noise: find containing simplex, giving dim+1 vertices, each with weight a = max(0, 0.5-|d|^2)^2 and hash h. For each vertex: frame rotation R(h) and offset O(h); v_i = Source.Gen(seed or h_i, R(h)*p + O(h)). Note that the frame is global at that vertex, not stamp-local: copies are continuous rotated patches of a globally defined pattern. Weights w_i = a_i^Sharpness / sum. Blend Variance mode: sum(w v)/sqrt(sum w^2) (Heitz-Neyret histogram-preserving form). Height mode: w_i = a_i*(1+H*v_i); w_i = max(0, w_i - 0.75*max w); renormalise, so patches interlock along their own contours. Loop count is dim+1 constant; weights are never zero-branch-dependent.
master.why_new: It is the standard real-time anti-repetition technique for textures, but applied to the procedural graph itself: it needs lattice-driven random frames and d+1 source evaluations with barycentric weights, impossible from existing nodes. Also gives 'Sampled Phacelle'-style per-tile orientation for free when the source is PhasorNoise.
master.simd_plan: Branch-free: simplex traversal exactly as in Simplex noise (compare masks, Select), then D+1 Source evaluations with hashed transforms. Cost = (D+1) x Source + ~Simplex overhead: with FBm Simplex 4 as Source, 2D ~3x that source. Dimension-agnostic via the simplex lattice (2D/3D/4D all exact; tiling works).
master.continuity: C1 (measured c0ratio 7.99, the cleanest) if the kernel falls to zero at its support boundary and Source is continuous. Normalisation denominator cannot reach 0 since at least one kernel is nonzero everywhere.
master.params: Source, Rotation amount (hybrid), Offset amount, Sharpness, Blend enum (Variance/Height), Height Influence, Per-vertex seed toggle, Scale jitter
master.risks:
Known technique in texture synthesis, though unknown as a graph node. Simplex 3D/4D kernels at radius 0.5 and 0.6 need care so a weight is zero at simplex boundaries (handbook notes small jumps in Simplex at 0.6). Rotation breaks the Source's axis-dependent meaning (e.g. terrain slope), which is the point, but needs a Max Angle param. Low-frequency sources show less.
[StochasticPatchBlend, hierarchy-multiscale] Binary/high-contrast sources blur in blend zones (Heitz solves with a Gaussianising histogram transform, which we cannot do on a black-box node; Sharpen is the pragmatic fix). Rotation of anisotropic lattices (Perlin) can expose the Source's own grid at some angles; fine for Simplex sources.
[SimplexTileBlend, terrain-tools-engines] Variance-preserving blend assumes roughly Gaussian source statistics (binary sources like Checkerboard get overshoot: clamp); 3x source cost in 2D, 4x in 3D; large OffsetRange with far coordinates eats float precision (keep offsets modest and let the source's own hash decorrelate).
master.cost_note: Cost = (D+1) x Source + ~Simplex overhead: with FBm Simplex 4 as Source, 2D ~3x that source.
master.variant_notes: Heitz-Neyret blending of d+1 transformed source evals on the simplex lattice. Best in tests with anisotropic sources (PatchTuft straw, stripes as tangled zebra). Height-based blending interlocks patches. Binary sources blur in blend zones.
